  rejected on the text itself: a role is the identity on stage, one at a time, while the order's first
  line says it *supplements* a role, and the traits in this terminal are defined as exactly that
  ("goes on over the role and stays with her across roles"). `id: cody`, `kind: text` (it shapes the
  reply; it renders nothing), title `CODY — Operational Realist (SYS.AI.MUSE.TERPSICHORE)`, worn with
  `/load cody`, put down with `/unload cody`.
- **The text is his, whole.** Embedded verbatim (~13,100 chars) with one lead-in sentence that names
  the Human as Patrikios and marks it as standing rather than a temporary mode. Nothing was condensed,
  cut or reworded — an order that opens with *"Do not perform engineering theater"* is not one to
  paraphrase for length. The attachment died with that session's `scratch/`;
  `src/corepack/corepack.json` is now its durable copy.
- **Smallest necessary change:** one object appended to `skills` in `src/corepack/corepack.json`, and
  the manifest's `version` 2 → 3 (nothing in `src/js` reads that field — checked, not assumed). No new
  file, so `src/pack/files.json` needs no regeneration and `staleCheck()` stays null. No code, no kv
  key, no change to the order of the stack.
- **Verified live** (`page_refresh`, then the same functions the `/load` command calls):
  `packs.skillList()` and `packs.catalog()` list it; `getSkill("cody")` resolves; `loadTrait("cody")`
  → kv `loaded_traits` `["chronicle","cody"]`, `traitsSummary()` `CHRONICLE, CODY`, and
  `traitBlock()` carrying the order (14,316 chars, from the `LOADED TRAITS` header through
  "Collect cash."); `unloadTrait("cody")` → back to `["chronicle"]`, summary `CHRONICLE`. `chat.js`
  (lines 15 / 40 / 82) is the wiring that puts that block into the built instruction — inspected, not
  assumed. **His loaded stack was left exactly as it was found**, and nothing was worn on his behalf:
  loading a trait is his act, and a 13k-char order is a real cost on every turn, so it goes on when
  the engineering work starts.
- **His call, if he wants it otherwise:** a RoleLayer (`src/roles/cody.md` + an entry in
  `roles.json`) would put CODY *on stage* instead of over the layer she is already wearing. Same text,
  small move — not made, because he did not ask for it and one home is enough.

## 1u. A recording in her line of sight — the one predicate the queue was missing (DONE 2026-09-21)

His report, verbatim: *"There is a problem with the 'ai-text-plugin' generator… Error: ai-text-plugin:
attachment must be a png/jpeg/webp image Blob (got type "audio/wav")."*

- **FINDING.** The sight queue could hold anything. `queueSight()` (images.js) had no kind test at
  all, and the two callers that did try to exclude non-pictures excluded only VIDEO by mime
  (`!/^video\//.test(r.mime || "")` - `/sight <n>` in chat.js, `/embed show` in chat.js), so a
  recording rode straight through. The gallery's `◉` is offered on a music tile too, and the turn
  path hands every queued id with `kind:"attach"` into `attachPool` → `attachSeen` → the *direct*
  attachment Blob. That blob is what the plugin validates, so a `audio/wav` in the queue throws
  before a single token is generated.
- **EVIDENCE.** The vault holds two recordings as ordinary attachments -
  `mmubezc7ltliu5` *Beyond the Veil-MASTERED.wav* and `mmubezcc2cw4z3` *Orbital Pulse-MASTERED.wav*,
  both `kind:"attach"`, `mime:"audio/wav"` (vault.js stores `mime: blob.type || "image/jpeg"`, so the
  mime is authoritative for everything real — and see §1v, where that line became the whole problem:
  the type is now RESOLVED rather than taken on trust). Both are the NEWEST records in the vault, which is why
  `/sight 2` was the shortest road into the error.
- **IMPACT — the worst case was worse than one failed reply.** Because every unseen ATTACHMENT is
  kept in the queue uncapped (by design: he chose it, so it is never dropped unseen), a queued
  recording would not fail once. It would fail on *every* message until the queue was cleared by
  hand - a bricked terminal, from one press of `◉` on a song. Nothing was wedged when I looked: the
  queue was empty, so the error he saw had already spent itself.
- **ACTION - the smallest change that removes the class, not the instance.** One predicate,
  `lookable(id)` in images.js (a blob, not `kind:"video"`, mime `image/*`), asked at the queue's own
  door: `queueSight()` now refuses anything else, NAMES it on screen, and evicts it if it was somehow
  already waiting. `loadSight()` filters the same way, so a queue stored before the gate existed
  cannot wedge a boot either. The two chat.js filters now call `lookable()` instead of re-inventing
  half a rule, and the gallery's status line reports the truth (`taken`/`refused`) rather than
  claiming a queue that did not happen. Deliberately NOT done: per-caller guards (every caller goes
  through the queue) and a config knob (there is nothing here to tune).
- **VERIFICATION, live.** 363 records in the vault, 359 lookable; both wavs and both clips `false`,
  an upscaled jpeg `true`; `queueSight([wav1,wav2])` → `{queued:0, refused:[both]}`, queue still
  empty; `queueSight([picture])` → `{queued:1}` and the id present; a poisoned kv queue
  (`unseen_sight: [wav1]`) dropped by `loadSight()` with the refusal named; **`/sight 3` through the
  real input box queued three `image/jpeg` pictures - not the two newest records, which are the
  wavs** - and `markSeen` restored the queue to empty; the gallery's `◉` on the music tile answers
  *"NOTHING TO LOOK AT :: 1 OF THESE IS NOT A PICTURE - ONLY IMAGES GO IN FRONT OF HER, AND A CLIP
  REACHES HER AS THE STILL IT CARRIES."* while the same button on a picture tile still queues
  (`1 QUEUED`, `image/jpeg`). `master_log` was 389 before and 389 after every test - the record was
  never written to - and the queue was left exactly as it was found (empty).
- **REMAINING UNKNOWN / his call.** `◉` is still offered on music and clip tiles; it now refuses with
  a reason instead of queueing. Hiding it on those tiles is a one-line change in the tile builder -
  not made, because the refusal is informative and the look of the gallery is his. And no real model
  call was spent proving the end of it: the gate makes a non-picture unreachable, and his next turn
  with a picture queued is the honest end-to-end.

## 1v. The audio lane: an untyped file is not a picture, and audio/mpeg is not a .mpg (DONE 2026-09-21)

His report, verbatim: *"Audio problem. We do .wav and .mp3"*. Terse, so the lane was audited end to
end rather than a single symptom chased - the two formats in play are `.wav` and `.mp3`, and both
were put through every door (`attach.add()` the paperclip, `media.add()` the vault, the gallery's
IMPORT PICTURES / MUSIC, the sight queue, the lightbox stage, `fileName()`/SAVE) with real bytes.
Two defects fell out, both in the same class as §1u and both invisible while a browser reports the
mime it is supposed to.

- **FINDING 1 - an untyped recording became a PICTURE.** `vault.add()` wrote
  `mime: blob.type || "image/jpeg"` and IGNORED both the caller's `meta.mime` and the file name. A
  browser does not always report a type: an `.mp3`/`.wav` dragged out of a file manager, or unpacked
  from an archive, arrives as `file.type === ""`. Defaulted to `image/jpeg` that record then
  1. files itself in **/images** instead of /music (`folderOf` reads the mime),
  2. is painted as a tile with no picture in the gallery (`gallery.kindOf` reads the mime),
  3. becomes **lookable** - so it is handed to the vision model, which throws and takes the whole
     turn down, exactly the bricked-terminal failure §1u just closed through the other door, and
  4. would have been SAVEd under a `.jpg` name.
- **FINDING 2 - `audio/mpeg` was saved as `.mpg`.** `extFor()` tested `/mpeg/` (a *video* container
  test) before `/mp3/`, so the standard mime of an mp3 - `audio/mpeg` - came back as the video
  extension: a piece of music came out of the vault named `….mpg`. `audio/mp4` hit the same trap and
  came back `.mp4` instead of `.m4a`.
- **FINDING 3 - a silent type was sent as silence to the transcriber.** `transcribe()` handed the
  service `file.type || "application/octet-stream"` (Whisper) and an untyped FormData part
  (ElevenLabs Scribe), which a service is entitled to refuse; the resolve below fixes what is sent
  without re-encoding a byte.
- **EVIDENCE, live (each one a real File through the real door).** Untyped `.mp3` → record
  `mime:"audio/mpeg"`, `folderOf` **/music**, `lookable` **false**, `fileName` `probe-untyped.mp3`;
  BEFORE the change the same file → `mime:"image/jpeg"`, **/images**, `lookable` **true**. Untyped
  `.wav` → `audio/wav`, /music, lookable false; untimed probe of `media.extFor`: `audio/mpeg`→**mpg**
  before, **mp3** after; `audio/mp4`→mp4 before, **m4a** after; `audio/wav`, `audio/x-wav`,
  `audio/mp3`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/flac`, `audio/aac`, `audio/x-m4a` all resolve to their own
  extension now. Through the paperclip (`window.attach.add([untypedMp3, typedMp3])`): both chips read
  `AUD … .mp3`, both records in /music, no rejection in the log. Through the gallery
  (`gallery.importFiles([untypedWav])`): *"1 KEPT IN THE VAULT"*, record `audio/wav`, tile in the
  MUSIC filter with the ♫ glyph in /music, not a broken picture tile. The gallery's file picker
  (`#galFileInput`) also carried only `image/*,audio/*`, which on a platform that reports an unknown
  type greys out the very files this is about - it now lists the extensions too (`.wav`, `.mp3`, …),
  as the paperclip's input already did.
- **ACTION - the smallest change that makes the class impossible, not the instance.**
  `src/js/vault.js`: a `MIME_BY_EXT` table + `mimeFor(blob, name, told)` - the blob's own type, then
  the caller's, then **the extension of the name**, then the old image/jpeg fallback - used by
  `add()`, so *every* record born in this vault now knows what it is, and exported for callers
  (`attach.js` for its documents and the transcribe headers, `gallery.js` for its imports).
  `extFor()` answers every `audio/*` mime before any container test, so no sound can ever be saved
  as a video or a picture, and `fileName()` now writes an audio master back out **under its own name
  in its own container**, which is what the clip rule next door has always done (a piece of music is
  his master too, and the lightbox says so) - so `Beyond the Veil-MASTERED.wav` saves as
  `Beyond the Veil-MASTERED.wav`. `src/js/images.js`: `lookable()` first grew to three witnesses (the
  blob's type, the record's mime, the name's extension) and was then reduced to the ONE that is
  right: the plugin's own test, over the **blob** - `/^image\/(png|jpeg|webp)$/`, read off the
  plugin's source at `imports/ai-text-plugin/main.pjs:149`, which is the thing that actually
  validates the attachment (a GIF and an untyped blob are refused there too). The record's mime is
  not what the model reads, so asking the blob is what closes the whole class: a record written
  *before* this fix (stored `image/jpeg` over an untyped recording or a nameless untyped blob) fails
  on its empty type, while every picture the terminal itself writes is canvas/service
  `image/jpeg`/`png` and passes - 359 of 363 records, the same four refused as before.
  `src/js/archivax.js`: its private `isPicture()` became the same predicate (`lookable`), removing
  the second copy of the rule that §1u left standing.
- **VERIFICATION, live.** After `page_refresh`: 363 records in the vault, the two wav masters both
  `/music`, `galleryKind` music, `lookable` false, `fileName` now their own names; `queueSight()` on
  freshly imported untyped audio → `{queued:0, refused:[…]}` while a picture still queues; the
  lightbox opens each of them on its own player (scrubbed to the last check below). Every probe
  record was deleted, the queue left empty, the test's log lines removed, and the vault count is
  **363** at the end, as it was at the start. The gate was then re-checked over the whole vault (359
  lookable; lookable records whose blob type the plugin would reject: **0**), and a nameless untyped
  audio blob - the one case no type and no name can identify - is now **refused by the gate and by
  the queue, named**, instead of being carried into a turn; a canvas jpeg still queues.
  **What is NOT verified: playback of a newly imported
  untyped file**, because the preview document reported `visibilityState: "hidden"` for the length of
  this work and a browser will not load media in a hidden document (`readyState` stayed 0 and
  `play()` stayed pending, for an untyped file *and* for a typed one) - the masters themselves were
  played on the stage earlier in the same session, with the same element and the same code path.
  Re-running the import-and-play check on a visible tab is the honest end-to-end.
- **REMAINING UNKNOWN / his call.** (a) `◉` is still offered on music and clip tiles and refuses with
  a reason (§1u) - unchanged, still his look to decide. (b) `CLIP_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB) is shared by
  clips and recordings, so a WAV master longer than about seven minutes is announced by name and not
  kept (`ONLY ITS WORDS`). Nothing was changed here: it is a real storage decision, not a bug, and if
  his wav masters grow past it the knob deserves its own config entry (`LIA_ATTACH_MAX`-style) rather
  than a quiet bump. (c) The transcription call with a real key is still unproven (§3) - the only
  change on that road is *what type is declared*, so it can only help.

## 1w. THE AUDITION BUS — one transport, and her ears (DONE 2026-09-21, verified live on his key)

His ask, verbatim: *"I'd love to be able to hear her live comments while 'auditioning' together. That
would be a great feature for all media. We need an audio audition BUS. It is simply audio playback for
now where we both listen together. Is there audio learning like vision learning?"* Three things were
built, and one of them is the answer to the question.

- **FINDING 1 - THE MODEL SHE SPEAKS THROUGH HAS NO AUDIO SENSE AT ALL.** The text plugin validates an
  attachment as `/^image\/(png|jpeg|webp)$/` (`imports/ai-text-plugin/main.pjs:149`) and nothing else;
  there is no audio path in it and nowhere to put one. So "audio learning" cannot be done in the voice
  she speaks through - but there are two real roads to it, and both now exist: the WORDS road
  (speech-to-text - ElevenLabs Scribe, Whisper - already wired into ATTACHMENTS) and the SOUND road
  (a second model call that is actually handed the audio). The second one is what HER EARS is.
- **FINDING 2 - TWO PLAYERS IS NOT LISTENING TOGETHER.** Before this, a tune made its own `<audio>`
  inside the lightbox, and nothing tied playback to the conversation at all: her turns were answered
  with no idea a piece was playing, and there was nowhere for a comment about it to live. "Both listen
  together" needs ONE transport with ONE shared playhead, and her turns need to know where that
  playhead is.
- **FINDING 3 - A MODEL THE KEY CAN REACH IS NOT A MODEL THAT WILL LISTEN.** With his Google key
  stored, `HER EARS` failed on *"this model is currently experiencing high demand"*. Measured: a
  text-only call to `gemini-3.8-flash` returned **503** too (so for that name it was not the audio
  payload at all), `gemini-2.5-flash` answered *"no longer available to new users"*, and
  `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` answered a TEXT call **200** while the very same model returned **503** for
  the audio part - so what congests is the audio-understanding backend, per model, moment to moment.
  `gemini-flash-lite-latest` listened fine. The code made two mistakes in the face of that:
  `pickModel()` wrote its CHOICE into the settings BEFORE any call (so one busy name stuck as "her
  ears" for good), and the retry fired only on "not found / unsupported / permission" wording - never
  on *busy*. One congested alias therefore bricked the button while a working listener sat next in
  the list.
- **ACTION - `src/js/audition.js` (new), plus the wiring.** One `<audio>` for the whole terminal
  (`#busAudio`), one transport painted into every `[data-bus-rack]` host (`#busStrip` above the input,
  `#lightboxRack` on the full stage), `block()` riding in her instruction on any turn answered while a
  piece is on, `ask()`/`deliver()` for a comment with no words from him (the road `/checkin` already
  used: static prompt first, task last), the unasked cadence, the audition log, ducking, and `learn()`
  - her ears: the vault's own blob decoded through `AudioContext` and re-rendered by
  `OfflineAudioContext` as mono 16 kHz 16-bit WAV, sent as `inlineData` to Gemini `generateContent`,
  the answer written onto the record as `heard`. Knobs in `config.js`, strip + deck AUDITION button in
  `index.html`, a new CSS block in `terminal.css`; the lightbox's tune branch and the gallery music
  tile's ▶ put their piece on the bus instead of making their own player. **`src/pack/` was regenerated
  as part of this** (`index.html.txt` byte-for-byte, and `files.json` now lists `js/audition.js`) -
  the bus added BOTH a script tag and a new source file, which is exactly the pair that makes the
  packed backup stale, and `backup.staleCheck()` returned `null` again afterwards. **And the model
  choice is a fact about the SERVICE, not about the list** (FINDING 3): `rankedModels()` (cached 30
  min) + `pickModel(list, used)` (the model that WORKED last first, then the ranking) +
  `modelFailed()` with a ten-minute cooldown + `EARS_TRIES` (4) attempts, each refusal printed by
  name, and `settings.earsModel` written only once a piece has actually come back.
- **EVIDENCE, live (real files, real DOM).** A 37 KB mp3 and a 30 MB WAV through the real doors:
  `load()` → the strip visible with name, `LOADED · LINE 1`, `NO EAR YET · NO GOOGLE KEY`, transport,
  scrub and time; the gallery music tile's ▶ loads AND plays; the lightbox stage for a tune shows the
  rack and playback survives closing it; `/bus` and `/hear` both through the real input box; `/hear
  ears` with no key refuses honestly and names the key. The EAR LANE was driven end to end with the
  keyring stubbed over a real 30 MB WAV: the request body carried `mimeType:"audio/wav"`, magic
  `RIFF`/`WAVE`, rate **16000**, channels **1**, bits **16**, 960000 data bytes (exactly 30 s), on
  `gemini-3.8-flash` (the embedding model was correctly skipped), and the answer landed as `heard` on
  the record. The COMMENT road was driven with `generateText` and `voice.onReply` stubbed: her line in
  the log, the archive entry with `audition:{id,name,at:0,dur:333.9,why:"asked"}`, the remark in the
  audition log. `block()` was read in both states - with a `heard` (told what she heard, as her own
  earlier reading) and without (told in as many words that she has NOT heard it and must not pretend
  to). Every probe was cleaned up: the `heard` fields, the log lines, the archive entry, the audition
  log and the settings were all restored, and the vault is back to **363** records, 359 lookable.
- **VERIFICATION, visual.** The strip was captured and looked at at desktop width and at 390×844: no
  horizontal overflow at phone width (`scrollWidth === innerWidth`), the transport wraps into a head
  row and a control row inside 366 px, and the badge and the × were confirmed present and hit-testable
  by geometry and `elementFromPoint` - a strip-only screenshot had cropped them at the right edge,
  which is what the vision model reported as "missing". The full-page phone frame has both, in frame.
- **EVIDENCE 2 - LIVE, ON HIS KEY (the end-to-end this section was missing).** `keyring.test("google")`
  → `{ ok:true, status:200 }` against `/v1beta/models`. `learn()` on `Orbital Pulse-MASTERED.wav`
  (173.2 s, 29.1 MB) → `heard` written, `{ model: "gemini-flash-lite-latest", seconds: 173.2,
  total: 173.2, rate: 16000, note: "a mono 16 kHz reduction made on this device" }`, the picker having
  stepped down from `gemini-flash-latest` by itself (FINDING 3). `learn()` on
  `Beyond the Veil-MASTERED.wav` (333.9 s, 56.2 MB) → `{ seconds: 180, total: 333.9, note: "a mono
  16 kHz reduction made on this device, from 0:00 of 5:34" }` - the cap is stated on the record and in
  what she is told (`heardText()`), so she cannot think she heard the whole of it. The gallery
  captions now read `♫ "…"` from the reading, the strip reads `SHE HAS HEARD IT` / `LISTEN AGAIN`, and
  the full stage shows it in its meta line. Then her live comments USED it: *"That low end is
  absolutely relentless. It feels like it's trying to push us right out of the room."* at 0:42 of
  Orbital Pulse (her reading: *"strong emphasis on the low end"*) and *"That hum in the beginning
  always makes me feel like I'm floating just above the floor. I love the way the beat finally
  catches."* at 1:30 of Beyond the Veil (reading: *"opens with a spoken female vocal over an ethereal
  hum, then transitions to a driving dance beat"*). The six comments already in the audition log from
  BEFORE the key are all blind by comparison (*"I cannot hear the music … but I can feel the weight of
  the silence"*), which is the honest behaviour working as designed. Every one is in the archive with
  `audition: { id, name, at, dur, why }` and in the audition log with the moment it was made at.
  Geometry checked at 390×844 and 1920×1080: no overflow, the × inside the strip, nothing escaping the
  rack.
- **ALSO WIRED: HER HEARING IS A SEARCHABLE FACT (`embed.js`).** The media lane now embeds a
  recording with her `heard` reading beside its name (`mediaWords()`), and the change signature
  includes it, so a piece whose reading arrives LATER is re-embedded instead of skipped - which is
  what makes her learning useful rather than decorative: `/embed find <words>` finds a piece BY WHAT
  SHE HEARD IN IT. Verified live: `indexMedia` took both masters (one skipped as unchanged, one
  `wordsOnly`), and then `findMedia("ethereal hum that turns into a driving beat")` returned
  `Beyond the Veil` FIRST (its reading: *"opens with a spoken female vocal over an ethereal hum, then
  transitions to a driving dance beat"*) while `findMedia("dark club track with a relentless low
  end")` returned `Orbital Pulse` first. **ONE MEASURED LIMIT:** the embedding request is inline-only
  with a 50 MiB payload ceiling, and base64 inflates by a third - so the 29 MB master went in whole
  and the 56 MB one came back *"Request payload size exceeds the limit: 52428800 bytes"*.
  `MEDIA_EMBED_MAX` (34 MiB) now decides: over it, the record is indexed **by her words for it and its
  name alone** and the run reports `wordsOnly` instead of failing - a big master is still findable by
  what she heard, just not by its samples. (Cutting the first N seconds through the ears reducer and
  embedding THAT is the obvious next step, if he wants the sound itself in the space for a long
  piece.)
- **REMAINING UNKNOWN.** (a) The service congests per model and per moment: one press can burn all
  `EARS_TRIES` (4) and fail - observed once, ~2 minutes of trying - and the answer is to press again
  later, because a refusal writes nothing and touches nothing. (b) There is no per-attempt timeout:
  `keyring.request()` builds its own `init` and does not forward an `AbortSignal`, so a queued model
  can hold the press open (a 174 s wait was observed once). Giving the ears call a timeout is part of
  the router work below. (c) The transcription road (a speech-to-text key) is still unproven from
  §1v(c) - ElevenLabs is in the ring now and both its action permissions are live, but the account
  has **0 credits** and the Hugging Face token is **rejected by HF itself** (§3), so the words road
  cannot be exercised until one of those accounts is usable; its code is unchanged and its own §1v
  fix (what type is declared to the transcriber) still stands. The ears lane does NOT replace it,
  because her ears are a reading of the sound and not a transcript of words. (d) The cadence and the duck remain logic-verified only (`quietEnough()`
  refuses while hidden / sending / speaking; `duckCheck()` drops the element to 30% and restores it) -
  they were not watched against a real speaking voice over a real playing piece. (e) Nothing on the
  bus is ever uploaded and the master is never re-encoded: what leaves the device is only the reduced
  seconds, and only when HER EARS is pressed.
- **THE BUS IS ALSO THE FIX FOR §1v's UNVERIFIED END.** §1v could not verify playback of a freshly
  imported untyped file because the preview document was hidden and browsers defer media in hidden
  documents. The document became visible later in the same session and playback was measured working
  (`playing:true`, position advancing) through the bus - which is the same element and the same code
  path the lightbox now uses, because there is only one.

## 1x. THE BOOT AUDIT, THE ONE-OFF LOAD FLAKE, AND WHAT THE THREE KEYS CAN DO (2026-09-21)

Patrikios: *"i have a ELEVENLABS, HF and GEMINI all saved."* All three were checked with real calls
rather than by believing the keystore - and the check found one platform flake and one hole in the
terminal's own diagnostics.

- **THE THREE KEYS.** **Google (Gemini) - WORKING**: `/keys test` 200, and the ears lane listened to
  both masters (§1w, EVIDENCE 2). **ElevenLabs - LIVE, ACCOUNT EMPTY**: `text_to_speech` and
  `speech_to_text` are both permitted (a `POST /v1/text-to-speech/<Matilda>` and a 3-second
  `POST /v1/speech-to-text` excerpt each answered `quota_exceeded`, not `missing_permissions`), and
  the account has **0 of its 10,000 credits**, so neither speaking nor transcribing can work until it
  is topped up; the READ permissions are absent as before (`user_read` / `voices_read` /
  `models_read`), which the shipped voice palette already covers. **Hugging Face - TOKEN REFUSED BY
  HF ITSELF**: both whoami endpoints answer 401 *"Invalid username or password"* while the header the
  ring builds is well formed (`Authorization: Bearer hf_…`, no whitespace, the value is `hf_` + 30
  chars) - a revoked or mistyped token; re-copy it from `huggingface.co/settings/tokens`. The full
  measurements are in §3's two bullets. **Nothing in the code is wrong for any of the three**: the
  ring reports each in its own terms, and `reportTest()` now names the empty-account case too -
  verified through the real `/keys test` path with the measured provider response shimmed in
  (*"KEY CHECK :: ELEVENLABS :: THE KEY IS LIVE, BUT THE ACCOUNT HAS NO QUOTA LEFT"*).
- **THE MISSING-MODULE AUDIT HAD FOUR HOLES.** index.html's boot audit pairs each `src/js` file with
  the global it exports and paints a red `#bootFail` banner listing any that did not run - but
  `audition.js`, `keepsake.js`, `archivax.js` and `chat.js` were never in the list, so a load that
  lost one of them lost it in silence. All four are added (27 entries now, and `#bootFail` staying
  absent is itself the proof that every entry resolves), and the banner's wording now admits the
  second cause - *"a single file can also fail to arrive on a load that is otherwise fine"* - instead
  of asserting the files are simply not in the saved copy.
- **THE FLAKE ITSELF (reported to the platform, 2026-09-21).** One `page_refresh` produced a load in
  which `src/js/forge.js` never executed: `window.forge` and `closeForge` undefined, `main.js` dying
  at load with *"Uncaught ReferenceError: closeForge is not defined (main.js:226)"*, and - because
  main.js's top-level code aborted - `boot()` never ran, so `keyring.load()` was never called and the
  ring reported **0 keys held while the kv record held three**. That is the dangerous shape: a lost
  script does not look like a lost script, it looks like missing user data ("she has no ear for this
  file yet", "no key is held"). All 29 files were verified syntactically valid and fetchable (HTTP
  200, full length) and a plain refresh fixed it. Two things to remember: **when a feature says a key
  or a record is missing, read `#bootFail` and `window.keyring.ready()` before believing it**, and
  reload once before diagnosing anything.

## 1y. THE IDEAL VOICE, PROFILED — AND THE FIVE WAYS ELEVENLABS SAYS NO (2026-09-21)

Patrikios handed over a full **ElevenLabs Agent export** — *"ELEVENLABS custom Agent with ideal LIA
voice profile"* — an agent built in the ElevenLabs UI, named `BARBELO`, carrying the voice profile he
considers hers. Nothing was asked for beyond handing it over; this is the recording of it, the wiring
that makes it reachable in one command, and the measurement of why it cannot be heard yet.

- **FINDING 1 — the ideal voice is unreachable ON THIS PLAN, and it is the VOICE, not the model.**
  `POST /v1/text-to-speech/0oYUKTNPbymIKVAkDQqh` answers **HTTP 402 `paid_plan_required`** — *"Free
  users cannot use library voices via the API. Please upgrade your subscription to use this voice."*
  — at **every** model id tried (`eleven_v3_conversational`, `eleven_v3`, `eleven_multilingual_v2`).
  A bogus id answers `404 voice_not_found` instead, so the id is real and the refusal is about its
  *category*: `0oYUKTNPbymIKVAkDQqh` is a **library** voice, and the shipped palette is the premade
  set a free plan may speak. The refusal lands **before billing**, which is what makes it measurable
  on an account with no credits at all.
- **FINDING 2 — the model table is measurable for free, and `eleven_v3_conversational` is HALF
  RATE.** Seven ids accepted, two deprecated (`eleven_monolingual_v1`, `eleven_multilingual_v1`
  answer HTTP 400 `unsupported_model`). The credit figure the provider quotes for a **three-character**
  probe is its rate: `eleven_multilingual_v2` 3, `eleven_v3` 3, `eleven_v3_conversational` 2, and all
  four turbo/flash ids 2 — so v3-conversational and turbo/flash cost **half** what the shipped default
  costs for the same text. That is the first cost lever this terminal has ever had on her voice, and
  it is recorded in `src/voice/voices.json` → `elevenlabs.models` **with the date on it**.
- **FINDING 3 — the agent around it is unreachable for a second reason, and it is a permission.** A
  ConvAI session is speech-to-speech over one websocket, and **a browser websocket cannot carry
  `xi-api-key` on the handshake** — so the signed-url endpoint is the only door, and it answers HTTP
  401 `missing_permissions convai_write`. `convai_read` is absent too (the agent cannot even be
  listed or read back), and the account holds 0 of 10,000 credits. So the agent lane is blocked at
  **three** independent gates, none of which is code.
- **WHAT WAS BUILT** (small, and every piece of it verifiable today):
  1. **The profile, recorded** — `elevenlabs.profiles.lia` in the design file: voice id, model,
     settings, first message, the Greek preset, the agent's facts (Scribe ASR, gemini-3.7-flash,
     turn_v2, pcm_16000, a 600 s cap, the client-event list), and **its own measurement** with the
     date. The agent id is **not** in `src/` (it is this account's identifier and belongs in kv with
     the rest of the device state), and the agent's **prompt is not copied into the repo at all** —
     it is Patrikios' proprietary control-protocol spec and `src/` is public.
  2. **`/voice profile [<NAME>]`** — lists the profiles, and applies one to the role on stage *as a
     set*: its voice id, its model, and its settings taken exactly (`settingsExact`, so nothing merges
     in from the shipped design underneath). Applying prints the measurement, so a blocked voice is
     never discovered in the middle of a sentence. `/voice profile reset` (or `/voice reset`) puts the
     shipped design back, and the kv box is pruned rather than left as `{}`.
  3. **`/voice models` and `/voice model <ID|default>`** — the measured table, printed, plus a
     per-role model override. An id outside the table is still sent as given (a record is not a gate);
     it simply arrives with the warning that it is unverified.
  4. **Every refusal translated** — `paid_plan_required` / `quota_exceeded` / `missing_permissions` /
     `voice_not_found` / `unsupported_model` / `model_not_found` each print as `ELEVENLABS CALLED IT
     :: <CODE>` + `WHY` + `WHAT WOULD FIX IT`, with the provider's own sentence as the headline and
     the `request_id` kept as the handle they would ask for. `keys.js` gained the matching branch, so
     `/keys test` calls a plan limit a **plan state** rather than a rejected key.
- **VERIFICATION (live, on his own key).** `/voice profile lia` applied → `state()` reports voice
  `0oYUKTNPbymIKVAkDQqh` / model `eleven_v3_conversational` / profile `lia`; a real `speak()` then
  posted to ElevenLabs with those and came back **HTTP 402 `paid_plan_required`**, the log carrying
  the four translated lines and the request id (the browser engine was stubbed to take the fallback,
  so nothing was heard in the room); `/voice models` and `/voice profile` printed through the real
  `window.send()` path; `/voice profile reset` returned her to the shipped design (Alice /
  `eleven_multilingual_v2`, no profile) with nothing left behind in kv. Two defects were found and
  fixed **by measuring rather than assuming**: the first version parsed a **truncated** body (the
  402's own JSON runs past 220 characters) and got its sentence right only by luck of the wording, and
  it matched only the `code` label — but the permissions refusal carries `code "unauthorized"` **and**
  `status "missing_permissions"`, so a scoped key read as a dead one.
- **REMAINING UNKNOWN. (a)** Whether `eleven_v3_conversational` *sounds* right for her: the ids are
  accepted and priced, but nothing here can hear them, and the shipped default was deliberately left
  alone (`/voice model eleven_v3_conversational` is the one-line trial, and it is cheaper). **(b)**
  Whether the library voice is usable *through the API* on a paid plan: the refusal is plan-shaped,
  but that is the provider's policy statement, not a guarantee about what a paid plan unlocks — one
  call re-measures it the moment the plan changes. **(c)** The agent lane below, never exercised at
  all. **(d)** The profile is a per-role override like every other `/voice` setting, so applying it
  while off stage sets it for `default`; wearing BARBELO afterwards is a different role (the print
  names the role it applied to for exactly that reason).
- **THE AGENT LANE (NOT built, deliberately).** A ConvAI session would **replace** the terminal's
  browser-STT → text turn → TTS loop with a single websocket carrying its own ASR, its own LLM and
  its own TTS. So it would not pass through her role block, the LOREPACK turn, the ECHO GUARD or THE
  HOLD unless a lane is built to route around them — and none of it is verifiable from here
  (`convai_write` absent, 0 credits, and the websocket needs the signed URL because a browser cannot
  set the auth header). It is the natural home of the **router** in §2 (THE SWITCHER): a
  `speech-to-speech` capability sitting beside `text-to-speech`, chosen by what is reachable. What
  would make it buildable: a key with `convai_read` + `convai_write`, and credits.

**UPDATE 2026-09-30 - THE WHOLE EXPORT, HANDED OVER.** Patrikios: *"UPDATE: Here is the json config
for Custom Agent with ELEVENLABS:"* - the complete config export of the agent, where §1y had only what
could be read off the profile. Nothing in §1y was wrong; the export confirms it field by field and adds
the envelope around it.

- **CONFIRMED, FACT BY FACT.** voice id `0oYUKTNPbymIKVAkDQqh`, model `eleven_v3_conversational`,

- **A FOURTH GATE, AND IT IS A DESIGN ONE: `enable_auth` is true.** The agent is **private** - no
  allowlist, no shareable token - so a session has to be signed server-side. That is the same wall §1y
  measured from the other side (a browser websocket cannot carry `xi-api-key`), and it means the

- **THE ENVELOPE, none of which was known before**: **10 calls a day**, concurrency unlimited

- **THE RECORDING TERMS, which are the picture lane's question in another form.** `record_voice:
  true` with `retention_days: -1` - every conversation is **recorded and kept indefinitely by
  ElevenLabs**; zero-retention off, `delete_audio` off, user memory off. The picture lane's rule here
  is "never public"; this is "recorded forever by a third party", and it is equally his call - flagged
  in `src/voxpack/README.md`, not changed on his behalf.
- **THE GUARDRAILS, and the one that bites.** focus and prompt-injection detection **on**; content:
  violence on at threshold medium with its action set to **END THE CALL**, sexual **off**,
  harassment / profanity / self-harm / religion / medical all off; moderation: violence,
  violence_graphic, hate, hate_threatening and sexual_minors on (0.3, and 0.5 for sexual_minors). So
  the explicit road is open and the **violence road ends the call** - a Mythos conversation would trip
  that rule the first time she said something violent out loud.
- **THE PROMPT IS A SPEC, NOT A PERSONA - and that is the real finding.** The agent's system prompt
  is VOXCONPACK v0.1 verbatim: an Architectural Specification (Merk Morassi, LLC; *"ALL SIGNAL. NO
  NOISE.™"*), whose §2 principle is *"**Voice is an input modality, not authority.**"* and whose §3
  diagram names the family - COREPACK, AUTHPACK, GATEPACK, JUDGEPACK, FINPACK, GAMEPACK, LOREPACK,
  Other PACKs. Talk to `BARBELO` today and it answers as **the architect of the document**, not as the
  Mother. So the first decision is not technical: either the spec becomes the preamble to a persona,
  or the prompt is the wrong document for the agent he wants to hear.
- **WHERE IT IS KEPT, AND WHY NOT HERE.** The identity fields (agent id, version id, branch id,
  creator), the operational envelope and the prompt **verbatim** are in kv `lia_settings / agent` -
  device state, which is §1y's own rule ("the agent id is this account's identifier and belongs in kv
  with the rest of the device state"). **The prompt is still NOT in `src/`**: it is proprietary and
  this tree is public, so the hand-over does not publish it by itself. Every fact that is safe to print
  goes into `src/voice/voices.json` → `profiles.lia.agent`, the folder `src/voxpack/` is created as the
  declared placeholder (a README, nothing else - the `src/archpack/` shape), and **the question of
  whether the spec ships as a document is asked, not assumed.**
- **ANSWERED THE SAME DAY - THE TEMPLATE SHIPS, AND IT IS THE STANDARD.** Patrikios sent the
  document again with a line over it: *"Standard Template for all LIAs with ElevenLabs access."* So
  the rule §1y made on 2026-09-21 (*"the agent's prompt is not copied into the repo at all"*) is
  **retired by his own designation**, and "does the spec ship in src/voxpack/?" is answered. What
  ships is his text, verbatim and unedited, at **`src/voxpack/VOXCONPACK.md`** (2,277 characters -
  verified **byte-identical** to the copy on the device in kv `lia_settings / agent` and to the prompt
  inside the config export). What stays out of `src/`: the account material (agent id, version id,
  branch id, creator) and the operational envelope, both in kv. `src/voxpack/README.md` is the
  folder's record and carries the envelope table.
- **AND THE QUESTION MOVES RATHER THAN CLOSING.** "Standard template" settles what the prompt *is*
  and does not settle what goes **around** it: as it stands the agent answers as the architect of the
  document, and if the template is the floor for all fifteen ALIAs then a **persona** is what each one
  adds on top. That is the first thing to settle before an agent is built for a second ALIA.
- **UNCHANGED: the lane is not built.** ConvAI would still replace the browser-STT → turn → TTS loop
  rather than feed it, and the four gates still stand.

## 1z. THE STORY LANE — longform rendered elsewhere and played here (2026-09-21)

His spec, verbatim: *"We build a Text-to-Speech audio creation playback engine for long storytelling
sessions. She creates the text > sends to ChatterBox > plays back audio inline. She listens only. If
interrupted or asked a question, switch to LIVE CHAT TTS. Then keeps playing back audio. When done,
she returns to LIVE Text-to-Speech. Cuts cost down because any longform is sent to HuggingFace."* -
and, pointing at the Space: *"That one sucks and ignores the audio sample. This one is better:
https://huggingface.co/spaces/ResembleAI/Chatterbox."* Built as `src/js/story.js` (THE STORY LANE in
the README).

**FINDING 1 — the road he named is the right one, and its cloning is real.** `ResembleAI/Chatterbox`
is Resemble AI's own TTS with genuine voice cloning: its `app.py` does
`if audio_prompt_path_input: generate_kwargs["audio_prompt_path"] = audio_prompt_path_input` and the
model turns that clip into **speaker conditionals** (`prepare_conditionals`), so the sample DEFINES the
voice. EVIDENCE, measured in the page 2026-09-21 against a live Chatterbox (`OLAVAUD/Chatterbox_Unlimited`,
the same model on `cpu-basic`), one sentence, seed held at 42, autocorrelation pitch taken from the
returned wav: reference clip at **220 Hz** → render at **216 Hz**; the same clip pitched down to
**159 Hz** → render at **148 Hz**. Two references, two outputs, each following its reference. (The
older `ResembleAI/Dramabox` road *did* receive the reference - its schema was matched and its own
`app.py` shows `audio_ref` → RE-USE denoise → VAE encode - but that is a style/timbre pass, not a
speaker-conditioned synthesis, which is why it stayed as a fallback rather than the default.)

**FINDING 2 — the ceiling is 300 characters, and it truncates silently.** Chatterbox's own line is
`current_model.generate(text_input[:300], ...)`, so a part is capped at 300 characters (≈22 s of
speech) in `story.js`, `voice.chunk` breaks at sentence ends and word boundaries, and a piece that
still exceeded the ceiling would be said out loud rather than swallowed. The Space also carries an
inaudible **Perth** watermark on every clip it returns.

**FINDING 3 — the `/call` shortcut is not the road; the space's own queue is.** Gradio offers
`/gradio_api/call/<name>` + its event stream, and its own queue (`/queue/join` → `/queue/data?session_hash=`).
EVIDENCE: against `OLAVAUD/Chatterbox_Unlimited`, `/call` answered `"404: Session not found."` while
the queue road **completed and returned audio** (33 characters → 111,404 bytes; the same call shape
elsewhere answered `/call` happily). The order matters and was measured: **join first, then open the
stream** — the join is what registers the session, so a stream opened before it is told the session
does not exist. `startCall()` now tries one door and falls back to the other (retrying the other way
round if the preferred one fails), and remembers which door worked (`preferTransport`).

**FINDING 4 — the anonymous GPU quota is small, shared, and it is the most likely thing in the way.**
EVIDENCE, verbatim from a Space: *"You have exceeded your ZeroGPU runs limit. Authenticate with a
Hugging Face token for more quota."* - and a held key changes that: on the same Space, with his
Hugging Face key attached, a 32-character line rendered **keyed** in 26-28 s. So the keyring
attachment is not decoration; it is what buys the runs. (This also *corrects* §1y's reading of the
key: the key stored in the ring IS accepted by the GPU spaces, whatever the account endpoints said.)

**FINDING 5 — `ResembleAI/Chatterbox` itself answers NO API client right now, by either door.** Every
request tried (all parameters, with a reference, without one, with his key, anonymously, through
`/call` AND through the space's own queue with a proper session hash and trigger id) came back
`event: error` + `404: Not Found` / `session_not_found`; its `/call` POST is accepted and given an
`event_id`, and the stream then reports the session does not exist. The space is RUNNING (2 replicas)
and its model repo is intact (all five files `ve.pt`/`t3_cfg.pt`/`s3gen.pt`/`tokenizer.json`/`conds.pt`
present, not gated), so what is failing is its queue/session layer, not the model files and not the
request shape (the same shape renders on other spaces). That is why the lane carries a second
Chatterbox road (`chatterbox-cpu`) and keeps `/story test` as a one-word way to see which road is
open. **Not verified from here:** whether its UI works for a logged-in human (a browser session may
be treated differently) - the honest one-line check for Patrikios is to press Generate on the Space's
own page.

**FINDING 6 — the clone source is ONE PER AGENT, not one for the terminal.** His ask, verbatim:
*"You'll need a audio sample per Agent LIA. I've done this before."* The clip IS the voice (see FINDING 1),
so a single sample for the whole terminal is the wrong shape: each RoleLayer has to carry its own, the way
it already carries its own live voice (`src/voice/voices.json` `roles`, overridden per role in kv
`lia_settings` / `voice`). BUILT: `story.js` keeps `samples` keyed by role id (`""` = LIA herself, off
stage; `"*"` = the FALLBACK for any agent with none of its own, which is exactly what the lane's single
sample used to be - `load()` moves an old `sample` record into that slot, so every setting made before
this change keeps its meaning and no behaviour regressed). `/story sample` with no argument prints the
table (roster, each agent's sample or fallback, the vault's audio records, and any record whose name
carries an agent's id or title offered as a suggestion - suggestions are never uploaded by themselves);
`/story sample <ID|NAME>` sets the agent ON STAGE, `... for <AGENT>` one who is not on stage (so samples
can be attached without shifting roles), `... as default` the fallback, and `... off [<AGENT>|default|all]`
clears. A record that is not `audio/*` is refused by name (a picture would fail the whole render at the
Space, after the upload). **A story LOCKS the voice it began in**: the sample is resolved once, in
`makeJob()`, and every part of that job is rendered from it - so shifting her onto another layer
mid-chapter cannot change voice mid-sentence (one story, one performance - the same reason the seed is
fixed), the strip shows whose voice it is, and the lane says so once if the role changes while a story
plays. `state()` exposes `samples`, `sample`, `sampleOwn`, `sampleFallback`, `sampleRole`; `engine()`
exposes `samples` and `lockedRole`.

**FINDING 6a — the vault lookup in the sample path was BROKEN, and had been all along.** `refBlobOf()`
read `window.media.url(rec)` — **passing the whole record where `media.url()` takes the ID** (it is a
lookup in the vault's own object-URL table, which every other caller indexes by id). No exception, no
warning: `url()` simply answered `null`, `refBlobOf()` returned `null`, and `ensureRef()` reported *"THE
SAMPLE "X" IS NOT IN THE VAULT ANY MORE"* — so the lane would have rendered **in the Space's own voice
while saying it had lost a sample it was actually holding**. Fixed to `window.media.url(samp.id)`. This
also qualifies FINDING 1: what was measured there was the SPACE cloning from a reference clip (pitch in →
pitch out), NOT this lane carrying a clip out of the vault - that last hop had never moved a byte until
now. VERIFIED 2026-09-21 with `fetch` stubbed inside the page (so nothing left the device): a render in
Barbelo's voice read the vault once and issued exactly one multipart upload — `Orbital Pulse-MASTERED.wav`,
30,556,644 bytes, `audio/wav` — a second render from the same sample uploaded **nothing** (the
per-session `refPath` cache), and a 56 MB sample was refused with the number **before** any upload. The
real network was never used for this check.

**FINDING 7 — the official `ResembleAI/Chatterbox` Space is NOT broken; the token is.** He said
*"This the one that works. I just tested it."* with the Space URL, and it is worth recording exactly
what was measured here, because the two claims are not in conflict. `/config` on the official Space is
healthy (1 dependency, `api_name: generate_tts_audio`, inputs `[4,5,6,10,9,7,11]`, output `[17]`
audio, version 6.3.0). The lane's failures were traced in order, with the page's own fetches: (1) the
Hugging Face token in his key ring answered `GET https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2` with **HTTP
401 `{"error":"Invalid username or password."}`**; (2) that means every Space call went out
**anonymous**; (3) the anonymous ZeroGPU share was spent, and the raw queue probe returned a
`process_completed` event carrying `output.error` *"You have exceeded your ZeroGPU runs limit.
Authenticate with a Hugging Face token for more quota"* with title `ZeroGPU quota exceeded`. So the
Space works for a logged-in human session (his test) and the lane was being refused for lack of a
live token (his key). **BUILT:** `queueCall()` no longer swallows the Space's own error on
`process_completed` (it used to answer *"handed back no audio"* for every failure) - it surfaces
`output.error` / `title`, and it now finds the output element that actually carries a file instead of
assuming `out[0]` does, and reports the SHAPE if none does. Plus a token check: `checkKey()` asks
whoami once per session, sets `keyDown` + `keyNote` on 401/403, and `render()` calls it when a
refusal looks like the anonymous quota; new verbs `/story key [again]` (aliases `/story token`,
`/story huggingface`); `keyLine()` in `/story road`, plus `keyVerdict` in `state()`/`engine()`.
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-21: `/story key` printed the 401 verdict with the fix instructions, and
`/story test` on `chatterbox` printed the Space's own quota sentence **plus** *"AND THE HUGGING FACE
TOKEN IN KEYS ▾ WAS REFUSED BY HUGGING FACE ITSELF (HTTP 401)"*. **Open:** paste a fresh token from
`huggingface.co/settings/tokens` (a Read token is enough) into KEYS ▾, then `/story key` and
`/story test` - the lane is already set to `chatterbox`, so it will render the moment the token is
good. The lane is currently on `chatterbox` (his pick, persisted in kv `lia_settings` / `story`).

**FINDING 8 — AUTOSAVE (his ask, and what it can and cannot do).** His ask, verbatim: *"Autosave after
every clean build please. I'm afraid to leave this page to get the main save to fire on F5 refresh."*
The fear is measured, not imagined: the editor lives on another origin, so **this page cannot press
SAVE** - `saveGenerator`, `save`, `generatorSave`, `editorSave` are all `undefined` on the preview
window (probed 2026-09-21). The autosave is therefore insurance, not a save. **BUILT** in
`src/js/backup.js` (`window.backup`) and wired in `src/js/main.js`'s `boot()` right after
`announce()`: at every boot, if the build is **COHERENT** (`staleCheck() === null` - the packed
`src/pack/index.html.txt` names exactly the scripts this page actually loaded) AND the source is not
all on the server yet, the whole tree is zipped and the Blob is kept in kv (`lia_settings` /
`backup_zip`, newest only) with a record in `lia_settings` / `backup`. **"Clean" is defined honestly:**
a missing module or a startup fault is RECORDED into the snapshot (`modulesMissing`, `issues`) and the
log line's tail, but does NOT veto it - because on one of a rapid run of reloads during this session
the platform failed to deliver `src/js/vault.js`, and then `src/js/attach.js`, while the files
themselves were perfectly readable; refusing to keep the source in that state would be the worst
possible failure mode. Verbs: `/backup kept` (when, how many files, how big, why), `/backup pull`
(download the kept snapshot), `/backup snapshot` (take one now), `/backup autosave on|off`. VERIFIED
LIVE 2026-09-21: boot printed *"AUTOSAVE :: THIS BUILD IS CLEAN, AND THE SOURCE IS NOT ALL ON THE
SERVER YET - SO THE WHOLE TREE WAS KEPT ON THIS DEVICE :: 55 FILES / 2068 KB AT 2026-09-21 12:28:13
MST"*; the stored Blob was read back and parsed - real ZIP (`PK` signature), 55 entries, `main.pjs` +
`index.html` + every `src/` file + `_server-saved/index.html` + `PACK-INFO.txt`; `/backup kept`,
`/backup pull` (2,117,891-byte download) and `/backup autosave off|on` all work; kv `lia_settings` /
`backup` = `{auto:true, at, name:"lia-terminal-source-20260921-122813.zip", files:55, bytes:2117891,
ms:1198, missing:20, of:51, stale:false, modulesMissing:1, issues:4, why:"boot"}`. **Left ARMED (ON)**,
as he asked. **Still his move:** SAVE - 20 of 51 files are not on the server and `/backup status`
names them; if he would rather not press SAVE yet, `/backup pull` downloads the same zip and he can
attach it to the chat, from which every file can be written back.

**WHAT IS BUILT AND VERIFIED LIVE** (all through the running terminal, 2026-09-21):- `/story test` on `chatterbox-cpu`: **"THE ROAD IS OPEN … ANSWERED IN 0:26 WITH 107 KB OF AUDIO ·
  ROAD KEYED · TRANSPORT THE SHORTCUT CALL"**; on `chatterbox`: a measured refusal that names both
  doors tried and the roads that are open.
- `/story read <text>`: one part rendered, the strip appeared (`PART 1 / 1 · PLAYING`), the audio
  element advanced (0.6 s → 3.6 s of a 7.8 s part), the log carried the part count, the total and who
  rendered it, and `/story stop` cleared the job and hid the strip.

## 1aa. KILLER UPSCALE — AUTO UPSCALE ACTION (DONE 2026-09-21)

A second upscaler road, built because the first one CANNOT be automatic. `src/js/upscale-local.js` is
the whole of it; UPSCALING in `README.md` is the account of it. Below: what he asked for, what the
measurements forced, the vision-checked tuning loop, and the live verification.

**FINDING 9 — "KILLER UPSCALE, AUTO UPSCALE ACTION" (and then: "PNG only!").** His words, in order:
*"Now for what you have been waiting for: killer upscale auto upscale action. Attached:"* (the
attachment never arrived - see REMAINING UNKNOWN) and, while the work was being tested,
*"PNG only!"*. **The measurement that decides the design:** the existing upscaler (bigger.pics,
`src/js/upscale.js`) needs a REAL CLICK (a `window.open` from anything but the click is blocked) and
takes only ONE PICTURE AUTOMATICALLY (their own integration refuses a second, observed). Both were
already on the record; together they mean an UNATTENDED upscale through that road is impossible by
construction. So "auto upscale" could only be built as a second road that runs here.
**A CORRECTION TO THAT SECOND LIMIT, and it came from his own other generator** (the i8ixqmhq2p
source he sent, read 2026-09-21): the refusal is only about the AUTOMATIC hand-over. A PERSON can
add up to seven more pictures by hand in that same window (`MAX_BATCH = 8`, 16 MiB each) and the
window's "Send this back to ..." button posts EVERY finished picture back, one message each. So a
batch through bigger.pics IS possible - it just needs a human, which is precisely what "auto" does
not have. **FIXED in `src/js/upscale.js`:** the session no longer ends on the first result (a second
result used to hit `if (!session) return` and be SILENTLY DROPPED), it ends when the WINDOW ends,
each result between is filed on its own, a second `ready` now answers with the batch hint instead of
a refusal, and a window closed with more than one result says how many came back. The trade-off is
`LIA_UPSCALE_CLOSE`: the shipped `true` shuts the window a moment after the FIRST picture (right for
one, too quick for a batch - set it to `false` for the batch workflow). VERIFIED LIVE with a
stand-in window (`window.open` stubbed to a fake popup whose `frames` contain the page, then real
`bigger-pics-ready`/`bigger-pics-result` messages dispatched through `window`): a second `ready`
produced the batch hint, TWO results were both filed as their own vault records, and the close
reported "THE WINDOW IS CLOSED. 2 PICTURES CAME BACK FROM IT, AND EVERY ONE IS IN THE VAULT". The two
test records were then deleted (the vault back to 363).
**BUILT:** `src/js/upscale-local.js` (`window.upscaleLocal`) - a scaled **Lanczos-3** resample on
this device's GPU (WebGL2: 13 taps per axis per output pixel, kernel stretched to the 2x step,
weights normalized at the border, one axis at a time, so 4x is two 2x steps and the tap count stays
bounded), plus a **detail pass** whose masks were tuned BY VISION CHECK, not by taste (see below);
a stepped-`drawImage` + JS fallback when there is no WebGL2, with the same masks; the result filed
as a normal `kind:'upscale'` record carrying the prompt/sent/seed/negative/tags/folder of the
original and a `note` naming the engine, the factor and the milliseconds. **AUTO** rides a new
primitive in the vault - **`media.onAdd(fn)`** (`src/js/vault.js`): the one door announces every
stored record, so `consider()` enlarges every `kind:'gen'` picture the moment it lands (never an
attachment he handed over, never a clip, never music, never another upscale), quietly - nothing
opened, nothing added to her eyes. `/upscale here [ID] [2|4]`, `/upscale auto on|off|status`,
`/upscale help`, and an **UPSCALE HERE · Nx** button on every picture's full stage beside the
bigger.pics one. **PNG ONLY** (his word, and it agrees with the measurement): `LIA_UPSCALE_FORMAT`
and `LIA_UPSCALE_LOCAL_FORMAT` are both `"png"` now, because a jpeg re-encode after a resample throws
away part of the detail that was just reconstructed - seen directly in the working, where the jpeg
output brought blocking back into the smooth areas the resample had cleaned. Knobs in `config.js`:
`..._AUTO` (shipped `false`), `..._FACTOR` (2), `..._SHARPEN` (0.5), `..._FORMAT` ("png"),
`..._MAX_MP` (16, past which the factor steps down and says so). Setting kept in kv `lia_settings` /
`upscale_local`.
**THE TUNING LOOP, ON THE RECORD** (1:1 crops of a real render - the eye close-up, id
`mmub1ozmy97c0v` - against the browser's own smoothing as the baseline): **v1** (3x3 blur, a 0.15
floor on the mask everywhere, jpeg output) - the check said *"over-sharpened: white outlines and
haloes along the eyelashes, blocky jpeg artifacts amplified in the iris, the left panel looks
better"*. **v2** (5x5 blur, a structure mask that truly reaches zero, png output) - still read as
ringy at the specular cluster. **v3** (**coring** below ~1/255 and **roll-off** above ~0.09 added to
the mask) - *"no obvious haloes, not overly crunchy, looks like a natural slightly sharper
photograph - I would keep panel 3"*, ranked over both pure Lanczos and the browser. The orientation
question was checked the same way (side-by-side full frames, "is the right panel upside down?" - it
is not): the canvas stores its rows bottom-up and the offscreen targets do not, hence the shader's
`uFlip`.
**VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-21:** `upscaleLocal.state()` = `{engine:"webgl2", factor:2, sharpen:0.5,
format:"png", maxMp:16, hooked:true}`; `upscaleBlob` on a real render - 2x in **129 ms** (2,591,254
bytes, `image/png`, 1536×1024) and 4x in **367 ms** (7,284,743 bytes, 3072×2048); the vault path
filed `barbelo-photograph-3500-bce-...-x2-1536x1024.png` as `kind:"upscale"`, `how:"upscale-local"`,
folder `/images/upscaled`, prompt inherited, with a note naming lanczos-3, the detail amount, 98 ms
and the source; the **automatic road end to end** - `autoCmd('on')`, a synthetic `kind:'gen'` record
stored, the 2x copy (480×320, png) appeared without anything being pressed, then `auto on` off again
and all three test records deleted (`media.del`), the vault back to **363** records. No test artifact
was left in his vault. **The device was then left with the automatic road ON** (`/upscale auto on`),
because that is what was asked for; kv `lia_settings` / `upscale_local` = `{auto:true, factor:2,
upscaled:3}`, while the SHIPPED default in `config.js` stays `false` - a device switch outranks the
shipped line by design, and `/upscale auto off` is the one command that puts it back.

**OPEN, and deliberately kept in one place so none of it is lost:** REMAINING UNKNOWN in §1z, items
**(a0)** the attachment that never arrived (if it was a spec or a model, it has not been seen),
**(g)** his own verdict on the local road (`/upscale here` on a render he likes),
**(h)** the vault weight of PNG-ONLY with auto on, and **(i)** a resampler versus a trained
super-resolution model - the local road recovers crispness, it does not invent detail.

## 1ab. THE SHOT LIST and THE BATCH — the standalone generator's two best ideas (DONE 2026-09-21)

**His word:** *"It's got everything a filmmaker needs (more or less) we add this to your app and we
have a mini production studio."* And before that, the instruction that set the scope: *"Save the
lists and how they influence the output, leverage the selection of which generated images get sent,
then send up to six to bigger.pics, leverage how the user simply manual clicks and sends them back to
and places them in the gallery already upscaled. Note how the multiple randomizers work... dig deep
and pull out every piece of code we don't have and actually need."*

**WHAT IT IS.** The source of Patrikios' standalone image generator ("Kali Malindra and the Cult of
Fire", `perchance.org/i8ixqmhq2p`) was handed over in full - 27 files - and read for what the
terminal did not have. **That generator is NOT touched**: it is a different, self-contained thing,
and it was named as the reference. What was grafted is two ideas, and neither is a port of its UI.

### (1) THE SHOT LIST — `src/js/idea.js` + the lists in `main.pjs` + the panel row in `forge.js`

- **The lists were taken BYTE-FOR-BYTE** out of that generator's `main.pjs` (lines 146-1674 of it:
  `joinFragments`, `dice`, `mythGlossary` and all 24 dimension lists) with the comment block that
  carries the **curation rule** (the Minoan Aegean, 1500 BCE, in-period material for the scene
  dimensions, film vocabulary deliberately modern, every adult in every combination, the
  deprecated-terms list). That block is the spec for editing the lists, and it is much easier to keep
  if it travels *with* the lists. 1,640 lines: `main.pjs` went from 6 lines to 1,646.
- **Why `main.pjs` and not JSON.** Perchance's engine IS the randomizer, and the whole point of the
  measured behaviour is that it survives: `{a|b}` branches, `^` odds (read per item off `getOdds`, so
  a `^8` default stays eight times as likely as one added phrase), computed items, and `joinFragments`
  gluing a multi-line item back into one `", "` chain. In JSON all of that would have had to be
  re-implemented and would still be a subset.
- **The engine** is `window.idea`: `rollAll()`, `rollOne(name)`, a `dice` reader (a named die beats
  the catch-all; a die is added *only* in `main.pjs`), `compose(values, into)` with per-dimension
  glue and `into`/`replaces`/`see`, `sceneTitle()` (read-only, composed out of the roll, never
  written into a prompt), and `addPhrase`/`forgetPhrase` - the one way his own words become part of
  a list. Held in kv `lia_settings` / `idea`; additions in `lia_settings` / `idea_extras`.
- **Where a roll goes:** nowhere on its own. `forgeBook.write()` puts it in the boxes - the positive
  prompt outright, the negative list **only into an empty negative box** (the house rule the prompt
  book and the recipe book already follow).
- **The panel row** (SHOT LIST, in IMAGE FORGE): a button per die built from the `dice` list at
  open, `ROLL ALL`, `CLEAR`, a chip per held dimension (`↻` re-rolls that one, `✕` drops it and
  rewrites the prompt from what is left), and the SCENE line.
- **Commands:** `/idea`, `/idea <DIE>`, `/idea <DIMENSION>`, `/idea dice|list|held|scene|drop|clear|
  add|forget`; `/help idea`. Two entries added to `src/commands/commands.json` (56 now).

### (2) THE BATCH — `src/js/batch.js` + the tick box in `images.js` + batch mode in `upscale.js`

- **The exact flow he described**, built on the site's real behaviour (measured twice: their
  `app.js` and their own `batch.js`): the site takes **one automatic hand-over per window**, a
  **person** can add up to seven more **by hand** in that same window (8 pictures, 16 MiB each), and
  its **"Send this back to ..."** button posts **every** finished picture here. So: one window, one
  picture across by itself, the rest added by hand, everything filed on arrival.
- **`LIA_BATCH_MAX = 6`** (`config.js`): six fits inside one window's eight, so a whole selection is
  ONE click and ONE window - which is why "send up to six" is the right number and not an arbitrary
  cap. Anything ticked beyond six stays ticked and the bar can send it after.
- **The tick box** is drawn in `fillTile()` (`images.js`), in the caption bar beside SAVE/UPSCALE -
  never floating over the picture (the plugin's embed owns all four corners; that correction is
  theirs and it is kept). **The bar** (`batch.js`) attaches to any picture grid (a forge run, a line
  in the log), reads the ticks off the DOM at the press, and stays hidden until a tick box exists.
- **`upscale.js` gained a batch mode**: `open(id, {batch:true, onResult, onClose})` - the window is
  left STANDING (the self-close would fire on the first picture and cut a hand-added batch short) and
  the bar is told when it closes. Everything else is the same code, so the result path - file on
  arrival, `kind:'upscale'`, the original's prompt/seed/negative/tags, into `/images/upscaled`, PNG
  only - is unchanged and was already what he asked for ("places them in the gallery already
  upscaled").
- **Commands:** `/batch`, `/batch stop`, `/batch help`; `/help batch`. Both commands are in the
  registry.

**VERIFIED LIVE (this device, in the preview):** the lists read off `root` (24 dimensions, dice
d6=6/d20=18); a full roll wrote a 1,830-character prompt into `#cpPrompt` and the 3,301-character
negative list into the empty `#cpNegative`; a `d6` roll moved only its six chips and left the other
14; re-rolling `camera` changed only `camera`; `/idea`, `/idea dice|held|scene|list|add`, `/batch`
and `/help idea|batch` all answered from the real dispatch; `/idea add` then `/idea forget` round-
tripped a test phrase (extras back to 0). The batch was driven end to end with a **stand-in window**
(`window.open` stubbed to a popup whose `frames` hold a real same-origin iframe, then real
`bigger-pics-ready` / `bigger-pics-result` MessageEvents): the handshake reached the frame
(`how:"ready"`), one result landed and was **filed (vault 363 -> 364)**, the bar's tray showed it,
and closing the window ended the session and left the bar offering `SEND NEXT (1 LEFT)` with
`1 OF 2 HANDED OVER`. The test record was deleted afterwards (vault back to **363**), and the tick
box / bar / select-all / counts were checked against a real three-picture grid.

**OPEN / his call:**
- **(k1)** The lists as shipped are the *Minoan* domain (subjects, settings, poses, actions). They
  are the reference material he asked to keep; **the film half is the part that is terminal-neutral**
  (crop, shot, angle, camera, capture, lens, focus, light, grade, lut, style), so his own domain

- **(k6)** **The one graft that changes a render without being asked: `negativePrompt`.** It is one

- **(k2)** `mythGlossary` came with the lists (45 entries, the English → myth-register table the
  standalone generator's MYTH line used to name a still from its own pixels). **The MYTH line itself

- **(k3)** The standalone generator's `src/vocab.js` + `extras.js` + `picker.js` (the prompt read

- **(k4)** Whether a **six-picture window really takes five hand-added pictures** end to end on his

- **(k5)** Once the batch is used for real, the vault weight of PNG-only upscales at 2x/4x (see §1aa

## 1ac. The gallery crash — a window index that could step past the tiles (FIXED 2026-09-22)

**Finding.** Patrikios, using it: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '__galSrc')`
at `loadThumbs (src/js/gallery.js:556)`, with the platform's "an error has occurred somewhere in your
code" banner. Reproduced on demand, same message, same line, same banner.

**Mechanism.** `loadThumbs` (gallery.js:512) loads a WINDOW of thumbnails by arithmetic instead of
`loading="lazy"`, and it maps a scroll offset to a tile INDEX through ONE sampled row pitch
(`rowH` = the distance between the first tile and the first tile of the next row). When the grid's
first row is SHORTER than the rows below it, that sample understates the real pitch, so
`first = (floor(scrollTop / rowH) - 1) * cols` steps far past the end of the list. The forward loop
is harmless (its `last` is `Math.min`-ed to `tiles.length`), but the BACK-FILL loop below it starts
at `first - 1` and walks down - and `tiles[j]` is `undefined` there, so `b.__galSrc` throws. The
ticker (every 350 ms while the gallery is open) then throws again on every tick.

**Evidence.** Unfixed code, injected state (the first five tiles given `aspect-ratio: auto; height:
6px`, which makes row 0 short), vault at 1198 records, scrolled to the bottom at 390x844:
measured `rowH` 68 (true pitch ~245), `scrollTop` 140765, computed `first` 3320 against
`tiles.length` 1198 - overshoot 2122. Result: six uncaught TypeErrors at gallery.js:556 and the
platform banner, exactly the report. Every state that DID reproduce nothing is worth recording too:
deep scroll + each of the five sorts (`newest oldest biggest az turn`), a filter that narrows the
grid to 24, close-and-reopen at a deep scroll, a collapsed (content-visibility) grid, and desktop
->390px resize - in all of those the geometry stays consistent (`first` 1040-1110 of 1198) and
nothing throws. It throws when, and only when, the derived index leaves the array.

**Change** (4 small edits in `src/js/gallery.js`, no behaviour change when the geometry is sane):
clamp `first` and `last` to `tiles.length` after the window is computed, and null-guard both loop
bodies (`if (!t || !t.__galSrc)`, `if (!b || !b.__galSrc)`).

**Test.** The identical injected state, the identical overshoot (computed `first` 4140 against 1198),
run against the fixed file: 0 errors across ~6 ticker ticks. Regression on the normal grid:
38 tiles carry a blob URL at the top, 58 at mid-scroll, 72 at the bottom (a window, never the whole
vault), the tiles at the VIEWPORT row are loaded at all three positions, and a captured thumbnail
decodes to a real picture (checked visually, not assumed - a black box would have failed).

**Remaining unknown.** The exact state he was in is not reproduced - the injected short first row
proves the failure mode and the fix, not his path to it. If it happens again, what was on screen
matters: which sort/filter, and whether the vault had just gained or lost pictures. Residual
fragility, not a crash: with a short first row the WINDOW can still be wrong (the tick then loads
from the end of the list and walks up - self-healing, but the picture he is looking at may wait a
tick or two). The robust form is a binary search over tile rects (~11 `getBoundingClientRect` calls
for 1198 tiles) instead of one sampled pitch; not done unasked.

## 2. The API key ring — next steps

Built and device-local; keys live in kv `lia_settings` / `api_keys` (see API KEYRING in the README).
The structure is done. What is left:

- **Sealing the record.** Encrypt `api_keys` with a passphrase the user types at unlock: WebCrypto
  PBKDF2 → AES-GCM over the whole record, unlocked for the session, locked again on reload. Makes
  the ring survive a shared laptop rather than a curious extension. Optional, off by default.
- **A local provider registry.** `src/keys/providers.json` is public and shipped, so it can describe
  the big public services but not a private/internal endpoint. A device-side overlay (kv
  `lia_settings` / `key_providers`, same schema) with a small editor in the KEYS panel would let
  Patrikios add providers without touching `src/`. Registry entries are structure, never secrets.
- **A use log.** `lastUsedAt` is written on a successful `request()`; a per-key last-N-use list
  (which feature called it, at what time, verdict) would make it obvious when a key is being spent.
- **Auto-test on store** (opt-in), so a bad paste is caught at the moment of typing rather than at
  the first real call.
- **A Google (Gemini) key now does three jobs** - the meaning lane's embeddings, and the audition
  bus's ears (HER EARS), which is its own second `generateContent` call. When one is stored, the
  things to re-run are `/embed now`, `/embed media`, and HER EARS on one piece; the bus remembers the
  model whose listening worked in `lia_settings / audition.earsModel`, so the choice is made once.
- **`superFetch` import.** `mode: "proxy"` in the registry already routes through `root.superFetch`,
  but the generator does not import it yet — add `superFetch = {import:super-fetch-plugin}` to
  `main.pjs` when the first proxy-mode provider (e.g. Replicate) is actually wired.

- **THE SWITCHER/ROUTER — asked for, deliberately NOT built yet (Patrikios, 2026-09-21).** *"If we are
  going through Gemini for audio, we may as well build the switcher/router for this kind of stuff but
  not yet."* The need is already visible in the code: one CAPABILITY (hearing, seeing, embedding,
  transcribing, speaking) should be a role the key ring can fill with any provider that can do it,
  picked by what is reachable, what is affordable and what is answering RIGHT NOW - instead of each
  feature naming its provider in source. The audition bus has grown half of that by accident and it
  works (FINDING 3 in §1w): a ranked candidate list per capability, a cooldown for anything that
  refused, and the choice remembered only after it produced. Generalising it means a
  `capability → providers` table (in `src/keys/`, structure not secrets), per-call routing with the
  reason reported, a per-attempt timeout that `keyring.request()` currently cannot carry (it builds
  its own `init` and drops `AbortSignal`), and a "who did this call" line in the SEARCH LOG. Worth
  doing before a second provider is wired for anything, because that is when the shape gets set.
