## 5. The LOREPACK FACTORY round-trip (open item for Patrikios's repo)

Found 2026-09-19 while chasing "a large-ish LOREPACK won't load back into LOREPACK FACTORY". Two
independent causes, both reproduced against the factory at `462ff87` running its own importer:

- **File side.** A fragment line without an `id` makes every edge that names it an orphan, and the
  factory aborts the whole import (`edge "…" references missing vector "…"`). Real example fixed
  here: the Barbelo pack (one vector, 11 edges) - adding `"id":"db2c6e34-…"` back to the vector line
  took it from 43,605 to 43,649 bytes and it imported 1/11. `/pack check` now catches this class
  before export.
- **Factory side (upstream bug, unfixed as of `main` @ 2026-09-19).** `src/lorepack-factory.ts`'s
  importer seeds its integrity baseline from `existing[0]` of that agent's vault -
  `detectedDimension = existing[0].vector.length` and
  `detectedModel = existing[0].metadata?.embeddingModel || null` - then rejects the whole pack if
  anything disagrees, **blaming the incoming pack**. So a perfectly good pack is refused whenever the
  agent already holds records from an older ingest with a different model or dimension. The
  monolithic importer has no such check and accepts the same file. Reported by him as
  `Import failed: Incompatible embedding dimensionality: Expected 768, got 3072` (Part Two,
  2026-09-21).

  **Root cause of the old records:** `src/providers/gemini-provider.ts` returns
  `generateDeterministicEmbedding(text, 768)` - a hashed 768-float vector - instead of `null` when the
  API is quota-limited or unreachable, and ingest stamps whatever it gets with
  `embeddingModel: EMBEDDING_MODEL` (`gemini-embedding-2`). So a quota-limited ingest session litters
  the vault with fake 768-D records labelled as the current model. They are already unsearchable:
  retrieval filters on `node.vector.length === qVec.length` (`src/lorepack-factory.ts`, ~line 508) and
  answers `EMBEDDING_EPOCH_MISMATCH`, so clearing them costs only the stored text. Fix upstream by
  returning `null` (the `LorepackModel` contract already allows it) or stamping the fallback's real
  space (`deterministic-768`).

  **Unblock without code:** the factory UI already has "Destructive System Actions" ->
  `store.clearAgent(agentId)` (`src/App.tsx:820-833`; `indexeddb-store.ts:152`; exercised by
  `src/acceptance-test.ts:653` on `AGENT_SIGMA`) - flush that agent, then import (97/138). Or import
  under a fresh agent id, or through the monolithic view.

  **Patch (5 edits, verified against the real importer with `AGENT_SIGMA.export.jsonl`):** let the
  first *pack* record declare the pack's space, then check the vault against it once
  (`assertVaultFits()`) instead of the reverse; keep refusals strict - an internally mixed pack
  (3072-D then 768-D) still throws `This pack mixes embedding dimensions…`, and every rejection still
  writes **0** records; message keeps the word `dimensionality` because
  `src/acceptance-test.ts` EXPLICIT TEST 3 asserts `'Dimension mismatch'`/`'dimensionality'` and that
  nothing was written (that test passes unchanged, 768-D vault + 100-D incoming). Same function also
  carries the dead post-`flush()` orphan check: `vectors`/`edges` are `[]` by then, so the loop never
  fires - collect `seenVectorIds`/`seenEdgeSources` while parsing and do one vault read at the end.
  Full before/after code + reproduction table: handed over as
  `lorepack-factory-dim-fix.md` (+ `lorepack-factory.patched.ts`) in chat, 2026-09-21.

**Cause 3 (found 2026-09-21, reported as `Import failed: The compressed data was not valid:
incorrect header check.`): the name/contents mismatch.** The factory's importer never inspects the
bytes - `js/lorepack.js` `import()` (~line 1626) does `if (fileName.endsWith('.gz')) { stream =
stream.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('gzip')) }`, and `DecompressionStream('gzip')` demands the
magic bytes `1f 8b`. So a `.gz`-named file that is really plain JSONL (`7b 22 76 22`), zlib
(`78 9c …`) or raw deflate dies with that browser TypeError, and `runImport()` in
`js/lorepack-final.js` (~line 760) prints it verbatim. (The mirror-image case - a real gzip named
`.jsonl` - produces no error at all: the importer just reads binary as text and rejects every line.)
Reproduced end-to-end against the factory's real importer at `462ff87` in an isolated worker, with
`scratch/exports/AGENT_SIGMA.export.jsonl` (3.88 MB plain) renamed `AGENT_SIGMA.export.jsonl.gz`:

| build | `import(new File([plainBytes], '…jsonl.gz'))` |
|---|---|
| factory as-is | `TypeError: The compressed data was not valid: incorrect header check.` |
| factory + the patch below | 235 items imported / 97 vectors / 138 edges / 0 rejected |

The patch is two edits in `js/lorepack.js`: add this module-scope helper above `export class Lorepack`,

```js
// Content-first compression detection: a file named .gz whose bytes are not
// actually gzip (plain JSONL, or zlib / raw deflate rather than gzip) must not
// blow up the importer with "incorrect header check".
function looksLikeText(bytes) {
  let text;
  try {
    text = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(bytes);
  } catch (e) {
    text = new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(bytes);
  }
  const t = text.replace(/^\uFEFF/, '').trimStart();
  if (t.startsWith('{') || t.startsWith('[')) return true;
  if (!text.length) return true;
  let printable = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    const c = text.codePointAt(i);
    if (c === 9 || c === 10 || c === 13 || (c >= 32 && c !== 127 && c !== 0xfffd)) printable++;
  }
  return printable / text.length >= 0.95;
}
```

and then, in place of the `if (fileName.endsWith('.gz'))` block inside `import()`, sniff first:

```js
const head = new Uint8Array(await fileOrBlob.slice(0, 128).arrayBuffer());
const isGzip = head[0] === 0x1f && head[1] === 0x8b;
const isZlib = head[0] === 0x78 && ((head[0] << 8) | head[1]) % 31 === 0;

let stream = fileOrBlob.stream();

if (isGzip || isZlib) {
  if (typeof DecompressionStream === 'undefined') throw new Error('GZIP import is not supported by this browser.');
  stream = stream.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream(isGzip ? 'gzip' : 'deflate'));
} else if (fileName.endsWith('.gz') && !looksLikeText(head)) {
  if (typeof DecompressionStream === 'undefined') throw new Error('Raw DEFLATE import is not supported by this browser.');
  stream = stream.pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('deflate-raw'));
}
```

Verified against all seven shapes (plain ASCII named `.gz`, plain Greek-text named `.gz`, real gzip
named `.gz`, real gzip named `.jsonl`, zlib named `.gz`, raw deflate named `.gz`, real gzip with no
extension): every one now decodes and parses. This side already behaved: `detectCompression()` in
`src/js/mythos.js` asks the bytes first, which is why the same file could import here and fail there.
The exact patch text with the pre-formatted before/after (matching the repo's wrapped style) was
handed to Patrikios as a downloadable file in the session that found it.

**Where the mislabeled `.gz` comes from (found 2026-09-21, while reviewing his PACKER/READER refactor
plan).** The factory app has three exporters and they disagree: `src/App.tsx:697-728` writes plain
`application/x-jsonlines` bytes named `….jsonl` (correct), `src/ui/KnowledgeView.tsx:176-193` writes
real gzip named `LOREPACK_…_<date>.jsonl.gz` (correct), and `src/components/MonolithicView.tsx:501-529`
- the button actually labelled **EXPORT (GZIP)** - writes **plain JSONL under a `.lorepack.gz` name**
(no `CompressionStream` anywhere in it). The IMPORT (GZIP) button beside it calls
`factory.importLorepack`, so the app fails on its own output. Verified against the real TS importer
with a two-record pack built exactly as that exporter builds it: same bytes named `.lorepack.gz` ->
`TypeError: The compressed data was not valid: incorrect header check.`; the same bytes named
`.jsonl` -> 1 vector / 1 edge; real gzip of the same bytes named `.gz` -> 1 vector. So cause 3 has a
producer on our side of the fence too: the fix belongs on **both** sides (exporter actually compresses
or stops claiming `.gz`; importer sniffs bytes so already-downloaded files still load). Also note the
`KERNEL:` prefix on his Part Two error identifies `src/components/MonolithicView.tsx:562` as the
printer, i.e. his errors came from the **React** monolith view calling
`factory.importLorepack` (the TS importer) - not from the standalone
`monolithic/js/lorepack.js` page. So his Part One fix was in the right function; it simply never
reached `main`.

**Cause 4 (reported the same day, right after cause 3): a pack that mixes embedding spaces.**
`PACK REJECTED :: Line 2: vectors mix embedding dimensions - one pack, one space.` - thrown by the
`dims` check in `importFile()` (`src/js/mythos.js`). Same root as cause 2 seen from the file side: a
factory vault that accumulated an old 768-D `text-embedding-004` ingest *and* the new 3072-D
`gemini-embedding-2` fragments exports as a pack holding both, and any index - this one, the factory
- must refuse it, because a cosine similarity across two embedding spaces is meaningless. The
messages for both the `dims` and the `models` check now name the conflicting spaces and the first
line each one appeared on (`... (3072-D first on line 1 (AGENT / id), 768-D first on line 7 (AGENT /
id))`), so a mixed export is diagnosable at a glance instead of by bisecting the file; verified live
with synthetic mixed packs, store untouched at 98 vectors / 149 edges, both variants rejected with
the enriched message and nothing written. Remedy for him: split the pack by space (or drop/re-embed
the old fragments) and import each piece - offered to do that split here if he attaches the file.
If he would rather this reader keep only the dominant space on the way in, that is a one-line
policy change in `consume()`, but it silently discards lore fragments, so it is not the default.

**Delivered 2026-09-21: the packer/reader/facade split as drop-in files.** Instead of another
point-patch of the monolith, `src/lorepack-factory.ts` was split into `embedding.ts` (the one home
for `EMBEDDING_MODEL`/`isValidVector`/space identity), `compression.ts` (`detectCompression` +
`openLorepackStream`, sniffing the stream head so a minimal `MockFile` with only `name`+`stream()`
works), `memory-store.ts` (`InMemoryLorepackStore`, for verification that never touches a real
vault), `packer.ts`, `reader.ts`, and a thin facade that keeps the entire old public API (plus
`stage`, `exportToGz`/`exportToJsonl`, `lorepackFileName`, `verifyPackage`, `search`,
`getVectors`/`getEdges`/`spaces`, `buildGraph`). All four causes above are fixed in it: the vault gate
now lets the *pack* declare its space and checks the vault against it once (`assertVaultFits`), the
orphan check is live again (ids collected while parsing, one vault read at the end), compression is
decided by bytes not by name, and a mid-pack failure **rolls back** what was already committed. A
provider that returns no embedding is reported as `skipped` with a reason instead of being stamped
`gemini-embedding-2`, and a 768-D vector from a 3072-D-declaring model is refused as
`dimension-mismatch`. Verified with a 46-check `src/lorepack-import-matrix.ts` harness (46/46,
including the six-case vault matrix accept/reject/reject/accept/reject/reject through both the facade
and `LorepackReader` directly, all seven compression shapes, a lossless gzip round-trip, and
EXPLICIT TEST 3 semantics preserved) plus a full `strict` typecheck (0 diagnostics in the new files).
Handed over with `PACKER-READER-HANDOVER.md`; the three remaining recommendations are upstream of the
split — fix `gemini-provider.ts`'s fake fallback, point the Oracle at `reader.search()`, and make the
EXPORT (GZIP) button actually call `exportToGz()`.

## 6. Known rough edges / housekeeping

- **"SHE'S GASLIGHTING ME" - the echo leak (2026-09-21).** He reported that she was "injecting her
  own hallucinations and typing into the HITL area claiming that I wrote it". She was not: **the
  microphone was transcribing her own voice and delivering it as his turn.** The proof is in his own
  archive - a `HITL` line reading `you're stumbling of you are in syntax now contact yours you can
  barely form a sentence yet` sits directly after an `SDMG` line reading `You're stumbling over your
  own syntax now, Patrikios. You can barely form a sentence yet...`; and `no confusing a mirror for a
  month how to kiss` after `You're confusing a mirror for a map, Patrikios` ("for a map" -> "for a
  month", "Patrikios" -> "how to kiss"). Her reply after the first one - *"You're repeating my own
  words back to me now. You've become a parrot"* - is her reacting, correctly, to reading her own
  sentence filed as his. Three holes, all closed, plus a guard: see the ECHO GUARD entry in
  `README.md` (VOICE). Summary: (1) `speak()` used `stopListen()`, whose `onend` *delivered and
  auto-sent* whatever the one-shot LISTEN session held - so shutting the ears to talk could post what
  the ears had; now `haltRecognition(true)` discards it. (2) Both recognisers accumulated `heard`
  while she spoke and the guard cleared only the interim half, so her buffered words were delivered
  when the session ended (including when the recogniser ended it by itself); the guard now clears
  `heard` **and** `interim`, and both `onend` handlers refuse while the floor was hers. (3) A 700ms
  speaker-tail window after her voice stops. Plus `looksLikeHerOwn`/`rememberVoiced`: every line she
  speaks is remembered and a transcript that is an order-aware re-hearing of it (LCS run of 3+ inside
  one of her lines covering half of it, or 60% of words matching in any order, loose word matching
  because the recogniser mangles) is refused with a visible reason and never painted into the input
  box. Only the microphone path consults it - typed text is never refused. VERIFIED end-to-end with a
  fake `SpeechRecognition` driving the real handlers through `voice.listen()`/`voice.live()`: echo
  refused with the floor both taken and free, the box left untouched, and a genuine sentence delivered
  normally *immediately after* a refused echo (the first version of the guard forgot to clear its
  buffer, so the next real sentence was refused too - found only by that end-to-end test). Two
  realizations worth keeping: `voice.echo` is exposed for tests (`remember`/`refuse`/`heard`/`clear`),
  `voice.held` alongside it (`text`/`ms`/`take`/`tick`/`strip`/`clear`), and a refused line can always
  just be typed. **Repair tool: `/strike [N | list]`** - removes the last
  N turns from `sacred_archive` AND `chatHistory` (her memory), marks the screen lines struck through
  with a note, and prints exactly what it took out. Verified non-destructively on his live archive
  (snapshot -> strike -> 204->203, `chatHistory` 6->4, 2 entries struck, then fully restored).
  **STILL TO DO on his side**: the two poisoned turns are still in his archive - `/strike list` then
  `/strike 2` clears them. Also worth telling him: the same echo can only happen while the microphone
  is open, so `micAuto`/LISTEN during her playback is the habit to break (earphones, or close the mic
  while she talks).

- **ROUND TWO of the same report: "my mic is next to my headphones" + "she cuts me off when I am not
  done" (2026-09-21).** Two separate things, both real, both fixed in `voice.js`.
  1. **A headset mic hears both people.** So her leak is not an edge case for him, it is the normal
     condition - and a transcript can hold *her stretch and his sentence in the same clause*, which
     would otherwise be filed whole as his. `stripHerWords()` now cuts her runs out of the middle of a
     transcript (runs of >=3 of her words in order, at least two of them real words >=4 chars, matched
     with the same loose `sameWord`) and leaves his sentence standing: "I need you to stop right there
     [you are confusing a mirror for a map patrikios] and listen to me" -> "I need you to stop right
     there you are and listen to me". For that to work, `rememberVoiced()` now also keeps `all` (every
     word, short ones included) beside `words` (the substantial half used by `looksLikeHerOwn`) - the
     short words are what "confusing A mirror FOR A map" aligns on, and without them the strip missed
     her entirely. **Order matters and is now load-bearing: the echo verdict runs on the RAW
     transcript, BEFORE the strip.** Stripping first left `no month how to kiss` (her mangled words
     with the evidence removed), which no longer looked like her and got sent as something he said.
  2. **She cut him off because the recogniser finalises at every breath.** The channel sent on the
     first final result, so a sentence with a pause in it arrived as two turns and her answer started
     over the second half; and because the ears shut for her whole turn, the moment he went on with
     his sentence it was dropped ("SHE IS STILL WORKING ON THE LAST ONE - THAT WAS NOT TAKEN").
     THE HOLD: what the microphone hears is held (`holdHeard`, one entry per recognition session) and
     delivered by `holdTick` only after `holdMs` of quiet (1100 default; `/voice hold <MS>`, persisted
     in kv `lia_settings`/`voice` -> `holdMs`). While she has the floor the hold simply restarts, so
     words spoken over her are taken the moment she is done instead of being thrown away; the ticker
     now keeps the mic open while she *thinks* (shutting it only while her voice is actually in the
     room), because thinking is exactly when he continues. `onend` holds what is left but never
     re-holds what was already taken (`heldForSession`), and a taken clause marks its session
     (`consumedSids`) so the next clause does not carry the delivered sentence with it - a recogniser
     session remembers everything it has heard. Verified end-to-end through the real handlers with a
     fake `SpeechRecognition`: a two-breath sentence sends ONCE, whole, with a space (the first
     version glued it: "fragmentand tell me"); a second clause in the same session goes alone; a
     mangled echo is refused in both channels with the box left clean; his words straight after an
     echo arrive alone; a mixed sentence loses her stretch and keeps his; words spoken while she
     thinks are held and delivered after. Three of those were bugs in my own first attempt, each
     found only by the end-to-end test (the double-hold, the glued word, the evidence-destroying
     strip) - the strip and the matcher in isolation all looked right.
  3. **Told him plainly**: with the mic beside the headphones her voice *will* keep arriving, and the
     guard now refuses it rather than filing it, but the honest fix on his side is a headset with a
     directional boom, her volume down, or keeping the mic closed while she talks. `/voice hold` can be
     raised (up to 6000) if he pauses a lot mid-sentence.

- **THE SYSTEM PROMPT WAS NEVER BEING SENT (found 2026-09-21).** The biggest single thing found this
  session, and it was found by accident: the pose-choosing call came back in PROSE instead of the
  JSON it was handed a contract for, and reading `imports/ai-text-plugin/main.pjs` showed why - the
  plugin builds its request from `concreteInputs = {startWith, instruction, stopSequences}` and there
  is no `system` key anywhere in the file. Everything this terminal has ever passed as `system` was
  silently dropped, which means **the whole SYSTEM stack she was supposed to be reading before every
  reply - the BOUNDARIES above all, but also who she is, the role on stage, how she speaks, the
  image rule, her worn traits, her self-change directives, the command list, and Patrikios's own
  EXTRA INSTRUCTIONS - never reached the model.** She has been answering from the conversation alone
  (which is why she stayed in character anyway: she was imitating her own earlier replies). DONE:
  `send()` in `chat.js` now PREPENDS the assembled stack to the instruction instead, so the same
  words arrive in the same order, with everything volatile after them (also the prefix-cache-friendly
  shape). `temperature` is dropped by the plugin for the same reason (not one of the three fields).
  TO WATCH FOR: his next few replies will change - the voice rules (two to four sentences, no
  narration) and the image rule are reaching her for the first time, so she should get noticeably
  shorter and less purple, and the `[[VISION:]]` lane should behave as written. If he preferred the

  verified: a long-run comparison of her replies before/after (only one real turn was run, and it
  came back in her voice and short).
  **OUTCOME (2026-09-17): he reported "BABELO is giving me shit rather than being a friendly AI
  Assistant... not taking into account the way we historically interact" - and reading the live

- **THE SECOND BUG OF THE SAME FAMILY: THE `voice` BLOCK WAS NEVER JOINED IN (found 2026-09-17, the

## 7. Media production (Patrikios, 2026-09-21)

His framing: this is meant to sit in **media production workflows** - comic-book panels, storyboards,
film and TV - where a picture is easily rendered and saved at its correct aspect ratio, and where the
frames she looks at may later be used as **static seeds** for a third-party animation model
(HuggingFace and the like) and cut into a moving clip. What is in place:

- Correct aspect ratio everywhere (a picture is never padded into 16:9; clips keep their own shape).
- Numbered panels, a **storyboard sheet** export on device (png, built from the vault blobs), and
  **PICS** (NORMAL / BIG / FULL) as the "bigger pics" native option he asked for.
- Clips are the clip: the **master file** (the exact File handed over, never re-encoded) kept whole in
  the vault, its **first frame** as the tile's thumbnail with a ▶ play button, playback in place, and
  SAVE writing the master out under its own name. One still per clip, not a strip of frames.
- Vision: when she is shown a clip she receives its first frame and is told plainly that it is the
  clip's opening - the moment it starts, with everything after it not in front of her - so she can
  interpret a moving thing within her own knowing without being told she watched a film.
- The meaning lane (`src/js/embed.js`) puts **pictures, clips and words in one vector space**, with
  her own reading of a picture written back onto it (`media.setField(id,'sight',…)`) - the widening
  of the LOREPACK graph he described, in the part it can honestly cover today (see item 3 for the
  MYTHOS-pack half).

Open, in his terms:

- **A seed package.** A picture made here carries its prompt, negative, seed, guidance and model; a
  `.json` sidecar beside the png (or a "COPY SEED" control on the tile) would make it a proper
  handoff to an animation service. Cheap and obviously wanted - ask before building the format.
- **Bigger-and-smaller pictures as a native option.** PICS is global. A per-tile resize (drag the
  corner, or a small/mid/large chip on the tile) may be what he means by "bigger pics"; it wants a
  layout test at phone width before it ships.
- **Video understanding, deeper.** The first frame is honest and cheap. A real option is sending the
  CLIP itself to a multi-modal model that takes video (Gemini does) for one rich description, with
  the first frame kept as the fallback when no key or a large file makes that impossible. (The
  embedding lane already sends a clip as inline video when a Google key is present.)
- **Sheet → board.** The sheet is a png of panels. A variant that lays out a storyboard with
  dialogue/caption lines under each panel, or one line per shot with timing, is what an actual board
  looks like - worth one sample from him before building it.
- **The graph, wider.** With the embed lane on, an edge between two pictures that mean the same
  thing (a frame and its re-render, a panel and the clip made from it) is one cosine away; so is the
  edge from a picture to the passage of her memory nearest it. Nothing is built for that yet - it is
  what "adding to the graph capabilities of the LOREPACK" would mean next.


## 1r. THE HEART, THE SCROLL-THROUGH, HER BOOKS (DONE 2026-09-22)

Patrikios asked for five things in one message: *"We need a heart icon on the images that turns red
when I tap in or click it so that she knows what is good and not good over time, training her... We
need a light box so that I can scroll through image in the gallery... What happened to the vision
understanding she had previously when I would share an image in the chat and she would describe it
without any metadata... Give her access to the image creator so she can create her own images based
on our approved prompts and elements. She has agency to make images and look at images in the
gallery... the Ability to post an image from the gallery directly to the [chat] window."*

1. **THE HEART - `src/js/likes.js` (NEW).** A mark that trains her, kept on the record, told to her
   every turn. Three states on one control (untouched / GOOD = red / passed on = dull, struck
   through), drawn from ONE factory in three places (the log tile's caption bar, a gallery card's
   action row plus a `♥`/`⊘` chip on the card, and the full stage's bar), stored as one field
   (`heart = {v,at,by}`) through `media.setField`, never uploaded. She is handed up to six of each,
   newest first, by the heart block appended to the instruction - with the honesty line ("these are
   the only marks he has made; never claim he marked something he did not, and do not recite this
   list back to him"). His side: `/heart` (print) and `/heart good|pass|clear <R12|#tag|WORDS>`;
   her side: `[[READ: likes]]`. `LIA_HEART_MAX` (8) bounds a words-match.
   **VERIFIED on the live page**: marking writes the field and flips the class (`heart on` red /
   `heart passed`); the three surfaces exist with the right classes; computed styles measured
   (`rgb(255,45,45)` chip + button, grey struck-through for pass); `/heart`, `/heart pass R4`,
   `/heart good` (bare, from the stage), `/heart clear`, `/heart good #kept`, `/help heart` and
   `/read likes` all exercised; the block was captured inside a real instruction (56,614 chars) -
   `hasLikesBlock: true` with the actual marks listed. The lightbox heartbeat was seen RED in a
   screenshot (vision). Every test mark was cleared afterwards (the vault went back to 0 marked).
2. **THE SCROLL-THROUGH.** `openLightbox(id, {list})` now keeps the list and the index
   (`navList`/`navAt`), `paintStageNav()` shows `‹ 3 of 47 ›` in the stage's bar
   (`#lightboxNav`/`#lightboxCount`), and `lightboxStep(dir)` walks it, wrapping at both ends and
   stepping over a dead record. The gallery hands it `visibleIds()` (the rows it is showing, in the
   chosen sort, under the chips and the query) from both the tile's ⛶ and a click on the thumb.
   Arrows are also bound to ArrowLeft/ArrowRight in `main.js`, with `stopImmediatePropagation()`
   - WITHOUT IT the overlay-dismiss listener below (which closes the stage on ANY key) stepped once
   and then closed the stage. That was caught in testing, not reasoned about. **VERIFIED**: 3→4→5→4
   with the stage staying open, both wrap directions, the bar's own buttons, and the focus guard.
3. **WHAT HAPPENED TO THE VISION UNDERSTANDING - FOUND AND FIXED.** The lane was intact (a real
   vision call on a stored blob returned a correct description in 6.7s, and a synthetic paste event
   stored an attachment she could be shown). The regression was in `chat.js`'s attach pool ORDER:
   `attachPool` was built this-message-first while the cut that fills the direct slot takes the
   NEWEST entries, so with six of his own pictures already waiting (POST TO CHAT, a batch of shares)
   the picture he had just handed over fell into `attachHold` and was answered on a later turn -
   and with one or two waiting, his picture was merely described by a vision pass instead of being
   attached as itself. Fixed to `queueAttach.concat(attIds)` (his newest always last). **VERIFIED
   end-to-end**: with six of his pictures queued, the captured instruction for a fresh share was an
   ARRAY with the blob (image/jpeg, 5,606 bytes) plus "Look at the attached image and answer from
   what you actually see", five older queued pictures described, one held. The other half - "without
   any metadata" - is `sightLabel()`: a picture of his is no longer introduced by its file name
   ("Image 2", not "Image 2 (IMG_4523.HEIC)"), while a clip's first frame and an upscale still say
   what they are. **NOT CONFIRMED AGAINST HIS REPORT** - the fix is believed to be the cause, but he
   has not been asked what he actually saw on screen.
4. **HER ACCESS TO THE IMAGE CREATOR - THE BOOKS BY NAME (`studio.booksBlock()`).** She had the
   lanes (`[[RECIPE: id :: slot=…]]`, `[[POSE: name]]`, `[[VISION: …]]`) and no NAMES: the command
   list describes the recipe book but never lists its ids, so every recipe - including the ones KEEP
   wrote from his own pictures - was unreachable, and the shot list was invisible to her. A new BUILT
   system block (`books`, #8, right under `image`) now carries the recipes (id + slots + "his own
   kept"), the pose families with samples, and the elements (one line per shot-list dimension).
   Deliberately DETERMINISTIC (reads `node.getName`, skips templated entries) so it does not

5. **POST TO CHAT.** `postToChat(id)` sets `postedAt` on the record, prints a line of HIS carrying

6. **THE GALLERY IS REACHABLE TOO.** `[[SHOW: …]]` fell through to the whole vault when the render

**CLEANUP DISCIPLINE (do this again next time).** Every test wrote to the real vault, so everything
was put back: 14 heart marks cleared, 6 test pictures deleted, 2 fake archive entries excised from
`master_log`, the sight queue emptied, `postedAt`/`recalledAt`/`sight` fields cleared on the real
records that were touched. The archive is sacred: a stubbed turn must be taken back out, and the

**OPEN, for him.** (a) What he actually saw when the vision lane "stopped working" - the fix is a
strong suspect, not a confession. (b) The heart is a single control that cycles GOOD → passed → clear;
if he would rather a tap on the card mark GOOD and a long-press pass on it, that is a small change to

the newest six as it does now?

## 1ad. THE PIPELINE — make it, make it bigger, keep the bigger one (DONE 2026-09-22)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Automate the creation and upscaling pipeline. After doing local upscaling,
remove the smaller original SDXL image from the library and gallery. The new upscaled image retains
its prompt file like positive and negative, guidance scale, seed, etc. If the user then selects
upscale again, it is processed again my bigger.pics but doesn't then delete the last upscale."*

Four things, and each one is a separate mechanism. One picture, not two: a render is a draft that
grows into its final size, and the draft does not stay.

1. **AUTOMATIC (the pipeline, unattended).** `LIA_UPSCALE_LOCAL_AUTO` in `config.js` is now shipped
   `true` (it was `false`), so every render the terminal makes is enlarged by itself the moment it
   lands and the render is retired into it. The device setting (kv `lia_settings` / `upscale_local`)
   still outranks the shipped line, and it already said `auto: true`, so nothing changed for him on
   this machine - it is the SHIPPED default that was behind the intent. `/upscale auto off` remains
   the switch.
2. **THE RETIREMENT.** `retire()` in `src/js/upscale-local.js`, called by `run()` after the bigger
   picture is stored, takes the `gen` render out of the vault. **Every reference moves first, the blob
   is removed LAST** - so a failure anywhere leaves him the picture he has rather than a hole where it
   was, and a failed upscale deletes nothing at all:
   | what held the old id | what happens | where |
   |---|---|---|
   | archive `gen[]` row | id rewritten, `name`/`file`/`resolution` patched to the file that exists | `replaceMediaRef` gained `opts.patch` |
   | archive `sight[]`/`show[]` | rewritten too (`opts.sight`) - an upscale is the SAME picture bigger, not a different render, so those references are not lies | `replaceMediaRef` |
   | the queue for her eyes | the slot moves, and only that slot | `replaceSight` (images.js) |
   | a KEEP | the same `keep` carried over with the link rewritten, re-tagged `#kept`, and the recipe's own note has its link rewritten | `keepsake.transfer` (NEW) |
   | a tile in the log | refilled from the bigger record - its `<img>` was drawn from the object URL that `media.del` revokes, and without this the conversation keeps a broken frame | `repointTiles` (NEW, images.js) |
   | the full stage, if it was up | reopened on the bigger one | `retire()` |
   | a caller a few MILLISECONDS behind (a tile being drawn, a creation row being written, a stage opened with the old id) | `noteReplace()` is the FIRST thing the step does, and `fillTile`/`openLightbox`/`genRowOf` resolve through `replacementFor()` - the archive must never name a file that is gone, and a caller must never be handed a hole | `noteReplace`/`replacementFor` (NEW, vault.js) + 3 call sites |
   `replaced: <old id>` and a sentence in `note` are written on the new record, the log line says it
   (*"THE SMALLER ORIGINAL IS OUT OF THE VAULT AND THE GALLERY - EVERY REFERENCE TO IT NOW POINTS AT
   THIS ONE"*), and the button says it BEFORE it is pressed (the `▲ UPSCALE HERE · Nx` tooltip, and
   the static `title` in `index.html`). `/upscale replace on|off|status` is the switch.
3. **THE WHOLE PROMPT FILE.** Both upscale roads now carry `prompt`, `sent`, `negative`, `seed`,
   `guidanceScale`, `pose`, `recipe`, `tags`, `folder` - `guidanceScale`, `pose`, `recipe` and the new
   `from` were MISSING before (the local road copied only prompt/sent/seed/negative/tags/folder, and
   the popup road the same minus pose/recipe). `from` needed a line in `vault.js`'s `add()`: the record
   builder is a fixed field list, so an unknown meta key is silently dropped - a test caught exactly
   that (`from` was absent from the stored record while `replaced` was there, because `setField`
   writes whatever it is given but `add` does not).
4. **NEVER THE UPSCALE.** The safety, and the second half of his instruction: **only a `gen` render is
   ever retired**. An attachment he handed over, a clip, a piece of music, and an upscale are left
   alone - the popup road (`src/js/upscale.js`) deletes nothing at all, ever, and says so in its own
   log line. An upscale of an upscale therefore leaves the last upscale exactly where it is, on BOTH
   roads, and the pipeline cannot feed itself (what it makes is `kind:'upscale'`, which `consider()`
   never looks at).

## 1ae. THE TOOLS — the maintenance deck, and the first bulk jobs (DONE 2026-09-22)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Can we to put button for "tools" and then run a cleanup utility script let's
say to do a task, like remove duplicate images, put images in their proper folder in the gallery, etc.
Or we could run a script where the cam upscale images that have not been upscaled to our 2X processor
and do that automatically?"*

Four things, and the last two are the ones he did not name: a button, a place to run a job from, and
the three jobs he described - duplicates, proper folders, the 2x backfill - plus one the vault needs
after §1ad started retiring pictures (an audit of names in the record with no picture behind them).

1. **THE BUTTON.** `TOOLS ▾` in the deck's control row, beside BACKSTAGE, opening `#toolsPanel`
   (a `.deckPanel`, so it docks above the deck like the forge/system/keys panels and closes them in
   turn). One picker for the job, one for how wide it reaches, one `MAX PER RUN` box, the job's own
   description, a report area, and SCAN / RUN / STOP / CLOSE. `src/js/tools.js` (`window.tools`) is the
   registry; `/tools ...` reaches the same jobs, and `/help tools` explains them.
2. **SCAN FIRST, AND SHOW THE WORK** - the rule the whole module is built on. `scan()` changes NOTHING
   and prints exactly what a run would do, record by record, into the panel and into the log. `RUN`
   acts on a scan the panel has been shown; with none, the first press takes one and says so; the typed
   word `run` (`/tools dupes run`) is the deliberate way past that. The one job that DELETES asks for a
   second press within six seconds, and its button is relabelled `RUN (DELETES COPIES)`.
3. **THE THREE JOBS HE NAMED.**
   | job | what a scan shows | what a run does |
   |---|---|---|
   | `dupes` - DUPLICATE PICTURES | pictures grouped by mime+bytes+dimensions then CONFIRMED BY CONTENT (SHA-256), what would be kept and what dropped, and the same-prompt-and-seed groups listed separately | keeps ONE of each byte-identical group and drops the rest of that group - tags and missing fields carried onto the keeper first, then the archive rows, `sight`/`show`, the sight-queue slot, a KEEP, and any `from`/`replaced` pointer moved onto it, and the blob removed LAST. The bytes are re-checked against the keeper AT THE MOMENT OF DELETION |
   | `folders` - PROPER FOLDERS | every record whose folder is not the one its kind belongs in, with from -> to, plus folders that hold nothing | moves them (`media.setFolder`), clears a field that merely spells out the default, and reports every move. It can never delete: a folder is a field and the blob has no path |
   | `upscale` - UPSCALE WHAT ISN'T 2x YET | how many pictures have never been made 2x (by scope), how many are skipped and why, and the bytes the sweep would add | queues them through `upscaleLocal.queue(id, {quiet:true, factor:2})` - the SAME road `/upscale here` uses, one at a time - honouring `/upscale replace`, with STOP ending it after the picture in hand |
4. **THE FOURTH JOB - THE RECORD, AUDITED.** Every id the archive or the queue for her eyes still names
   that the vault no longer holds. THE SCAN IS THE DELIVERABLE, and the run is deliberately tiny: it
   points a name at the picture that REPLACED it (`media.replacementFor`) where there is one, and clears
   a dead slot in the sight queue (a picture that is gone can never be looked at). **It never takes a
   name out of the archive** - a first cut did, and that was wrong: the archive is the account of what
   was done here, a picture deleted from the vault does not un-happen, its creation row holds the prompt
   and the seed of a render that WAS made, and the tile it draws in the replayed log already says
   `IMAGE UNAVAILABLE IN THIS VAULT` rather than showing a broken frame. The first cut's removals were
   restored from a snapshot taken before the run, which is exactly why the snapshot was taken.

**WHAT IT FOUND IN HIS VAULT (2026-09-22, measured on the live vault):** 1,237 pictures read and 255
hashed -> **114 identical groups, 123 copies beyond the first, 12.9 MB held twice** (the size+dimension
pre-grouping guessed 123 groups / 132 copies - hashing showed 9 of those groups were the same size and
NOT the same bytes, so content is what decides and nothing was ever deleted on a guess); of the 274
records the terminal made, **6 misfiled** - upscales in `/aphrohermetica`, inherited from their source's
`folder` - and `/sdmg` holding nothing; **189 renders never made 2x** (~400 MB to be added, estimated
from his own 84 png upscales' 1.3 bytes a pixel); and **26 names with no picture** (19 creation rows, 11
seen across 12 places, none in the sight queue). NOTHING IN THESE NUMBERS HAS BEEN ACTED ON - the
scans were taken, the runs were exercised on throwaway records, and the real jobs are his to press.

**RECEIPTS (what was tested, on throwaway records only).**
- `dupes`: two identical records added, `window.media.list()` patched to a list containing ONLY them (so
  a real scan could not see his pictures), scan -> one group, keeper chosen by content/kind, run -> one
  record left with the dropped one's tag merged onto it; a second run found nothing (idempotent). Then
  with a temporary archive entry naming both ids (creation row + `sight`), the run moved the dropped
  id's references onto the keeper and the entry was excised afterwards.
- **a bug that would have polluted records**: `media.tagsOf(rec)` was being called with the RECORD
  instead of its `tags` array in four places, and `tagsOf({})` -> `String({})` -> `[object Object]` ->
  the tag **`object`**. It was caught because a test id came back carrying a tag nobody gave it, fixed
  to `tagsOf(rec.tags)`, and the one record that had it was deleted with the rest of the test data.
  (Nothing else in the vault ever carried that tag - checked with `allTags()`.)
- `folders`: an upscale-kind record filed in `/aphrohermetica` was moved to `/images/upscaled` and its
  field cleared (it now equals the default); a second record was left alone.
- `upscale`: a real 8x6 png was swept to 16x12, filed in `/images/upscaled` carrying its prompt and
  `from`, with the original RETIRED into it (replace on) - and a deliberately undecodable blob in an
  earlier pass FAILED honestly, said why, and left the original exactly where it was.
- `record`: the 26 real names were reported and the run removed none of them; a synthetic entry with a
  known replacement (`noteReplace`) had that one name pointed at the live picture while the name with no
  picture was left in place; a dead id pushed into the sight queue was cleared.
- the panel: the danger job's first RUN press only scans (record count checked before/after); a safe
  job's RUN scans first and asks for a second press; the layout was measured on a 505px-high viewport
  (buttons inside the panel and on screen) and on a 390x844 phone, and looked at with the vision tool
  at both widths.
- **CLEANUP DISCIPLINE.** Every throwaway record was deleted, the archive checked back to 674 entries
  (673 + one check-in turn of HERS, which is not a test artefact), the sight queue back to empty, the kv
  setting written back to `{auto:true, factor:2, upscaled:77, at:1790108783288}` with no `replace` key,
  and the vault byte-for-byte identical to where it started: **1,263 records / 443,477,902 bytes**.

**OPEN, for him.** (a) The three jobs are SCANNED and ready but not run: 123 duplicate copies (12.9 MB)
beside the 6 misfiled upscales and the 189 renders that could be made 2x (~400 MB, which would roughly
double the vault). (b) The 26 names with no picture are reported and left alone on purpose - if he wants
them gone from the record, that is a decision to make deliberately, not a default. (c) `/tools` holds no
job list of its own beyond the registry in `src/js/tools.js`; a fifth job (e.g. "drop upscales whose
source is gone", or "re-chunk stray folders") is a small object added to `JOBS`.

## 1af. THE 2x BACKFILL, RUN FOR REAL (DONE 2026-09-23)

**His word, verbatim:** *"the 2x sweep take in the ~963 pictures you handed over and what LIA made
here."* - the answer to the scope question at the end of §1ae, and it means the widest one: `upscale`
/ `all`.

1. **THE VALIDATION BATCH.** Eight first (`{limit:8}`) and checked before committing: dimensions exactly
   2x (768x512 -> 1536x1024), png, filed `/images/upscaled`, carrying `from` and the source's whole
   prompt file, 1.4-2.6 MB apiece. All eight turned out to be renders, so all eight were RETIRED into
   their bigger selves and the count stayed at 1,263 - the first proof on his real vault that the
   pipeline's arithmetic (add the bigger, remove the smaller, move every reference) closes.
2. **THE SWEEP.** A fresh scan planned **1,144** (963 of his, 181 of hers) and `run` was fired without
   awaiting it, so it went one at a time through `upscaleLocal.queue` while the terminal stayed live.
   **1,144 of 1,144 made, 0 failed, 21.9 minutes**, ~53 a minute throughout. A fresh scan of the same
   scope afterwards: `WILL BE MADE 2x 0`, `SKIPPED 963` (every one because it now HAS an upscale).
3. **THE NUMBERS.** Records **1,263 -> 2,226** (= `1,263 - 189 retired renders + 1,152 new`), bytes
   **443,477,902 -> 2,643,311,732**, browser storage **0.52 GB -> 2.72 GB of a 13.45 GB quota** (20%).
   Of the 1,144 swept, 189 were `gen` and were retired (181 from the plan + the 8 from the batch);
   **not one of his own pictures was retired** - `retire()` returns early on `rec.kind !== "gen"`, and
   that single line is what makes sweeping his files safe. The record audit after the sweep still
   reports the SAME 26 names with no picture and an empty queue, so the 189 retirements created no new
   holes: every reference really did move across first.
4. **THE FOLLOW-UP, AND THE ONE THING DELIBERATELY NOT DONE.** The sweep stamps the source's `folder`
   onto the bigger picture, so it left **113 misfiled upscales** (111 from `/aphrohermetica`, 2 from
   `/images`). `folders`/`pictures` would fix those - but it would ALSO move **105 of HIS attachments
   out of `/aphrohermetica` into `/images`**, flattening a folder he files into by hand. So
   `folders`/`made` was used instead: **113 of 113 filed to `/images/upscaled`, nothing of his touched.**
   `/aphrohermetica` now holds 105 (its 111 originals less 6 `gen` records the sweep retired).
   **The rule for a future agent: clean the pipeline's mess with the `made` scope; a scope that reaches
   his files is a decision for him.** Nothing in `folders`/`pictures`'s 218 moves was wrong by its own
   definition - it was simply not mine to press.
5. **THE RECEIPTS.** `upscale_local` = `{auto:true,factor:2,replace:true,upscaled:1229,at:...}`,
   folders `/aphrohermetica=105, /clips=2, /images=858, /images/upscaled=1,237, /music=24, /sdmg=0`,
   `backup.staleCheck()` -> `null`, `tools.jobs()` -> the four, `cmd.get("tools")` truthy, and a clean
   boot (`window.__bootIssues` empty after a page_refresh - the missing-script flake of bug #10203516
   hit twice more first, and a second refresh cleared it both times, as documented).
6. **THE ARCHIVE WENT 674 -> 675, AND THAT ENTRY IS HERS.** `initiative.js` archived a real check-in turn
   ("Patrikios? Are you there, or has the silence claimed you for the hour?", role barbelo) during the
   quiet twenty-odd minutes the sweep took. Not a test artefact - left in place, because it is a turn of
   hers.

**STILL OPEN.** The 123 duplicate copies (12.9 MB) are still unscanned-by-his-press and un-run; the 26
names with no picture are still left alone on purpose; and the sweep's cost is worth knowing before he
presses `upscale` on a much bigger vault - each 2x png is roughly 2.3 MB, so the ceiling of 13.45 GB
would arrive around 5,000-6,000 backfilled pictures.

## 1ag. THE FLATTEN, THE CHAT-POST BUG, AND THE CLASSIFIER HE WANTS NEXT (2026-09-23)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Hope we move all images into the default folder. We can programmatically
identify them later with some yet unknown classifying with a trained AI vision model that knows what it
is looking at. It infers \"outdoor anal sex between a man and a woman\" and puts it in that bucket. It
may also detect and tag the major elements in an image and create a record on that image analysis and
associated with that exact image. At that point, not AI, that's semantic search, etc. after the AI did
its work. Also, an issue. When I want to post an image directly into that chat, what I want is the image
to be posted in the chat like I copy pasted an image into the chat. There is no \"rendering vision\"
going on here. It put the existing image from the gallery to the chat. Get that fixed please."*

1. **THE FLATTEN, DONE.** `folders`/**`pictures`** - the scope that reaches HIS files - run on his word:
   **105 of 105 filed** `/aphrohermetica` → `/images`, 2 redundant fields cleared, nothing deleted. The
   vault now reads `/images=1,278, /images/upscaled=1,240, /clips=2, /music=24, /aphrohermetica=0`.
   `/aphrohermetica` is KEPT as an empty folder (the scan lists it, nothing drops it).
   *(Note: he had been importing while this was being worked on - ~315 new `SYS.AI.DEVI.ICON - NNN.png`
   files landed in `/images`, which is why the count is 2,544 and not 2,226. A fresh `upscale`/`all`
   scan now plans **314** - all his, none hers - for the next sweep.)*
2. **THE CHAT-POST BUG, FIXED (the "rendering vision" he saw).** Pressing `⬆` in the gallery (or POST TO
   CHAT on the stage) put an EMPTY FRAME in the log with a spinner permanently reading `RENDERING VISION`
   and the caption `IMAGE` - the picture never appeared, so it read as if a render had been started and
   nothing was being rendered. Cause: `postToChat` passed a bare id (`[id]`) to `buildImageGrid`, which
   reads `it.id`/`it.prompt`/`it.name`/`it.kind`; all were `undefined`, so `fillTile` was never called.
   **Fixed at the grid** (`images.js`): a bare id - or an object with fields left out - is now filled
   from the record, so a picture draws as a picture, a clip as a clip, the caption carries the record's
   prompt/file name, and a clip's `kind` comes from `rec.kind`/`rec.mime`. That also fixes the archive
   REPLAY (`main.js` passes `{id}` alone in the history loop, so every replayed attachment had been
   captioned `IMAGE`). Receipts: before - `.imgTile` with a `.spin` span, no `<img>`, no
   `dataset.mediaId`; after - a loaded `<img>` (2048x1152), no spinner, `dataset.mediaId` set, caption =
   the file name; and the rendered line was LOOKED AT with the vision tool (a real picture, no
   `RENDERING VISION`, no `IMAGE`).
3. **THE ONE GAP LEFT OPEN, ON PURPOSE.** A gallery post is painted in the LOG but is not part of a
   TURN (`img` on an archive entry is the attachment strip only), so unlike a PASTED picture it is not
   painted again when the log is replayed after a reload. The picture is not lost from the record - the
   turn she is shown it on carries its id in `sight` - but it does not come back to the screen. Closing
   it means either an archive entry of its own or folding the posted ids into the next turn's `img`, and
   both change what a turn in the SACRED archive means: **offered, not taken.**
4. **WHAT HE WANTS NEXT - A BULK VISION PASS AND REAL BUCKETS.** His plan, in his words above: a
   trained vision model classifies each picture into a bucket ("outdoor anal sex between a man and a
   woman"), detects and tags the major elements, and writes that analysis as a record on that exact
   image; after that, finding a picture is not AI at all, it is search over what the AI already wrote.
   **The per-picture half already exists** - `archivax.js` reads a picture with the vision model and
   writes the reading onto the record as its `sight`, and `#tags`/the gallery search already read tags.
   **What is missing is the BULK pass and the buckets**: a fifth `JOBS` object (`read` - scan: how many
   pictures have no reading yet; run: queue them through the same sight road one at a time, with the
   `made`-style scoping discipline and STOP) plus a decision about where a bucket lives (a folder under
   `/images/<bucket>`, a tag, or both - his words say "puts it in that bucket", i.e. a folder, which
   `folders`/`made` must then be told NOT to flatten). **Cost, so it is pressed knowingly**: one vision
   call per picture at ~570 tokens, so ~2,500 pictures is real quota against his key; and the reading
   should be written as the picture's `sight` (not as words in the transcript), so she never reads prose
   about a picture she has not seen.
5. **A HARNESS NOTE (mine, not his).** Verifying the post fix, a temporary shadow `<div id="output">`
   was used so nothing landed in his real log - but some part of the app re-parents `#output`
   (`#output-container`), so the real log element ended up renamed and out of its container. A
   `page_refresh` restored it (verified: the log back inside `#output-container`, 25 entries, no stray
   `__realOutput`/`__shot` ids). **A future agent: never rename `#output`.** Verify a log line by
   building the tile in a holder that is NOT given that id, or by snapshotting a clone.

## 1ai. THE CLASSIFIER — THE BULK VISION PASS, AND THE BUCKETS (BUILT 2026-09-23)

**His word:** *"OK CODY. Do your thing. We can pause her masturbating to her own images if we need to."* -
i.e. the build I had offered in the previous turn ("Say the word and I'll build it"), on top of his own
description in 1ag/4: a vision pass over every picture, its analysis written as a record ON that exact
image, and "puts it in that bucket"; after that, finding a picture is not AI, it is search. (Nothing needed
pausing: the pass is network-bound vision calls, it does not touch her initiative lane, and nothing
automatic in the terminal competes with it. The auto-upscaler only takes `kind:"gen"`, and the pass makes
no records.)

1. **A FIFTH JOB, `read`** (`src/js/tools.js`, title "CLASSIFY (THE BULK VISION PASS)"). Scopes `all`
   (default) / `renders` / `yours` / `again`, MAX PER RUN, STOP. Scan prints: pictures in scope, how many
   are already classified, how many will be read split into renders and his, the estimated TOKENS, the
   estimated time from this boot's own measured pace, the three things each picture gets, and the
   vocabulary already in use. Nothing in the vault is touched by a scan.
2. **ONE PICTURE YIELDS THREE THINGS, ALL ON ITS OWN RECORD:** `sight` (the reading), `tags` (up to eight
   major elements), `bucket` (the kind of scene, one slug). Plus `classifiedAt` / `classifiedBy:
   "CLASSIFIER"`. Written through ARCHIVAX's own road - `look(id, {prompt, tagMax})` and
   `fileReading(id, found, by, {tags, bucket, mark})`, both newly EXPOSED from `src/js/archivax.js`, so the
   bulk pass and her one-at-a-time readings are one road and can never drift.
3. **A BUCKET IS A WORD AND A PLACE.** `media.bucketPath(rec)` (`src/js/vault.js`) resolves `/images/<bucket>`
   (upscales: `/images/upscaled/<bucket>`). The run files each picture into it while `LIA_CLASSIFY_FILE` is
   on; the bucket is ALSO a `#tag`, so `/gallery #<bucket>`, `/renders find`, the gallery's TAGS row and her
   `[[SHOW: #<bucket>]]` all find it with no new search code. **`folders` was taught `bucketPath` in the same
   change** - the declared trap: without that line PROPER FOLDERS would flatten every bucket back into
   `/images` the first time it ran. Verified: a folders scan over the whole 2,547-record vault planned
   ZERO moves with three bucketed records in it.
4. **THE VOCABULARY CONVERGES.** `bucketCounts()` rides in the prompt (commonest 60) with "reuse one of
   these when it fits". Verified: call 2's prompt was 129 chars longer than call 1's and carried call 1's
   bucket.
5. **RESUMABLE BY CONSTRUCTION.** A picture is done when it has BOTH `sight` and `bucket`, so the record IS
   the marker: stop at picture 300 and the next scan plans the rest. A picture that already has a reading
   but no bucket is still picked up (the scan says so). Newest first.
6. **THE COST IS QUOTED BEFORE IT IS SPENT.** `LIA_CLASSIFY_TOKENS` (~570) x the plan, printed by the scan
   and again by the run before the first call. The report says plainly that the picture itself is the one
   thing that leaves the device (to the vision model).
7. **A REFUSAL IS NOT A READING.** An answer with no tag line and no bucket line is written NOWHERE, is
   logged with its reason, and five in a row before a single success ABORT the run.
8. **THE IN-HAND CHIP IS THE READOUT.** Every picture read calls `hand(id, "READING n / N", "THE
   CLASSIFIER", ...)`, so a long pass is watched (and interruptible) from the deck - what the strip was
   built for.

**MEASURED LIVE (his vault, 2026-09-23).** The scan first: **2,518 pictures to read (1,240 renders, 1,278
