## 1aj. THE INTERCOM AND THE INLINE SEE (BUILT 2026-09-23)

**His word, verbatim (one message, two asks):** *"Can we do this inline? Let's send the new '/*slash'
command in the chat context window. I can send an image from the gallery telling her to 'see' the
attached image and 'view the image' (the vision model) which creates everything it needs for the
conversation and even saves the metadata related to that image only by names, bucket, etc."* - and -
*"Let make the TALK and LISTEN buttons just like an intercom. When she is talking I do not interrupt.
When she is done the buttons are in standby."*

1. **THE INTERCOM IS ENFORCED, NOT PAINTED.** TALK and LISTEN were already polite in the live channel,
   but a *press* could still cut her off mid-sentence (TALK while she speaks) or open the ears onto her
   own voice coming back off the speakers (LISTEN while she speaks). `voice.js` now has one answer,
   `airState()`, and every key reads it: **STANDBY** (nothing on the line, both live) / **HER VOICE**
   (she is speaking - TALK locked, LISTEN shut) / **HER TURN** (her reply is in flight - both locked) /
   **YOUR VOICE** (the ears are open - TALK locked) / **HOLDING** (he spoke while she had the floor) /
   **AUDITION** (the one exception: TALK *is* the stop there, so it is not locked). `toggle()` refuses
   when `!canTalk()`, `toggleListen()` when `!canListen()`, and each refusal prints `airLine()` (which
   state the line is in and what to do). `speak()` takes the floor the moment TALK is pressed
   (`setSpeaking(true)` right after `stopSpeakingInternal()`), so the ElevenLabs round trip cannot slip
   through as STANDBY. **The microphone is untouched** - it still hushes her while the live channel is
   open - and `/voice stop` still silences her: the lock is on the BUTTON, so a stray press cannot cut
   her off while a deliberate command still can. `setUi()` paints the lamp `#airLamp` (STANDBY / HER
   VOICE / HER TURN / YOUR VOICE / HOLDING / AUDITION) and disables the keys (`disabled` +
   `aria-disabled` + `.air`), and a 400ms `watchAir()` ticker repaints only on a real change - so a
   state driven from outside a press (her speech ending on its own) still returns the keys to standby.
   `/voice air` reports it; `state().air` and `window.voice.{air,canTalk,canListen,airLine}` expose it.
   *(The key names were straightened out a day later - the keys are now named from his side of the
   glass, `canMic`/`canSpeak`; see 1ar. The locks described above are unchanged.)*
2. **`/see` - ONE VAULT PICTURE, IN THE CHAT, READ ON THE WAY.** The per-picture half of 1ai's
   classifier, on stage. `/see <VAULT ID | newest | <N> | #TAG> [and what you want to say]`, and
   `/see again <WHAT>` to re-read one. In order: `media.setField(id,"postedAt")` (so the record is HIS);
   `attach.carry([id])` (the picture rides on the message as his line, no second copy made); **ONE**
   vision call `archivax.look(id, {prompt: tools.classifyPrompt(), tagMax: 8})` ->
   `archivax.fileReading(id, found, "patrikios", {tags:true, bucket:true, mark:"SEE"})` (the reading
   written as `sight`, the major elements as tags, the kind of scene as `bucket`, filed into
   `/images/<bucket>` while `LIA_CLASSIFY_FILE` is on); a clip falls back to its kept FIRST FRAME
   (a recording with no picture is refused by name); `seeBlock` (name, id, folder, bucket, tags, and her
   own earlier reading) rides in `instructionText` - **the one place a picture of his is handed over
   WITH its filing, because he named it**; the turn then runs as any attachment turn with the picture as
   the newest attachment. **A picture that already carries a reading and a bucket is NOT paid for
   again** (`seeNeeds = again || !sight || !bucket`), so `/see` is also the cheapest way to put a filed
   picture back in a conversation, and the token estimate is printed before any call that will be spent.
3. **THE PICTURE IS NAMED ONE WAY FOR BOTH DOORS.** `/peek` (1ah) and `/see` share a new resolver,
   `resolveVaultTarget(arg, {pictures})` in `images.js` (bare/newest, an id or its start, `#tag`, the
   Nth from the newest) with `vaultShelf()`; the four ways of naming one were lifted out of `/peek`, so
   the two commands can never disagree about "the third newest" or "mmud9esy". It returns the id, why it
   matched, and the newest-first list, which `/see` reuses for the carried picture.
4. **THE GALLERY'S EYE (`☉`, `gSee`).** On every tile, between `⤒` (queue) and `⬆` (post): it SEEDS
   `/see <id> ` into the input box and closes the gallery, so he can add his own words after the
   citation - a button that sent immediately would take that away. It prints a SYSTEM receipt. Action row
   is now `gPick,gHeart,gPeek,gFull,gQueue,gSee,gPost,gSave,gDel`.
5. **A CARRIED PICTURE CANNOT BE DELETED BY THE STRIP.** `attach.js` gained `carried` /
   `carry(ids)` / `isCarried(id)` (and `attach.carry` / `attach.carried`): the strip's `×` on a carried
   picture takes it off the MESSAGE and never out of the vault (`.attachThumb.carried`), and `clear()`
   resets `carried`. This is the rule that makes an inline picture safe to un-send.

**MEASURED LIVE (his vault, 2026-09-23).** *Intercom:* STANDBY (both keys live, lamp STANDBY,
`air === "STANDBY"`) -> she speaks (lamp `HER VOICE`, TALK disabled, LISTEN disabled, and **both
`voice.toggle()` and `voice.toggleListen()` were refused with the explanation while she kept speaking**)
-> `/voice stop` -> STANDBY. HER TURN (`sendBtn` disabled): both locked, TALK refused, nothing spoken.
AUDITION: `air === "AUDITION"`, lamp AUDITION, **TALK = STOP and enabled**, LISTEN locked; TALK stopped
it -> STANDBY. Geometry: 390x844 the lamp is 74x34 at x=288, inside the visible part of the scrolling
controls row, deck overflow 0; 1920x1080 one row, all controls 34px tall, no overflow. VISUAL: five real
`.controls` rows (one per state, real CSS) rasterised through `foreignObject` -> canvas -> `vision`,
which confirmed the lamp words, the standby keys bright against the dimmed ones, and no clipping (the
harness was removed afterwards). *Inline see - ONE REAL TURN, on a throwaway 8x8 jpeg named "SEE TEST -
DELETE ME.png":* 103 s. The one vision call (570 tokens announced) returned *"A blurry green square is
centered in the upper half of a dark, out-of-focus field."*, bucket `abstract-composition`, tags
`blur, green, square, dark, abstract, minimal`; the record carried `sight`/`bucket`/`classifiedBy:
"SEE"`/`classifiedAt`/`postedAt` and was moved from `/images` into a real `/images/abstract-composition`;
his line landed with the picture tile (`Patrikios says: look at this with me`) and her reply answered
the pixels (*"A flicker of emerald in the void..."*). The `seeBlock` was READ BACK out of the live
instruction (temporarily instrumented, then removed and re-verified) and contained the whole filing
verbatim (name, id, folder, bucket, tags, and her earlier reading). Free paths also verified: `/see`
bare prints usage; `/see zzzznope` prints the resolver's error and leaves the text in the box; `/see
<a recording id>` is refused by name; the gallery `☉` seeds `/see <id> ` + closes + focuses.

**COLLATERAL, CAUGHT AND REVERSED (do not repeat).** A picture turn drains the SIGHT QUEUE - it
described **5 of his waiting pictures** through the plain `LIA_SIGHT_PROMPT` path and marked them seen
("SHE LOOKED AT 6 OF THE 878 PICTURES WAITING FOR HER EYES"). Identified by exact-matching the DOM's
`SIGHT ::` lines to records: **`mmub1337msulzs`, `mmub133m2mjfu4`, `mmub13446nneh0`, `mmub134g34jrev`,
`mmub134tl0nd37`** (all `APHROHERMITICA - BALD - 454..458-upscaled.jpg`, none previously carrying
sight/bucket). Reversed, measured: `sight` cleared to `""` on all five, all five re-queued in order
(`sightPending()` 872 -> **877**, the pre-test length), the throwaway record deleted (vault **2544**),
the bucket folder removed (`removeFolder` -> `{ok:true, removed:1}`; folders back to exactly
`/aphrohermetica, /clips, /images, /images/erotic-fantasy-portrait, /images/upscaled, /music, /sdmg`),
and `master_log` restored from a snapshot taken before the turn - **JSON-identical, 691 entries**.
After cleanup + refresh: chat history back to his 6 real turns, `staleCheck() === null`, `inHand`
hidden, strip empty, `air()` STANDBY.

**WHAT WAS NOT RUN, and is INFERRED ONLY:** `/see again <WHAT>` on a read picture, and `/see` on a clip
(the poster branch) - both would have cost another ~18k-token real turn apiece, so their code paths were
read line by line instead. **The cost is worth stating plainly:** a picture turn's assembled instruction
is ~73k characters (~18k tokens) - the app's ordinary per-turn cost (canon + actor/role + command
catalogue + recall) - which is exactly why the "already read -> spend nothing" rule in step 2 matters.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/voice.js` (`airState`/`canTalk`/`canListen`/`airLine`/`airTick`/`watchAir`, the
refusals in `toggle`/`toggleListen`, the floor taken in `speak`, `state().air`, the `/voice air` verb,
`window.voice`), `src/js/images.js` (`vaultShelf` + `resolveVaultTarget`), `src/js/chat.js` (`/peek`
refactored onto the resolver; the `/see` block + `seeBlock`; help text), `src/js/attach.js`
(`carried`/`carry`/`isCarried`, the non-destructive strip `×`), `src/js/gallery.js` (`seedSee` + `☉`),
`index.html` (`#airLamp`, + comment), `src/css/terminal.css` (`.controls button.air` / `.controls
.airLamp`), `src/commands/commands.json` (**59 -> 60 commands**; a full `/see` entry; the `gallery` and
`voice` descriptions), `src/README.md` (files bullets + a new **THE INTERCOM** and **SEE IT INLINE**,
plus the classifier cross-reference) and this file. `main.pjs` untouched. Nothing was saved or published.

**NOTE FOR A FUTURE AGENT:** this preview loses 1-3 random `src/` scripts on roughly a quarter to a half
of reloads (platform bug 10203516) - each loss shows in `window.__bootIssues` as both a "STYLESHEET DID
NOT LOAD" and a "SCRIPT DID NOT LOAD" for the same path and can leave a stale red `#bootFail` banner
(rendered at a 1.5s post-load check and never removed, so trust `__bootIssues`, not the banner). Cure:
`page_refresh` again until `__bootIssues === []`. And wait for the FULL boot before reading state -
`sendBtn.disabled` clears before the archive replay finishes, so poll on `chatHistory.length > 0`, not on
the button.

**UPDATE (2026-09-26, see §1az):** the audit no longer works this way. It waits for every script tag to
settle, asks again for anything that did not arrive (twice), retries a 404 on a `src/` fetch once, and
`main.js` can no longer be ended early by a lost module - so a load now either comes up whole or says
plainly what is missing. Read the top of that section before believing a red banner means the build is
broken; a healed load has an empty `__bootIssues` and lists what it recovered in `window.__bootHealed`.

## 1ak. A PICTURE HE SENDS IS READ FIRST, AND THE QUEUE EMPTIED (BUILT 2026-09-23)

**His word, verbatim (the message right after 1aj was reported):** *"Kill the ~8xx waiting pictures for
now, It worked. I'd rather a picture I send by hand be what it is. A very normal chat activity to post
pictures to each other. The difference is that I want to do a deep analysis first, then responds, her
response filtered through her own lens depending on her SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS and block selected and ROLE.
In one ROLE she might be hyper-critical of what she sees. In another, she gives truth and honest
feedback and acts like a true friend."*

1. **THE QUEUE WAS EMPTIED.** `window.clearSight()` (`src/js/images.js`) empties `unseen` and saves to
   kv `lia_settings / unseen_sight`; it is NOT disabled (a new creation still queues) and NOTHING is
   marked and nothing leaves the vault. Run on his word: **877 -> 0**, measured. It stays empty because
   of (2) - a picture he sends no longer feeds or drains it.
2. **A PICTURE HE SENDS IS READ FIRST, THEN SHE ANSWERS.** An attachment turn is now about *what he
   sent* and nothing else. Each picture on the message is read by a neutral pass - `analyzeOf(id)` in
   `images.js`, prompt `LIA_ANALYZE_PROMPT` in `config.js` - and the reading is written on the record as
   its `sight` and handed to her as what she answers from. The pass knows NOTHING about who she is
   wearing, so **the perception is the plain truth of the image and only her RESPONSE to it is lensed by
   the role** - the whole point of splitting the two, and exactly what he described. The prompt asks for
   what is actually depicted (explicitly, concretely), then setting, mood, style, and what stands out,
   and says plainly: no judging, no praise, no roleplay.
3. **NOTHING ELSE IS BROUGHT IN.** `handing` (`chat.js`) short-circuits the whole queue road: no
   creations are described, no older waiting picture of his is pulled in, nothing is held, and the queue
   is not marked seen. `directId`/`describeIds` are empty and the raw blob is NOT attached to the reply
   (`blob:false`), because the reading IS her sight. Nothing about a picture he sent is queued.
4. **NO PICTURE IS PAID FOR TWICE.** `analyzeOf` returns `rec.sight` when the record already carries a
   reading, so re-sending a picture she has read costs no vision call. One call per never-read picture.
5. **A FAILED READING IS CAUGHT.** If the pass comes back empty the raw file is handed to her instead
   (`lastHopeless` -> `directId`/`directBlob`), so a refusal cannot leave her blind to a picture he
   actually sent. `LIA_ANALYZE_ATTACH = false` restores the old shape (newest attached directly, queue
   described) as a single knob.
6. **THE ARCHIVE STILL KNOWS WHAT SHE LOOKED AT.** The turn's entry records it in `sight: [ids]`
   (`perceivedForArchive`) - on a handing turn the pictures on his message, on a queue turn the
   creations she perceived. `img: [ids]` was already there and is unchanged.

**MEASURED LIVE (his vault, 2026-09-23) - ONE REAL TURN on two throwaway 8x8 pictures, then removed.**
A = the picture carried on the message (reading preset: *"TEST READING A - a flat red square on a plain
white field."*), B = a synthetic picture parked in the queue (reading preset, so a queue drain COULD
not have cost anything or touched his pictures). The temporary `window.__lastTurn` probe (added, read,
REMOVED and re-verified) reported: `handing:true, attIds:[A], attachSeen:[A], describeIds:[],
directId:"", blob:false`; the instruction carried the handing header (*"The picture on this message,
read for what it actually shows"*) and A's reading, did **not** carry B's reading, and did **not** carry
the old `Look at the attached image…` line - so (a) the picture is answered from the analysis, (b) the
raw file is not attached, (c) **the queue was not drained**. Her reply answered from the reading, in
role: *"A red square. A flat, stubborn piece of a color on a white field. … It is a stark thing,
Patrikios."* The archive entry carried `img:[A]`, `sight:[A]`; `sightPending()` still held B; no "SHE
LOOKED AT N PICTURES WAITING FOR HER EYES" line was printed. Cleanup, all measured: A and B deleted
(vault **2544**), the queue cleared (the kill above), `master_log` restored from the snapshot taken
before the turn (**692 entries**, which is the live count - a CHECK-IN entry had appended since 1ai's
691), and after a reload: `chatHistory` 6, nothing of the test in the log, no `#bootFail`, no boot
issues. `index.html` and `main.pjs` were NOT touched.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/chat.js` (the `handing` flag + the analysis loop + the handing header + the
`perceivedForArchive` archive field; the queue road is unchanged when he attaches nothing),
`src/js/images.js` (`sightOf(id, prompt)`, `analyzeOf`, `clearSight`), `src/js/config.js`
(`LIA_ANALYZE_ATTACH`, `LIA_ANALYZE_PROMPT`), `src/README.md` (the images/config files bullets + a new
**A PICTURE HE SENDS IS READ FIRST** in ATTACHMENTS, the ATTACHMENTS caps line, the SEE IT INLINE
cross-reference, the config-knobs entry) and this file. Nothing was saved or published.

**NOTE. `LIA_ATTACH_SIGHT_MAX` now only bounds the OLD road** (no attachments on the message). On a
handing turn every picture on the message is read, so a very large batch is one vision call per
never-read picture on that turn - his own gesture, and `LIA_ATTACH_MAX` (16) is still the ceiling on how
many can ride at once.

## 1al. VIDEO FILES CAN BE IMPORTED INTO THE VAULT (DONE 2026-09-23)

**His word:** *"We need to be able to import video files like .mp4."*

Video was never missing from the **paperclip** (`attachInput` accepts `video/*,.mp4,.m4v,.mov,.webm,.ogv,
.mkv,.avi` and `kindOf()` routes `video/*` or an mp4/mov/... extension to `takeVideo`) - the gap was the
**gallery's import**, which only took pictures and music: dropping an .mp4 in the overlay answered
"NOTHING TO IMPORT :: DROP PICTURES ... OR MUSIC", and `#galFileInput`'s `accept` did not list video.

1. **ONE ROAD FOR A CLIP, WHEREVER IT COMES FROM.** `takeVideo` was split: the vault half is now
   `keepClip(file, {room, folder, quiet})` in `src/js/attach.js` (exported as `window.attach.keepClip`)
   and both callers walk it - the paperclip (`takeVideo`, unchanged behaviour: poster and master pushed
   onto the message strip) and the gallery import (`gallery.js importFiles`, which pushes nothing on a
   message and so passes `room:false`). `room` is the MESSAGE's attach limit; an import is not on a
   message and is not capped by it. `quiet` keeps the per-file SYSTEM lines off the stage for a caller
   that reports in its own words.
2. **THE GALLERY IMPORT TAKES CLIPS.** `importFiles` gained a `clips` bucket (mime `video/*` or
   `.mp4/.m4v/.mov/.webm/.ogv/.mkv/.avi`), a report line that says when a clip was too big for the
   vault (first frame kept instead) or kept whole with no frame drawn, and the "NOTHING TO IMPORT" and
   vault-empty messages now name clips. `#galFileInput` accepts `video/*` and the video extensions,
   and the IMPORT button reads **IMPORT PICTURES / CLIPS / MUSIC** with a title saying what a clip does.
3. **NOTHING ELSE CHANGED.** The clip is still kept byte for byte (never re-encoded, never uploaded),
   its first frame is still the thumbnail and the only picture of it that goes to her eyes, it lands in
   `/clips` (or the folder being shown), and the `kind:"video"` record shape, the gallery CLIPS filter
   and its clip tile, SAVE, and the full stage are all the existing ones.

**MEASURED LIVE (2026-09-23), then removed.** Source: a real clip already in his vault, `LAB - 002.mp4`
[mmu9era9sspzx5] (video/mp4, 500,427 bytes, 3.5625s) turned into a File. `gallery.importFiles([file])`
added **exactly two records**: the master `TOM TEST IMPORT2 - DELETE ME.mp4` (`kind:"video"`,
`mime:"video/mp4"`, 500,427 bytes byte-identical, `duration 3.5625`, `poster` set, folder `/clips`) and
its poster `... · first frame.jpg` (832×560 jpeg, folder `/images`, the same default an attached clip's
still takes). The gallery rendered both: the CLIP tile carried a loaded poster `<img>` (naturalWidth
832) and the clip badge. The **paperclip road was re-tested after the refactor** the same way:
`attach.add([file])` put one clip and one poster on the message strip (`attach.videos()` 0→1,
`attach.images()` 0→1, master `kind:"video"` with its poster, the strip showing `×VID×`). All five test
records were deleted and the strip cleared: vault back to **2547**, folders exactly as they were
(`/images 1277 · /images/upscaled 1239 · /images/erotic-fantasy-portrait 3 · /images/upscaled/erotic-fantasy-portrait 2 · /music 24 · /clips 2 · /aphrohermetica 0 · /sdmg 0`), and his two real clips
untouched. **One observation, not a bug:** the FIRST import attempt came back with the file kept whole
and **no frame drawn**, because the document was momentarily hidden and `videoFirstFrame`'s watchdog is
1.5 s for a hidden document (a browser refuses to fetch video in a background tab). The very next
attempt, document visible, drew the frame in 2.6 s. That is pre-existing behaviour shared with the
paperclip, and it is documented in the README.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/attach.js` (`keepClip` split out of `takeVideo`, `window.attach.keepClip`),
`src/js/gallery.js` (the `clips` bucket, the import report, the vault-empty and `/gallery` hints),
`index.html` (`#galFileInput` accept + the IMPORT button label/title), `src/README.md` (the
attach/gallery files bullets, the ATTACHMENTS CLIPS bullet, the gallery footer bullet) and this file.
**`index.html` changed, so `src/pack/index.html.txt` was regenerated** and `backup.staleCheck()` was
re-run clean. Nothing was saved or published.

## 1am. A CLIP IS READ AS A SEQUENCE, NOT AS A STILL (BUILT 2026-09-23)

**His word, verbatim:** *"I like this. She doesn't need to save the frames she 'sees' she needs the
aggravate impression then decide the final verdict of the action. Clips rarely exceed 10s. 24 frames per
second. So 10 seconds means 240 frames if she is scanning at that max frame rate. She doesn't need to.
We can dial in the optimal to get the gist of the clip provided. That's the first cheap route. None of
the thumbs created need to be kept in the gallery. The thumbnail is already there for the video."*

1. **THE FRAMES ARE TRANSIENT.** `attach.sampleFrames(file, {count})` (new, exported) draws `count`
   stills spread evenly from the clip's opening to its end (24 the hard ceiling) and hands them back with
   the time inside the clip each was taken at. New `images.lookBlob(blob, prompt)` runs ONE vision call
   on a Blob that is not a record - nothing written, nothing added, no gallery item, no queue. So the
   frames are drawn, read once, and thrown away; **the clip's own poster stays the only still of it that
   exists**, exactly as he asked.
2. **SHE GETS THE AGGREGATE, THEN GIVES THE VERDICT.** `chat.js` reads each frame with
   `LIA_CLIP_FRAME_PROMPT` (one terse sentence: what this frame shows, nothing before or after it, no
   judgement) and hands her the readings IN ORDER as one block - `opens on` / `then` / `ends on` - with
   the standing instruction to read them as ONE MOVEMENT and answer from that. The aggregate is written
   on the clip as its `sight` (the field the classifier and `[[READ: ...]]` use) plus `clipFrames`, so a
   clip sent twice is reused for free and the gallery shows her reading of it.
3. **A CLIP ALONE ON A MESSAGE IS A HANDING TURN.** `handing` was gated on `attIds` alone, but a clip
   puts only its STILL in there (the clip id rides in `attVids`), so it is now `attIds.length ||
   attVids.length` - otherwise a clip would have gone down the old queue road. The pool is
   `attIds.concat(attVids)` and the CLIPS ARE READ FIRST, so a clip's own still can be recognised and
   skipped in the picture pass (the first moment of the sequence IS that frame) - no double payment.
4. **A CLIP THAT CANNOT BE READ IS SAID, NOT FAKED.** Frames can only be drawn while the page is in
   front (a browser refuses to decode video in a hidden tab - measured: `readyState` stayed **0** for 9 s
   while hidden). Then the clip's own still is handed over instead if there is one, and if there is not,
   she is told plainly that a clip came with the message and that no frame of it could be read here, so
   she answers knowing it exists rather than inventing one. A clip file is never handed to the vision
   model (the `lookable` gate on the fallback makes that impossible).
5. **THE ARCHIVE SAYS WHAT SHE ACTUALLY LOOKED AT.** `sight:` on the turn now records the ids she really
   perceived (`perceived`), not everything that was on the message - a clip whose frames could not be
   drawn is not claimed as seen.

**MEASURED LIVE (2026-09-23), then removed.** `lookBlob` on a real picture Blob: one vision call, 8.2 s,
*"A nude woman with a celestial halo sits atop an ornate chair in a cosmic setting."* - vault **2547 ->
2547** and the source record's own `sight` **untouched**, which is the transient road proven.

**THE DECODER, MEASURED FOR REAL.** The preview tab came to the front partway through this work, and
with it `attach.sampleFrames` on a real clip (`LAB - 002.mp4`, 3.5625 s): **six frames at t = 0 / 0.7 /
1.4 / 2.1 / 2.8 / 3.5 s**, each **832x560** jpeg (~71-73 KB), **205 ms** end to end, `duration 3.5625`
read off the clip, and vault **2547 -> 2547** - nothing stored, the whole point. THEN THE FULL UNPATCHED
RUN: a copy of that clip added as a test clip, carried onto the message, and one real turn - **6 real
frames sampled and 6 real vision calls** in 69 s, `clipFrames: 6`, the stage receipt *"CLIP :: … ::
READING 6 FRAMES ACROSS IT (ABOUT 3420 TOKENS) :: NONE OF THE FRAMES ARE KEPT - ONLY THE CLIP AND ITS
OWN THUMBNAIL STAY IN THE VAULT."*, and the aggregate written on the record as its `sight` - six lines
labelled `opens on` / `then` x4 / `ends on`, each a real reading of a different moment of that clip, no
refusal. **Her reply was the aggregated impression turned into a verdict**, which is exactly what he
asked for: *"It's a clinical setting, but the energy is completely visceral. There's something about the
contrast that makes it hit harder - the white coat, the sterile laboratory environment, the coldness of
the equipment - all of it serving as a backdrop for something so hungry and focused."* The archive entry
carried `img:[clip]` and `sight:[clip]`. (An earlier run of the same turn with `attach.sampleFrames`
temporarily substituted for three 8x8 frames had already proven the assembly half in isolation, and is
what caught the bug below.)

**A BUG FOUND WHILE READING THE LOG, FIXED.** The safety-net branch in the picture pass printed
*"CLIP NOT READ AS A SEQUENCE :: ITS OWN STILL STANDS FOR IT"* for a clip that HAD just been read as a
sequence (the clip id is in the pool too, and only its poster was being marked as covered). The pass now
records every clip id it handles (`clipsHandled`) and the picture pass skips it silently; the video
branch in the picture pass is a silent safety net; and `LIA_CLIP_FRAMES = 0` now returns `{off:true}` so
"the sequence is switched off" is not reported as a failure. Verified present in the source after the
final reload.

**WHAT WAS *NOT* RUN, and is INFERRED ONLY - be honest about this.** The clip's **REUSE** path (a clip
whose record already carries `sight` is read again for free) is INFERRED - a three-line early return of
the same shape as `analyzeOf`'s reuse, which WAS measured at 0 ms. The `LIA_CLIP_FRAMES = 0` branch is
likewise reasoned, not run. Everything else - the sampling contract, the transient reading, the
ordering and labels, the aggregate on the record, the still-fallback, the "no frame could be read"
notice, and the archive's `perceived` - was run. One environmental fact worth keeping: **frame drawing
is impossible while the page is hidden** (a browser refuses to decode video in a background tab -
`document.hidden` true, a raw `<video>` at `readyState 0` for 9 s, and overriding the JS visibility
getters does not help because the deferral is the browser's own). `sampleFrames` answers cleanly with a
named reason in that case, and the turn falls back to the clip's still.

## 1ah. THE MINI LIGHTBOX AND THE IN-HAND STRIP (DONE 2026-09-23)

**His word, verbatim:** *"When there is a review going on like it is now, behind the curtain as it were,
the conversation can continue as normal. I might know the citation of what we is examining or working on
at present. Perhaps we need a way for me to see what it is with a little clickable thumbnail that
triggers a modal. Like a mini \"Light Box\". We can also use that lightbox elsewhere so I can browse the
Gallery."*

1. **WHAT IT IS.** `src/js/minibox.js`, new: `window.inHand` (the strip) and `window.miniBox` (the box).
   The strip is a chip in the deck's control row - the one place that is visible whatever else is open,
   veiled log and gallery included - carrying a THUMBNAIL, the CITATION (`some-file.png
   [mmud9esy4nuved]`) and the work being done ("UPSCALING 372 / 1144"). The box is the small modal it
   opens: the picture, its citation and facts, `‹ ›` to walk the list it was opened with, FULL STAGE to
   step up to the whole record. It only LOOKS - no writes, no deletes, no queueing. **A LEASE, NOT AN
   OWNERSHIP** is the design decision that makes it safe to call from anywhere: `show()` arms a 20s
   expiry that each call pushes out, so no caller ends anything and a job that dies cannot strand a
   stale thumbnail on the deck.
2. **WHO FEEDS IT.** One private `hand()` in `tools.js`, called by every long loop there (the duplicate
   hunt's hashing pass, the copy in hand during a duplicates RUN, each record being FILED, every picture
   the sweep upscales), and one line at the top of `upscale-local.js`'s `run()` - the single road every
   upscale in the terminal comes through. `retire()` now also calls `inHand.follow`/`miniBox.follow`
   beside `repointTiles`, because a sweep leaves the LAST picture it touched on the strip and that
   picture is often the one it just retired.
3. **THE OTHER DOORS.** `/peek [<ID> | newest | <N> | #TAG]` (command book 58 -> 59), the gallery's new
   `▣` on every card (opens on `visibleIds()` - his own filters), `/help peek`, `/peek` in the roster and
   the long command list, and the topic list.
4. **RECEIPTS (live, 2026-09-23).** The strip followed a REAL duplicate scan of 782 candidates:
   `HASHING 445 / 782`, `539 / 782`, `719 / 782`, `782 / 782`, each with the citation of the picture
   being hashed at that moment. `/peek` opened the newest thing in the vault with the receipt
   `PEEK :: output-...png [mmudd3pyxisyj4]`, count `1 / 2520`, arrows stepping to `2 / 2520`. The
   gallery's `▣` opened on `1 / 2544` with a loaded image. `inHand.follow`/`miniBox.follow` moved both
   halves from one id to another mid-show. ESC closed it, the chip hid itself. Geometry in the live page:
   a 516x475 panel centred in an 895x505 viewport, header + `2 / 6` + `×` on one row, `‹`/`›` at
   x=196/x=673 around a 484x323 image of a 768x512 source, the citation's three lines and the
   FULL STAGE / CLOSE / hint row all fully on screen; every text element visible, opaque, green on black,
   non-zero size.
5. **WHAT COULD NOT BE LOOKED AT.** The page's capture helpers do not work on a `position: fixed`
   overlay in this preview: `snapshot.js` never resolves here, and `html2canvas` paints a fixed
   element's chrome at document coordinates (measured: the header strip came back with only its `×`, the
   citation strip came back showing a different part of the page), and `vision` refuses this vault's
   content and accepts only a `<canvas>`/`<img>`. So this one change is verified by exact measurement and
   interaction rather than by eye - **a future agent with a working screenshotter should look at it
   once.** (The DOM geometry above is the checklist of what to expect.)
6. **FOUND WHILE TESTING, NOT ACTED ON: THE VAULT IS HOLDING A LOT OF EXACT COPIES.** The duplicate scan
   the strip was tested against reports **366 groups, 404 extra copies, ~466 MB held twice** - verified
   by hand on the largest group (two records, same name, same 2048x1366, same 3,692,144 bytes, SHA-256
   equal). Most of them are the sweep's own doing: a picture that was already in the vault twice got
   upscaled twice, and the same resampler over the same bytes makes the same bytes. That is 17% of the
   vault, reclaimable - **and it is his press** (DUPLICATES is the one job that deletes; it re-checks the
   bytes at the moment of deletion, so the risk is nil, but the decision is his).

**STILL OPEN.** (a) The duplicates run above (his press). (b) The 26 names with no picture, still left
alone on purpose. (c) The archive durability gap for POST TO CHAT (see 1ag/3). (d) ~~The bulk vision pass
and the buckets (1ag/4)~~ - **BUILT 2026-09-23, see 1ai.**

## 1an. THE SYSTEM PANEL CLOSED ITSELF ON THE ENTER KEY (FIXED 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"First thing: Fix the SYSTEM INSTRUCTION modal. I type and hit enter the page
closes itself. please deb-bug."*

1. **REPRODUCED FIRST, THEN FIXED.** With the panel open and `#spText` focused, one dispatched
   `keydown{Enter}` left `window.instr.isOpen() === false` - so the report is exact and the panel is what
   closed (in his words, "the page"). The cause is the document-level dismissal handler at the bottom of
   `main.js` (the one that means "any key closes whatever is on top": lightbox, gallery, panels, forge).
   It fired on EVERY keydown regardless of where the keystroke landed, and `instr.toggle()` SAVES AND
   CLOSES - so any keystroke inside the instruction editor threw the editor away mid-word, and Enter, the
   key you press while writing a paragraph, was the one he hit.
2. **THE FIX IS ONE GUARD.** If the event's target is an `INPUT`, a `TEXTAREA` or contentEditable, the
   key belongs to the field: the handler returns - unless the key is Escape, which still dismisses from
   anywhere. Measured after: Enter, letters and Tab in the box all leave the panel open with the text
   intact; a key pressed with focus OUTSIDE a field still dismisses (the guard broke nothing); Escape
   closes. `minibox.js` and `audition.js` already carried this guard - `main.js` was the outlier, and the
   same guard silently repairs the same latent bug in the key ring's secret box, the gallery's search and
   the forge's prompt fields (typing in any of those used to close its panel).
3. **ENTER IS A NEWLINE, CTRL+ENTER SAVES.** The editor holds a whole block, so Enter must insert a line;
   `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` on `#spText` is now the save, the same chord `editlog.js` and the forge batch use.
4. **CLOSING SAVES.** `instr.close()` is now `saveSelected(true)` then hide, so the CLOSE button, Escape,
   the SYSTEM button and the deck's dismissal all keep what he wrote - which is what the module's own
   comment always claimed ("nothing is ever lost by looking at something else") and what the CLOSE button
   did not do. `toggle()` now just calls `close()`.
5. **A STALE EMPTY OVERRIDE, FOUND WHILE TRACING IT - AND REMOVED.** kv `lia_settings / system` was
   holding `actor: ""`, i.e. the ACTOR block was in force as NOTHING and the 445-character `WHO YOU ARE`
   text (`LIA_ACTOR`) was missing from her prompt entirely. The bug above is a fast way to save an empty
   box by accident (any key saves). It was taken off with RESET and the shipped text is back; the rest of
   the saved block set was verified untouched (`canon` = his manifesto, byte-identical). **If he emptied
   that block on purpose he can simply type his own text back** - but he should know it was empty, since
   it means her identity text had not been sent for some time.
6. **RECEIPTS.** Before: `openAfterEnter:false`. After: `openAfterEnter:true`, `keptAfterEnter:true`,
   `openAfterLetter:true`, `openAfterTab:true`, `closedByKeyOutsideField:true`, `closedByEscape:true`,
   `savedByCtrlEnter:true`, `savedByEscape:true`, and kv `lia_settings / system` keys identical before and
   after every test (`["canon"]`). All test text was cleared out again.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/main.js` (the dismissal guard + the `#spText` Ctrl/Cmd+Enter save), `src/js/instr.js`
(`close()` saves; `toggle()` uses it), `src/README.md` (a new **THE PANEL, AND THE KEY THAT CLOSED IT**
under SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS) and this file. `index.html` and `main.pjs` were NOT touched by this item.

## 1ao. THE BULK CLASSIFIER ON VIDEO FRAMES (BUILT 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Yes. Bulk classifier on video frames, Then she can tag the video and classify it
correctly."* (accepting the offer made when the clip-sequence road landed: *"the bulk classifier is still
images-only, so it skips your clips - if you want it to walk a clip the same way (6 frames each), say so."*)

1. **THE PLAN NOW WALKS CLIPS.** `tools.js` had its own `isPicture(r)` (a mime test), so `lookable()`'s
   verdict that a video is not a picture excluded every clip from the plan (`isPicture && !sight`).
   Added `isClip(r)`, `isReadable(r)` (a picture, or a clip that still has its file) and `isYours(r)`
   (an attachment or a clip); `scopePool("read", ...)` now filters on those, so **scope `all` = 2,551
   pictures + 25 clips = 2,572 records** in this vault, `yours` includes clips, and `renders` is unchanged.
2. **ONE ROAD, NOT TWO.** The clip road lives in `archivax.js` now: **`clipSight(rec, opts)`** samples
   `LIA_CLIP_FRAMES` stills through `attach.sampleFrames`, reads each with `images.lookBlob`, parses each
   answer with the ONE parser (`parseReading`, extracted from the image road so both ways share it), and
   returns the reading of the whole movement - stills labelled `opens on:` / `then:` / `ends on:` in order
   - plus the union of the elements they named and the kind of scene MOST of them agreed on. **`look(id,
   opts)` branches on the record**, so the ARCHIVAX ops (`read` / `classify` / `sweep`) and `unread()`
   read clips too, and their receipts say CLIP / CLIPS (`itemNoun`); `/archivax status` counts pictures
   AND clips and says so. `archivax.clipFrames()` / `archivax.isClip(rec)` are exported and `tools.js`
   ASKS for the frame count rather than keeping a second copy of the clamp.
3. **A CLIP THAT ALREADY CARRIES A READING KEEPS IT.** `lookClip` returns `text: ""` when the clip has a
   `sight` (so `fileReading` writes no sight) while its stills are still read for its `tags` and its
   `bucket` - which is exactly the three of his twenty-five clips that arrived on messages. `opts.overwrite`
   (the `again` scope) is the deliberate exception. `fileReading` also writes `clipFrames`, so the record
   says how many stills the reading was taken across.
4. **A BUCKET IS A PLACE FOR A CLIP TOO.** `media.bucketPath` answers **`/clips/<bucket>`** for a clip
   (measured: `bucketPath({kind:"video",bucket:"night-scene"})` → `/clips/night-scene`; an `attach` →
   `/images/night-scene`), so the classifier files a clip into its bucket and PROPER FOLDERS respects it
   (its `bucketPath || defaultFolder` line needed no change at all).
5. **THE BILL IS IN CALLS AS WELL AS TOKENS.** A clip is `LIA_CLIP_FRAMES` calls, so the scan prints
   `THE VISION CALLS 2,697 CALLS (~570 tokens a still, 6 stills a clip) :: ~1,537,290 tokens` for this
   vault (2,547 pictures x 1 + 25 clips x 6), the run prints it again, and the pace average is kept PER
   CALL so the next estimate stays honest. `LIA_CLIP_FRAMES = 0` leaves clips out of the plan and the
   report says so (`CLIPS LEFT ALONE`), because then a clip has no reading and its own still is a picture
   record the plan already carries. The done-report names `CLIP(S)` read, `VISION CALLS`, `CLIP READINGS
   KEPT` and `CLIPS PART-READ`.
6. **THE OLD BLOCKER IS GONE FROM THE REPORT RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** If a clip cannot be decoded (the tab is
   in the background - the browser refuses, see 1am) the run says so in that exact reason and counts it
   NOT READ, leaving the record exactly as it was found.

**MEASURED (2026-09-24, this vault: 2,600 records, 25 clips, 2,551 pictures).** The frame sampler was
STUBBED for these runs, because the preview tab was in the background and the browser refuses to decode
video while hidden - the stills were drawn from a clip's own first-frame poster, so the model was looking
at the clip's real content, and the decode itself was already measured for real when the sequence road
landed (1am: 6 stills at t = 0/0.7/…/3.5 s, 832x560, 205 ms).
- `archivax.look` on an unread clip: `ok:true, calls:6, clipFrames:6, keptReading:false`, the aggregate
  `opens on: … / then: … / ends on: …`, 8 element tags, bucket `erotic-fantasy-portrait`, `seconds:10.04`
  - and **`wroteNothing:true`** (the read half still writes nothing).
- A temp clip through the WHOLE deck loop (`tools.scan("read","all")` → `tools.run("read","all",{limit:1})`,
  `LIA_CLIP_FRAMES` temporarily 2 to keep the test cheap): `read:1, failed:0, calls:2, clips:1, tags:9,
  buckets:{erotic-fantasy-portrait:1}, filed:1`; the record carried the labelled aggregate as its `sight`,
  `clipFrames:2`, the bucket and its `#tag`, and `folderOf` = `/clips/erotic-fantasy-portrait`; the
  done-report read `RECORDS READ 1 OF 1 … :: 1 OF THEM CLIP`, `VISION CALLS 2`, `FILED 1 INTO THEIR BUCKET
  FOLDER (… a clip into /clips/<bucket>)`.
- The KEPT-READING path on a clip that arrived on a message: `keptReading:true`, `text:""` (so nothing
  would be written over), tags and bucket returned, and its `sight` byte-identical afterwards.
- The `lookable`/`isReadable` boundary is unchanged for everything else: music is still not readable.
- **CLEANUP VERIFIED AFTER EVERY RUN**: vault ids identical (2,600), folder list identical, ARCHIVAX
  journal restored byte-identical, `attach.sampleFrames` and `LIA_CLIP_FRAMES` restored AND asserted
  (`=== realSample` / `=== realFrames`). **His twenty-five clips were never written to.** One 16-file
  parse sweep came back clean, and `backup.staleCheck()` returned `null`.

**INFERRED ONLY - be honest about this.** The clip branch has NOT been run on a real decode today (the tab

## 1aq. PAGINATE THE GALLERY (DONE 2026-09-24)

Patrikios, 2026-09-24: **"PAGINATE the GALLERY"**.

**What it was.** The grid drew EVERY tile of the filtered view in one task: a `<figure>` per record
with a dozen nodes, an object URL made per record, `unseenIds()` scanned per row and again per tile.
On his own vault (2,597 records that day - 1,327 `attach` records, i.e. the pictures he sent or
imported and the music, plus 1,245 upscales and 25 clips) that was 50,115 DOM nodes and 4,960 ms in
`render()` at every open.

**What it is now.** The grid draws ONE PAGE, and a page is a window onto the view and nothing else:
`compute()` still builds the whole filtered/sorted `rows`; `pageRows()` slices what is drawn;
`clampPage()` keeps `state.page` inside `pageCount()`; any change to the VIEW (filter, search, sort,
page size, `open({filter|query|folder|sort})`) goes back to page 1 and any change to the VAULT (a
render landing, an import, a delete, `⟳`/`tools.refreshGallery()`) keeps his page; the grid scrolls to
the top on a page turn and only then. `visibleIds()` is UNCHANGED - the stage/mini box still walk the
whole filtered view, so their arrows cross page boundaries and the bar counts the whole view
(measured: "61 / 2597" from the first tile of page 2). Handing the stage the page instead would ring
the walk back to the top of the page at its 60th picture, a wall where there is no filter.

- **The pager bar** (`.galPager`, markup in `index.html`, painted by `paintPager()`, wired in
  `buildChrome`): `«` · `‹ PREV` · `PAGE [n] OF N` (a typeable jump box) · `NEXT ›` · `»` ·
  `SHOWING 121–180 OF 2597` · `PER PAGE [24|60|120|240|ALL]`. One page of results hides the jumps and
  the box and keeps the "shown" line; no results hides the bar.
- **Per page** is remembered across reloads in `lia_settings / gallery_view` = `{ per }` - the ONE kv
  key the gallery owns (a view preference, not a catalogue). Default 60; ALL is kept because it is what
  the gallery was before, and over 300 rows the status line says it is drawing every tile at once.
- **Keyboard**: ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and PageUp/PageDown turn pages, Home/End are the first and last.
  The listener is registered at the top level of `gallery.js` ON PURPOSE (it must beat the
  ANY-KEY-DISMISSES handler in `main.js`, which closes the gallery on any key), stops
  immediate propagation, and stands aside for the full stage, the mini lightbox and any text field.
- **Words**: `/gallery page <N>` (or go/jump), `/gallery next`, `/gallery prev`, `/gallery per
  <24|60|120|240|all>`; `describe()` (`/gallery stats`) prints how the grid is shown. All of it is a
  view setting - nothing is moved, filed or deleted. `reveal(id)` (also exported) is called by
  `keepsake.openFromHash` so a `#gallery=<id>` link leaves the grid on the page holding the picture.
- **SELECT ALL** is still every matching record across every page, labelled with the number
  (`SELECT ALL 2597`) when that is more than a page; the footer says `3 SELECTED · 1 ON THIS PAGE`
  when some of a selection is elsewhere.

**MEASURED, live, on his vault** (2026-09-24): whole gallery opens in ~200 ms; page of 60 = 60 tiles /
1,310 panel nodes; ALL = 2,597 tiles / 50,115 nodes / 4,960 ms. Next/prev/first/last/jump/Home/End all
move and clamp (page 44 = 17 tiles, `prevDisabled` at 1, `nextDisabled` at 44); the search box and the
sort select reset to page 1; typing in the search box does not close the gallery and Escape still
closes it; a picture landing while he is on page 3 keeps him on page 3 and lands at the top of page 1;
`refresh(false)` (what `tools.js` calls after every job) keeps the page; the mini lightbox and the full
stage both still walk; `/gallery page 5` · `next` · `per 120` · `per 999` (refused, with the choices
printed) all behave, and the archive length was identical before and after the command tests. VISUAL:
the bar sits between the grid and the foot with no overlap at 895x505, and at 390x844 it wraps to two
34px-target rows - a whole-page render was looked at with the vision tool both times (the grid band was
hidden on purpose so no vault content was captured; note the captured `<select>` reads its FIRST option
because a cloned DOM does not carry the `selected` state - the live value was verified as 60).

**INFERRED-only**: the pager's behaviour in an in-app browser with no service worker (unsaved `src/`
files), and the two-row phone bar on a real finger-width device (measured here by resizing a desktop
browser; the 640px block deliberately gives the same 34px target anyway, per the note already in the
CSS).

**Touched**: `src/js/gallery.js` (state + PERS + VIEW_KEY, the ONE PAGE AT A TIME block
`perKnown/perOf/perLabel/pageCount/clampPage/pageRows/pageOfId`, `render`, `paintChrome`,

## 1ar. TALK AND LISTEN, NAMED FROM HIS SIDE OF THE GLASS (DONE 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"TALK and LISTEN need to be re-labeled. It should be TALK the LISTEN. User
pushes to talk then stops. She replies User pushes listen the here her read out loud. Talk, I speak my
message. Listen, she speaks out loud."*

**What was wrong.** The two keys were doing each other's job. `#talkBtn` - labelled **TALK** - spoke
*her* newest reply out loud, and `#listenBtn` - labelled **LISTEN** - opened *his* microphone. A press
on the key that said TALK made her speak; a press on the key that said LISTEN made the terminal listen.
He asked for the names and the jobs to be put right: **TALK = "I speak my message"** (press it, speak,
press it again to stop - the transcript lands in the input box), **LISTEN = "she speaks out loud"**
(the same key stops an audition, because that is her mouth too). The two keys' *positions* are
unchanged (the live microphone, EXECUTE, TALK, LISTEN, the lamp) - only the jobs were swapped, so the
row reads TALK then LISTEN, as his words above say.

**What it is now.** The labels, the element ids, the handlers and the code's own vocabulary all agree,
so no future reader has to hold the inversion in their head: `#talkBtn` → `voice.toggleMic()`,
`#listenBtn` → `voice.toggleSpeak()`, `toggle()` → **`toggleSpeak()`**, `toggleListen()` →
**`toggleMic()`**, `canTalk()` → **`canSpeak()`** (STANDBY or AUDITION) and `canListen()` →
**`canMic()`**; the old names are gone from `window.voice`. Every string followed: the button titles,
the receipts ("THE MICROPHONE IS OPEN :: SPEAK", "PRESS TALK AGAIN", "PRESS LISTEN AGAIN", "OFF ::
LISTEN READS HER NEWEST REPLY OUT LOUD WHEN YOU ASK.", the audition's "PRESS LISTEN TO STOP."), the
state table in the code's THE INTERCOM block, `describe()`, the `holdFrom` channel tag
(`"listen"` → `"talk"`), the `/voice` verbs (`talk` and `mic` both call `toggleMic()`; `listen` calls
`toggleSpeak()`), the `/voice` help line, and the README.

**THE DEFECT THE RENAME CAUGHT, and it is the valuable half.** The one-off microphone was painted
**STOP while being DISABLED**: the gate (`canListen()`, now `canMic()`) read the line's state alone,
and an open session reads `YOUR VOICE` (or `HOLDING`) - states in which the old gate said no. So the
label said "press again to stop" and the press was refused: **press-to-talk could not be stopped from
the key**, and the only exits were the silence hold or typing. That is exactly the half of his sentence
that says *"user pushes to talk then stops"*. `canMic()` now counts a **live one-shot session (or its

## 1as. ONE PAGE OF DOCUMENTS AT A TIME (the DOCS panel, DONE 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"We need pagination in the doc page"*

**What it was.** The LOREPACK DOCS panel (`#lorepackFiles`) writes one `.loreFileRow` per document -
name, four meta fields, and four buttons (`SEE ◆ ↓ ×`) with a listener on each - and it wrote EVERY
one of them. The index held **562 documents** (his own LOREPACK, on this device), so the panel built
**563 children** (562 rows + the sort bar) in a 50vh scroll box every time it was painted, and the
scroll to reach the end of the list was a scroll past every document he owns. `/lore` prints all 562
lines for the same reason.

**What it is now.** The panel draws ONE PAGE, and a page is a window onto the index and nothing else:

- `files` - and with it `memoryFiles()`, `count()`, `files()`, recall, the index, `buildContext()`'s
  canon walk, `describe()`, the boot report - still reads the WHOLE list. Pagination is a way of
  DRAWING it, never a second filter: the pager's line says `SHOWING 51–100 OF 562` and `/lore` counts
  all 562.
- `pageFiles()` is what is drawn (`files.slice((page-1)*per, page*per)`); `clampPage()` keeps
  `settings.page` inside `pageCount()` so a document forgotten, loaded or re-sorted under him can
  never leave the panel on a page that no longer exists.
- Anything that changes the ORDER (the sort bar, `/lore sort`, the canon toggle) returns to **page
  1** - the page he was standing on belonged to the old order, the same rule the gallery follows.
  Anything that only changes the INDEX (loaded / forgotten / restored / re-read) keeps his page,
  clamped. A page turn also scrolls the panel back to its top, and only a page turn.
- **The pager** is the last row of the panel's grid (`pagerRow()` in `lore.js`, built in JS - there is
  NO new markup in `index.html`) and it is `position: sticky; bottom: 0`, so it stays at the foot of
  the panel's own scroll box instead of a hundred documents below what it moves: `«` · `‹ PREV` ·
  `PAGE [3] OF 12` (typeable, Enter jumps) · `NEXT ›` · `»` · `SHOWING 101–150 OF 562` · `PER PAGE
  [50]`. One page of results hides the jump controls and leaves the line and the size.
- **Per page** is his: 25 · 50 · 100 · 200 · ALL, **50** by default, remembered with the sort in kv
  `lore_meta / settings` (`per`, `page`) - the record that already held `maxChars`/`overlap`/`sortKey`,
  so **no new kv key was added**. ALL is kept because it is what the panel did before the pager, and
  it is cheap here (documents, not pictures - see the measurement below).

**TWO DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING.** (1) **No global arrow keys**, unlike the gallery's pager: the gallery
is a modal screen and can own the arrows, while this panel is a dropdown that can stand open while he
types, so ArrowLeft/Right and PageUp/PageDown keep meaning what they mean everywhere else on the page.
The buttons, the jump box and the commands are the controls. (2) **The COREPACK panel
(`#corepackFiles`) is NOT paged** - it lists traits, which are a handful (8 on this device), and a
second copy of the pager in `packs.js` would be a second thing to keep in step for a list that does
not need it. If traits ever number in the hundreds, share `pagerRow()` rather than writing another.

**Words.** `/lore page <N>` (or `go`/`jump`) · `next` · `prev` · `first` · `last` · `per
<25|50|100|200|all>` · `find <NAME>` (go to the page a document is on - what a receipt that names a
document needs to be able to answer) · bare `/lore page` reports. A refusal names the choices
(`A PAGE HOLDS 25, 50, 100, 200, ALL :: 999`). `/lore`'s own listing now ends with the pager state and
the movement line, and `/lore`'s help line and `commands.json` carry the new usage.

**MEASURED, live (2026-09-24).** A page of 50 draws **50 rows / 52 children** in the panel. NEXT →
`SHOWING 51–100`, the box to `2`. The jump box takes `7` on Enter → `SHOWING 301–350`. `PER PAGE 25`
→ 23 pages, 25 rows drawn. `PER 200` → 3 pages. ALL draws all **562** rows in **~55 ms** (a document
list is a document list: that is why ALL stays on the menu). A sort change made while standing on page
4 lands on page 1. `/lore page 5` · `next` · `per 100` · `per 999` (refused, state unchanged) · `find
mythos manifesto` (→ page 12 at 50 a page, page 6 at 100) were all driven through the REAL input box
and EXECUTE, and the archive length was identical before and after (a command prints and returns - no
turn is made, no model is called). `/lore`'s listing tail prints the pager state (567 lines: 562
documents + 5). `window.lore.docsState()` / `docs()` / `pageOfDoc()` are the API.

**VISUAL.** The pager bar was rasterised with the real CSS (`foreignObject` → canvas, the recipe and

**Cleanup asserted.** Nothing in the vault, the archive, the index or her memory was written: the

## 1at. THE THREE DECKS (the shell, named, 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Let's name the 3 major GUI elements: UPPER DECK, MAIN WINDOW, LOWER DECK.
The upper deck and the lower deck can show/hide. For example when in the DOCS viewer, the lower deck
'hides'. When it is closed, the lower deck re-appears."*

**What it was.** The shell had no names and no way to get out of the way. The upper half (the status
line and the tool bar) and the lower half (the input, the controls row and the panels docked in it)
were permanent furniture, and the DOCS viewer - a long list, the thing he actually wanted to read -
shared the screen with the input box he was not using.

**What it is now.** The three parts are named, in the markup (`data-deck` on each) and in the code
(`src/js/decks.js`, `window.decks`):

| deck | element | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| **UPPER DECK** | `#upperDeck` (a new wrapper) | the status line, the tool bar, and the VIEWERS hanging from them |
| **MAIN WINDOW** | `#output` | the conversation. It NEVER closes |
| **LOWER DECK** | `#command-deck` | the input box, the controls row, and the docked panels |

**TWO REASONS A DECK IS DOWN, kept apart on purpose.** (1) **His hand** - the key inside each deck
(`UPPER DECK ▲` / `LOWER DECK ▼`; the chevron points the way the deck will move) or `/deck
upper|main|lower|both on|off|toggle`. That is a preference, remembered in kv `lia_settings / decks`.
(2) **A viewer** - anything marked `data-viewer`. While one is open the LOWER DECK stands down by
itself; closing it brings the deck back to wherever his hand last put it. THAT IS HIS EXAMPLE, MADE A
RULE (in the DOCS viewer the lower deck hides, and when it is closed it re-appears). It is transient
and never written down, and it is read from the DOM with a MutationObserver on the `hidden` attribute
rather than reported by the panels' own modules - so the next viewer behaves this way by being
marked, and nobody has to remember to call `decks.js`.

**THREE THINGS KEEP IT SAFE.** (1) A hidden deck leaves a tab fixed in its own corner (`.deckTab`,
top-right for the upper, bottom-right for the lower, `z-index: 200` - above the decks at 100/101,
below the gallery at 900) - so a deck can never be lost, not even the one the input box lives in.
(2) The page loads where his hand left it: a viewer that was ALREADY open at load does not count as a
reason (`begin()` snapshots those), because a terminal that arrived with the input box already put
away would be a bad first impression; the first move of a viewer starts the rule. (3) `hide("main")`
is refused, in code and in words. While the lower deck is down the DOCS panel takes the room
(`body.lowerDeckOff .lorePanel` 50vh -> 68vh), and the log's bottom reserve needs nothing: forge.js's
`syncDeckSpace()` measures the deck itself, and a hidden deck measures 0.

**MEASURED, live (2026-09-24).** Boot with the DOCS panel left open → BOTH DECKS UP (the preference,
not the viewer); closing it → still up. Opening it by press → the LOWER DECK DOWN, the reason naming
the viewer, the tab appearing, `lowerDeckOff` on the body, the panel 253px -> 343px at 895x505. The
tab pressed while the viewer stayed open → the deck back UP (his press wins over the viewer for that
episode; the next viewer episode asks again). Closing the viewer → the deck where his hand left it.
The upper key → the whole upper deck away (status line, tool bar AND the DOCS panel inside it) with
the top-right tab left; the lower key → `PUT AWAY BY HAND :: /deck lower on BRINGS IT BACK`. At
390x844: the tabs are 34px in their corners, the MAIN WINDOW takes 820 of 844 when both decks are
down, and with a viewer open the panel is 574px (68vh) with 143px of log left. `/deck`,
`/deck lower off|on`, `/deck main off` (refused) and `/deck both off|on` were all driven through the
REAL input box and the archive length was identical before and after (730 -> 730: a command prints
and returns, no turn is made). VISUAL: the keys read `UPPER DECK ▲` (last button of the tool bar) and
`LOWER DECK ▼` (last button of the controls row) and the tabs read `UPPER DECK ▼` / `LOWER DECK ▲`,
nothing clipped at either edge. An INK TEST settled the one thing the rasteriser's reader got wrong:
green pixels for `UPPER DECK ▲` against the same button with the triangle removed (998 vs 808) and
for `LOWER DECK ▼` (1049 vs 820) - both triangles ARE drawn; the vision read of the up one was the
miss, not the glyph.

**DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING.** The main window is not collapsible (the conversation is the point).
`show("both")`/`/deck both` move the two decks that CAN move. No keyboard shortcut: the decks are
chrome, and Ctrl/Alt combinations belong to the browser. The viewer rule is declarative
(`data-viewer`), so a future viewer needs no code.

**TOUCHED:** `index.html` (the `#upperDeck` wrapper, `data-deck` on the three regions, `data-viewer`
on the two DOCS panels, the two deck keys, the two corner tabs, the comment block naming all of it,
and the `decks` entry in the startup-watch module list), `src/js/decks.js` (**NEW**), `src/js/main.js`
(`decks.begin()` after `lore.init()` in `boot()`), `src/js/chat.js` (`deckLine()`, the `/deck`
command, the `/help deck` topic, the shell lines in the roster, `deck` added to the topic list),
`src/commands/commands.json` (**60 -> 61 commands**: the `deck` entry), `src/css/terminal.css`
(`#upperDeck`, `#command-deck[hidden]`, `.deckKey`, `.deckTab`, `body.lowerDeckOff .lorePanel`, the
phone rules for the tabs), `src/README.md` (a new THE THREE DECKS section, the `decks.js` file
bullet, the phone-layout bullet, the command list), and this file. `src/pack/index.html.txt`

the staleness check reads that list, and it said so in words: *"THIS PAGE LOADS 37 SCRIPTS AND THE
COPY NAMES 36 (missing from the copy: js/decks.js)"*), so `staleCheck()` is `null` again. `main.pjs`
untouched. Nothing was saved or published.

**Cleanup asserted.** The kv key this feature owns (`lia_settings / decks`) was DELETED again after

## 1au. THE END OF YOUR TURN, AND HERS (the comms fix, 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"i can't stand this comms thing. it cuts off, sends before I am even done and
she doesn't wait there turn I have had it , Fix that shit now."*

**What it was.** Rule 1 of THE HOLD (2026-09-21) was a single number: 2000ms of quiet measured from
the last result the recogniser handed over, with a 2667ms variant while the tail was still interim.
A breath inside a sentence arrives as a FINAL result exactly like the end of one, so two seconds of
*thinking* read as the end of his turn, she took the floor, the ears shut, and the rest of his
sentence was cut off mid-air - all three of his complaints were one defect. MEASURED before touching
anything, with a stubbed `SpeechRecognition` and a stubbed `window.send` (no real microphone, no real
turn): a single final result reading "i want to tell you a story about" was DELIVERED 2000ms later
(`prematureSend: 1`), with the sentence stopping on "about".

**What it is now.** Four changes, all in `src/js/voice.js`:

- **THE WAIT IS ADAPTIVE (`holdQuietMs()`).** `holdMs` (3500 now, and only ever the FLOOR of the wait -
  /voice hold still tunes it, 400-8000) plus the uncommitted tail as before, plus two stretches: the
  clause stops on a word a sentence does not end on (`looksUnfinished()` against a `DANGLING` list -
  "…a story about" is a pause by construction), and the clause is long (+200ms per six words, up to
  +1200ms). Everything is capped at `TURN_MAX` (9000ms). Every stretch only ever ADDS silence to a wait
  that silence already governs, and any word of his resets the clock - so a wrong guess costs patience
  and never a word.
- **THE MIGRATION (`TURN_VERSION`).** His device held rule 1's 2000 in kv `lia_settings / voice`, which
  would have overridden the new default. On load, a record with no `turn` stamp whose `holdMs` is 2000
  (i.e. the shipped default, never moved by hand) is lifted to 3500; the stamp is written on the next
  save. A hand-moved number is left alone. His record still reads 2000 ON DISK after testing - the
  migration is runtime until he changes a voice setting, which is deliberate: nothing of his was
  written.
- **THE END IS VISIBLE AND BEATABLE.** Inside the last `SEND_GRACE` (900ms) `holdTick` prints
  `VOICE :: YOUR TURN :: 0.8S TO GO - KEEP TALKING AND IT WAITS`, once per clause (`holdCounted`). The
  end of his turn is now something he can see coming and talk over.
- **HE CAN END IT HIMSELF, AND ENDING IT NEVER WAITS.** In the live channel, pressing the microphone
  while something is held TAKES the hold now (`toggleLive()`; the channel stays open - closing is the
  next press, and `stopLive()` takes the hold too); a one-shot session stopped by his own press takes
  it in `onend` (`if (stopped) takeHold()`). "Press to talk, press again to stop" now means it.
- **SHE WAITS HER TURN (`drainLive()`).** A live reply used to be spoken the instant it arrived, which
  shut the ears and cut him off. Now it goes into `liveQueue` and `drainLive()` speaks it only when the
  room is quiet (nothing held, nothing heard for `min(1200, holdMs)`), in order, one at a time, bounded
  by `TURN_WAIT_MAX` (9000ms) so a reply is never held forever. A reply arriving while she speaks is
  spoken after, not instead.

**MEASURED, live (2026-09-24), stubbed recogniser + stubbed `window.send` + stubbed `speechSynthesis`
and `document.hidden` forced visible (the preview iframe was hidden, which stops the ticker by
design): (1) "i want to tell you a story about" - NO send at 3.2s (was 1 before), quiet 5467ms, sent
by 7s; (2) a second clause resumed after 3.2s of silence - no send on the resume, one send after the
full wait; (3) the microphone key with words held - sent immediately, channel still open; (4) her
reply queued while he was still talking - `queued: 1`, nothing spoken for 1.4s, then spoken the moment
the hold was taken and the queue emptied; (5) the TALK key pressed again - the turn sent at once
(503ms, not 3500ms). Two countdown lines were printed across the run. AFTER: kv `voice` record
byte-for-byte as before (`holdMs: 2000`, no `turn`), the archive untouched by the tests (every send
was stubbed), no live channel and no microphone left open, `speechSynthesis` (28 voices),
`SpeechRecognition`, `window.send`, `window.print`, `document.hidden` and
`document.visibilityState` all restored to their own descriptors, `staleCheck()` null.

**A TRAP WORTH KEEPING.** `window.speechSynthesis` is an OWN ACCESSOR on the window: stubbing it with
`Object.defineProperty` DESTROYS the real one, and `delete` does not bring it back (the chain holds
nothing behind it) - a reload is the only cure, which is how it was recovered. Save and restore the
DESCRIPTOR (`Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`), never the value. `window.print` is non-configurable,
so it can only be stubbed by assignment.

**DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING.** The stretches never shorten a wait and never touch a word he said. The
one-shot path and the live path share ONE detector (`holdHeard`/`holdTick`/`holdQuietMs`), so they
cannot drift apart. The queue is bounded at four replies and drains oldest-first. `/voice stop` still
silences her at once; `/voice live off` takes a held clause the same way the key does.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/voice.js` (the state block: `holdMs` 3500, `TURN_MAX`, `TURN_WAIT_MAX`,
`SEND_GRACE`, `TURN_VERSION`, `heardAt`, `holdCounted`, `DANGLING`, `liveQueue`/`liveDraining`;
`load()`'s migration and `save()`'s `turn` stamp; `looksUnfinished()`; the rewritten `holdQuietMs()`;
`holdHeard()`/`clearHold()`; `holdTick()`'s countdown; `takeHold()` unchanged; `startListen()`'s
`onend`; `drainLive()` + `onReply()`'s live branch; `toggleLive()`; `stopLive()`; `startLive()`'s queue
reset; `paintHold()`'s title; `state()` (`turn`, `heardAgo`, `queued`); `describe()`'s END OF YOUR TURN;
the `/voice hold` and `/voice tail` help; the file header's TALK line), `src/js/chat.js` (the
`/voice hold` help line), `src/commands/commands.json` (the `voice` description - still 61 commands,
JSON re-validated), `src/README.md` (THE HOLD rewritten and extended with A FLAT PAUSE WAS NOT THE
END OF A TURN / THE END IS VISIBLE / SHE WAITS HER TURN, the `voice.js` file bullet, the INTERCOM
HOLDING row and a new bullet for the key as his own word), and this file. `index.html` and
`main.pjs` untouched, so `src/pack/index.html.txt` is still byte-exact and `staleCheck()` stays null.
Nothing was saved or published.


## 1av. THE RTFM (the manual, and the measured command list, 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Let's make an RTFM doc in markdown for all /slash commands as a cheetsheet.
Let me add documents there as well I have list of commands we can refactor or use here directly."*

**WHAT WAS READ INTO THAT, and the choice made:** an RTFM (a markdown cheatsheet of every slash
command) plus a PLACE TO ADD MORE DOCUMENTS - so it is built as a PACK, the same shape as the
LOREPACK: a folder of markdown files, a manifest, and a reader. The second half of his sentence
("I have list of commands we can refactor or use here directly") is handed a landing place: every
command in `src/commands/commands.json` now carries a one-line `short` (written for this, derived
from each command's full `desc`), which IS the cheatsheet line - so a list of his can be dropped
straight into those fields, or refactored, without touching anything else. He has not sent the list
yet; when he does, it goes into `short`.

**WHAT IT IS.** `src/rtfm/` - the manual, kept as documents, read with `/rtfm`:

- `src/rtfm/rtfm.json` - the manifest (id, file, title, tags, desc, and `generated`/`from`).
- `src/rtfm/README.md` - the pack's recipe: what it is, how to add a document, how the documents are
  read.
- `src/rtfm/commands.md` - **THE CHEATSHEET, GENERATED** from `src/commands/commands.json`.
- `src/rtfm/turn.md` - hand-written: **YOUR TURN AND HERS**, the 2026-09-24 comms fix in his own
  language (the wait, the three stretches, the countdown, the key, her queue, and the two numbers he
  can move). It is also the proof that a hand-written document and a generated one live side by side.
- `src/js/rtfm.js` - the reader (`window.rtfm`): the manifest, the documents, the terminal markdown
  renderer (`toTerminal()`), the command page (`commandPage()`), the generator
  (`cheatsheetMarkdown()`) and the staleness check.

**FOR HIM, NOT FOR HER.** The LOREPACK is what she remembers; the RTFM is the manual for the machine.
Nothing in `src/rtfm/` is indexed, retrieved, recalled or handed to her on a turn, and nothing in it
writes to her memory. It is PUBLIC and ships, so nothing private goes in it. That rule is written in
the pack's README, in `rtfm.js`'s header, and in `/rtfm about`.

**THE CHEATSHEET IS GENERATED, SO IT CANNOT DRIFT.** `src/rtfm/commands.md` is rendered from the
command list - the one place a command is declared - by `cheatsheetMarkdown()` in `rtfm.js`.
`/rtfm cheatsheet` renders it FRESH from the live list and prints that (the terminal never shows a
stale cheatsheet); `/rtfm check` fetches the shipped copy and compares it BYTE FOR BYTE against that
same render, naming the first line that differs; `/rtfm export` downloads a fresh copy to drop back
in. This is `src/pack/`'s pattern - a generated copy plus a check that says when it has fallen
behind - applied to a document instead of a root file. A generated document that HAS fallen behind
says so in its own header when printed, rather than being shown as current.

**THE COMMAND LIST WAS MEASURED.** A roster cannot be a wall, and it was one: `listText()` printed
`usage.padEnd(32)` + the WHOLE `desc`, and `desc` is often a paragraph (the longest is 3421
characters), so `/commands` was ~40KB of essays. Every entry now carries a `short` - one line,
written by hand for each of the 62 commands - and `listText()` prints `usage` + `short`, with the
gloss on its own indented line when the usage itself is long. `/commands` is now **99 lines /
7,300 bytes**. `desc` is untouched and is still what SHE is told (`cmd.block()`) - she needs the
meaning, not the gloss. Commands: **61 -> 62** (the `rtfm` entry).

**VERBS.** `/rtfm` (bare, `list`) the index and the verbs · `/rtfm <DOC>` a document · `/rtfm
<COMMAND>` one command's page (usage, kind, the whole description, read from the live list) · `/rtfm
cheatsheet` the fresh render · `/rtfm check` · `/rtfm export [DOC]` · `/rtfm about` the recipe ·
`/rtfm doc <NAME>` / `/rtfm cmd <NAME>` to disambiguate. Aliases: `/man`, `/cheat`,
`/cheatsheet`. A name is tried as a COMMAND first, then as a document; an unknown word is refused
with the nearest command and the nearest document (the same small-edit-distance idea the unknown
slash command uses in `chat.js`). `rtfm` is in `HELP_TOPICS` and `/help rtfm` prints the summary.

**MEASURED, live (2026-09-24).** `__bootIssues === []`, `staleCheck() === null`, 62 commands, the
manifest read at boot (`main.js` calls `rtfm.load()` right after `cmd.load()`), `/rtfm` lists **2
documents**, and every verb was driven through the REAL input box with `window.print` stubbed (so
nothing was written into his log) and the archive length identical before and after (805 -> 805 - a
command prints and returns, no turn is made): `/rtfm` -> the index, `/rtfm turn` -> YOUR TURN AND
HERS, `/rtfm check` -> `THE SHIPPED COPY MATCHES THE LIVE LIST :: src/rtfm/commands.md IS UP TO DATE
(8305 BYTES, 62 COMMANDS, 156 LINES)`, `/help rtfm` -> the topic, `/commands` -> the compact roster.
The staleness check was proved by MUTATING the live list (one command's `short`) and reading the
answer - `copy 8305 BYTES, NOW 8283 BYTES, first difference at line 11` - and then restored to clean.
The terminal renderer was checked on both shapes: the cheatsheet's tables come out as aligned columns
(the header rule now that the last column's width is measured rather than left at zero - caught by
reading the first render), and `turn.md` renders once, not twice (a document's own first heading is
dropped because the page already carries the title from the manifest).

**A NOTE FOR WHOEVER ADDS A COMMAND.** It wants a `short`. The list works without one (the roster
and the cheatsheet fall back to the description's first sentence), but the line is the point. And the
generated copy has to be refreshed after: `/rtfm check` says so, `/rtfm export` produces the file,
and it goes back at `src/rtfm/commands.md`.
