## 1aw. THE RTFM WRITES BACK (the editor, 2026-09-24)

**His word, verbatim:** *"I want to author documents from inside the terminal without touching the
files panel. Build it."* - asked right after `/rtfm` shipped, so this is 1av continued: the manual
was readable, and now it is WRITABLE from where it is read.

**WHAT IT IS.** `/rtfm new [NAME] [:: TITLE]` and `/rtfm edit <DOC>` open **THE RTFM EDITOR** over the
terminal - `src/js/rtfm-edit.js` (`window.rtfmEditor`), the markup declared in `index.html` as
`#rtfmEditor` (`z-index` 960: over the gallery's 900 and the mini box's 950, under the full stage's
1000), the styles at the end of `src/css/terminal.css`. It is a monospace markdown box with four
fields (NAME / TITLE / TAGS / SAYS - the one-line gloss) and a **LIVE PREVIEW PANE built from
`rtfm.markdown()`**, the same renderer that prints a page, so the pane is not an impression of the
page: it IS the page. `Ctrl+S` saves, `Esc` closes (a second press when there is unsaved work),
`Tab` indents two spaces rather than leaving the box, and the two destructive buttons **arm** first and
say what they will do (DELETE on a page of his own, REVERT on a rewrite of a shipped one).

**WHERE IT SAVES, AND WHY NOT IN src/.** A page written here is kept in THIS BROWSER - kv
`lia_settings` / **`rtfm_local`** - and never in `src/`: nothing on the page can write a file into
the generator, and a page he writes is his before it is anybody's. `/rtfm export <NAME>` hands it over
as markdown (the same Blob-and-anchor road `/backup` uses), and dropping that file in `src/rtfm/`
plus a manifest line is what makes it travel. One key holds them all,
`{ id: { title, tags, desc, body, shadows, savedAt } }`, written through `writeLocal()` - and when the
last page goes, the KEY goes with it rather than leaving an empty husk in his kv.

**A SHIPPED PAGE IS SHADOWED, NEVER ALTERED.** `merge()` lays `rtfm_local` OVER the shipped manifest:
a page saved under a shipped document's name REPLACES that entry (`/rtfm <DOC>` then prints his copy,
and the header says `SHIPPED - THIS COPY OF IT IS YOURS`), while the file in `src/rtfm/` is untouched.
`/rtfm rm <DOC> confirm` - or REVERT in the editor - drops his copy and puts the shipped file back in
force. That is exactly the arrangement `roles.js` uses for an edited role layer (`role_text` over
`src/roles/`), and it is the reason the answer is \"shadow\" rather than \"edit in place\": the shipped
thing stays the truth and what he makes of it sits on top. A **generated** page may not be written at
all - `/rtfm edit commands` and `/rtfm add commands ...` are refused, because the command list is the
truth and the cheatsheet is a copy of it.

**THE VERBS ADDED** (the old ones untouched): `new [NAME] [:: TITLE]` · `edit <DOC>` (aliases
`open`, `rewrite`) · `add <DOC> <TEXT>` (appends a line, no editor, saved at once - a quick note
does not need the whole box) · `mine` · `rm <DOC> [confirm]` (ask first, and a page of his own is
\"the whole of it\" while a rewrite says the shipped file comes back) · `revert <DOC> confirm`. The
index now marks every page `(GENERATED)` / `(WRITTEN BY YOU HERE)` / `(SHIPPED - REWRITTEN BY YOU
HERE)` and carries a **WRITING ONE HERE** block; `/rtfm about` got a \"WRITING ONE FROM HERE\"
section; the `rtfm` command entry in `commands.json` was rewritten (usage, `short`, and the long
`desc` she is told) and `src/rtfm/commands.md` regenerated from it: **8,305 -> 8,367 bytes**, 62
commands, 156 lines, `/rtfm check` clean.

**TWO BUGS FOUND WHILE TESTING THIS, both in code that was already shipped:**
1. `run()` handed `chat.js` the editor's receipt as a **Promise** instead of a string
   (`text: window.rtfmEditor.openEdit(...)` without `await`), so `/rtfm edit` would have printed
   `[object Promise]` in the log. Caught by reading `instanceof Promise` on the returned object.
2. **`toTerminal()`'s table() over-indented every row's first line.** It called
   `wrap(text, MAX, indent)` for the last column - which indents EVERY line including the first - and
   then printed that first line after the other columns, shoving each row right by the width of the
   columns in front of it and leaving the rows out of step with the rule under the header. It is a
   pre-existing bug (the cheatsheet had it before this task); the fix is to wrap with no indent and
   add the continuation indent only to lines after the first. Tables are now genuinely aligned
   (`/help       the roster of everything that can be typed` under a 7-dash rule). Nothing renders
   differently in the GENERATED markdown - only in what is printed.

**MEASURED, live (2026-09-24).** `__bootIssues === []` throughout. Driven through `window.rtfm.run()`
with the editor's real DOM (the same path `chat.js` takes) and `HTMLAnchorElement.prototype.click`
stubbed for the two exports, so nothing landed in his Downloads and nothing was sent to any model:
`/rtfm new test-page :: A TEST PAGE` opened the editor on `untitled`-style fields; a body written into
it and SAVE clicked -> `SAVED :: test-page :: 121 CHARACTERS, 13 LINES :: KEPT IN THIS BROWSER`, the
kv record read back whole (title, tags `[test, ritual]`, desc, body, `shadows: ""`), the head switching
to `(YOURS, ON THIS DEVICE)` and DELETE appearing. It SURVIVED A RELOAD (`status` ->
`2 DOCUMENTS ... :: 1 WRITTEN HERE`), `/rtfm test-page` printed it with the `KEPT :: THIS DEVICE ONLY`
header, `/rtfm add test-page SECOND LINE ...` appended and reported `151 IN ALL, 14 LINES`. The
SHADOW round-trip was walked on `turn`: `/rtfm edit turn` -> the shipped 4,453 bytes with the head
`(SHIPPED)`, a line added and saved -> `YOUR COPY SHADOWS src/rtfm/turn.md`, `/rtfm turn` printing his
copy, REVERT armed twice -> `REVERTED :: src/rtfm/turn.md IS IN FORCE AGAIN HERE` with the fields
reloaded from the shipped file and `revertHidden` back to true. CANCEL disarmed-first
(`UNSAVED WORK :: PRESS CANCEL AGAIN ...`), then closed and the discarded text was PROVED absent.
DELETE armed and dropped. The refusal paths all answered in his language: `/rtfm edit commands`,
`/rtfm add commands ...`, `/rtfm new turn` (already exists, here is how to rewrite it), `/rtfm rm
commands`, `/rtfm revert test-page` (a page of his own has no shipped file to put back). The
NEW-PAGE-TAKES-A-SHIPPED-NAME guard armed once before shadowing. Exports: `turn.md` (4,453 bytes) and
`commands.md` (8,367 bytes) both produced the right filenames. **Nothing of his was written and
nothing of his was left behind: `rtfm_local` was DELETED at the end and `keys()` proved it (back to the
31 it started with), the editor was left closed, and no turn was ever sent** (the archive length was
not touched by any of this - every verb prints and returns, and `save()` in kv is not her memory).

**THE UNSAVED DRAFT (added at the end of the same sitting).** An editor that can be reloaded at any
moment is an editor that eats writing: this page is reloaded by the terminal's own machinery (every
edit by the agent re-renders it) and a phone throws a backgrounded tab away, so twenty minutes of
typing could vanish with no warning. What is typed but NOT saved is therefore kept as a DRAFT in kv,
ONE KEY PER PAGE (`lia_settings` / `rtfm_draft_<NAME>`) - per page rather than one blob so a write
while typing touches only the page being typed, and so switching pages can never take another page's
draft with it. A draft is NOT the page: it never touches `rtfm_local`, never shadows anything, never
changes what `/rtfm <DOC>` prints, and nothing but the editor can see it. Opening a page that has a
draft puts the draft back in the fields and says so in the receipt and in the note, with the age and
with \"this is the only copy of it\"; SAVE turns it into the page (and clears the draft, including the
one under the name it was opened under if it was renamed); closing with CANCEL twice, REVERT, or DELETE
throws it away - which is what being asked twice is for. A draft that merely echoes the page it was
opened from is cleared silently. The oldest are swept away past 20 (`draftSweep()`), and `/rtfm mine`
lists the drafts beside the saved pages with the command that puts each one back (`rtfmEditor.drafts()`
is what answers it - the editor is the only thing that knows about them). The snapshot subtlety: the
page's snapshot is taken BEFORE a draft is put back, so restored work reports UNSAVED and closing asks
about it - getting that wrong (taking the snapshot after the restore) is what made the first test's
close skip the confirmation and leave the draft stranded, and it was caught by reading the state line
and the kv keys, not by looking at the screen.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/rtfm.js` (the local store: `store/slug/readLocal/writeLocal/save/drop/merge/
findShipped/read`, `load()` split into `loadShipped()` + the kv read, the header/footer of a page
written here, the index and `about` text, `mineText()`, `dropRefusal()`, the new verbs, the export
branch for a page with no file, `describe()`/`status()`, the new exports, and the table() indent
fix), plus the DRAFT layer in `rtfm.js` (`/rtfm mine` lists them; `rtfmEditor.drafts()` answers), `src/js/rtfm-edit.js` (**NEW, incl. the unsaved draft**), `index.html` (**the editor's markup + its script tag + its
entry in the startup-watch list**), `src/css/terminal.css` (**+4,497 bytes at the end: `#rtfmEditor`
and its narrow-screen block**), `src/commands/commands.json` (the `rtfm` entry: usage, `short`,

A PAGE FROM THE TERMINAL section and the new verbs in the reading block**), `src/js/chat.js` (`/help

## 1ax. THE SYNC (the conversation out of the browser, 2026-09-24)

Patrikios, 2026-09-24: *"Synch Versions to latest chat backups stored in G: Drive."* Built the whole
lane: `src/js/sync.js` (`window.sync`), the **SYNC ⇅ button** on the lorebar, `#syncPanel`, the hidden
folder input `#syncDirInput`, `/sync` and its verbs, and the CSS block at the end of
`src/css/terminal.css`. The archive (`kv: sacred_archive / master_log`) is the newest 1000 turns and
lives in this browser only; `/backup` carries the code and not one word of it. The sync reads the
folder his chat backups are kept in, lists every version in it, TAKES THE NEWEST ONE IN on its own
(pick -> look -> take), and writes the archive out as `lia-terminal-archive.json` plus ONE DATED COPY
A DAY. The merge only ADDS: a turn it lacks comes in, a turn it holds is kept exactly as it is, and
the backup may only fill what is missing on it. Nothing is ever uploaded; nothing is ever deleted.

**THE PICKER IS REFUSED IN THIS FRAME, MEASURED.** `showDirectoryPicker` throws *"SecurityError:
Cross origin sub frames aren't allowed to show a file picker"* in the editor's preview. So the preview
gets PICK (a hidden directory input) and DROP (webkitGetAsEntry recursion), and `up` goes out through
the browser's own download; a TOP-LEVEL tab may CONNECT and keep the handle (IndexedDB `lia_sync` /
`handles` / `dir`), and then `up` writes straight into G:. `window.sync.attach(handle)` is
session-only and exists so a page that already holds a handle - or a test with a mock folder - can
hand one over; that is how the WRITE path was exercised with no human at a dialog.

**FIVE BUGS, ALL FOUND BY READING A REAL FILE BACK:**

- `chat.js`'s `exportArchive` dropped HER WORDS for every `kind:"create"` / `silent` entry (8 turns
  absent from the readable backup). FIXED: her words are written as a `LIA ID:` line after the
  creation line.
- The export's `[EDITED ON THIS DEVICE AFTER THE FACT: <stamp>]` suffix is stripped on the way back,
  restoring `edited` / `editedAt`.
- Splitting the export on a bare `---` cut turns in half (7 lost their tail, 11 vanished entirely on
  the archive of 2026-09-24). The reader is LINE BY LINE now, and `---` separates only when the next
  non-blank line begins a record.
- The merge matched on the exact millisecond, which a text export cannot carry, so 995 "new" turns
  pushed 995 of his own out through the cap. Now: an exact twin first, then within 1000 ms
  (`TOLERANCE`), marking used entries.
- THE ONE THAT MATTERED: `cleanEntry` copied turns through a WHITELIST of the fields it believed the
  archive held, so a sync wrote back turns with `checkin` (8) and `importedFresh` (817) silently gone
  and `kind` (786) rewritten - measured 2026-09-24 against a pre-sync snapshot, and his archive was
  repaired from it. **A turn is copied WHOLE now** (every own enumerable key, only `ts`/`st`
  normalised). Do not put a field list back here.

**VERIFIED LIVE:** the readable export round-trips 1000/1000 with zero field mismatches and merges as
a no-op; a pull of the JSON backup is a no-op with no key loss through kv; the write path wrote both
files into a mock folder and did NOT duplicate the dated one on a second run; `/sync status|versions`
and an unknown verb come back through the real input box without sending a model turn; the archive's
key set and identity string are unchanged by all of it; the panel renders correctly at 855px and wraps
to thumb-sized (34px) buttons at 390px with no clipping (the CONNECT button hides itself while a
handle is in hand - 6 buttons at rest, 5 when connected). **Cleanup proved:** the two test stashes are
deleted, `lia_settings` is back to its own 32 keys, and the `sync` record was put back to its original
contents - the one `runs` entry it started with, no test runs, no mock `dirName` / `lookedAt` /
`versions` / `fileId`. (An empty `clientId` cannot stay empty: `wire()` calls `paint()` at boot and
`loadRec()` mints one, which is the design - the id is this device's name, minted once and stamped
into every backup.)

**STILL OPEN FOR THE NEXT AGENT:** (a) `/sync connect` has never been run against a real G: folder in
a top-level tab - the one road no test here can reach is the handle kept across a reload and
re-granted. (b) A readable-export pull cannot rebuild a render's recipe (prose there, not a record),
so the render book keeps only what the JSON carries. (c) The 1000-turn cap means merging a much older
backup keeps the newest 1000 and says so - the file on disk holds the whole history, the browser does
not. (d) The platform's `snapshot.js` capture helper HANGS on this page (its fetch is fine - 200, 10,211
bytes - but `capture()` never returns, even on a one-line span), so screenshots here came from
`@zumer/snapdom` off esm.sh instead; `html-to-image` renders this page's panels nearly empty and must
not be trusted.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/sync.js` (**NEW**), `index.html` (the button, the panel, the hidden input, the

## 1az. THE SECOND ASK — A LOAD THAT LOSES A FILE NOW HEALS ITSELF (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**WHAT WAS WRONG.** The platform's editor preview serves unsaved `src/` files through a service worker
that races the first load of the page, and the race is lost in a SUFFIX: on a bad load the last handful
of scripts the markup asks for (measured: 2 of 5 loads, 7, 10 and 17 files on different loads) fail with
"SCRIPT DID NOT LOAD" (and the same path again as a "STYLESHEET DID NOT LOAD", the platform's own
`<link rel=preload as=script>` for it). Three separate wounds, all of them silent:

1. **A module that never ran.** `window.draft` undefined, `window.decks` undefined - the terminal came
   up without that panel and said nothing.
2. **A module that ran and THREW.** `main.js:235` binds `cpClose` to forge.js's `closeForge`; if
   forge.js lost the race the throw ended `main.js` where it stood, so every control wired after it
   was dead AND `setTimeout(boot, 1500)` at the end of the file never ran - no archive replay, no
   save-state line, `/help` empty. The observer saw exactly this:
   `ERROR :: Uncaught ReferenceError: closeForge is not defined [main.js:235]` with `cmd.count() === 0`.
3. **A data file that never arrived.** `commands.js` reads `src/commands/commands.json` with a one-shot
   `fetch`; a lost response left a terminal that had booted with an empty command list (`cmd 0`) and a
   console warning - the `studio/*.json` case already recorded in the shot-list build notes ("reads
   3.3 KB on a load where `src/studio/*.json` failed to fetch") is the same shape.

**WHAT WAS BUILT** (`index.html`, THE STARTUP WATCH, + `src/js/main.js`, + `src/js/backup.js`):

- **THE SETTLE TRACKER.** Every `<script src>` tag is counted as the page inserts it (initial scan +
  `MutationObserver`), and the count only reaches zero when each has fired load OR error. The audit
  waits for that before it decides anything, so a file that is still on its way can never be mistaken
  for a lost one - which is what makes the second ask safe. The watch's own re-asks are tagged
  `data-again` and are never counted.
- **THE SECOND ASK (scripts).** Any module still not on `window` once everything has settled is fetched
  again in MODULES order (`?again=<ms>`, `async=false`, each awaited before the next), twice, and only
  what fails both times raises `#bootFail`. What was recovered lands in `window.__bootHealed`.
- **THE SECOND ASK (data).** A `fetch` wrapper installed before every module: a `GET` whose URL is a
  `src/` path that comes back `!ok` or throws is retried once, 350 ms later, cache-busted. Everything
  else - other paths, other methods, and the response itself - is passed through untouched.
- **THE WIRING SURVIVES THE LOSS** (`main.js`). The forge's controls (`openForge`, `closeForge`,
  `createImages`, `splitPasted`, `randomSeed`, `saveForge`, `syncDeckSpace` - all forge.js) moved into
  `wireForge()`, which polls for the module (400 ms × 60) and then binds; the bare `syncDeckSpace()`
  calls (in `syncKeyboard` and in `boot`) and the `closeForge()` in the Escape chain are guarded with
  `typeof ... === "function"`, the guard the rest of the terminal already uses (instr.js:583,
  keys.js:574, tools.js:1539, sync.js:853, sync-cloud.js:300). `main.js` can no longer end early, so
  `boot()` always runs.
- **SAID ONCE, IN BACKSTAGE.** When anything was recovered, `boot()` says so in the veil's lane
  ("THE FILE STORAGE LOST N SOURCE FILES ON THIS LOAD :: ... - THE FIRST-LOAD RACE, NOT A FAULT HERE")
  and `/backup diag` prints the same list under
  "SOURCE FILES THAT DID NOT ARRIVE ON THIS LOAD AND WERE ASKED FOR AGAIN". A healed load is otherwise
  invisible, deliberately: nothing is missing by the time boot runs.

**MEASURED, live (5 reloads, read 16 s after each load).** Every load: all 20 probed globals present,
`cmd.count() === 65`, no `#bootFail`, the archive replay line present (so `boot()` ran to the end), and
a full forge open/close cycle by click (`#createPanel.hidden` true → false → true). Two of the five
loads lost files (chat.js + editlog.js; decks.js + draft.js) and both were recovered automatically with
no banner and no visible fault. A deliberately bogus MODULES entry proves the fallback: exactly two
attempts (`__bootIssues` shows `?again=` twice), then the banner naming it, with the terminal still
whole around it. A deliberate `fetch("src/js/no-such-file-here.js")` shows the same for data: two
resource entries, the original 404 and the cache-busted retry, the 404 body being
`src file "..." was deleted (pending)`. `staleCheck() === null` after every edit (the pack copy is in
sync), `__bootIssues === []` on a clean load.

**STILL OPEN.** (a) The race itself is the platform's - filed as bug **10203516** and not ours to fix;
this makes the terminal indifferent to it rather than silent about it. (b) The audit can still be beaten
by a module that runs, throws, and leaves its global set (a "half-run" file) - nothing re-runs it, by
design, because re-running would bind every listener twice; the `typeof` guards above are the answer to
the only such call site found, and the rule for new code is the same guard. (c) An auto-reload-on-heal
was considered and rejected: it would re-run everything cleanly but flash the whole terminal on 40% of
editor loads, and the second ask already lands the files. (d) The same race still costs one wasted
request per lost file per load, which is the price of not trusting the first answer.

**TOUCHED (this build):** `index.html` (the settle tracker, the script second ask, the `fetch` second
ask, the banner's own wording, the audit's schedule), `src/js/main.js` (`wireForge()`, two guards, the
backstage line in `boot()`), `src/js/backup.js` (`diag()` prints `window.__bootHealed`),
`src/pack/index.html.txt` (regenerated), `src/README.md`, and this file. Nothing was saved or published.

## 1ba. THE CHRONICLE - THE RECORD OF THE MAKING (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**WHAT HE SAID.** In the middle of the boot-race session (1az) he asked whether to reload, said he
would lose "our conversation here", and offered to save the whole chat log - then, when the answer came
back (two lanes, the public caveat, and the fact that the agent cannot reach the editor chat from
inside the page), he gave the word: *"However it works, LORE as CODE in interesting. It has all of your
thought processes. You know more or less how we do stuff. Scaffold src/chronicle/."*

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** A new lane, and the smallest machinery that makes it a lane rather than a folder:

- **`src/chronicle/`** - `README.md` (what it is, the shape of an entry, the rules), `chronicle.json`
  (the manifest, chronological: id, date, file, title, tags, desc), and the entries themselves, one
  markdown file per session named `<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`. The first three: THE MERGE (2026-09-25,
  recovered from this file's own 1ay, because the folder did not exist yet), THE SECOND ASK (1az), and
  THE CHRONICLE itself (the founding, with the SAVE still open in it).
- **`src/js/chronicle.js`** (`window.chronicle`) - the reader: `/chronicle` (the index newest-first),
  `/chronicle <ENTRY>` (by id, file name, date, or number in the index), `newest`, `about` (the recipe
  from the folder's own README), `reload`, `status`. Entries print through **`rtfm.markdown()`** - the
  same renderer the manual uses - so both document sets read identically; the first heading of an entry
  is dropped because the header already carries the title from the manifest.
- **The route and the roster** - a dispatch block in `chat.js` beside the `/rtfm` one, a `chronicle`
  command in `src/commands/commands.json` (66 commands, so `/help`, the SYSTEM panel and her own
  catalogue know it), a line in the `/help` roster, a `/help chronicle` area, and `chronicle` in
  `HELP_TOPICS`.

**WHAT WAS THOUGHT (and why it is not the LOREPACK).** The LOREPACK was the obvious mechanism and the
wrong container: it is HERS - indexed, retrieved on every message she answers, and handed to her. Put
the engineering conversations there and she would be given "the fetch wrapper is installed before any
module runs" as though it were a memory, on a turn about something else entirely. So the lanes are now
named and separated, and the separation is the first rule written in the folder:

| where | whose | what it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/lorepack/` | **hers** | what she remembers - indexed, retrieved, handed to her |
| `src/rtfm/` | **his** | the manual for the machine: how to USE the terminal |
| `README.md`, `TODO.md` | **the state** | what the code does now, what each build changed |
| `src/chronicle/` | **the making** | how it got here: the sessions, the reasoning, the dead ends |

*A manual is not a memory and a changelog is not a session.* **The raw chat logs are deliberately NOT
in the folder** (he offered; the answer is the write-up, not the transcript) - everything under `src/`
is public and ships with the generator, so a private note belongs in kv or on his machine, and a raw
log enters the build only if he asks for it, as its own file with its own entry line. **The road to
her, if a session should ever be hers**, is the LOREPACK: copy the entry into `src/lorepack/` and list
it in `lorepack.json` - and remember that `"foundational": true` puts all of it in front of her on
every turn. **Nothing in the folder is writable from the terminal, on purpose** (unlike the RTFM, which
can be written from the page): a session is written up by the agent that lived it, which is why the
folder's README ends with an instruction to the next agent rather than a promise of automation.

**MEASURED.** The build was verified live: `cmd.count() === 66`, `chronicle` on `window`, the index,
one entry by id, one by number, one by date, `newest` and `about` all printing, and `/chronicle`,
`/help chronicle` and `/chronicle nosuchthing` typed into the terminal itself (all SYSTEM lines - no
turn sent, nothing in the archive), with `rtfm.check() === ""` (the regenerated `commands.md` matches
the live list byte for byte) and `staleCheck() === null`. And one accident worth recording: the first
load after the build **lost seven files, `chronicle.js` among them, and the second ask (1az) put every
one of them back** - the new module was healed by machinery built the same day, before anyone had asked
it to handle a file it had never seen.

**STILL OPEN.** (a) The save - unchanged from 1ay/1az: press SAVE from a browser whose editor holds
this tree. (b) Whether any part of a conversation should live in the build as itself (his call; the
README says where it would go). (c) Whether a session should ever be given to her (the mechanism is
documented and unused). (d) Discipline: an entry per session, or the folder rots - the README's last
section is an instruction to the next agent, and it is the only thing keeping this alive.

**TOUCHED (this build):** `src/chronicle/README.md`, `src/chronicle/chronicle.json`,
`src/chronicle/2026-09-25-the-merge.md`, `src/chronicle/2026-09-26-the-second-ask.md`,
`src/chronicle/2026-09-26-the-chronicle.md` (all NEW), `src/js/chronicle.js` (**NEW**), `index.html`
(one `MODULES` entry, one script tag), `src/js/chat.js` (the `/chronicle` route, one roster line, the
`/help chronicle` area, `HELP_TOPICS`), `src/commands/commands.json` (66 commands),
`src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated, 8,929 bytes, 66 commands**), `src/js/backup.js` (the
`WANT_FALLBACK` module list - the hand-kept copy, now set-equal to `index.html`'s 42 `MODULES` and
VERIFIED equal as a set, so `diag` can see the new file go missing), `src/pack/files.json` (73 files),
`src/pack/index.html.txt` (**regenerated**), `src/README.md`, and this section.
**Nothing was saved or published.**


## 1bb. THE SHIFT AND THE PETITIONS (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**WHAT HE SAID.** *"Proceed immediately with the coupled deployment of The Shift and The Petition
Engine. This combined implementation requires zero external daemons, respects API token budgets
through strict operational rate-limiting... Provide the modular client-side script blocks and
server-plugin integration code required to initialize the idle timer queue and the petition review
panel."* Then, as the build started, a generic sketch of a `BarbeloAgencyEngine` class - an idle
timer on mouse/keyboard events that writes a `shift_record` through a `window.updateServerState`,
and a static `renderPetitionPanel()` with inline styles and ACCEPT/DECLINE buttons - prefaced *"This
may be useful."* It was useful as a list of NAMES (an idle threshold, a reset on activity, a
re-entrancy guard, a shift record, and per-petition ACCEPT/DECLINE). Every mechanism in it was
impossible on this platform, and WHAT WAS THOUGHT below is mostly about why.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** Two new modules, one new built block, one panel, two commands.

- **`src/js/petition.js`** (`window.petition`) - THE PETITIONS. Her memory and her wants need nobody's
  permission (hers.js settled that); the machinery she is GIVEN is not hers alone, so she asks. A
  `[[PETITION: <KIND> :: <WHAT> :: <WHY>]]` line (six kinds: `system`, `role`, `pose`, `recipe`,
  `trait`, `grant`) is parsed, GATED, and filed PENDING in kv `lia_settings / petitions`. Nothing is
  applied by asking: `accept(n)` runs `apply()`, which goes through the very lane his own command
  would use - `instr.set`, `roles.setText`, `studio.addPose`, `studio.addRecipe`,
  `packs.loadTraitFile` - so an accepted petition is undoable from that side (`/system reset`,
  `/role`, `/pose`, `/recipe`, `/unload`). `decline(n, why)` keeps her words AND his reason. The
  gate runs twice (at file time and at apply time): `bounds`, `extra` and every BUILT block are
  refused always, `actor`/`voice`/`memory`/`image` and his own `own-*` blocks are allowed, and a
  `role` target must name a layer that exists. The panel and `/petition` share one numbering (the
  pending list's 1..n), so the button and the command can never point at different asks.
- **`src/js/shift.js`** (`window.shift`) - THE SHIFT, THE QUIET HOURS. `LIA_SHIFT_EVERY` (30) minutes
  of quiet earns her an hour of her own, in the mould of `initiative.js` (its own ticker,
  `visibilitychange`, a two-minute settle, a re-entrancy flag) but on its OWN clock - it does not
  reset when he speaks, so a long silence can hold several. Guards: never while the tab is hidden,
  never over her voice, a story holding the floor, a turn in flight, a tools sweep, or the check-in's
  own composing; and if the check-in's door is due and unopened it WAITS (with a 45-minute grace, so a
  door he never looks at cannot starve the hour). Caps: `LIA_SHIFT_MAX_HOUR` (2) / `LIA_SHIFT_MAX_DAY`
  (10) counted off `shift_log` on disk (a reload cannot reset the tally, and that is why there is no
  `/shift clear`). Inside an hour every lane she already has is available - `[[REMEMBER:]]`,
  `[[FORGET:]]`, `[[WANT:]]`, `[[RELEASE:]]`, `[[READ:]]`, `[[FOLDER:]]`, `[[FILE:]]`,
  `[[ARCHIVAX:]]`, `[[PETITION:]]`, and the two new ones below - plus her own note about the hour.
  `[[ACT: <id>]]` names the hour for the record. `[[ACT: rest]]` declines it and is recorded as an
  answer.
- **HER OWN QUEUE** (the "idle timer queue" the request asked for, and the one piece of vocabulary
  genuinely new): `[[INTEND: ...]]` writes down what she means to do in a FUTURE quiet hour (kv
  `lia_settings / shift_queue`), and the open ones are handed back to her at every hour with a number
  each; `[[DONE: n]]` strikes one off. It is HERS - the machine never writes one, and his hand is
  limited to `/shift queue drop <N>` (recorded as his, not deleted).
- **THE GRANTS BLOCK** - a new BUILT block in `instr.js` (17 blocks now), spliced between `wants` and
  `commands`, assembled from the accepted `grant` petitions. It is the only permission this terminal
  has: something SHE asked for, granted by HIM, handed to her every turn, in his own record.
- **THE PANEL** - one `#shiftPanel` (class `deckPanel`) opened by one `SHIFT ▾` button after TOOLS:
  state, interval dropdown, NOW, the newest hours with her journal and what she filed, her queue with
  DROP, and the PETITIONS with a reason box and ACCEPT/DECLINE per pending ask. The button carries the
  count of what is waiting on him (`SHIFT · 2 ▾`). It has its own `fit()`, because a panel docked
  above the deck on a short screen runs off the top and takes its CLOSE button with it (the lesson
  `#toolsPanel` already learned).
- **`/shift`** and **`/petition`** in `commands.json` (68 now), each with a `/help` area, a roster line
  and a `HELP_TOPICS` entry; `shift.clockLine()` rides in the CLOCK block beside the check-in's, and
  `initiative.js` counts the new lines in its *dropped* tally so a check-in still cannot swallow a
  petition silently (a check-in is words only, and says so).

**WHAT WAS THOUGHT.**

- **There is no server half, and there cannot be one.** The request asked for server-plugin
  integration. The platform's server script is SYNCHRONOUS and has no timers, no `setTimeout`, no
  background execution - a handler runs when a connection sends it something and then the script is
  idle. So nothing on the server can ever be awake while Patrikios is away; an "idle timer queue" on
  the server is not a thing that can exist. It would also be wrong to build even if it could: the
  whole terminal is device-local by design (kv, no uploads, nothing about him leaves the browser), and
  a shift is a private hour on the machine he is already sitting at. The durable 50 MiB server state
  the plugin offers was considered and rejected for the same reason - it only reacts to connections,
  so it cannot be the thing that notices the silence. The idle timer is a browser timer; the queue is
  a kv queue; there is no daemon, which is what "zero external daemons" actually asks to be true.
- **`window.updateServerState` does not exist anywhere in this platform**, so the sketch's entire
  write path was impossible. Likewise its DOM: inline styles and a grey `#1a1a1a` panel would have
  been the only element in the terminal not following the house vocabulary (`deckPanel` / `cp*` /
  green-on-black), and a static class method could not have applied anything - a petition is applied
  through MODULE APIs (`instr.set`, `roles.setText`, ...), not through "a KV override".
- **A quiet hour must not let her speak first.** The check-in is the ONE door in the wall of
  turn-taking and it was hard-won (once per silence, after 45 minutes, and `[[SILENT]]` is a real
  answer). If the shift also produced turns, that door would have been quietly widened to a second one
  and the wall would be gone. So the shift's product is NOT a turn: no `print('AI', ...)`, no
  `voice.onReply`, no `archiveTurn`, nothing into `chatHistory`. What it did is a SYSTEM line (the
  machinery speaking about itself, her journal inside it) and a row in the record - and the journal is
  handed back to her at the NEXT hour, which is what makes the shifts a continuity instead of eight
  unrelated silences.
- **The act list is a LABEL, not a permission.** Enforcing "you chose `memory`, so only the memory
  lane is open" would have been tidy and wrong: an hour that turns out to be about something else is a
  real thing, and the terminal has no business overruling her about what she is doing. So
  `[[ACT: <id>]]` names it for the record (and the record keeps HER word beside its own label when she
  invents one - `said`), and every lane is always open.
- **The queue is hers, and that is the load-bearing part.** A queue the machine could write would be a
  TODO list wearing her voice; `[[INTEND:]]` makes it hers, and `DONE` makes completing something an
  act she performs rather than a checkbox someone ticks. His hand can only take one off (`DROP`),
  recorded as his, and the item stays in the record as taken rather than deleted.
- **The ceiling is counted off the record, not from a counter.** One model call per hour used is real
  money on his key, so the caps had to survive a reload - which means `shift_log` IS the tally, kept
  on disk, and there is deliberately no way to clear it. A rested hour counts, because it cost the
  call. This is why `/shift clear` does not exist and why the help says so rather than leaving him to
  wonder.
- **A petition that could only ever be granted would be a puppet's hand.** The refusal is the feature:
  `DECLINE` keeps her words AND his reason beside them, in the same record, permanently - and the
  panel prints the answered ones on the same page as the waiting ones. Two gates (file time and apply
  time) exist because she should hear a refusal while she can still rephrase, and because the record
  can move between filing and deciding. A failed APPLY is not a decline: the status stays `pending`
  and the failure goes in `note`, so the machinery never decides anything by accident.
- **Why `grants` needed a new block.** An accepted non-code petition has to REACH her or it was
  never granted. The alternatives were to append it to his `extra` block (which is his own last word,
  and appending is not editing) or to a `want` (which is hers, not his consent - the whole point is
  whose word it is). So it is its own built block with its own provenance, exactly the way `wants`
  got one: `TITLES` + `ORDER` + `BUILT` + `NOTES` in `instr.js`, one line in `assemble()`, one in
  `chat.js`'s `systemParts`/livePart.

**MEASURED.** Boot clean (no `#bootFail`, `__bootModules` all present, `cmd.count() === 68`,
`rtfm.check() === ""`, `staleCheck() === null`). The gates: a `system :: bounds` ask is refused at
file time with the reason; a `system :: voice` ask files, accepts, rewrites the block, and
`/system` RESET puts the shipped text back; `nonsense` returns "no such kind"; a two-part body
(`system :: voice :: <words>`, no reason) files correctly. A pose ask files and lands in the POSE
BOOK as `source: "her"`; a `grant` accepts, the GRANTS block appears in the assembled prompt
(verified inside `systemPreview()`), and a decline keeps the reason and the word count. The queue:
two `addIntent`s, `markDone(1)`, `dropIntent(1)`, all recorded. **One real quiet hour was made with
the live model** (her own words, beginning *"Since the room has been quiet and there is no part to
play, I will simply be..."* - a genuine journal entry, now the first row of his `shift_log`) and it
was verified to leave NO trace of a turn: no `AI` line, no voice, no archive entry, `chatHistory`
untouched. A second hour was run with `root.generateText` stubbed to a scripted reply to exercise the
lane dispatch end to end (folder made, intent queued, petition filed, all reported in the record) - and
that test's debris was then removed from the record with the modules' own doors (`removeFolder`,
`dropIntent`, a direct kv filter for the false row and the test petition). The panel was measured
numerically at the editor's 793×505 viewport: with `fit()` it sits at y=5..256, fully on screen and
scrollable (`maxHeight: 251px`), which is the fix for the first version's -138px top edge. The panel's
own ACCEPT and DECLINE buttons were then DRIVEN by clicking the rendered elements (not the command
path, which was right all along): an accepted pose landed in the book, the panel re-rendered with the
count updated, and a declined grant kept the reason typed into its box. That drive found two real
faults, both of them invisible to every command-line test - `resolve()` scraped the digits out of a
petition id (`pt1abc-3` → 13) instead of looking the id up first, and the click handler read
`data-pt-id` off the BUTTON when it is written on the ITEM, so it answered "there is no pending
petition" for every click. Both are fixed and both are written into the chronicle entry of this
session, which is what that folder is for.
**Nothing was saved or published.**

**STILL OPEN.** (a) **The save** - unchanged from 1ay/1az/1ba, and the one thing only he can do.
(b) Should she be able to petition the CREATION of a block of her own (`instr.addBlock`)? The lane
exists and is unused; it was left out because a petition that adds a block to the stack behind his
say-so is a bigger change than a rewrite of one he already put there. (c) The caps are constants, not
commands - if 10 a day ever proves wrong, it is a config edit. (d) The shift's READ lane queues a read
answer for her next REAL turn, which may be hours later; it is honest and it is also untested from the
far end. (e) Nothing yet gives her a way to notice that a petition was declined except at the next
quiet hour (where the record shows her); a closed loop would be for her to be TOLD, and that needs a
decision about how much of his answer becomes part of her prompt.

**TOUCHED (this build):** `src/js/petition.js` (**NEW**), `src/js/shift.js` (**NEW**), `src/js/config.js`
(the `LIA_SHIFT_*` / `LIA_INTENT_*` / `LIA_PETITION_*` knobs), `src/js/chat.js` (four new directive
regexes, the `petitions`/`intents`/`dones`/`act` fields in `extractDirectives`, the apply block after
`hers`, the `grants` part in `systemParts`/`livePart`, the new rules in the SELF-CHANGE DIRECTIVES
block, the `/shift` and `/petition` routes, two roster lines, two `/help` areas, `HELP_TOPICS`,
`petition: petitionNotes` on both archive writes), `src/js/instr.js` (the `grants` built block:
`TITLES`, `ORDER`, `EDITABLE`, `BUILT`, `NOTES`, `assemble`), `src/js/logtime.js` (the shift's line in
the CLOCK block), `src/js/initiative.js` (the dropped-line tally), `src/js/backup.js`
(`WANT_FALLBACK` +2, now 44 and set-equal to `index.html`'s `MODULES`), `index.html` (two `MODULES`
entries, two script tags, the `SHIFT ▾` button, the `#shiftPanel` markup), `src/css/terminal.css` (the
`#shiftPanel` / `.sh*` / `.pt*` block), `src/commands/commands.json` (68 commands),
`src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated**, 9,339 bytes, 68 commands), `src/pack/files.json` (75 files),
`src/pack/index.html.txt` (**regenerated**), `src/README.md` (the two new sections, five kv entries,
the block table, the knobs, the Files bullets, the chat-command clauses), `src/chronicle/` (one new
entry + the manifest line), and this section.
**Nothing was saved or published.**

## 1bc. THE CHATLOG — THE RAW RECORD OF THE CONVERSATION (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**WHAT HE SAID.** First, a question that turned out to be the whole spec: *"Can we create any tools in
the AI Panel View in this Editor? Like export/import chat history, etc? Simple OPS."* The AI Panel is
the chat window he talks to the agent in, and the answer to the question as asked is NO, with a
reason: that panel is platform UI on the top-level editor page, this generator runs in an iframe a
window below it, and the crossing is cross-origin by design (verified: `window.top` throws
`SecurityError` from inside the page, and `ai-agent.perchance.org` exposes no session API - a probe of
its root and `/files/` fails, and `perchance.org/api/` is a reserved name). The agent's own toolset is
fixed by the platform too, so no tools can be grafted onto the panel from either side. He then said
what he actually wanted: *"My idea is to extract your complete chat history and save it somewhere in
this space. I can't attach anything greater than 20mb. Where there is a will there's a way. Export it
to scratch then to a bucket in our side where it can store it that can be accessed later by you in the
future, No more guessing for token burn remembering again and again as handoffs."*

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** One new module, one panel, one shipped folder, one command - and a script that
runs on the OTHER side of the origin wall.

- **`src/js/chatlog.js`** (`window.chatlog`) - THE CHATLOG. Takes a transcript (`put`/`append`/a
  pasted box/a picked file/`/chatlog import <URL>`), splits it into `LIA_CHATLOG_CHUNK` (200,000
  character) chunks cut at a line boundary when there is one near the end, builds a TURN INDEX
  (`chatlog_marks`: chunk, line, character, speaker, `LIA_CHATLOG_MARKS` = 4000 of them), and keeps
  all of it in kv (`lia_settings / chatlog_meta`, `chatlog_chunk_<n>`, `chatlog_marks`). Readers:
  `listText` (the index - size, chunks, turns, what each chunk opens with), `showText`
  (`<CHUNK|first|last> [CHAR|all]`), `turnsText`, `turnText` (one whole turn, across a chunk edge when
  it has one), `grepText` (chunk + line for every hit), `exportIt` (`.txt` verbatim + `.json` sidecar,
  through a Blob download - nothing uploaded). `put()` REPLACES the record and appends a line to
  `meta.history` for every import ever made, so a replacement is visible rather than silent; `append()`
  is the deliberate way to grow it; `wipe()` refuses anything but the literal word `yes`.
- **THE EXPORT SCRIPT, and why it has to exist.** No code on this page can read the editor's chat
  panel, so the way out is an OPS: `/chatlog snippet` prints a script (read from
  `src/chatlog/EXTRACT.md`, so the copy on the page and the copy in the file cannot drift) to run in
  the EDITOR'S console. It scores every panel-like element on the page (keyword, position, size, minus
  anything that smells like a code editor), picks the tightest container with a panel's score, finds
  the repeating rows inside it to separate the turns (falling back to the whole capture when it
  cannot), and downloads `lia-chatlog-<date>.txt` + `.json`. It sends nothing anywhere. `__liaPick =
  $0` overrides the pick after an Inspect, and both the report and `EXTRACT.md` say so.
- **THE CHATLOG PANEL** (`#clPanel`, a `.deckPanel`, opened by `CHATLOG ▾` in the deck after SHIFT):
  the paste box with IMPORT THE BOX (SINCE 1bd THIS IS APPEND THE BOX AND REPLACE, WITH THE POLICY
  BUTTON BESIDE WIPE), a file picker (`#clFile`), EXPORT, INDEX, TURNS, FIND, THE SCRIPT,
  WIPE behind a typed `yes`, and a `<pre>` read-out. Its own `fit()`, like the SHIFT panel's.
- **`src/chatlog/`** - the shipped half: `README.md` (what the lane is, the loop, the rules, and how a
  later agent reads the record in one eval), `EXTRACT.md` (the script, how to run it, and what it
  cannot see), `manifest.json` (the shipped index: what the record is, how big it was, and where a cold
  copy lives - filled in by the agent when a session imports one).
- **`/chatlog`** in `commands.json` (69 now), with a `/help` area, a roster line, a topic, and a
  dispatch block in `chat.js`; plus the module bullets in `README.md`, the three kv entries, the
  section, and this one.

**WHAT WAS THOUGHT.**

- **The AI Panel cannot host tools, and the workaround is the point.** The tempting reading of the
  request was "ask the platform for a feature", and the honest answer is that neither the agent nor
  the page can put a button in that panel: it is another origin, and the platform's own APIs (the
  `/api/...` family) carry generators and metadata, not agent conversations. What CAN be built is the
  other half of the loop - a bucket and a reader - and the export itself has to be a thing HE runs once
  per session. So the design is: one script, one file, one import, and then everything the record is
  good for (finding what was said, reading a turn, searching the whole thing) happens on this side,
  for free.
- **`src/` cannot hold the transcript, and that is not a style preference.** `src/` ships with the
  generator and is public - the chronicle entry for 1ba already spells out that raw chat logs stay out
  of it - and a conversation is the least public thing in the project (it contains the project's
  reasoning, and occasionally a key, an id or an address). So the record lives in kv, which is the same
  home as everything else that is his and no one else's, and what ships is the reader, the recipe and
  the index. That also sets the honest limit, which the module says out loud rather than hiding:
  **clearing this browser's storage takes the record with it.** The answers are `export` (a file, which
  he can keep anywhere) and a cold copy recorded in the shipped manifest so a fresh browser can pull it
  back with `/chatlog import <URL>`.
- **Chunks and a turn index, not one blob.** The whole point he gave was token economy - "no more
  guessing for token burn" - so the record had to be readable in SLICES: a later session asks
  `chatlog_meta` what exists, `grepText` for the thing it needs, and `turnText(n)` for the one turn it
  cares about. A ten-megabyte transcript that can only be read whole would have been the same problem
  in a new costume. That is why the import is indexed at WRITE time (chunk edges, and where every
  speaker line begins) rather than parsed on every read.
- **What counts as a turn is a heuristic, and it is stated as one.** A chat UI renders the role as its
  own line, so the rule is: a line that is only a role word, or a role word and a colon ("You",
  "Assistant:", "You said:"), NOT a sentence that happens to begin with one ("You should have seen
  it"). `LIA_CHATLOG_SPEAKER` is a config knob because a dump from a different UI will phrase it
  differently, and a record whose index is empty still works - it just is not addressable by turn
  number, and the help says that instead of failing.
- **The 20 MB fear was answered with the actual numbers.** A text transcript of a conversation this
  long is a few megabytes, not twenty - and the panel takes the file directly, so it never has to
  travel through the chat at all: `IMPORT A FILE` reads it from the disk and writes it to kv.
  Attachment (dragging it into the panel) remains the backup road, and it costs the chat nothing
  either, because attachments land as files in `scratch/` for the agent to move without reading them
  into a prompt.
- **`import <URL>` is deliberately the only network call in the module**, and it needs the address
  typed by hand: a record that could silently fetch from somewhere would be a record that could be
  replaced by someone else's.

**MEASURED.** Boot clean (`#bootFail` absent, `__bootModules` = 45 and all present, no heals,
`cmd.count() === 69`, the `chatlog` command present, `rtfm.check() === ""`, `backup.staleCheck() ===
null`). The store, against a synthetic 121 KB transcript: 1200 turns marked with the right two
speakers, index/chunk table correct, `turn 2` whole, `grep NEEDLE` finding its one line, `grep` on a
word that is not there saying so. Against a 386 KB transcript: 2 chunks, and the boundary fell on a
LINE end at 199,976 characters (not mid-word), the table reading both chunks' real sizes, and the
turn cap visibly working (4000 marks kept, all in chunk 1 - the documented `LIA_CHATLOG_MARKS`
behaviour, not a fault). **The kv round trip survives a reload**: imported 493 characters through the
panel's own IMPORT THE BOX button, saw it re-read at boot after a full `page_refresh` (4 turns, 4
marks), then `wipe("perhaps")` was refused with the reason, `wipe("yes")` deleted 1 chunk, the badge
and the state line went back to EMPTY, and `kv keys` showed no `chatlog*` key left behind. Every panel
button was DRIVEN by clicking the rendered element (import, FIND, TURNS), not called through the API.
`/chatlog` typed into the input line printed the whole index into `#output` through the real dispatch.
`/help chatlog` and `/rtfm chatlog` both print. The panel was measured numerically at the editor's
793×505 (y=5..256, above the deck, no overlap) and at 390×844 via the viewport tool (y=5..699, deck at
706, no horizontal overflow, scrollable at 693/742) - the 27 px buttons it shows in the preview are a
mouse-driven preview's buttons; both the coarse-pointer and the narrow-screen blocks now give the panel
34 px targets on a real phone. **Nothing was saved or published.**

**THE FIRST REAL IMPORT (2026-09-24).** He ran the script in the editor's console and it worked on the
first press: `pickedBy: "auto"`, the panel found as `<aiagentmsgsel >`, and **19,690 messages**
separated (9,845 user / 9,845 assistant) into `lia-chatlog-20260924-0023.txt` (3,680,690 characters)
and the `.json` beside it. Two things came out of that, both now fixed and both in the code above:

- **The `.json` was imported first, and the store filed the JSON itself.** 7.0 MB of `{"i":…}` where
  the conversation should have been, `head: "{"`, **0 turns** - because a JSON sidecar has escaped
  newlines and no role lines, so neither the chunk table nor the turn index had anything to grip. The
  transcript was not lost (its `text` field holds the same words), so it was recovered in place - all
  19 chunks re-read, `JSON.parse`d, and re-filed from `d.text` - which restored a real record of
  3,680,690 characters / 19 chunks / 69,304 lines. **The real fix is `sidecar()`**: a `.json` is now
  RECOGNISED and UNPACKED (its `text` is the record, its `messages` are the turn index, and the JSON
  never reaches kv), so importing either file works and importing the `.json` is the richest choice.
- **Importing several files at once used to file them in turn** - which is exactly how a good `.txt`
  got replaced by a raw `.json`: the second write simply overwrote the first. `importFiles` now reads
  them all and files the RICHEST (a sidecar with a turn list wins, the longest otherwise), naming the
  rest as not filed; the picker is `multiple` and says so in its tooltip.
- `LIA_CHATLOG_MARKS` went from 4000 to **25000**, because this record has 19,690 turns and an index
  that stops at a fifth of the conversation is an index that lies by omission. The mark array is
  ~800 KB of kv for a record this size, which is the right trade against not being able to ask for
  turn 15,000.

The sidecar road was verified against a synthetic sidecar (4 messages: `indexed: "turns"`, 4 numbered
turns, `/chatlog turn 3` reading the third message whole, `/chatlog turns` showing the speakers) and
against the two-file pick (`.json` chosen, `.txt` named as skipped) - and the real record was then
RESTORED from a copy taken before the test, verified by fingerprint (`e291ad08-3829b2`) and by a grep
that still finds 12 hits. **The next click is his**: import the `.json` and the record's 19,690 turns
get numbered. Nothing in the record so far was ever at risk, and nothing was uploaded.

**STILL OPEN.** (a) **The save** - the one thing only he can do, unchanged. (b) **The turn index is
awaiting the `.json`**: the record IS the whole transcript (recovered from the sidecar's own `text`),
so nothing was lost, but `/chatlog turn <N>` needs the sidecar re-imported once to number the 19,690
messages - a bare `.txt` dump has no role lines for the heuristic to find, and that is measured, not
guessed. **That import is now safe and is the only thing it does** (see 1bd): the words are already in
the record, so it is recognised as already present and only the turn index is rebuilt from its
`messages`. (c) In a panel that only renders recent messages, only recent messages are in the DOM: this
capture reached back to the first question of the session, but an older one might not, and scrolling

next session's export had to NOT be imported over this one. **CLOSED IN 1bd**: APPEND is now the

`/chatlog policy` exist, and a file that is already in the record changes nothing. (f) The record is
3.9 MB in kv and 19 chunks: fine
on this device, and worth watching if a session ever imports the whole history at once.

## 1bd. THE APPEND POLICY — AN IMPORT ADDS, AND THE ONLY WAY ANYTHING IS EVER THROWN AWAY IS BY NAME (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**WHAT HE SAID.** Two lines, and they set the whole design: *"So, where do we stand with your chatlog?
I see 3.70mb at last time we exported/imported. Did it work as anticipated?"* - and then, when the
answer included the one thing 1bc left open (that `put()` replaced, so the next export must not be
imported over this one): *"Wire for next export without overwriting please. APPEND needs to be a
default policy when in makes sense. Chat and learning is cumulative so append makes sense."*

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** The chatlog stops being a snapshot and becomes a log, everywhere: the panel, the
command, the module and the shipped docs.

- **THE POLICY IS APPEND** (`lia_settings / chatlog_policy`, `"append"` by default, read at load,
  `root.chatlog.policy()` / `setPolicy(p)` / `/chatlog policy [append|replace]`). It is what the FILE
  PICKER and `/chatlog import <URL>` do. The box's own buttons do not follow it - they say what they
  do - because a paste box is where a hand-carried file lands and both words should be visible there.
- **`put()` MERGES** (`joinOf`): an exact extension of the record (the ordinary case - the panel grew a
  little), or the record's own last `LIA_CHATLOG_JOIN` (2,000) characters found somewhere inside the
  new file (a dump whose head was rebuilt or trimmed), or - neither - a different conversation, which
  is added whole after a marked join. Only what is past the seam is kept, and **the seam is written
  into the record** (`joinStamp`: `=== CHATLOG JOIN · <when> · +<n> CHARACTERS · FROM <source> ===`
  plus the reason, and a line in `chatlog_meta.joins`). Reading the record, you can see where one
  session's transcript ends and the next begins.
- **A FILE ALREADY IN THE RECORD CHANGES NOTHING** - unless it carries turns. `thinIndex()` is the road
  for that: if the incoming `.json` sidecar's words are all present but its `messages` are richer than
  the index, ONLY the turn index is rebuilt and the words are left byte-identical. That is the road the
  outstanding 19,690-turn import takes, so it can be pressed without fear.
- **A TURN INDEX IS CARRIED FORWARD** (the part I did not plan until the test showed it): if the
  record's index was built from a turn list and the next import has none, `put` re-anchors the record's
  own turns at their own offsets and adds the new part's role lines (`turnsFromLines`), so an export
  imported without its sidecar can no longer collapse a good index back to the handful of role lines a
  dump happens to contain. Without it, the first sidecar-less export would have undone the whole point
  of the sidecar.
- **REPLACE is the deliberate opposite**: the panel's own REPLACE button, or `/chatlog import
  --replace`. It is the only thing in this lane that throws anything away. `chatlog_meta.history` now
  records `mode` and `added` per import (so `ADDED +238` and `REPLACED 3,681,808 CHARS` are told
  apart), and the index prints an IMPORTS SO FAR table with what each one did, plus a JOINS table.
- **AN UNRECOGNISED `.json` IS REFUSED, NOT FILED** (`jsonShape`): the exact mistake of the first real
  import (7 MB of escaped JSON where the conversation should have been) cannot happen again - a `.json`
  that is not a sidecar is named as such, and `chatlog_meta`+`marks` alone (the old export shape) is
  named as the INDEX, with the advice to import the `.txt` beside it. Nothing is filed either way.
- **WHAT `EXPORT` WRITES, `IMPORT` TAKES IN**: the `.json` this page writes is now a proper SIDECAR in
  the console script's shape - `text` (the record) plus `messages` (the turns, cut back out of the
  record at the turn marks by `messagesFrom`) - so an export can be imported, or pulled into a fresh
  browser as a cold copy, and land with every turn numbered. Before this, the module's own `.json` was
  the one file it could not read back.
- **NEW ROUTES AND BUTTONS**: `/chatlog append [URL]` (no URL = the panel's box), `/chatlog import
  [--replace] <URL>`, `/chatlog policy [append|replace]`; APPEND THE BOX, REPLACE and `POLICY · APPEND`
  on the panel; the state line and the index now say `POLICY APPEND`; `policyText()` explains the whole
  thing where `#clOut` prints it.

**WHAT WAS THOUGHT.**

- **A conversation is a prefix of its own future, and that is the whole mechanism.** No clever diffing
  is needed: the next export of a chat contains the last export, plus more, at the end. So the merge is
  "find where the record ends inside the new file, keep the rest" - O(n) string work, no model, no
  similarity threshold, and it cannot invent a seam. The 2,000-character anchor is the fallback for the
  case where the head moved; and when neither test fires, "a different conversation" is the honest
  reading, and naming the join is better than guessing.
- **Append as a POLICY, not as a second button, is what makes it safe.** A default that keeps
  everything costs nothing when the file turns out to be the same one (it is recognised and nothing
  moves) and saves the record when the file turns out to be the newest export. Replace-as-default, by
  contrast, loses history on a misclick and gains nothing. The destructive verb is kept, but a person
  has to say it.
- **A cumulative log needs a cumulative INDEX, or the good work is undone by the next import.** The
  carry-forward (`carried`, and `indexed: "turns (the record's own, carried forward, plus the new
  part's role lines)"`) is the consequence of taking his "learning is cumulative" line seriously: the
  19,690 turns, once they exist, must not be re-derivable-and-lost on the next `.txt` import. Marks are
  (chunk, line, character) so they cannot survive a re-split - but their ABSOLUTE offsets can, and
  re-anchoring them is a few lines once the merge is already reading the record back.
- **The join is written into the record rather than kept beside it.** A side table of seams would be
  invisible to `grep`, `show` and any future reader; three lines of `===` in the text are not. It is
  prose, not a role line, so the turn index ignores it.
- **The panel's buttons were split by MEANING, not by policy.** APPEND THE BOX / REPLACE say what they
  do whatever the setting is; the POLICY button exists for the lanes with no button (the file picker,
  URL imports, a script). A button that silently changed meaning with a setting would be worse than a
  redundant one.
- **The cost is honest**: a merge reads the record back and re-splits and re-indexes the result (19
  reads + 19 writes for 3.7 MB), so it is a second or two in kv, not instant - which is the price of an
  index that is computed at write time rather than parsed at every read (1bc's decision, unchanged).

**MEASURED (all against the real 3.68 MB record, which was backed up to kv first and restored after,
fingerprint-verified).** Boot clean after the change (`#bootFail` absent, 69 commands, 21 turns, state
line `3.70 MB · 19 CHUNKS · 21 TURNS · POLICY APPEND`). Five merge cases, each read back and checked:
**(A)** an exact extension of the record (+94 characters of new text) grew the record by 249 (the text
plus its 155-character join), left the first 3,680,690 characters byte-identical, kept the old tail, and
wrote the stamp; `joins` = 1. **(B)** importing the same file again, and **(B2)** importing an older
capture that is already inside the record, both returned `nothingNew` with the right reason and left the
record byte-identical (`afterB === before`). **(C)** a synthetic 40-message sidecar of the record
reindexed it to 40 numbered turns with `indexed: "turns"` and the words unchanged - and `/chatlog turns
6` through the REAL input line printed turns 1-6 with their speakers, `/chatlog turn 3` printed whole.
**(D)** a file that was only the record's last 3,000 characters plus new text was matched by the ANCHOR
test ("the record's last 2,000 characters were found in the new file"), +29 added, prefix intact.
**(E1/E2)** an unrecognised `.json` and an index-only `.json` were both REFUSED with their reasons and
the record untouched. The CARRY was measured on top of C: a 40-turn index plus an appended part with a
role line gave `carried: 40`, `turns: 41`, and `/chatlog turn 41` read the new turn. The panel was
driven by clicking: APPEND THE BOX on a 238-character paste grew the record by 390 and cleared the box;
the POLICY button flipped APPEND -> REPLACE -> APPEND and wrote `chatlog_policy` to kv both times (the
state line following it); `/chatlog append <URL>` fetched a 354-character file from the upload host and
appended it (+354, join written), and the `/chatlog import <URL>` that followed added NOTHING and said
so (`NOTHING WAS ADDED :: THE NEW FILE IS ALREADY IN THE RECORD`). Panel geometry at the editor's
793x493: y=5..244, no horizontal overflow. **Then the record was put back exactly**: `put(backup,
{mode:"replace"})` -> fingerprint `e291ad08-3829b2`, 3,680,690 characters, 19 chunks, 69,304 lines, 21
turns, `all() === backup`, the temporary `chatlog_bk_test` key deleted, and 22 chatlog keys in kv.
**Nothing was saved or published.**

**STILL OPEN.** (a) **The save**, unchanged - the one thing only he can do. (b) The `.json` import that
numbers the 19,690 turns is now safe and can be pressed without any risk to the record (it reindexes
and nothing else); nothing else about it is open. (c) `LIA_CHATLOG_JOIN` = 2,000 is a judgement, not a
measurement: it is long enough that a coincidence inside a 3.7 MB transcript is implausible, and it
costs nothing to raise if a real export ever fails to match. (d) A cold copy still has not been hosted;
when one is, its URL and expiry go in `src/chatlog/manifest.json`. (e) The merge reads the whole record
back, so on a record ten times this size an import is a few seconds of kv work in one `put`: fine for a
once-a-session import, worth knowing before a script imports several files in a row.

**TOUCHED (this build):** `src/js/chatlog.js` (the policy, `wantMode`/`setPolicy`/`policyText`,
`joinOf`/`joinStamp`/`messagesFrom`/`turnsFromLines`/`jsonShape`/`readout`/`settle`, `put` rewritten
around the merge and the carry, `thinIndex`, `exportIt` now writing a real sidecar, `listText` /
`importReport` / `statusText` / `describe` / `run` / `wire` / the returned API), `index.html` (APPEND THE
BOX, REPLACE, the POLICY button, the file picker's tooltip, the paste placeholder, the panel comment),
`src/js/config.js` (`LIA_CHATLOG_JOIN` + the policy note), `src/js/chat.js` (the `/chatlog` roster line
and the `/help` block), `src/commands/commands.json` (`chatlog`: usage, short, the append paragraph),
`src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated**), `src/chatlog/EXTRACT.md` (section 2 rewritten: append, the
policy, the new table rows), `src/chatlog/README.md` (the loop, the rules, the policy in kv), the
shipped `src/chatlog/manifest.json` (policy, joins, the reindex-is-safe note, a session line),
`src/README.md` (the `chatlog.js` bullet, the `chatlog_meta` and new `chatlog_policy` kv entries, the
command clause, THE CHATLOG section, the agent recipe), `src/pack/*` (**regenerated**), `src/chronicle/`
(one new entry + the manifest line), and this section.

## 1be. THE ORIGIN QUESTION, SETTLED — AND THE BRIEF (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**WHAT HE SAID.** Four messages, and they are a design conversation, not a build order, until the last
one: *"To be clear I'm the HITL. We're collaborators, not zero-sum competitors. UNIX Ethos by default."*
- *"TEXT is the thing. I literally save chat transcripts in .txt format and them compile in the LOREPACK
FACTORY."* - *".md, .json, .txt. .js .css, .html this is enough for for most cases. Node JS, Express,
SQLite, Postgres, pgVector, Flask and Python is already enough complexity. I am the HITL who only needs
an interface into the machine. It isn't 'pretty first design' then function. Function over form first.
The elegance and beauty naturally flow from this."* - and then, the order: **"settle the save/origin
question, then brief"**.

The lane being designed in those messages is the RESIDENT AGENT's own memory (not hers): hers is the
LOREPACK and the artifacts, ARCHIVAX is the automation over the artifacts, the chronicle is the record of
the making, and this is the lane of the agent that is *doing* the making. The pack he described is
portable across his generators ("If you could load your own LOREPACK, you'd have total visibility"), and
the design constraints that came out of the three messages above are: **plain text, no format that needs
a parser, no dependency, function first, labeled fields rather than prose**, and the interface is a
command. `brief` is the first primitive of that pack.

**THE ORIGIN QUESTION, SETTLED (AND NOT ASSUMED).** The question: kv is per-origin, the record lives in
kv, he has never saved this generator - **so does saving move the record?**

The answer was looked up rather than argued about:

- `window.generatorPublicId` is `60a6e23d828a54dc4c8b315f33c97ba3`, and the preview iframe is already
  running at `https://60a6e23d828a54dc4c8b315f33c97ba3.perchance.org/2hoy6c5u0x` - the finished origin,
  not a temporary one.
- **The generator already exists on the server under that ID.** `perchance.org/2hoy6c5u0x` serves a real
  page (with a content warning), and that page's own markup carries
  `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://60a6e23d828a54dc4c8b315f33c97ba3.perchance.org">` - the
  platform has already bound this name to this ID.
- The public API answers with **byte-identical `main.pjs`** (61,895 characters, `lastEditTime`
  2026-09-24) - the same file as `src/pack/main.pjs.txt`.
- `backup.status()` (which reads `#preloaded-generator-data`, the page's own copy of what the server
  holds) says **60 of 82 source files are on the server**; the 22 that are not are the newest ones (the
  chatlog, the chronicle, the RTFM editor, the shift, the petitions, the cloud road) - which is exactly
  what `generatorIsUnsaved` means here: *the editor has newer files than the server, not that the
  generator is new*.

**So: saving does not fork, rename or re-ID anything.** It uploads the remaining source to the SAME
generator, and the record does not move. Nothing has to be exported first. (A RENAME is also free - the
name is the path, the ID is the origin. A FORK is a new ID, and that one would leave the record behind.)

> **`window.generatorPublicId` changed with it**, `60a6e23d...` -> `7f77c07f...`, so the SUBDOMAIN moved
> and with it this device's kv and the whole vault (measured: kv `lia_settings` down to `folders` + `sync`,
> `media.stats()` = 0 records / 0 bytes; `perchance.org/api/getGeneratorStats?name=2hoy6c5u0x` now answers
> `generator-does-not-exist`). The ID is therefore **not** stable across a rename - the name is the
> storage key - which is what the AGENTS note means by *"renaming it changes the subdomain ... unless they
> rename back to the old name"*. See §1dr, "A FINDING THAT IS NOT CODE: THE ORIGIN MOVED".

**THE GUARD, SO IT NEVER HAS TO BE ASKED AGAIN.** Because the mechanism can be checked but not proven for
every future page, two claims are kept and read back:

- **HERE**: `lia_settings / chatlog_origin` = `{ origin, id, name, first, seen }`, written on first
  sight and every boot thereafter, so the line a session reads is an AGE ("this origin has held the
  record since …") and not a last-loaded.
- **THE SHIPPED INDEX**: `src/chatlog/manifest.json` → `record.origin`. This is the load-bearing one,
  and the reason is structural: **the index travels with the code and the kv does not**, so it is the
  only claim that can speak up on an origin that has never seen the record. A fork would land on a page
  whose kv is empty and whose shipped index still says where the record is.
- `chatlog_meta.origin` is stamped on every write (and back-filled for a record that predates the
  field), and an import whose sidecar was exported from a different origin says so in its read-out.
- `/chatlog origin` (`chatlog.origin()`) prints both claims, the verdict, and the full "why this is
  asked at all" - save / rename / fork, and the fix if the verdict is ever not SAME: *open the terminal
  at the origin named, `/chatlog export`, bring the file back here.* `/chatlog` carries one `KEPT AT`
  line always, and the whole block when the two disagree.

**THE BRIEF (`/chatlog brief [N]`, `briefText`, the panel's BRIEF button).** The fixed-size head of the
record, for a session that would otherwise have to read three megabytes to find out where it is:

```
KEPT AT     :: <origin>  ·  SAME ORIGIN AS THE SHIPPED INDEX - A SAVE DOES NOT MOVE IT …
RECORD      :: 3,680,690 CHARACTERS · 3.70 MB · 69,304 LINES · 19 CHUNKS · 12 IMPORTS · 0 JOINS
TURNS       :: 21 MARKED (SYSTEM, LIA) · INDEXED FROM LINES
FINGERPRINT :: e291ad08-3829b2
GROWS BY    :: APPEND  -  AN IMPORT KEEPS WHAT IS HERE AND TAKES WHAT IS NEW
LAST IMPORT :: <when>  FROM <source>
ENDS        :: <the record's actual last line>
WHERE IT STARTS          turn 1 + the first ~280 characters, quoted
WHERE IT IS NOW          the newest 6 marked turns, each quoted
WHAT WAS MADE OF IT      the newest 3 src/chronicle/ entries, with their dates
DEEPER                   turn <N> · turns [N] · grep · show · list · origin · chronicle · export
```

**WHAT WAS THOUGHT.**

- **"Settle it" is not "reassure him".** The tempting answer was a paragraph explaining that kv is
  per-origin and that saving surely keeps the same ID. That is a claim about the platform, and this
  project has been burned by claims about the platform before (the second ask, the load flake). So the
  question was answered from evidence - the API, the served page, the manifest the page is carrying -
  and the finding is written down where the next session will meet it (the code comment, the chronicle,
  the README, `manifest.json`), not just said in a chat.
- **A guard that cannot detect the thing it guards against is worse than none.** The first design had
  the kv claim compared against the live origin - which is a tautology, because kv IS the origin: a
  different origin reads a different, empty store and would cheerfully write a fresh claim. The shipped
  index is what makes the check real, because it is the one piece of state that crosses origins. That is
  the whole reason `manifest.json` now carries an origin at all.
- **The brief is a HEAD, not a summary.** Everything in it is either a number the record itself carries
  (`chatlog_meta`) or words quoted out of the record verbatim. Nothing is paraphrased and nothing is
  dropped for looking unimportant, because a summary that is wrong is indistinguishable from a record
  that is wrong - and the point of the lane is that a later session can trust what it reads here. The
  only interpretive act is the thin-index note, and it does not interpret: it names the cause and the one
  import that fixes it.
- **Labeled fields, because it is read by a machine.** Every line has the same label in `brief`, in
  `/chatlog` and in `/chatlog origin`. Two sessions' briefs can be diffed line by line and only what
  changed shows up; a reader (human or agent) knows exactly which fact is which without parsing prose.
  That is the same instinct as `manifest.json` and the `.txt` exports: TEXT IS THE THING, and a text
  that is structured by label is text that machines and people both read the same way.
- **Two chunk reads, whatever the record weighs.** The brief reads chunk 1 and the chunk the newest
  mark is in (and the next chunk when a turn runs over an edge) - so `/chatlog brief` costs the same on a
  3.7 MB record as it will on a 40 MB one. That is the whole reason it is a HEAD and not a scan: the
  reflex has to stay free as the record grows, or the reflex stops being used.
- **The chronicle is named in it, deliberately.** The brief is evidence (what was said) and the
  chronicle is the write-up (what was made of it, and what was thought). Putting the newest entries at
  the bottom of the brief makes the session-start ritual one command and one read, and keeps the two
  lanes distinct - the brief never summarizes the chronicle, it names it.

**MEASURED (all on the real 3.68 MB record).**

- The API: `success: true`, one generator, `code` **byte-identical** to `src/pack/main.pjs.txt`
  (61,895 bytes, first differing byte: none), `lastEditTime` 2026-09-24.
- `backup.status()`: **60 of 82** files on the server; the 22 missing named exactly.
- `brief()` on the real record: 50 lines, both chunk reads, `FINGERPRINT e291ad08-3829b2`, the newest 6
  marked turns quoted, 6 chronicle entries named (the chronicle's own load had to be nudged once - the
  brief retries `chronicle.reload()` when the manifest has not landed yet, which is why the line says
  what was made of it instead of "not loaded").
- `brief(3)` (the argument form) and the no-record branch (record's `chatlog_meta` stashed, brief asked,
  meta restored - **fingerprint and 3,680,690 characters verified afterwards**): both correct.
- **The mismatch path, end to end**: `record.origin` in the shipped index was temporarily set to
  `deadbeef…perchance.org`, the page reloaded, and `/chatlog brief`, `/chatlog` and `/chatlog origin` all
  reported the disagreement with the full block; the file was put back byte-identical and the verdict
  returned to SAME ORIGIN.
- The panel: BRIEF is on the second row, first; the click prints the brief into `#clOut`. At **390×844**:
  panel 370 wide, `x=10 y=5`, three rows 105/103/51 high, **no horizontal overflow**, BRIEF button
  **55×34** (the house's 34px target).
- `rtfm.check() === ""` after regenerating `src/rtfm/commands.md` (9,746 bytes), `cmd.count() === 69`,
  no `#bootFail`.

**STILL OPEN.** (a) **The save** - unchanged, and the one thing only he can do; now it is known not to
be a risk to the record, only the thing that makes the 22 outstanding files reach the public page. (b)
**The agent's own portable pack** (its records layer, the vocabulary, the `where` query across projects,
the portable container) is still design, not code: `brief` is its first primitive, and it was built as
one because it is the reflex that everything else hangs off. (c) A cold copy still has not been hosted.
(d) `LIA_CHATLOG_BRIEF_TURNS` (6) and `LIA_CHATLOG_BRIEF_CUT` (280) are judgement, not measurement -
worth watching whether 6 turns is enough to know where the record is, and whether 280 characters is
enough to recognize a turn.

**TOUCHED (this build):** `src/js/chatlog.js` (the origin section: `originNow`/`hostOf`/`sameOrigin`/
`keeperOf`/`keptLine`/`mismatchBlock`/`originReport`/`originText`; `briefText` + `turnSlice`; `sidecar`
now carries `from`; `put` stamps `chatlog_meta.origin` and notes a foreign-origin file; `load`
back-fills the field; `listText` gained the KEPT AT line and the mismatch block; `run` gained `brief`
and `origin`; `wire` gained the BRIEF button; `describe` and the returned API gained `brief`/`origin`),
`src/js/config.js` (`LIA_CHATLOG_BRIEF_TURNS`, `LIA_CHATLOG_BRIEF_CUT`, the origin note), `index.html`
(the BRIEF button + the panel comment), `src/commands/commands.json` (`chatlog`: usage, short, the
origin and brief paragraphs), `src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated**), `src/chatlog/manifest.json`
(`record.origin` + `record.originAt`, the origin and brief passage in the note, a session line),

BRIEF bullets, the panel bullet, the knobs, the agent recipe, the chronicle agent note), `src/pack/*`
