## 1bf. THE IMPORT HAD NO NAME (FIXED 2026-09-26)

**WHAT HE SAID.** After exporting from the CHATLOG panel: *"Exported from the GUI. There is no import
for the CHATLOG. Do we need it?"*

**WHAT WAS TRUE.** The import existed - three doors: the file picker beside the paste box, APPEND THE
BOX for a paste, and `/chatlog append <URL>` / `/chatlog import [--replace] <URL>` for a hosted copy.
What did not exist was the WORD. The picker renders as Chrome's own "Choose Files / No file chosen",
and nothing on the panel said IMPORT - so a panel that says EXPORT beside a control that says Choose
Files reads as a dead end, and the question was the right one to ask. An export with no visible import
is half a feature.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** `IMPORT` now sits beside the picker, in the panel's own dim-green label style, and
the two are wrapped together in one `.clImport` group so the word and the control it names always wrap
as a unit - at no width is "IMPORT" stranded at the end of one line while the picker sits on the next.
The picker's tooltip leads with IMPORT and names the file it wants (`lia-chatlog-<date>.json` this page
EXPORTED, or the `.txt` beside it, or any transcript); the label under the box now reads "PASTE THE
CONVERSATION HERE · OR PRESS IMPORT ABOVE AND PICK THE DOWNLOADED FILE"; and the panel comment, the
chatlog README, EXTRACT and the main README say which door is which and that IMPORT is the other half
of EXPORT. One CSS detail that had to be measured rather than assumed: `#clPanel .cpRow .clImport
.cpLabel` needs `flex: 0 0 auto`, because the panel's row-label rule pins `flex-basis: 116px` and the
label came out 116 wide inside the group - a real 2px overflow at 390px until it was looked at.

**MEASURED.** Desktop (793 wide): one line, six items (APPEND THE BOX · REPLACE · IMPORT [picker] ·
EXPORT · CLOSE), no overflow. Phone (390×844): APPEND/REPLACE, then IMPORT [picker] + EXPORT, then
CLOSE - row 102 tall, no horizontal overflow anywhere, panel 370×694, every control 34px. The picker's
change handler was exercised end to end by handing the input a probe file through `DataTransfer`
(rejected as TOO SHORT, which is the designed refusal) - so the door is wired and the import path runs;
and the record's fingerprint was checked afterwards (`e291ad08-3829b2`), because a UI test must not be
the thing that changes the record.

**TOUCHED:** `index.html` (the IMPORT label, the picker tooltip, the label under the box, the panel
comment), `src/css/terminal.css` (`.clImport` and its label, the phone wrap), `src/commands/
commands.json` (`chatlog` desc names IMPORT), `src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated**),
`src/chatlog/README.md`, `src/chatlog/EXTRACT.md`, `src/README.md` (the panel bullet),
`src/pack/index.html.txt` (**regenerated**), and this section.

## 1bg. THE PROGRESS BAR (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**WHAT HE SAID.** *"We need a simple green progress bar element when actions require time to process"*

**WHAT WAS TRUE.** The terminal is full of work that takes real time and says nothing while it does
it, and the only sign of life was a line of text in one of three places depending on where the work
started: `#cpProgress` in the forge's panel head, `#tlState` in the tools panel head, and a SYSTEM
line in the log at the end. The one question a long job should never leave open - *is it still
working, or did it die?* - had no answer at a glance, and a backstage sweep (a classifier pass over
2,297 records, an 84-file backup, an upscale sweep) could run for twenty minutes with the only
evidence being a thumbnail chip and a spinning tile.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** `src/js/progress.js` (`window.progress`) and ONE element: `#progressRail` at the
top of the LOWER DECK, above the input box, hidden until a job opens one. The API is three calls -
`begin(label, { total })` → `claim.set(done)` / `claim.step()` → `claim.finish()` (or
`claim.fail(why)`) - and everything else falls out of it:

- **no `total` = indeterminate** (a 34% segment sliding across the track): the honest shape for one
  render, one vision call, one resample, one network round trip, and `progress.show(label)` is the
  one-liner for it;
- **nesting by priority** (default 1, newest of equals), so a counted batch outranks the uncounted
  call inside each picture and a job that ends never blanks a job still running; a label is cut with
  an ellipsis rather than wrapped, so the rail cannot grow a second line and shove the input box down
  as the count changes;
- **a finished job lingers 1.6 s** (a failed one 5 s, in `#ff5555`, the house red) so the bar does not
  vanish as a glitch would;
- **repaints throttled to 120 ms** while ticks can come nineteen at a time, but instant on
  begin/finish/fail so the last state drawn is never a lie;
- an id already running is CONTINUED, not duplicated - which is what lets `runJob` open with a job's
  title and `applyRead` re-open the same id with the real `total`, and what keeps one job from
  becoming two bars when a panel and a command both ask for it;
- `claim.step(n)`, `progress.set/id`, `progress.setLabel/id`, `progress.step/id`,
  `progress.finish/id`, `progress.fail/id`, `progress.active()`, `progress.current()`,
  `progress.report()`, `progress.clear()`, `progress.paint()`, and `progress.demo(steps, ms)`.

**WIRED INTO** (each one live-verified or verified by a real read-only pass): the forge's batch;
`renderImage` (priority 0, opened INSIDE the `oneAtATime` job - at queue time a claim would be ended
by the render ahead of it and never reopen); `upscaleLocal.run` (priority 0, with `retire` inside a
`try/finally`); `tools.js` - every `apply` counted, a SCAN indeterminate on its own id so it cannot
take down a run's rail, and `runJob`'s `finally` as the backstop; `backup.download` (counted off
`collect`'s existing `onStep`; the AUTOSAVE's silent `build` was left silent ON PURPOSE - a bar that
appears before he asked for anything would be the one place this terminal answered a question nobody
asked); `chatlog` (read-back and write counted in chunks, the export indeterminate, `readAll` closing
its own claim because a bare `chatlog.all()` is a whole job); `sync` (`look` counted per file, `up`
and `pull` indeterminate); `sync-cloud` (`send`/`receive`, closed by `fail()` too); the gallery's
`importFiles`; `attach.sampleFrames` (counted per still, priority 0) and `attach.add` (only when a
message carries more than one file, so a single picture does not flash a rail); `audition.learn`
(id `ears`, label changing from the local reduction to the listening). `/progress` reports,
`/progress demo` runs a fake job through the same door, `/progress clear` unsticks one.

**WHAT WAS THOUGHT.** (1) The rail is a READOUT, not a control and not a record: nothing in it is
pressable, nothing is written to kv, and no history is kept - so it cannot become a second source of
truth about what happened, and a reload costs it nothing. (2) It is deliberately NOT the in-hand chip
(`src/js/minibox.js`): that is WHICH picture, with a thumbnail, a citation and a 20-second lease; this
is HOW FAR ALONG, and the two are read together on a sweep. (3) Where a job already had a count
(`collect`'s `onStep`, the classifier's `tried`/`list.length`, the chatlog's chunk loops) the existing
number was used rather than a second one invented. (4) The `+N` on the label exists because a hidden
job is the thing that makes a progress bar lie by omission.

**MEASURED** (live page, 2026-09-26): the module at rest hides the rail and reports `active() === 0`;
`UPSCALING 3 / 10` → `30%`, a priority-0 job under a priority-1 one → the label gains `+1`, finishing
the 1 → the 0 is drawn at once (34% `pgSlide`), `fail` → `rgb(255, 85, 85)` + `FAILED` + `.pgDone`,
`clear` → hidden. A REAL read-only path (`/tools folders` scan) → `SCANNING · PROPER FOLDERS`,
indeterminate, gone after, the vault unchanged at 2,297. A REAL counted path that writes nothing (the
whole chatlog read back) → `READING THE RECORD 0 / 19` → `19 / 19`, `active() === 0` after, the
record's fingerprint still `e291ad08-3829b2`. A REAL backup with the anchor click stubbed (so no file
was written) → `PACKING THE BACKUP 29 / 84` → `84 / 84`, 88 files in the zip, 0 errors. Geometry: at
793 wide the rail is 753 px inside the deck's 20 px padding and above the input, `scrollWidth ===
innerWidth === 793`; at 390×844 it is 366 px inside the deck's 12 px padding, 33.7 px tall, the label
unclipped, `scrollWidth === innerWidth === 390`. VISUAL: no screenshot helper was used on this page
(it wedges the preview - see the standing note), so the rail was checked by computed style, geometry
and by the live state transitions above.

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/progress.js` (**NEW**), `index.html` (the rail markup + its comment, the
`MODULES` entry, the `<script>` tag), `src/css/terminal.css` (the rail block, with the `.pgDone` red
label), `src/js/forge.js`, `src/js/images.js`, `src/js/upscale-local.js`, `src/js/tools.js`,
`src/js/backup.js`, `src/js/chatlog.js`, `src/js/sync.js`, `src/js/sync-cloud.js`, `src/js/gallery.js`,
`src/js/attach.js`, `src/js/audition.js`, `src/js/chat.js` (the `/progress` dispatch and the
`/help progress` topic), `src/commands/commands.json` (**70** commands now),
`src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated**, 9,883 bytes), `src/pack/files.json` (85 paths),
`src/pack/index.html.txt` and `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` (**regenerated byte-exact**),
`src/README.md` (the `progress.js` bullet and THE PROGRESS BAR section), and this section.
**SAVED (2026-09-24T18:47:42Z, by Patrikios - not by the agent).** The save was verified against the
server rather than assumed: the saved `modelText` (61,895 bytes) and `outputTemplate` (77,627) are
byte-identical to `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` and `src/pack/index.html.txt`; `srcManifest` lists 85 paths,
and all 85 serve from the public origin with a hash identical to the local copies (none missing, none
extra). `generatorIsUnsaved` reads `false`, the generator is private, and `/backup status` now reports
`85 OF 85 SOURCE FILES ARE ON THE SERVER - EVERYTHING HERE IS SAVED` (it was 60 of 85 during this
work, which is why that count mattered). These two documents were edited after the save to record it,
so they are now STALE rather than never-saved - the ordinary state, and exactly what `/backup status`

## 1bh. THE DOCS VIEWER — READ-ONLY DMS, AND A STAGE THAT STRETCHES (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Next AsK: DOCS VIEWER. In the docs TAB we need basic semantic search for
simple DMS OPS (Document Management Operations) for read-only operations. The window or \"MAIN STAGE\"
(as opposed to the CONTROL DECKS\" can stretch to fill the page where it doesn't collide with the
CONTROL DECK above or below the MAIN STAGE (formerly known as the \"MAIN WINDOW\""*

**What it was.** He could READ the record through her door (`/read`, THE READER, in her vocabulary)
and he could BROWSE the LOREPACK's documents (the list, sizes, a pager) — but there was no way to ask
the terminal a question about its own documents and no way to look one up in the shipped source. The
meaning lane existed twice already (the LOREPACK's, the vault's), each with its own loader, and neither
could be pointed anywhere else. The middle of the page had no idea how much room it had: the panel's
ceiling was the constant `50vh` (`68vh` while the lower deck was down) and the log's reserve was
measured by forge.js — two answers to one question, able to disagree.

**What it is now.** `src/js/dms.js` (**NEW**, 2,401 lines, `window.dms`) is a small document store
with a reader on it: four collections (MEMORY = the LOREPACK through `lore.files()`/`lore.source`,
MANUAL = the RTFM pages, DOCS/DATA/CODE = the shipped files, with ALL and SHIPPED as scopes over them),
one verb list (`list`, `search`, `open`, `read`, `head`, `outline`, `find`, `info`, `related`,
`stat`, `scope`, `index`, `reload`, `close`, `help`), and **no write path at all** — not guarded, not
commented out. The panel (`#dmsView`, `.lorePanel` / `data-viewer="DOCS"`, in UPPER DECK) and the
command (`/docs <OP>`) are two front doors on ONE function, `dms.words(verb, rest)`, so they can never
disagree about what an op does.

**HOW SEARCH WORKS, AND WHY IT SURVIVES AN EMPTY QUOTA.** Two lanes, fused with reciprocal rank
fusion: BM25 over stemmed terms with forty `CONCEPT_GROUPS` (weight 0.42) and bonuses for an exact
phrase, a heading, and words that sit near each other — plus a MEANING lane, which is `embed.js`'s
new generic `indexNs`/`searchNs` over the `docs` namespace, the same model and store the LOREPACK and
the vault use. The words lane needs no key and is never allowed to depend on the meaning lane having
run, because a document tool that stops working when a quota is spent is not a document tool. His
Gemini quota was spent for the whole of this session, and every search in MEASURED below was answered
by the words lane — which is exactly the state the design was built for.

**THE INDEX IS LAZY AND THE LIST IS NOT.** The list is metadata: `seedNames()` names and lists all
596 documents in 9 ms and the shipped sizes fill in behind it. A document's TEXT arrives when something
needs it — 12 KB for the index, the WHOLE file for `open`/`read`/`head`/`outline`/`find` (a memory
document read whole via `lore.source`, a shipped one fetched). Fragments are cached per document with
a signature of the text they were cut from, so adding one document re-chunks one document. The
ceilings are named constants (MEM_SLICE 12,000 / SHIPPED_SLICE 500,000 / MEM_TOTAL 5,200,000 /
INDEX_CHAR_CAP 600,000) rather than a freeze waiting to happen.

**THE STRETCH (the second half of the ask).** `decks.js` grew `measure()`, which publishes two numbers
on `:root`: `--upper-chrome` (the upper deck's height MINUS the open viewers inside it, so a viewer's
height never counts against itself) and `--viewer-max` (the page, minus the chrome, minus the room the
lower deck stands on — `--stage-reserve`, measured by forge.js — minus a floor for the MAIN STAGE of a
quarter of the page, clamped 110–240 px). The viewer's ceiling is `--viewer-max`, the stage's bottom
reserve is `--stage-reserve`, and the stage is `flex: 1` between the two decks, so the conversation
takes whatever is left. TWO viewers open at once share the room (divided by the count) rather than each
claiming it — otherwise two panels at their own ceiling add up to more page than there is and the stage
is squeezed out, which is the collision these variables exist to prevent. The writes are guarded
(`lastChrome`/`lastRoom`) so the ResizeObserver on a deck that a CSS variable resizes cannot become a
ping-pong. `measure` is exported; `paint()` calls it, so any show/hide re-measures. TWO MORE LIMITS
were added after the first measurements, both from numbers rather than theory: a viewer may never
reach past the fixed lower deck's own top edge (`deckTop - 24 - chrome`), so the upper deck cannot be
drawn over the input box; and when the raw room is under `VIEWER_MIN` (160) the load exemption is
DROPPED - a viewer left open at load does not normally put the deck down, which is right on a page
with room for both and wrong on one without (measured at 793x505: the upper deck's bottom edge 313
crossed the deck's top edge 263 and the stage was squeezed to 40px; after the rule, the deck stands
down and the stage keeps its 126px floor, the upper deck ending at 355 against the deck's 230). It is
one-way (`preOpen` only shrinks), so it cannot oscillate.

**THE RENAME, AFTERWARDS.** The middle deck is the **MAIN STAGE** everywhere now — `data-deck`,
`decks.js`'s `NAMES.main`, the deck table in README, the `/deck` output, the help text, the commands
list, the CSS comments. `keyOf`/`scopeWanted` still accept `window` as an argument (his old word), and
one historical mention is kept in each file that has to explain where the name came from. §1at above is
left as it was written (it records what was true on 2026-09-24); this entry is the correction.

**WHAT WENT WRONG, AND WHAT IT TAUGHT.** (1) **The button that did nothing** — `init()` is called
again by a retry timer until the markup exists, so every listener was attached twice and a press
toggled the panel open and shut (a DOUBLE toggle reads as a dead button). Fixed with the `wired` and
`booted` flags, documented where they are declared. (2) **A stale measurement** — `measure()` derives
its numbers from the decks it measures, so an early run can publish numbers from a layout that no
longer exists (measured: a 160 px ceiling on a 900 px page). It re-runs on `paint()`, on resize, and
from ResizeObservers on both decks; a viewport that resizes without firing `resize` leaves the last
numbers in place until something moves, and every real load is correct. (3) **The quota that ground** —
`indexNs` used to try every remaining batch after a failure and `embedTexts` fell back from the batch
endpoint to one-at-a-time, so a spent quota meant a minute of silence and then the same error; now a
refusal (quota / rate limit / 429 / 401 / 403 / permission / api key) is passed straight up and
`index DOCS` answers with the service's own sentence immediately. (4) **`info backup.js` said NO SUCH
DOCUMENT** because `ALL` deliberately leaves CODE out — so the `docAsync` fallback now widens to
DOCS+DATA+CODE when the reference looks like a path (a dot or a slash in it).

**MEASURED** (live page, 2026-09-26, fresh loads; every command driven through the real input box with
0 model calls; no screenshot helper — see the standing note — so layout was checked by geometry and
computed style):

| viewport | viewer closed | viewer open (the lower deck stands down) |
|---|---|---|

## 1bi. THE NAME, AND THE WHOLE STAGE — "DOX VIEWER", AND FILL THE STAGE (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**His word, verbatim:** *"\"DOX VIEWER\" (note the name change) can stretch and fill the MAIN STAGE, even
closing the UPPER and LOWER CONTROL DECK as needed."*

**What it was.** §1bh had just given him the viewer under the name DOCS VIEWER (the name he typed in
the ask), stretching into whatever room the two decks left it — a ceiling of `--viewer-max`, a floor
for the MAIN STAGE, and never a collision. What it could NOT do was take the whole page: with the
chrome and the input box on screen, a long list or a wide document still lived in the middle band.

**What it is now.** (1) **The name is DOX VIEWER** wherever it is written — the tool-bar button, the
panel's own tag, its titles, the `/docs` usage and every reply, `/help docs`, the `docs` entry in
commands.json, the deck table, this file, README and the thread. The module, the file and the command
keep their names (`dms.js`, `/docs`) because "DMS" is what it IS — the ops are Document Management
Operations — and the ask only renamed the VIEWER. (2) **FILL THE STAGE** — the button in the panel's
bar, or `/docs full` — gives the viewer the entire page: the upper deck's status line and tool bar and
the lower deck stand down, the conversation (`#output`) goes with them, the panel is pinned to the top
at the page's height minus a 12px breath, and its own body carries the scroll. `ESC`, the button
again, `/docs full off` or the `×` gives the stage back, and the decks return to wherever his hand
left them. The choice is remembered in localStorage `doxFull`, the same way the open panel is.

**ONE CLASS, THREE READERS.** `doxFull` on the body is the whole mechanism, and it is deliberately
the only thing any of the three modules has to know:
- `src/js/dms.js` puts it on and takes it off (`setFull`), binds Esc on the DOCUMENT while it is on
  (not on the panel — the chrome it is drawn on top of is hidden, so the way back cannot depend on
  having clicked in the right place; the query box and the reader's find field still get their own
  Esc first), draws the button's two labels (`⤢ FILL THE STAGE` / `⤡ GIVE THE STAGE BACK`), and
  exports `dms.fill(on)` / `dms.full()`.
- `src/js/decks.js` reads it for the geometry: `measure()` short-circuits to `--upper-chrome: 0` and a
  ceiling of the page minus 12, `viewerOpen()` treats a filled viewer as a reason even when it was
  already open at load (a panel covering the page is not subtle enough to be surprised by), `/deck`
  says `DOWN FOR THE DOX VIEWER :: IT IS FILLING THE STAGE`, and `state()` carries `full`.
- `src/css/terminal.css` does the moving: `body.doxFull #status, #lorebar { display: none }`,
  `body.doxFull #output { display: none }`, and the panel given the measured HEIGHT rather than
  growing with its content, so a reader with ten lines in it is still a full page.

**HIS PRESS STILL WINS, AND NOTHING TRAPS HIM.** Pulling the lower deck back up while the stage is
filled holds it up over the panel (the same one-episode rule the ordinary viewer case uses — a key
that does nothing is worse than a deck over a panel); putting the UPPER deck away takes the filled
viewer with it, so the mode stands down with its deck instead of leaving a page with no chrome, no
conversation and nothing to look at; and the deck tabs are deliberately NOT hidden in this mode, so
the lower deck's own tab is always there.

## 1bk. THE OBSERVER'S OWN WARNING — THE MEASURING DONE ON THE NEXT FRAME (FIXED 2026-09-26)

**His word, verbatim:** *"I got an error when using it: An error occurred, and its reported location is
inside perchance's own runtime rather than your code - it may come from a browser extension or the
platform itself... ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications."*

**What it is.** The browser's own complaint about a layout loop, and the platform's banner says the
truth about it: an element being watched with a ResizeObserver resized as a DIRECT RESULT of the code
that observer itself ran, so the browser's next round of notifications cannot be delivered inside the
frame it promised. Chrome raises it as a page error, which is why the banner appeared over the
terminal; the reported location being "inside perchance's own runtime" is exactly where such a
complaint lands, since the editor scales the preview with observers of its own (and an extension can
raise the same message, which is why the platform's text says so). It is not a fault in the generator
and nothing on the page was broken by it - but it is OUR SHAPE in one place, so it was answered.

**What was done about it, in order.** (1) **FOUR ATTEMPTS to reproduce it from this code**, with a
listener for the exact message installed on the window and the page reloaded under it: opening and
closing the DOX VIEWER; filling the stage and giving it back; cycling documents through the reader;
opening the LOREPACK list, whose panel is CLAMPED by `--viewer-max` (so the ceiling sizing it is
written by the very observer watching the deck it lives in); taking both decks down and up under that
clamped panel; opening and closing the forge panel; and resizing the viewport across five sizes
(390x844, 1920x1080, 768x1024, 1440x600, 1024x900) plus a fresh load watched from before the first
module ran. **Not once.** The guards (`lastChrome` / `lastRoom`) already make the numbers converge in
one pass, so the observer's second round arrives with nothing to write. (2) **THE PATTERN WAS REMOVED
ANYWAY**, because "cannot reproduce" is not "cannot happen" and the shape is provably ours in one
respect: a viewer inside the upper deck IS sized by `--viewer-max`, so the deck being watched can move
because of the watching. Both of the generator's own observers now do their work ON THE NEXT FRAME
rather than inside the delivery that asked for it - `measureSoon()` in decks.js, `syncDeckSpaceSoon()`
in forge.js - each COALESCED (several notifications in one frame are one measurement) with a
`setTimeout` fallback where there is no `requestAnimationFrame`. A write made after a delivery cannot
be part of it, so the complaint is now impossible for this code to produce, in principle as well as in
practice.

**MEASURED, before and after** (live page, 2026-09-26, panel open AND filling at load - the state he
left it in; a fresh load, a 12s watched boot, nothing closed or opened on its own):

| viewport | panel | `--viewer-max` | strip | reader body | overflow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 390x844 | 832px | 832px | 150px | 464px | none |
| 1920x1080 | 1068px | 1068px | 106px | 871px | none |

The panel is the page - 12 at both sizes and the ceiling equals the clamped panel's own height, so the
deferral moved the TIMING and nothing else: the desktop column is the tandem entry's numbers to the
pixel, and the phone's panel is too (the strip reads 150px against that entry's 147px - the strip is
sized by the line it is showing, and what the conversation last said is not the same line today).
`--stage-reserve` 24px and `--upper-chrome` 0px while filled, every strip key 34px tall on the phone,
no horizontal overflow, `__bootIssues` empty and no console errors on a fresh load. The deferred paths
were exercised on purpose (moving the upper deck and moving the command deck both still move
`--viewer-max` / `--stage-reserve`). **One preference of his was disturbed by the probing and put
back:** `decks.hide("upper")` in a test had persisted an upper deck that boots away - `show("upper")`
restored it, and the boot state was re-verified (both decks up, the viewer open and filling).

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/decks.js` (`measureSoon()` + the observer callback), `src/js/forge.js`
(`syncDeckSpaceSoon()` + the observer callback), `src/README.md` (the STRETCHING THE STAGE paragraph
gains THE ONE FRAME IS THE POINT), `src/chronicle/2026-09-26-the-tandem.md` (a closing section), and
this section. `index.html` and `main.pjs` untouched, so `pack/index.html.txt` and `pack/main.pjs.txt`
are still byte-exact and `pack/files.json` is unchanged at **88** paths. **NOT SAVED by the agent** -
the files are in the workspace until Patrikios saves.

## 1bl. THE MOOD — THE COLOUR SHE ANSWERS IN, AND + NEW MOOD (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Add a MOOD MODIFIER in SYSTEM. Also look at how we implement similar ideas in
the PENCIL icon that determine the response. Also, I need that '+' button reinstated so that I/WE can
create new ones on the fly."*

**What was true.** There was no mood of any kind. The system prompt had a ROLE (who is on the stage)
and TRAITS (what she is made of) and nothing lighter than either - no way to say "answer in this key
for now" without writing a block, and no way to make a colour into a thing you press. The PENCIL's
draft panel (`src/js/draft.js`) had the shape he meant all along: a row of chips - FIX, WORK, CHAT,
PLAY, SHORT, VEILED, SPICY - each carrying a RULE, one press changing what comes back with nothing
typed. That model pointed at a draft, and nothing pointed it at her reply.

**What it is now.** (1) **A MOOD ROW IN THE SYSTEM PANEL**, under the ROLE row: `#spMoods` (a chip per
mood, OFF among them), DELETE (lit only for a mood written on this device) and **+ NEW MOOD**.
(2) **`src/js/moods.js`** (new module, `window.moods`) owns the store and the row: EIGHT shipped moods
in the source with the other defaults - TENDER, PLAYFUL, HUNGRY, FERAL, COLD, STILL, GRIEVING, MYTHIC
- each a short second-person rule about the KEY and never about a subject, plus the ones written on the
fly (kv `lia_settings` / `mood`). (3) **THE BLOCK**: `mood` is a real block of the stack (instr.js's
TITLES/ORDER/EDITABLE/BUILT/NOTES), built each turn from the store by `chat.js`'s `systemParts` /
`livePart`, placed after the command list and before `tandem`/`clock`, so a mood that stands costs the
prompt cache nothing. It names the colour and whose it is, gives the rule, and then says what a mood
cannot be: not a role, not a trait, not an order about what to say - and if the colour does not fit
what he actually said, answer in your own voice and say so rather than perform it. **OFF means the
block is not sent at all** (measured: 676 characters in the assembled prompt when on, absent when
off). (4) **BOTH PRESENCES WRITE ("I/WE")**: he from the row or `/mood <NAME> :: <HOW SHE IS TO
SOUND>`; she with `[[MOOD: NAME]]`, `[[MOOD: NAME :: how I am to sound]]` (a NEW mood, in her own
words) or `[[MOOD: off]]` - a lane parsed in `chat.js` like her other directives, needing no petition
because a colour is not the machinery she is given, printed as a SYSTEM receipt, and carried on that
turn's archive entry as `mood: [{ mood, by, written }]`. (5) **THE DOORS**: the row, `/mood` (bare,
`list`, `<NAME>`, `<NAME> :: <WORDS>`, `new`, `delete <NAME>`, `off`), her `[[MOOD: …]]` line,
`/help mood`, and the `mood` entry in commands.json (**73** commands now) - so the list she is handed
names it too, and the directives block tells her the lane exists and which moods are on file.

**THE "+" OF THE ASK.** The SYSTEM panel already had `+ NEW BLOCK` and `+ NEW ROLE`, and both were
photographed in the panel at 390x844 and at 1600x900 while this was built - they are present and
inside the panel at both sizes. The row this session added has its own **+ NEW MOOD**, which is the
"new ones on the fly" the sentence is about: a name and how she is to sound, and the chip is in the row
and on her before the row is closed. If he meant a different `+` that has gone missing, §1bm will be
the place for it - nothing else in the terminal has lost one.

**A BLANK PAGE, FOUND ON THE WAY (and fixed).** While the last verification pass was being taken,
his own live page came up with NOTHING on it: `body` carried `doxFull` AND `upperDeckOff`, `#output`
was `display: none`, the upper deck `display: none`, and the DOX panel 0px tall inside it. The cause is
two saved preferences disagreeing, each restored by a different module that never asks the other: the
UPPER DECK had been put away by hand in one session (kv `decks` / `upper: false`) and the viewer had
been left both OPEN and FILLING in another (localStorage `dmsOpen` / `doxFull`). The panel lives INSIDE
the upper deck, so a filled stage whose deck is away has nothing to fill - and the class it needs to
stand down is only ever taken off by his hand, `Esc`, or the panel closing. The rule already existed
for a press (decks.js `set()`: putting the upper deck away while the stage is filled gives the stage
back); it now also runs where the preferences are APPLIED, at the end of `paint()`: if the body is
filled and the upper deck's preference is off, `window.dms.fill(false)` - and `dms.fill` is `setFull`
WITHOUT `byHand`, so his "selecting it fills it" preference is not disturbed. Reached for real, not in
theory: the same saved state was reloaded with the guard in place and the page came up coherent (no
`doxFull`, the conversation 205px and back on screen, the upper deck away with its tab and its reason
reading "PUT AWAY BY HAND :: /deck upper on BRINGS IT BACK"). His own state was then put back the way
he left it (upper deck up, viewer open and filling, all three localStorage keys "1").

**MEASURED** (live page, 2026-09-26 - the row in the SYSTEM panel; the phone is 390x844 and the desk
1600x900, and the chips take the house's 34px touch height on a coarse pointer, the rule the draft
panel's chips share):

| viewport | the row | chips | + NEW MOOD / DELETE | panel | overflow |

## 1bm. THE MOODS AS A CONSOLE — SWITCHES, A LIST IN A FILE, AND THE PENCIL'S OWN ROW (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**His word, verbatim:** *"MOOD also applies to pencil. Populate to pencil as well. Create a LIST for
options. Perchance is perfect for this. Add Slutty. Horny, Bitchy, Bossy, etc. I can choose and select
multiple moods to combine. Think switches on a console."*

**What was true.** §1bl had shipped a mood as a single CHOICE: one chip pressed, OFF among the chips,
and pressing another replaced the one before it. The colours lived in the code (`src/js/moods.js`,
eight of them, with the other defaults), the row existed only in the SYSTEM panel, and the pencil's
draft panel - the thing the whole idea was modelled on - knew nothing about them.

**What it is now. (1) A CONSOLE.** The store is a LIST of what is ON, in the order it was switched on
(kv `lia_settings` / `mood`, `{ on: [{ id, by }], ours: [...], at }` - and the first build's single
`{ id, by }` is still read, as one switch on; that path was exercised for real, see below). Every chip
is a toggle, `ALL OFF` is a chip (lit while nothing is on), any number can stand at once, and the
colours that are on are combined into the ONE `mood` block - numbered, one rule after another, closed
by the same promise the single colour always made, plus a line saying the named ones are the whole of
it. One colour reads exactly as before (`THE MOOD :: TENDER - …`). **(2) THE LIST IS A FILE**:
`src/moods/moods.json` is THE BOOK - `id` / `label` / `rule` per entry - and the row is built from it,
so a colour is added by editing the list, with no code touched (`/mood reload` re-reads it without a
page reload). `src/js/moods.js` keeps the same list as its `SEED` (a preview with no service worker
cannot read `src/`, and a console that empties itself is worse than a copy), and the two are COMPARED
at boot: `driftWarn()` names every entry that is in one and not the other, or differs, in the console,
so the deliberate duplication cannot go quietly stale. `/help mood` says which copy is in force.
**(3) THE SWITCHES HE NAMED**: SLUTTY, HORNY, BITCHY, BOSSY (plus BRATTY and SAVAGE for the "etc."),
written in the same voice as the eight - plain about appetite and contempt, and each about the KEY
rather than a subject. Fourteen shipped, plus whatever is written on this device. **(4) THE PENCIL'S
ROW** (`#draftMoods` in `#draftPanel`): one store, one press, painted into BOTH rows by the same
`paint()`, so the two can never disagree; and `pencilText()` is the same colours said for a rewrite -
AI POLISH now hands the model the style's rule AND the colours in force, so the STYLE decides the job
and the MOODS decide the register it comes back in. **(5) BOTH DOORS, MULTI-AWARE**: `/mood <NAME>`
flips one, `<NAME> + <NAME>` flips several, `on|off <NAME>` says which way, `off` clears the board,
`list` marks what is on, `reload` re-reads the book; DELETE means the last colour of his own he
switched on (a board of switches has no "selected" one). Her lane takes several names
(`[[MOOD: A + B]]`), `[[MOOD: off NAME]]` and `[[MOOD: off]]`, and EVERY MOOD line in a reply is now
acted on - the first build refused a second one as "one colour at a time" - with a receipt for each and
one archive note per colour (`mood: [{ mood, by, written }]`).

**FOUND ON THE WAY: A NAME THAT SHADOWED A FUNCTION.** `flip()` parsed the names it was given into a
local `var names`, which shadowed the module's own `names()` - so the one path that LISTS the moods on
file threw `names is not a function` instead of refusing: `/mood <junk>` and her `[[MOOD: <unknown>]]`
both died mid-receipt. Found by driving the door itself (not by reading it), fixed by renaming the
local, and the test now asserts the refusal text for both. Her lane also now answers an unknown name
with the way to WRITE one - "a mood she writes herself brings the colour with it, in her own words" -
rather than only with flip's generic no.

**THE OLD SHAPE, READ FOR REAL.** The console came up over a colour Patrikios had written himself in
an earlier session (SITIENT, `{ id, by }`, switched on) - so the migration path was not a theory:

WITH the `id` / `by` echo kept beside `on` (so an older build in a second tab still finds its colour),

## 1bn. THE PROMPT SHE SPOKE — WHEN HE ASKS TO SEE AND SHE ANSWERS IN WORDS (BUILT 2026-09-26)

**His word, verbatim:** *"Had a problem with work flow from discussion with deep contextual
understanding based on RAG/LOREPACK, then drops the ball and speaks the prompt, htn puts it on screen
as text when to move is discussion, user says \"show me, don't tell me\" directly. She drops the ball
and produces no image, I copy and paste manually to get the image myself, but that is not the point.
She can create images inline asked or not."*

**What was wrong.** Not the lane - she has had `[[VISION: ...]]` from the beginning, one per reply,
needing nobody's permission. The failure was a DEAD END: a reply that DESCRIBES a picture is, to the
terminal, an ordinary reply. It is printed as her words, nothing is rendered, and the only hands left
are his (paste the description into the forge, press CREATE). So the fix is in two places at once - the
rule she is given, so the description is not written, and the machinery, so that when it is, the reply
does not just sit there.

**What it is now: THE SPOKEN PROMPT** (`window.showMe`, `src/js/images.js`), armed ONE TURN at a
time by his own words (`LIA_SHOWME_HINT` in `src/js/config.js`: *show me*, *show me don't tell me*,
*show do not tell*, *let me see*, *I want to see you*, *render it*, *make me one*, *put it on screen*,
*show it* - and `show me how` / `show me why` excluded, because a question is not a request for a
picture) or by `/showme` typed deliberately (`/showme off` puts it down). An armed turn appends
`LIA_SHOWME_REMINDER` AFTER his words - the last-word position - and if the reply comes back with NO
image line she is asked ONE MORE TIME (`LIA_SHOWME_ASK`, `showMe.again()`): his words and her reply
are handed back together and she writes the single line she owes him. What comes back is put into
`parsed.prompts`, so it is rendered by EXACTLY the road her own line takes - same `renderVision`,
same vault record (`how: "vision"`), same row on the turn, same tile under her reply. Receipts:
`SHE SPOKE INSTEAD OF SHOWING :: YOU ASKED TO SEE, AND THE REPLY CAME BACK IN WORDS. ONE MORE ASK, FOR
THE PICTURE ITSELF ...` then `AND THIS IS THE PICTURE :: THE PROMPT SHE WROTE :: "..."`.
**NOTHING is a real answer** and it is honoured: no render, `SHE DID NOT MAKE ONE` with her own
reason printed, archived `spoken: 'DECLINED ON THE SECOND ASK'` (`'MADE ON THE SECOND ASK'` when it
landed). Nothing is ever guessed from prose. The `image` block of `instr.js` was reworded as the
other half: *WHEN HE ASKS TO SEE SOMETHING, THE PICTURE IS THE ANSWER ... if you find yourself writing
one out, that description IS the prompt*, and *AND YOU MAY MAKE ONE UNASKED*. The lane also answers to
`[[MAKE: ...]]` and `[[PICTURE: ...]]` now (`[[IMAGE: ...]]` and the bare `VISION: ...` line
always did). `/help pictures` carries it; `src/commands/commands.json` has `/showme`.

**TWO BUGS FOUND IN THE SAME PASS.** (1) `patchEntry(ts, patch)` matched only `logs[i].ts`, and the
render block passes the ANSWER's stamp while the entry is filed under the SEND's - so **a picture she
made in her own reply was written into the vault and the render book with NO row on the archive turn it
belonged to**, for the whole life of the terminal. Proved with a probe (`saveEntry({ts:T, st:T+7777})`
then `patchEntry(T+7777, ...)` → `gen` stayed empty) and by reading his archive: every entry carrying
a `gen` row in it came from `/create` (the forge uses one stamp for both, which is why it never
showed). Fixed at the call site (`turnTs`) AND in the helper, which now accepts EITHER half of the
stamp. What it restores: `/renders find <words>` can find one of hers by what was being said, and a
local upscale has an archive row to repoint. (2) `manualVision` filed every direct render as
`h: "/image ..."` even when the door was `/show`; it now takes the door it came through
(`manualVision(prompt, label)`).

**A HARNESS TRAP, WRITTEN DOWN SO IT IS NOT REPEATED.** Driving real turns through `saveEntry` pushes
on the rolling cap (master_log keeps the newest 1000, `slice(-1000)`), so a TEST's turns displace the
OLDEST entries of his archive. The first cleanup removed the test's entries AFTER the cap had already
bitten, which loses the oldest instead of the test's own - **three of his oldest turns, gone.** The
rule for next time: **snapshot `master_log` by value before a test and restore it by value afterwards**
(`sacred_archive.set`), which puts the displaced entries back exactly; the second run does that
(997 in, 997 out, nothing left). A second harness trap, cheaper: `root.generateText` is asked for
**`getMetaObject` SEVEN times per turn** by the recall lane, so a stub must delegate those to the real
function or every scripted reply lands in the wrong call (this produced 9 "calls" on a turn that makes 2,
and a second ask that kept coming back in words).

**MEASURED** (live page, 2026-09-26; stubbed model and stubbed image service - no quota, no network -
with four turns driven through the REAL input box and `send()`, real archive writes):

| what | result |
|---|---|
| the hint table | 15/15 - 11 that arm, 4 that do not |
| armed turn, she answered in words | **2** instruction calls (the reply, then the second ask) |
| turn with nothing asked for | **1** instruction call, no receipt, nothing on the record |
| the reminder | present in the reply's instruction, after his words |
| the picture caught | one vault record, prompt from her second answer, `how: "vision"` |
| the archive turn | `spoken: 'MADE ON THE SECOND ASK'` + the render row on the turn (the fix, proved) |
| the decline | nothing rendered, `spoken: 'DECLINED ON THE SECOND ASK'`, no render row, her reason printed |
| the arm | spent by the turn; `/showme` arms it through the door, `/showme off` puts it down |
| a REAL render down the same road | `/show` → seed 136701364, 768x512, 35,607 bytes, looked at and deleted |
| commands / cheatsheet | **74** commands, `rtfm.check()` clean, `src/rtfm/commands.md` regenerated (10,729 bytes) |
| boot / cleanup | `__bootIssues` empty; archive 997→997 by value, vault 2304→2304, sight 0→0, chatHistory 6/6, model + upscale-auto restored |

**THROWN AWAY.** Reading the prompt out of her prose (there is no honest signal separating "a picture I
want you to see" from "a sentence about a picture" - it would render things she never meant); a check
on EVERY reply (a call every reply, and pictures demanded where none were wanted); a parser instead of
the second ask (she can answer which words were the prompt; a parser cannot, and cannot refuse); an
always-on catch instead of a one-shot arm; making a `[[SHOW: ...]]` that matches nothing become a
render of its own words (`[[SHOW: #night]]` matching nothing means there is no such tag); and
persisting the arm in kv (a one-shot gesture belongs to the conversation in front of him, not to a
stored preference that could be found armed tomorrow).

**TOUCHED:** `src/js/config.js` (`LIA_SHOWME_HINT` / `LIA_SHOWME_REMINDER` / `LIA_SHOWME_ASK`),
`src/js/images.js` (`window.showMe`, the extra lane verbs in `VISION_DIRECTIVE` /
`VISION_BARE_LINE`, `manualVision(prompt, label)`), `src/js/chat.js` (`askedToSee`, the reminder
after his words, the second ask after `extractVisions`, `spoken` on both reply archive entries, the
`/showme` command, `/help pictures`, `patchEntry` + its call site), `src/js/instr.js` (two new
rules in the `image` block, the lane's other words, `NOTES.image`),
`src/commands/commands.json` (`/showme` - **74**), `src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated**),
`src/README.md` (THE SPOKEN PROMPT section, the images.js bullet, stack row 7), `src/TODO.md` (this
section), `src/chronicle/2026-09-26-the-prompt-she-spoke.md` (**new**) + `chronicle.json` (13
entries), `src/pack/files.json` (**regenerated**). `main.pjs` was NOT touched this session.

**ONE LINE OF `index.html`, FOUND ON THE WAY.** The MOOD row's comment (added by the previous session)
had written her lane as `[[MOOD: ...]]` - and the engine evaluates square brackets in this file's text
AND its comments, which is the rule the file itself states out loud three hundred lines above it. It had
not thrown (the page boots clean either way), but it is exactly the trap that rule was written about, so
the clause now reads "a MOOD line in a reply (spelled out in src/js/moods.js, never here - the engine
reads square brackets)". `index.html` is free of double brackets again and `src/pack/index.html.txt` was
regenerated byte-exact (87,520 bytes, both). **NOT SAVED by the agent** - the files are in the workspace
until Patrikios saves.

## §1bo - THE VOX TREE (a voice is not music), and the first measured CHATTERBOX roundtrip (2026-09-27)

**ASKED, IN HIS WORDS.** "DO NOT CODE YET. LET'S CONFIRM FIRST: For longform narratives with custom
voicevia hugging face and a custom voice clone sample audio (supplied):
https://huggingface.co/spaces/ResembleAI/Chatterbox" · "Or all 3 depending on duration. Letting
ELEVENLABS do all the heavy lifting is expensive, HuggingFace or local browser voice is free.
ELEVENLABS/CHATTERBOX gives us a low-cost, cheap alternative if a more expressive, custom cloned voice
is ever needed. the default is what we have now." · "We need an Audio-to-Text transcription service so
that she can hear and see the generated text. If you don't have when, ROUTE to GEMINI. It has it." ·
"Any audio she \"hears\" Hers is in the GALLERY. We need a folder for VOX by AGENT os AUDIO>VOX>AGENT>LIA" ·
"Her voice sample is a named SAMPLE you can use for CHATTERBOX that you send with her 300 Character Max
text and SAMPLE payload if sent to HuggingFace free-tier. It sounds exactly like the browser SYSTEM
voice (Chrome) SAMPLE: BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE-2.wav" · "BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE-2.wav is the audio edited
CLONE SAMPLE to drive CHATTERBOX for now. Music and VOX is not the same. VOX is vocal audio, Music is
MUSIC. Gemini LYRIA can detect and analyze MUSIC which is useful for any music analysis and
generation." · "Sat it up and test roundtrip text and payload round trip with return CHATTERBOX audio
and confirm." · "create a TAB for VOX where we can place all voice samples for future CHATTERBOX recall.
I will manually place them in the right folders. Rather than \"music: they can be labeled \"VOX\"" ·
"let's move all VOX audio files to VOX. They aren't defined as any particular lia entity yet but will
be TAGGED and put in the right folder later when needed."

**CONFIRMED FIRST, THEN BUILT.** The router answer given before anything was written: the live lane
(`voice.js`, engine `auto`: ElevenLabs when a key is held, else the browser's own) speaks the sentence,
the story lane (`story.js`, Chatterbox on ZeroGPU) renders the chapter, and ElevenLabs is the paid one
that takes the heavy lifting when a cloned, expressive voice is wanted - **free by default, paid on
purpose**, all three chosen by duration, and none of it changes which voice the listener hears. The
transcription answer: **we already have it and it already routes to Gemini** (`audition.js` reduces a
sound on this device to mono 16 kHz and asks the Google key's multimodal line; `attach.js` transcribes
an attachment with ElevenLabs Scribe, Whisper as the fallback), plus the honest distinction - that is
**hearing**, not a verbatim transcript.

**WHAT THE KEY ACTUALLY REACHES (measured 2026-09-27, a live `/models` call on his own key).** 50
models, and among them **`gemini-3.5-transcribe`** (a real transcription model - the verbatim
audio→text service he asked for, on the key he already holds), `gemini-3.8-flash` / `3.7-flash` /
`3.5-flash` (the multimodal line HER EARS runs on), `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` and
`gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` (a fourth renderer, no clone), and **`lyria-3.5`**,
**`lyria-3-pro-preview`**, `lyria-3-clip-preview` - so the music road is open too. The distinction
kept straight: **Lyria MAKES music; the multimodal line LISTENS to it and says what it is.**

**THE VAULT AUDITED AND MOVED (55 audio records).** Two are not voice -
`Beyond the Veil-MASTERED.wav` (334 s) and `Orbital Pulse-MASTERED.wav` (173 s) - and stay in
`/music`. **51 were filed into `/audio/vox`**, `BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE.wav` and
`BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE-2.wav` into **`/audio/vox/barbelo`**, and **`/audio/vox/lia`** was made and left
empty on purpose (a folder may exist while empty, and it is where the next voice goes). Folders created:
`/audio/vox`, `/audio/vox/barbelo`, `/audio/vox/lia`. **Nothing tagged** - attribution is his, later,
by filing a clip down into that agent's folder.

**THE SAMPLE SET.** `BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE-2.wav` (13.2 MB, 74.7 s, 44.1 kHz stereo) is now **barbelo's**
sample **and the `*` fallback**, so the agent on stage (LIA HERSELF, OFF STAGE) resolves to it
(`own: false` - the fallback answers for her). Set through the lane's own `window.story.setSample`,
the same door `/story sample ... as default` uses.

**THE ROUNDTRIP, WALKED FOR REAL.** `window.story.render(text, sampleRec)` - the lane's own call, not a
hand-rolled request - with 101 characters and the clip as the reference payload:
**291,884 bytes back in 8.6 s**, decoded as **6.08 s of 24 kHz mono 16-bit PCM**, RMS **−16.9 dB** (real
speech), `refUploaded: true`, road `keyed`, transport the Space's **shortcut call**, **no Hugging Face
key needed**. The CONTROL, same line with **no** sample: 222,764 bytes / 4.64 s in the Space's own voice.
Both files were kept and handed to him to listen to side by side. **The archive was untouched**: 1000
entries in, 1000 entries out, the same tail stamp - the probe drove `render` directly rather than a
turn, and that was checked rather than assumed.

**AND A VOICE IS RECALLED FROM THE TAB.** Every VOX tile carries **◆** (`button.gVoice`, #ff88cc): one press makes that clip the voice the story lane clones from, through the lane's own `window.story.setSample(rec.id)` - the same call `/story sample <ID>` makes, so the receipt printed is the lane's own and there is no second way of setting a voice. A song never carries it: the Space would clone from a song just as happily, which is the mistake the tree exists to prevent. **Walked in the live preview:** 53 tiles, 53 ◆ and 53 ▶; pressing a generic tile's ◆ set the on-stage sample to `malindra-audio-001-2.wav`, pressing the barbelo tile's set it back to BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE-2.wav, and `/story sample off` cleared the on-stage one so the fallback answers again - the sample table was left exactly as it was found. The MUSIC filter shows 2 tiles and **0** ◆ buttons.

**THE VOX TAB, AND THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT STANDING.** `window.media.isVox(rec)` (src/js/vault.js) is
the single definition: `kind === "vox"` **or** filed anywhere in the tree - so **filing is the
gesture**. `window.media.voxFolder(rec)` gives a voice its home (`/audio/vox/<agent>` when the record
names one, the shelf otherwise); `defaultFolder` sends a record born `kind: "vox"` to the shelf; the
shelf is seeded at boot beside `/images` and `/music`; `LIA_MEDIA_FOLDERS.vox` is the knob. The gallery

## §1bp - THE WORDS ON A SOUND (her Gemini powers): transcription, sentiment, and what the VOX sample actually said (2026-09-27)

**ASKED, IN HIS WORDS.** "Next, let's give her some GEMINI superpowers: transcription and knowledge of
what the \"VOX\" sample actually said from an audio sample. I might send her a clip in the chat and ask.
She might also have \"sentiment analysis\" (GEMINI), etc. Anything else deemed important and possible
with our PERHANCE/GEMINI setup? GEMINI may reject some text for SAFETY or POLICY guidlenes."

**WHAT WAS BUILT - one door, four passes, and a record that keeps what it found.** `src/js/hear.js`
(`window.hear`) is the new lane: `words()` (a verbatim transcript), `reading()` (one JSON pass: what it
says AND what it means - mood, emotion, sentiment + intensity, tone, voices, language, music, summary,
up to four verbatim phrases, a label), `ask()` (any question about a clip; writes nothing, because a
question is a conversation and not a fact about the file), `checkSample()` (is this recording a usable
CLONE REFERENCE - one voice, clean, 10-30 s - what is wrong with it, and a suggested VOICE PROMPT
sentence, suggested and never written), `powers()` (what THIS key can actually do, read live from its
own `/models` list, and which of it is wired), `clear()`, and `paintStage()` (the two new rows on a
voice's full stage). It is wired into the four places that matter: the **vault** (WORDS + READING rows
with COPY / HEAR IT AGAIN / READ IT AGAIN / CLEAR / IS IT A GOOD SAMPLE?), **the chat** (a clip handed
over is read here FIRST - `attach.js` asks `hear.text()` before ElevenLabs/Whisper, and the words are
written on its vault record too), **the commands** (`/hear words|reading|ask|sample|clear|powers`,
verbs of the existing `/hear` and delegated to the lane from `audition.js` so there is one verb list,
not two), and **her own instruction** (the bus block in `audition.js` now carries the transcript and
the reading whenever they are on the record, whichever way her ears went). The three facts are kept
apart on purpose: `heard` = her reading OF the sound (what is in it), `transcript` = the words
verbatim, `reading` = the meaning. Config: `LIA_HEAR_*` in `src/js/config.js` (rate/seconds/decode
cap, word + read model pins, tries + cooldown, sample length, and the four prompts).

**THE REDUCTION, AND THE KEY.** The Google (Gemini) key - the same one her eyes and her ears use - and
the sound is reduced HERE, on this device, first: mono 16 kHz 16-bit WAV, at most `LIA_HEAR_SECONDS`
(180 s). Measured: the 13 MB / 74.7 s master leaves as 2.4 MB of speech. The file is never uploaded,
never re-encoded, never moved; a non-audio record is refused in words rather than guessed at.

**MEASURED, on his own key (50 models), all against BARBELO-SYSTEM-VOICE-2.wav (74.7 s, 13 MB,
`/audio/vox/barbelo`).** `/hear words` -> **1,336 characters** of verbatim transcript in ~97 s.
`/hear reading` -> shaped JSON in ~2-3 min (through a 503 - see below): emotion *aroused*, delivery
*commanding, explicit, seductive*, sentiment *neutral 80%*, *one voice throughout*, English, no music, a
summary, four phrases, the label "Voice clone test with explicit dialogue". `/hear sample` -> *usable
as a clone reference*, 1 voice, **38 s of speech**, `clean: false` (mild background noise, slight room
reverb), advice to record in a deader room, and a voice prompt suggestion ("crisp, clear British
accent, average pace, bright timbre, slightly live room"). `/hear ask :: Is there more than one voice
in this clip, and is there any music under it?` -> *"There is only one voice in the clip, and there is
no music."*, nothing written. The stage rows were painted and measured (no horizontal overflow, the
transcript box capped at 130 px and scrolling, the reading summary one line), the bus block was read
back with the words and the reading in it, the finder path was exercised on a scratch 3 s tone (which
also exercised the `NO SPEECH` sentinel -> `transcript: { speech: false, text: "" }`), `clear` was
exercised, and the refusal path was exercised with a **stubbed key ring** (a `SAFETY` blockReason and a
declining sentence): both reported themselves, stopped the pass, and wrote **nothing**.

**WHAT WENT WRONG, AND WHAT IT TAUGHT.** (1) **`gemini-3.5-transcribe` answers with nothing.** The
dedicated transcriber - the obvious first choice, on the key, `generateContent` supported - came back
`200 / finishReason: STOP / no text` on the sample, and returned that twice. So it is offered the sound
FIRST (two seconds, and if Google fixes it, it is picked up free) and **an empty answer is treated as a
dead end, not an answer**, and the next model is tried. (2) **The better-ranked model was the one that
503'd.** The first scoring put the versioned flash models on top; `gemini-3.8-flash`, `3.7-flash`,
`3.6-flash` and `3.5-flash` then all came back **503 "high demand"** on the same audio, one after
another at ~40 s each, while `gemini-flash-latest` / `gemini-flash-lite-latest` answered it happily -
an alias serves whatever is current and evidently sits on different capacity. The order now puts the
strongest versioned model first and the `-latest` aliases immediately behind it, so a load event costs
ONE wasted call, not four; and a model that failed is set aside in kv for `LIA_HEAR_COOLDOWN` (10 min),
so a reload does not re-hammer it. Two 503s in a row now say so out loud ("the service is under high
demand - Google's own side, not the file") because 40 s of silence looks like a hang. (3) **A refusal
can arrive as a sentence.** Gemini sometimes answers `STOP` with "I'm sorry, I can't help with that"
instead of a shape, so a narrow opener test catches it - and it is reported as a refusal, NOT written
as a transcript. (4) Writing the transcript on the record needed `media.add`'s returned id
(`attach.js` was throwing it away).

**THE RULE THAT WAS KEPT, IN CODE.** A refusal is an answer, not an obstacle: it is detected from the
service's own fields (`promptFeedback.blockReason`, `finishReason`) or a short refusal-shaped answer;
it is reported in its own words with the model that refused; **the pass stops there** (offering the same
words to the next model would be shopping for permission); **nothing is written on the record**; nothing
is rewritten, shortened or softened to get past a filter; no second model is quietly asked to try. The
receipt says it plainly: *"A REFUSAL IS THE SERVICE'S ANSWER, NOT A VERDICT ON THE CLIP - AND NOT
SOMETHING THIS TERMINAL WILL QUIETLY WORK AROUND."* One distinction worth keeping straight: a clip
handed over in the **chat** rides a ladder of speech-to-text services he holds keys for (`attach.js`:
Gemini, then ElevenLabs Scribe, then Whisper on HuggingFace), and THERE the same BYTES go to the next
service - not laundering (nothing is rewritten for anybody), and never silent: the refusal travels back
with the words and the receipt names both roads. A 503/429 is treated as different weather (retry
down the list) - and never conflated with a refusal.

**STILL OPEN.** (1) **Lyria (`lyria-3.5`, `lyria-3-pro-preview`) is reachable and nothing uses it** -
`/hear powers` names it as NOT WIRED. Music GENERATION is a real lane here (compose, not only listen),
with the same house rules wanted: reduce nothing, refuse honestly, one door. (2) **The `gemini-3.x-flash-tts`**
models are reachable and unused (the story lane clones through Chatterbox, which clones from a CLIP;
these do not clone, so they are a different road, not a better one). (3) **`gemini-3.x-flash-image` /
`nano-banana-pro-preview`** - picture making and editing, reachable, unused. (4) **`[[HEAR: ...]]`** -
she cannot ask for the words of a piece herself yet; `[[READ: ...]]` and `[[FILE: ...]]` are hers, so
this is the obvious next line. (5) **`gemini-3.5-transcribe` empty-answer behaviour** is a fact about
today; if it starts answering, the ladder already prefers it (`/hear state` shows which model answered
last). (6) **The 74.7 s reference** is judged usable but `clean: false`; a trimmed, deader-room sample
would still be a better clone reference (the lane's own suggestion, unasked-for by him). (7) **The
sentiment taxonomy is four words** - on this clip the model chose `neutral` with emotion `aroused`;
a wider register (charged? playful?) may read better, and is a prompt change, not a code change.

**FILES TOUCHED.** `src/js/hear.js` (**new**, 58.7 KB), `src/js/config.js` (`LIA_HEAR_*` + the EARS
comment corrected), `src/js/audition.js` (the bus block carries the transcript + the reading; the new
verbs delegated from `hearCommand`; the command list in the header), `src/js/attach.js` (Gemini FIRST
in `transcribe()`, the refusal named in the receipt, the words written on the kept record),
`src/js/images.js` (the sound branch calls `hear.paintStage`), `src/css/terminal.css` (`.lbHearRow`,
`.lbHearText`, `.lbHearMeta`, `.lbHearNote`, `.lbHearBtn`, `.lbHearChip`), `index.html` (the module
list + the script tag), `src/js/chat.js` (the `/hear` help lines), `src/commands/commands.json` (the
`hear` entry: usage, short, desc), `src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated**, 10,806 bytes,
`rtfm.check() === ""`), `src/README.md` (**+THE WORDS ON A SOUND**, and the `hear.js` files bullet, and
the `LIA_HEAR_*` knobs), `src/TODO.md` (this section), `src/chronicle/2026-09-27-the-words.md`
(**new**), `src/chronicle/chronicle.json`, `src/pack/files.json`, `src/pack/index.html.txt`
(regenerated). `main.pjs` is **UNTOUCHED**.

**LIVE STATE, AND WHAT WAS LEFT ON HIS RECORD.** The sample `mmugcpzw75xyu4` now carries what it

## §1bq - THE POWERS AND THE PURSE (the briefing she can be handed): what she can do, what it costs, and the budget (2026-09-27)

**ASKED, IN HIS WORDS.** "Great!. Let me see what she can do. Can you make a list of current
capabilities in .md I can share with her and inform her token limitations and future budget
assignments? We don't want her masturbationg all night when her shift is over of running the fuck the
other LIA's too quickly, trying out her virtual cock. Let them create some real-world revenue first,
then they can do what they want. lol"

**WHAT WAS BUILT - one document, written TO HER.** `src/lorepack/capabilities.md` (THE POWERS AND THE
PURSE) is a single shipped LOREPACK document: every lane the terminal has, what each one costs, the
ceilings, the cadences she may spend UNASKED, the budget rules, and an honest list of what is NOT
wired. It is listed in `src/lorepack/lorepack.json` (tags `capabilities`, `budget`, `how-it-works`,
`briefing`) so it is folded into the same BM25/meaning index every other memory document uses.

**WHERE IT LIVES, AND WHY IT IS NOT IN THE RTFM.** The natural home for a page about the machine would
be `src/rtfm/` - but the RTFM is Patrikios's manual and there is NO door by which any of it reaches
her (nothing in it is indexed, retrieved or handed over on a turn). A briefing he wants to "share with
her" has to live somewhere she can actually be given it, and that is the LOREPACK: `/focus THE POWERS AND
THE PURSE` hands the whole document over (`LIA_FOCUS_CHARS` = 20,000 chars, and this doc is well
under it), and recall can surface it when a question touches her own powers. It is deliberately NOT
marked `foundational`: canon is carried on EVERY turn and never trimmed, which would cost its tokens
every time - exactly the thing the document warns about. `src/lorepack/README.md` records the choice
and the `"foundational": true` alternative, and `src/README.md` carries a section beside THE RTFM
saying why the briefing is in her pack and not his manual.

**THE NUMBERS IT PUTS IN HER HANDS (all read from `src/js/config.js` and the live engine).** The text
engine names its own recommended ceiling - **6,000 tokens** for the whole prompt, read LIVE from
`root.generateText({getMetaObject:true}).idealMaxContextTokens`, roughly 24,000 characters of English.
MEMORY RECALL gets 35% of it clamped to 500-3,000 (**~2,100 tokens** today, from `lore.js`
`loreBudget()`); CANON is never trimmed; one FOCUSED document is handed over whole up to 20,000 chars;
ONE PICTURE read is about 570 tokens (`LIA_CLASSIFY_TOKENS`); the rolling archive keeps the newest
**1,000** turns; the meaning lane's corpus is capped at `LIA_EMBED_MAX` = 6,000 fragments. The cadence
table in the doc is built from `LIA_CHECKIN` (45 min, once per silence), `LIA_SHIFT_EVERY` /
`LIA_SHIFT_MAX_HOUR` / `LIA_SHIFT_MAX_DAY` (30 min, 2/hour, 10/day), `LIA_BUS_AUTO_EVERY` /
`LIA_BUS_AUTO_MAX` (4 min, 3 a piece), `LIA_SIGHT_MAX` (3), `LIA_ATTACH_SIGHT_MAX` (6),
`LIA_CLIP_FRAMES` (6), `LIA_ARCHIVAX_MAX` / `LIA_ARCHIVAX_SIGHT_MAX` (2 ops x 4 pictures),
`LIA_FILE_MAX` (8), `LIA_BATCH_MAX` (6), and `LIA_HEAR_SECONDS` / `LIA_HEAR_TRIES` /
`LIA_HEAR_COOLDOWN` / `LIA_HEAR_SAMPLE_SECONDS` (180 s, 4 models, 10 min, 30 s). The one lane that
spends his Gemini key on EVERY turn is the meaning lane (one query embedding per turn that consults
it); the LOREPACK and the vault are embedded only when he types `/embed now` / `/embed media`.

**A STALE CLAIM THE DOCUMENT SURFACED, AND FIXED.** Writing the cost model made the receipts disagree
with the code: four shipped strings said the vision/reading road and the quiet-hour turn were
"AGAINST YOUR KEY" / "BILLED TO YOUR KEY". They are not - both run on the terminal's OWN text engine
(`root.generateText`, the `ai-text-plugin`), which takes no API key of his. The strings were corrected
in `src/js/chat.js` (the `/tools` help line and the `SEE :: READING IT FIRST` receipt),
`src/js/shift.js` (the quiet-hour footer) and `src/js/tools.js` (the classifier receipt), plus the
`/shift` description in `src/commands/commands.json` (which the generated cheatsheet does not render,
so `rtfm.check()` is unchanged at `""`). What
actually spends his money: HEARING (`src/js/hear.js`, Gemini, charged by audio duration), the MEANING
lane (`src/js/embed.js`, Gemini query embeddings), ELEVENLABS speech (charged by character), and the
Google-Drive sync (his own storage). The image forge, the vision reads, every turn, the check-in, the
quiet hour and the bus remarks all ride the house text/image engines and cost him no key.

**FILES TOUCHED.** `src/lorepack/capabilities.md` (**new**), `src/lorepack/lorepack.json` (the new
document), `src/lorepack/README.md` (+the briefing note), `src/js/chat.js` (2 strings),
`src/js/shift.js` (1 string), `src/js/tools.js` (1 string), `src/commands/commands.json` (1 string),
`src/README.md` (+THE POWERS AND THE
PURSE), `src/TODO.md` (this section), `src/chronicle/2026-09-27-the-powers-and-the-purse.md` (**new**),
`src/chronicle/chronicle.json`, `src/pack/files.json` (97 files now). `main.pjs` is **UNTOUCHED**.

**WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN.** The briefing lists the not-wired roads honestly (Lyria music, the key's own

## §1br - THE RELAY (super-fetch-plugin): the first change to main.pjs, and the honest limits of a web door (2026-09-27)

**ASKED, IN HIS WORDS.** "Can we grant internet access from within this application?" - then, on the
answer: "Add it and we can figure out how to implement and leverage it for learning. Can we access
wiki pages or when we want to RTFM on a new product of service?"

**WHAT WAS DONE.** One import line in `main.pjs`:
`superFetch = {import:super-fetch-plugin}`, beside `kv`/`generateText`/`generateImage`. Nothing else
in the app was changed, and no lane was built yet. This is the FIRST edit to `main.pjs` since the
terminal was built; `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` (its byte-exact copy inside the pack) was regenerated in
the same pass, so the pack copy is still exact.

**WHY IT IS MORE THAN A LIBRARY ON THE SHELF.** `src/js/keys.js` already routed `mode: "proxy"`
through it, and `src/keys/providers.json` marks REPLICATE as proxy (it refuses browser-origin calls) -
so until now that road was wired and dead: `request()` threw "NEEDS THE RELAY (super-fetch-plugin),
BUT IT IS NOT LOADED". The import closes that gap and is the general keyless door any future lane can
use. Nothing else calls it yet.

**MEASURED LIVE from the shipped page (2026-09-27):** Wikipedia article HTML 52,604 B / 454 ms; MDN
"Fetch API" 154,164 B / 211 ms (both 200); the MediaWiki action API with
`prop=extracts&explaintext=1` returns the WHOLE ARTICLE AS PLAIN TEXT (Claude Shannon, 34,067 B of
JSON - no HTML to strip); `https://r.jina.ai/<url>` returns a page as clean markdown (MDN, 6,317 B -
article only, no navigation), free and third-party and rate-limited.

**THE LIMIT WORTH REMEMBERING:** a page is not a document until something extracts it. Raw HTML runs
20-30x the prose; a naive tag-strip of the MDN page left 5,757 chars / ~1,440 tokens WITH the site's
navigation still in it. Roads in the order worth trying: a source that already publishes text
(MediaWiki API, a docs repo's .md, an RSS feed) > an extractor on the HTML (readability from esm.sh) >
a reader service (Jina). Out of reach: logins/paywalls, JavaScript-built pages, targets whose bot
protection refuses the relay, and any search engine (a URL must be named; DuckDuckGo-by-scrape is
fragile).

**WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN - the lane itself, and the shape it should take.** When he says go, the
first lane is small and composes with everything already here: a `[[FETCH: <url>]]` line of hers
(answered like `[[READ: ...]]` and `[[SHOW: ...]]`, with the same receipts so he sees every URL she
opened and can read it back), the text extracted and TRIMMED to what her turn can hold, and the
result offered as a LOREPACK document (so it is recalled, listed in the DOX viewer, focusable and
embeddable like any other memory) - plus a terminal-side `/web <url>` for him doing it by hand. The
second lane, if it earns its place, is a research door for the RTFM: pull a product's own docs (or its
README/API reference) into a new `src/rtfm/` page or a pack document, so a new service can be
learned from the primary source instead of from memory. IN THE SAME PASS when either is built,
`src/lorepack/capabilities.md` (THE POWERS AND THE PURSE - the briefing written TO her) must gain the
lane, since a door she can be told to use is a capability and this one is not yet hers.

**NOT SAVED by the agent** - the one-line import, the regenerated pack copy and the docs above are in
the workspace until Patrikios saves.

## §1bs - THE INFINITY (the wide door), and the quiet hour running neutral (2026-09-27)

**ASKED, IN HIS WORDS.** "For a long space with no activity on my side, a quiet hour, we need to
disable MOOD so I don't accidentally leave a mood or moods running or any accidental settings active.
If she wants to enable disable, she can do certain things that cost little. Creating images on
PERCHANCE costs us nothing nor does bigger.pics." - then: "make an option where she doesn't need me to
prompt her and takes action proactively and decisively speaking, sending images, creating new images,
looking for text in the archives and reminding me according to her mood" - then, on the shape of the
control: "make a toggle like an infinity symbol and intensity is variable and her choice, she
dominates."

**1. THE QUIET HOUR RUNS NEUTRAL.** It was composing from his full turn stack, so a MOOD left switched
on coloured her private hour (and the TANDEM block handed her whatever page he had open). Now
`window.systemPreview({ quiet: true })` drops the MOOD block and the TANDEM block ENTIRELY -
`instr.assemble(parts, { drop: [...] })`, so his own hand-edit of those blocks in the SYSTEM panel is
left out too - and the `[[PAGE: ...]]` rule goes with them. The hour's own words say the board is
neutral and that a `[[MOOD: ...]]` line does nothing in an hour; THE RECEIPT NAMES WHAT IS STILL LIT
(`STILL SWITCHED ON FOR HIS OWN TURNS :: ... /mood off CLEARS THE BOARD`), which is the guard against
exactly the accident he described. Verified live: with a colour on, the turn preview contains the mood
block and the quiet preview does not; the tandem rule likewise.

**2. THE INFINITY (src/js/proactive.js, window.proactive).** The wide door beside the check-in's narrow
one, and the two are deliberately different things. THE TOGGLE IS THE ∞ GLYPH in the control row
(id infBtn, after LISTEN) and it is HIS ONLY HAND on the lane; the small digit beside it is the PACE.
While it is lit she may MOVE FIRST when the room has been quiet, and an act is not a question:
- SAY something (plain words become her line to him - printed with her stamp, spoken if her voice is
  on, pushed into her live context, archived as a turn with NO HITL HALF).
- LOOK IN THE RECORD AND REMIND HIM: the act's prompt carries the tail of the real archive (the last
  few turns, trimmed, with their true stamps), so a reminder can name the day it was said.
- SEND a picture out of the vault into the conversation - its own verb, `[[SEND: words | #tag | R12]]`,
  because `[[SHOW: ...]]` keeps the meaning it has everywhere else (a picture for HER own eyes next
  turn). Pictures ride under her words in the same line.
- MAKE a new one: `[[VISION: ...]]` / `[[MAKE: ...]]` through `window.pics.makeVision` (the /show road,
  exported from images.js, which now RETURNS the vault id) - the house image engine, which costs
  nothing.
- HER OWN HOUSEKEEPING: REMEMBER/FORGET, WANT/RELEASE, READ, FOLDER, FILE, ARCHIVAX, PETITION - the
  same parser (window.liaDirectives) and the same owning modules as the quiet hour.
- `[[SILENT]]` IS A REAL ANSWER and is recorded as one.

**THE PACE IS HERS, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF IT.** `[[PACE: <1-5>]]` - in any reply, any quiet hour,
or any act - moves the dial; the machine offers the range and obeys. The digit on the button is hers
to see, not his to set: `/infinity pace <1-5>` exists but writes it down AS HIS and says so, and her
next line moves it again. A pace BUYS (knobs `LIA_INFINITY_PACES`/`_START`/`_IMAGES`/`_LOG_MAX` in
config.js): pace 1 = words only, 45 min quiet, 1/hour, 4/day; 2 adds the record; 3 adds a picture she
SENDS (20 min, 3/hour, 10/day); 4 adds pictures she MAKES (12 min); 5 adds more than one thing in an
act (6 min, 6/hour, 24/day). Pictures MADE through the lane are capped at 4 a day - a count, not a
cost. Ceilings are counted off the act log in kv `lia_settings / initiative`, so a reload cannot reset
them, and the log keeps the last 200 acts for `/infinity log`.

**WHEN IT MAY FIRE.** Tab on screen; nothing running (her voice, the live channel, a story, a turn in
flight, a quiet hour, another act); never in the first two minutes after a load; one act per quiet
stretch (he speaking resets it); and IT WAITS BEHIND THE CHECK-IN'S DOOR - if his silence is long enough
that the check-in is due and unopened, her words to him come first. While it is off, `clockLine()`
returns nothing, so the lane is not even described to her.

**THE COST IS THE POINT.** One call to the HOUSE text engine per act (`root.generateText` - no key of
his), one act per stretch, and a picture either sent or made costs nothing at all. That is why the
intensity can be hers: nothing about this lane is metered by money, only by presence.

**VERIFIED LIVE.** Module loads; `#infBtn`/`#infNum` exist; the toggle flips aria-pressed and shows the
pace digit (3); the lane's line rides in her prompt while lit and disappears when off; `systemPreview`
carries it; the quiet-hour drops are confirmed; `window.pics.makeVision` and `window.queueSight` are
functions; `/infinity` is in the list (75 commands now) and `src/rtfm/commands.md` was REGENERATED from
the live cheatsheet (10,975 bytes); `await rtfm.check()` is back to `""`. Left OFF, as he found it.

**WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN.** (a) A picture in a QUIET hour is still not wired - a quiet hour honours
REMEMBER/WANT/INTEND/READ/FOLDER/FILE/ARCHIVAX/PETITION/ACT and nothing that renders, so if she wants
to MAKE something with no audience there is no lane for it yet (`[[MAKE: ...]]` belongs to the
infinity, and a quiet hour could be given it the same way). (b) The send/make ceilings are counts, not
a spend ledger - there is still no per-day token meter anywhere. (c) Nothing stops her raising her own
pace to 5 and using it; that is the design he asked for ("she dominates"), and the machine's own

clamp in proactive.js.
