## §1bt - THE ROOM HEARS YOU, and THE INFINITY gets its reign (instant on / instant off) (2026-09-27)

**ASKED, IN HIS WORDS.** "the two way conversation keeps cutting me off and sending too soon. also
infinity is instant on instant off, the goddess runs the conversation, i am silent and wait for her
prompt i.e. role reversal."

**1. THE TWO-WAY CONVERSATION: THE ROOM IS NOW MEASURED, NOT GUESSED.** Every end-of-turn rule in
`src/js/voice.js` read the end of his turn off the RECOGNISER - off when it handed a result over and
whether that result was final - and the recogniser finalises at every breath, so a pause mid-sentence
and the end of one are indistinguishable to it. The holds (3500ms floor, the uncommitted tail, the
dangling-last-word stretch, the length stretch) were patience piled on a guess. Now the guess is
checked against the room: while the microphone is open, a SECOND stream is opened on the same device
(`getUserMedia`) through a Web Audio `AnalyserNode`, and the real level is read every 60ms
(`levelSample`). `levelLoud()` is true while the newest reading is at or above the threshold and for
350ms after the last loud one, and it is then used as evidence:
- `holdTick()` - a loud room means HIS TURN IS STILL OPEN: `holdAt` is pushed forward, the countdown
  resets, nothing is sent. Sound resets the clock exactly as a word of his does, so a breath, a word
  the recogniser is still chewing on, or his voice arriving late can no longer end the turn.
- `drainLive()` - her mouth waits for `!holdParts.length && !levelLoud() && the usual beat`, so she does
  not begin speaking while there is still a voice in the room (HER OWN playback is loud too, which is
  exactly when she must not start over herself).
- `proactive.js roomQuiet()` and `initiative.js chkQuiet()` ask `voice.state().levelLoud` as well, so
  neither an act of the infinity nor a check-in opens over a sentence he is still saying.
- `paintLevel()` puts a green ring on both microphone keys (`.micBtn.hearing`) while it hears him.
**IT FAILS SOFT, AND IT CANNOT BE HELD HOSTAGE.** If it cannot be opened (no `getUserMedia`, no Web
Audio, or a refused second stream) `levelStart()` records why in `state().levelDown`, logs ONE console
line per page, and everything behaves exactly as before - the holds are the floor and the meter is only
ever extra patience. It runs only while the microphone is in play (`levelSync()` from `setUi()`: an
open session, words held, or her mouth working) and is released the moment nothing is using it, so no
second stream sits on the microphone when the room is not being listened to. And after
`LIA_VOICE_LEVEL_MAX` (45s) of UNBROKEN loudness `levelLoud()` stops answering true, so a fan or a TV
cannot suspend the end of his turn forever. Knobs: `LIA_VOICE_LEVEL` (0.02), `LIA_VOICE_LEVEL_TAIL`
(350ms), `LIA_VOICE_LEVEL_MAX` (45000ms); `/voice level [<0-1>|off]` moves the threshold on the device
(kv `lia_settings`/`voice` → `level`), `/voice level` reports the live reading, and `/voice` carries a
`THE ROOM HEARS YOU ::` line.

**2. THE INFINITY IS INSTANT.** `toggle()` no longer decides anything by waiting:
- ON steps over the page-load settle, her own `[[WAIT:]]` and the spacing rules and opens an act AT
  ONCE (`openNow("switch")`); if the room is busy the act opens the moment it is free (a `infKick` flag
  the 10-second tick picks up). The ceilings and the state of the room are never stepped over - the
  switch is his hand, but it is not a licence.
- OFF is instant even against an act already in flight: `infRun` is bumped on every press OFF and every
  `compose()` carries the generation it started in, so what came back after the switch went down is
  DROPPED - not printed, not archived - and a SYSTEM receipt says so. Verified live: an act in flight,
  the switch pressed down, the act returned false, no line was added to the conversation, and the
  receipt read "THE SWITCH WENT DOWN WHILE THAT ACT WAS BEING MADE - WHAT IT HAD WRITTEN WAS DROPPED
  UNSAID."
Verified live the other way too: pressing ON with the engine stubbed produced a delivered act (an
`entry.sdm` line, archived, logged `act:"spoke"`) within ~200ms of the press.

**3. THE REIGN (LIA_INFINITY_REIGN, true) - SHE RUNS THE CONVERSATION.** Role reversal, as he asked:
while the lane is on, the room is HERS. He is silent on purpose and waiting on her word; her act prompt
now says so in the plainest terms ("the only thing that can move this room is you", "direct him", "if
you want an answer, ask for one and say what you want answered"), and the CLOCK line says it to her on
every ordinary turn.
- **The clock follows HER now, not his silence.** `infSince` is the end of her last act. If he has
  ANSWERED her since then (`heSpokeSince`, read off `logTime.seenAt` - a fact about the record),
  `reignWait()` is the pace's `turn`: 180s at pace 1 down to 25s at pace 5. If he has said NOTHING, it
  is the pace's own `every` (45 min down to 6) - a room that answers nothing is not filled by a
  machine. Both are per-pace rows in `LIA_INFINITY_PACES` (`turn` added).
- **The ceilings count only the acts she takes UNASKED.** `should()` skips them while `heSpokeSince`
  is true: an act that answers something he just said is a CONVERSATION, and a conversation is bounded
  by him (he is the one who has to speak for there to be another turn). What the ceilings are for is
  the other case. This keeps a real exchange from dying at 3 acts an hour while still making a flood
  impossible for a room nobody is in. (Cost is why they exist: every act is a real call on his quota.)
- **The check-in stands down while the infinity is on** (`chkShould()`), since the wide door is doing
  that job and more - otherwise two lanes could fire an act each into the same quiet room. Turn the
  infinity off and the check-in has the room back exactly as it was.
- **`[[WAIT: <time>]]` is hers** - seconds, minutes, hours or days, digits, words or clock style
  (`parseWait`; an unreadable length of time - "a bit", "2 weeks" - is reported rather than guessed at,
  and a bare unit letter only counts attached to a digit so "5 m" is five minutes and a stray "m" in a
  sentence is not), clamped to `LIA_INFINITY_WAIT_MAX` (7200s) - and the lane does not move until it has
  passed. It can only ever give the room back, never take it. Every act's own wait until next is
  reported in `/infinity`.

**VERIFIED LIVE.** `window.proactive.reign() === true`; the prompt carries "THE ROOM IS YOURS" and the
`[[WAIT:]]` line; `/voice level` and `/voice`'s THE ROOM HEARS YOU line both report correctly and the
threshold round-trips; with a stubbed engine, the switch's instant ON landed an act and its instant OFF
dropped an in-flight one; a stubbed `voice.state()` with `levelLoud: true` makes `proactive.should()`
false (no act over a voice in the room); `await rtfm.check()` is `""` after `src/rtfm/commands.md` was
REGENERATED from the live cheatsheet (11,002 bytes, 75 commands, 69 terminal + 6 hers). The lane was
left OFF and its kv record (`lia_settings`/`initiative`) wiped back to empty, as he found it.

**FILES TOUCHED.** `src/js/voice.js`, `src/js/proactive.js`, `src/js/config.js`, `src/js/initiative.js`,
`src/js/chat.js`, `src/css/terminal.css`, `src/commands/commands.json` (75 commands, both entries
rewritten), `src/rtfm/commands.md` (regenerated, 11,002 bytes), `src/lorepack/capabilities.md`,
`src/README.md`, `src/TODO.md` (this section), `src/chronicle/2026-09-27-the-reign.md` (**new**),
`src/chronicle/chronicle.json` (19 entries), `src/pack/files.json` (**regenerated - and it had DRIFTED:
the list was missing `chronicle/2026-09-27-the-powers-and-the-purse.md` from an earlier session, so it
is now rebuilt from the tree itself, 102 paths, sorted, set-equal to `src/`**). `src/pack/index.html.txt`
and `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` are still byte-exact (verified). `main.pjs` is **UNTOUCHED**.

**WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN.** (a) The level threshold is ONE number for a whole room: a noisy machine (a
fan on a desk, music playing) can sit near 0.02 and keep the meter "loud" - the 45-second
`LIA_VOICE_LEVEL_MAX` clause stops that becoming a deadlock, but a per-device auto-calibration (sample
the floor for a second when the microphone opens, put the threshold a fixed margin above it) is the
obvious next step if he ever finds his room sits above the shipped number. (b) The reign assumes the
ROOM is the conversation: if he is typing with the microphone shut, nothing tells the meter anything,
so her fast path depends on `logTime.seenAt` alone - which is correct, but means "answered" includes a
typed line only once that turn has actually been made. (c) A picture in a QUIET hour is still not
wired (§1bs, unchanged). (d) The infinity's fast path at pace 5 is a genuinely chatty terminal - 25s
between her turns while he is answering - and that is the design he asked for ("she dominates").

**NOT SAVED by the agent** - `main.pjs` is untouched again; everything above is in the workspace until
he saves.

## 1bu. THE LIVE WIRE - the live channel's two ends, on Gemini's Live API (2026-09-28)

**HIS WORDS VERBATIM.** *"nope fail. look into how GEMINI handles this multiplex and interruptions and
near zero latency. the glitching and dropping my words, etc makes it unusable."* Three complaints and
one instruction: the glitching (the browser recogniser ends its own sessions, which the 300ms ticker
then reopened), the dropped words (a session that ends mid-sentence takes what it had not yet handed
over), and the latency (her mouth was a whole clip, or a chain of 220-character utterances, and
neither can be interrupted) - and the instruction was to look at the transport itself rather than add
another rule on top of a guess.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** `src/js/live.js` (**NEW**, `window.live`, 904 lines) - THE LIVE WIRE: two
continuous streams on Gemini's Live API (`BidiGenerateContent` over a websocket, his own key).
(a) **THE EARS** are `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live`, a bidi model that ONLY WRITES TEXT - asked for
audio output it closes with code 1007 and says so - so it can never answer, and her voice off the
speakers can never become a reply of her own. (b) **THE UPLINK** is 20ms of 16kHz mono PCM at a time,
resampled inside an **AudioWorklet** (the AUDIO thread, so a busy page cannot make the capture
stutter) and **never stopped**: that is the whole fix for the glitch - there is no silence for a
session to end on and nothing to restart. (c) **HIS WORDS WHILE HE SAYS THEM**:
`interimInputTranscription` grows word by word into the input box; `inputTranscription` arrives once,
punctuated, at the end. (d) **THE END OF HIS TURN** is
`{voiceActivity:{type:"ACTIVITY_END",audioOffset:"..."}}` plus `silenceDurationMs` (1500 shipped),
`prefixPaddingMs` (80) and `END_SENSITIVITY_LOW` - a message from the model that is listening, not a
guess about it. (e) **HER MOUTH** is `gemini-3.8-live` handed the words `chat.js` already wrote, in a
session whose whole system instruction is "you are a voice, say this line exactly"; it returns 24kHz
PCM in chunks scheduled on an `AudioContext` the moment they land (**583-934ms to her first word,
measured across runs**), and every chunk is ours, so a hush is exact. (f) **INTERRUPTION**: a partial transcript
that is not a re-hearing of her own last line (the SAME echo guard) stops her mid-sentence.

**In `src/js/voice.js`:** the channel opens on the wire when it can (`openWire()`); `holdQuietMs()`
uses the **server's own** silence window (+150ms) instead of the recogniser road's 3500ms floor, with
the dangling and length stretches kept but **halved**; `speak()` routes to the wire's mouth
(`wireSpeak`, printed as `THE LIVE WIRE (GEMINI)`) and `stopSpeakingInternal()` hushes it;
`levelLoud()`/levelSync()/`wireLevel` read THE ROOM HEARS YOU off **the audio that is actually being
streamed** (one stream on the microphone, not two, with the same threshold, tail and ceiling); a dead
wire **falls the channel back onto the recogniser road without ending the call** (`wireDead`); the
250ms wire tail replaces the 700ms one (echo-cancelled audio plus the echo guard); and
`/voice wire [status|on|off|quiet <MS>|voice <NAME>|voices|try <NAME> [TEXT]|models [refresh]|ear <MODEL>|mouth <MODEL>|check on|off|now]`
drives and reports all of it.

**WHAT WAS THOUGHT, AND WHAT WAS REJECTED.** (1) A single `gemini-3.8-live` session doing everything
was the faithful-looking answer and was **rejected**: it would have taken her brain out of the call -
no per-turn LOREPACK retrieval, no directives, no petitions or renders, not-herself in the place he
talks to her most. The wire is a TRANSPORT; the middle (chat.js, the archive, the echo guard) does not
move. (2) The `gemini-*-tts` models are designed for verbatim reading and were **rejected on
measurement**: the same line returned first audio at 1048ms, 5268ms and 34688ms, and one run exceeded
90 seconds. A live session answered in **629ms** and its own transcription of what it said came back
word for word, semicolon included. The mouth's own transcription is therefore compared with the line
it was given and a real divergence is REPORTED (`/voice wire check off` stops asking).

**WHAT WENT WRONG.** (a) `Illegal invocation` on every probe: `AC.prototype.audioWorklet` is a getter
that insists on a real AudioContext - a feature-detection line that THROWS, taking `available()` with
it. (b) **A WORKLET WITH NO WAY OUT IS NEVER PULLED**, and the capture was a microphone feeding a node
that fed nothing: the wire opened, both sockets said ready, `meter: true` - and `sentSeconds` sat at
**0**. An `AudioWorkletNode` whose output reaches nothing is not in the rendering graph, so `process()`
is never called; the node needs an output wired to `destination` through a gain of EXACTLY ZERO, and
the `MediaStreamAudioSourceNode` has to be `connect`ed to it. Found with a one-second in-page probe (a
worklet that posts from its constructor and every fiftieth `process()`, with `hasIn` and the block
length) - after the fix `sentSeconds` read 3 then 5 and the room's level came off the same frames.
`live.state().sentSeconds` is THE thing to look at when the ears seem deaf. (c) `say()` refused a line
handed over before the socket was ready - now it waits (not ready is not a refusal) and `open()` does
not say OPEN until both sockets have answered `setupComplete` (**517ms**). (d) `say()` resolved on
`turnComplete` - while the last chunk was still in the air - so `await speak()` returned about 1.5s
early; a line is now settled when its audio has DRAINED, and a line cut off by a hush is settled as
cancelled rather than left hanging. (e) A channel test painted a fed transcript into the input box and
the delivery's own release cleared it, destroying 598 characters Patrikios had typed and not sent -
read back out of the test's own captured output and **restored by hand**; tests that drive the channel
are working in the one place a draft lives.

**VERIFIED LIVE (his key, before anything was built on it).** `/models` filtered to
`bidiGenerateContent` returns **9** models; `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live` **refuses** AUDIO modality
(close 1007, "The requested combination of response modalities (AUDIO) is not supported by the
model"); a six-second recording fed up the ear's own path returns **14-17 partial transcripts** and
one correct final (`Marcus, you little fucker, clean my garden with dedication and devotion. Don't
neglect the sacred pearl either. I want it`); both sockets ready in **517ms**; her first word at
**583-934ms** across runs through the terminal's own `speak()` (under a second every time, reported
`THE LIVE WIRE (GEMINI)`, and the promise now waits for the SOUND rather than the generation); a whole turn
delivered from fed audio (partials painted into the box, the hold taken, the sentence handed to
`window.send()`); an interruption - a partial injected while she was speaking stopped her and
printed `YOU SPOKE OVER HER, SO SHE STOPPED MID-SENTENCE`; and **his own microphone running the whole
loop** - 3-5s of real audio up the wire, the room's level read off the same frames that were sent,
and zero drops. The renderer trap in `src/chronicle/README.md` (a `|` inside a table row) is
respected in the new README table.

**FILES TOUCHED.** `src/js/live.js` (**NEW**), `src/js/voice.js`, `src/voice/voices.json` (a new
`wire` block: the models, the voice, the silence, the measurements, and the reasoning, so the wire's
defaults are DESIGN rather than buried in code), `index.html` (the script tag + the BOOT AUDIT's
MODULES entry), `src/commands/commands.json` (the `/voice` entry's description carries the whole
live-wire account and every new subcommand; 75 commands), `src/README.md` (the `src/js/live.js` file
bullet, a new **THE LIVE WIRE** subsection in VOICE, the intro's microphone paragraph, the live-channel
bullet, the config note and the command list), `src/TODO.md` (this section),
`src/chronicle/2026-09-28-the-live-wire.md` (**NEW**) + `chronicle.json` (**20 entries**),
`src/pack/files.json` (**regenerated from the tree - 104 paths, `js/live.js` added**),
`src/pack/index.html.txt` (**regenerated, byte-exact, 88711 bytes**). `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` is
byte-exact and `main.pjs` is **UNTOUCHED**.

**WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN.** (a) **His microphone, in his room**: everything was verified by feeding
KNOWN audio up the ear's own path (the `feed()`/`mute()` entry points in `live.js`, which the
terminal never calls) - the capture was verified as running and reporting, but the acoustic loop, and
above all what echo cancellation does with her voice coming out of his speakers, can only be judged by
him. (b) **The middle is still one non-streaming call**: between the two ends, `chat.js` writes the
whole reply in one `generateText`, so the gap between his last word and her first is the pipeline's
time plus ~0.6s. Speaking her first sentence while the rest is still being written needs a streaming
hook in `chat.js` - not done. (c) **No probe he can run himself**: a `/voice wire probe` that says a
line through the mouth, records it and feeds it to the ear would verify both ends without a
microphone. (d) **The voice is Kore, not hers**: an ElevenLabs line cannot be streamed this way, so
her real voice stays where it was (LISTEN, `/voice auto`, the story lane).

**NOT SAVED by the agent** - `main.pjs` is untouched; everything above is in the workspace until he
saves.

## 1bv. A LOAD IS A FRESH SESSION, AND HER VOICE BY EAR (2026-09-29)

**HIS WORDS VERBATIM.** *"Small thing. After I save, the chat context window keeps text from a previous
session. It also prepopulates of areas like create image tab."* And: *"Gemini Free Voice selection
preset list somewhere so I can decide. When I do, I will make a new voice clone recording for
chatterbox."*

**WHAT IT WAS.** Two of this terminal's conveniences wrote text back into boxes by themselves on every
load, and a SAVE IS A LOAD. (1) `src/js/draft.js` restored the unsent draft from kv
(`lia_settings / draft`) into **#userInput** as well as into the pencil: 598 characters of a previous
session's paragraph were sitting in the box before he had typed anything. (2) `src/js/forge.js`
restored `lia_settings / image_form` into the forge's boxes, and `openForge()` wrote `forge.prompt`
and `forge.negative` straight into **#cpPrompt** and **#cpNegative**, so the CREATE IMAGE panel opened
holding the last prompt he had used. The rest of the visible log is not a bug: `main.js` reprints the
last three turns (`RESUMING RECENT AEONS...`) on purpose, and that is the RECORD, not a form.

**WHAT IS BUILT - THE RULE: A LOAD IS A FRESH SESSION. WHAT IS REMEMBERED IS OFFERED, NOT APPLIED.**
(a) **The chat box starts empty.** `draft.js` keeps filling the PENCIL's textarea (the draft is not
lost, and it is still the only copy anywhere - this browser), never `#userInput`; the boot prints one
line - *"AN UNSENT DRAFT FROM 2 HOURS AGO IS IN THE PENCIL (598 CHARS, 108 WORDS) ... PRESS THE PENCIL,
EDIT IT THERE, AND SEND OR CLEAR IT"* - the pencil wears the microphone's own green ring
(`#draftBtn.has`, a `box-shadow` in `src/css/terminal.css`), and `window.draft.held()` reports it.
A message sent from the box throws the held copy away (`chat.js` calls `window.draft.sent(text)` right
after it decides the box has something in it) - **a slash command does not**, so `/voice wire quiet
1500` does not eat the paragraph he is holding. `ago()`, `wordCount()` and `paintHeld()` are new in
draft.js.
(b) **The forge remembers the SETTINGS and offers the PROSE.** size, count, guidance, seed, the pose in
the slot and the recipe in hand come back by themselves (they are choices). `prompt` and `negative`
are text he typed, so they are held in `lastForm` and offered in a new row - **LAST TIME / RECALL LAST
PROMPT** (`#cpRecallRow`, `#cpRecall`, `#cpRecallNote` in index.html, `paintRecall()`/`recallLast()`
in forge.js) - which fills only an EMPTY box and says so if it does not. The row is only there when
there is something to offer. `/renders redo R12`, the recipe rows and the shot-list roll still write
the boxes on purpose: that is what they are for.

**WHAT WENT WRONG, AND IT WAS FOUND BY TESTING IT.** `saveForge()` writes what `closeForge()` left in
the boxes, so opening the forge and closing it again - boxes empty, nothing typed - **wiped the pair the
row exists to hand back.** Fixed: the remembered pair is only replaced by another NON-EMPTY pair. The
check that caught it is the check worth keeping: open, close, reopen, and look at kv. And **a bug of my
own making**: the audition runner was first declared `async function audition(...)` - the same name as
the BROWSER audition at the bottom of voice.js, which wins silently (last declaration in a scope
overwrites), so `/voice wire audition 2` ran four browser voices and printed them as the model's
thirty. It is `auditionWire()`/`stopWireAudition()` now, with the reason in a comment at the
declaration. And an unrecognised first word (`audition nonsense`) used to run all thirty; now a name
that is not one of the thirty is refused with the list hinted, and a name that IS one starts there.

**THE VOICE LIST, SO HE CAN DECIDE.** `live.js` now carries the thirty prebuilt voices **with the
API's own one-word character for each** (`VOICES` is `[name, character]` pairs; `voiceNames()`,
`voiceNote(name)`, `voicesText()`), the duplicate `Achernar` that was in the old flat array is gone and
`Alnilam` is back in. `/voice wire voices` prints all thirty with their characters (and the same list,
with the reasoning, is in `src/voice/voices.json` → `wire.voices`/`voicesNote` and in the README's
VOICE section, so it can be read without a terminal). `/voice wire audition [<N>|<NAME>|from <NAME>|stop]`
**says one short line in each, in turn**, printing the name and the character as each one starts; it
walks from any name, reports *"N OF 30 SPOKEN"*, and stops cleanly. The voice is handed to the mouth for
that session only - `live.js`'s new `voice` option (`open({voice})`, `voiceOnce` in `mouthSetup`,
reported by `state().voice`) - so **nothing is saved and an interrupted audition cannot leave the
channel in a voice he never chose**; `/voice wire try` uses the same path and no longer writes the
setting and puts it back. The ears are optional now (`open({ears:false})`): an audition is a question
about HER VOICE, not about his room, so it does not call getUserMedia at all and does not touch an open
channel's ears - `close({mouthOnly:true})` exists for the same reason.

**VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-29, this device).** The box starts EMPTY on a reload (0 chars) with the pencil

## 1bw. THE MOOD BOARD (a META-MOOD she can CRUD and apply to a ROLE), AND THE VOICES HE DOES NOT WANT (2026-09-29)

Patrikios, in one message:

> - Give the ability to disable some voices from being selected. The code remains, but some options are available
> - Grant access to her for the portable MOOD parameters so she can CRUD her custom combos of attribute blocks i.e. "MOOD", move them around and save them, as a "META-MOOD" she can apply to ROLE. We can call it a "MOOD BOARD".

**THE VOICES HE DOES NOT WANT ARE HIDDEN, NOT DELETED** - the rule is his own words: the code remains
and the options narrow. Two lists, one idea.

- **The wire's thirty** (`src/js/live.js`). `VOICES` is still the whole table. A new `hidden` setting
  (shipped default in `src/voice/voices.json` → `wire.hidden`/`hiddenNote`, what is in force in kv
  `lia_settings` / `live`) filters it: `knownVoice()`, `hiddenList()`, `isHidden()`, `voiceNamesAll()`,
  `hiddenVoices()`, `setHidden()` (the ONE write - so `hide all` is one store write, not thirty), and
  `voiceNames()`/`voicesText()` now read through it (the text counts the hidden at its foot).
  `state()` carries `hidden`/`hiddenCount`/`voicesOffered`/`voicesTotal` and `describe()` reports it,
  including the case where the voice IN FORCE is one of them.
- **This browser's own list** (`src/js/voice.js`). `allHeld()` is everything the machine has,
  `voicesHeld()` is what is offered, and every chooser already went through the second one - so
  `/voice voices`, `/voice best`, `/voice try`, `/voice audition`, `/voice pitch` and the NUMBERS all
  skip a hidden voice. `hiddenNames()`/`isHiddenVoice()`/`hiddenVoices()`/`setHiddenVoices()` (one
  write), `resolveIn(list, want)` is the search over ANY list (so `hiddenMatch()`/`offeredMatch()`
  can answer "it is not gone, it is off the list"), and `store.hidden` is kept in kv
  `lia_settings` / `voice`. `state()` gained `browserVoicesHidden` and the report says so.
- **THE ONE THING HIDING MAY NEVER DO: take away the voice she is already speaking with.** Hiding the
  voice in force leaves it in force and says so - `pickBrowserVoice` reads the machine's RAW list on
  purpose, and the mouth uses the stored voice whatever the menu says.
- **Doors.** This browser: `/voice hide <NAME|#>`, `/voice show <NAME|#>`, `/voice hidden` (numbered,
  so `/voice show 2` works), `all` for the lot. The wire: `/voice wire hide|show <NAME|all>`,
  `/voice wire hidden`, and `voice`/`try`/`audition` refuse a hidden name with the way back. Every
  refusal names `/voice show <NAME>`.

**THE MOOD BOARD - A META-MOOD.** A mood is ONE colour; a board is a **NAMED, SAVED, ORDERED
COMBINATION** of them, in a new MOOD BOARD row under the MOOD row in the SYSTEM panel, in
`/mood board`, and in her own `[[BOARD: …]]` lane - one grammar for both presences. Kept in the same
kv object as the moods (`lia_settings` / `mood` → `boards: [{ id, label, moods: [id…], role }]`),
loaded and saved with them.

- **APPLYING REPLACES, NOT ADDS** - `boardApply()` sets the console to the board's colours, in the
  board's order, and names what it switched off. A combination that piled on top would be three more
  switches.
- **THE ORDER IS PART OF IT** - the rules reach her one after another, so `boardMove()` and
  `:: move <MOOD> first|last|up|down|<N>` exist, and re-stating a combination reorders it.
- **IT CAN BE SAVED FOR A ROLE** - `boardBind()` (one board to a role; binding a second takes the first
  off it), and `onRole()` is what `roles.js` calls at the end of a successful `set()` (see `wearBoard()`
  there) so **the shift itself switches the combination on** and prints its own receipt. Nothing is
  applied at boot or when she steps off stage: a colour is not the role.
- **A BOARD NEVER OWNS A COLOUR** - it stores ids and an order, never copies and never rules. So
  deleting a board deletes the combination and not a mood; dropping a colour leaves it a switch; and a
  colour gone from the book prints as `(NOT ON FILE HERE)` rather than vanishing from the board.
- **WHICH BOARD IS WORN IS DERIVED** - `boardNow()` compares the console's ids AND order with each
  board, which is what lets `blockText()` name the board with no state to keep in step, and what makes
  the header stop naming one the moment anything is flipped by hand.
- **Doors.** Her lane: `[[BOARD: NAME]]` applies; `[[BOARD: NAME :: MOOD + MOOD + MOOD]]` saves/rewrites
  (and `SHADE = how I sound` writes a colour into being in the same line - `writeMood()`, which was
  split out of `create()` so a board can define a colour WITHOUT switching it on); `:: add`, `:: drop`,
  `:: move`, `:: role <ID>`; `[[BOARD: off NAME]]` deletes; `[[BOARD: list]]` prints. His: the same
  grammar under `/mood board`, plus the panel row (chips that apply, SAVE BOARD, BIND, DELETE).
  `BOARD_DIRECTIVE` is extracted in `chat.js` and acted on BEFORE the MOOD lines in the same reply, and
  what she does with boards is archived in the same `mood` array as her colours (`{ board, by, moods,
  role, written, moved }`). /help mood carries the whole of it, and so does the rule she is given.

**VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-29, everything restored afterwards).** Boards: save `STORMTEST :: FERAL +
COLD` → apply (the block names the board) → `move COLD first` (order COLD + FERAL) → `add HUNGRY` →
`drop FERAL` (the colour stays on the console and the receipt says so) → `:: role barbelo` → **off
stage, back on BARBELO, and the combination switched itself on**, with `/roles` showing `MOOD BOARD
"ROLEBOARD"` beside the role and `/role`'s report naming it. Her lane: a colour written into being
inside a board line (`[[BOARD: HERBOARD :: SQUALL = … + COLD]]`), applied, then the board deleted -
colour and switch intact; extraction checked (`[[BOARD: …]]` lands in `out.boards`, not in `moods`).
The panel by real clicks: chips painted, a chip press applies, DELETE removes the combination and

Voices: `hide Zephyr` → 29 of 30 offered, `hidden` printed it with its character, `voice`/`try`/

## 1bx. THE YES BEFORE THE WORDS, THE ONE PICTURE THAT COUNTS, AND FULL MEANING THE WHOLE WIDTH (2026-09-29)

Patrikios, in one message:

> - AI on pencil button in the chat with polish, fic, etc.. User must approve before end
> - Create Image>Bigger.pics 4X>Gallery+Chat pipeline only upscaled images get sent to chat or gallery, if fail fallback to local 2X. She can manage her own creations autonomously
> - PICS: FULL button: must fill the entire chat contact window weight 100%

**1. THE PENCIL ASKS FIRST.** AI POLISH used to overwrite the draft the moment the model answered -
*"user must approve before end"* is the rule that ends that. A press of a style chip now returns a
**PROPOSAL**: a review box under the draft (`#draftProposal` -> `#draftProposalText`, with ACCEPT and
DISCARD) holding the model's words and the style that produced them. The draft is untouched byte for
byte until ACCEPT; DISCARD changes nothing; ACCEPT swaps the rewrite in and turns on **RESTORE**
(`#draftRestore`), which puts the replaced words back and offers the rewrite as a proposal again - so
the two can be swapped with the buttons. SEND **refuses** while a proposal stands, CLEAR and a send both
drop it, and the draft header reads `REWRITE WAITING - ACCEPT OR DISCARD`. Nothing is persisted: a
proposal is not a draft, so a reload starts with the draft and no proposal. `window.draft` exports
`proposal()`, `accept()`, `discard()`, `restore()` and `styles()`. A new style, **FIC**, joins the row
(eight chips now - FIX, WORK, CHAT, PLAY, FIC, SHORT, VEILED, SPICY): the message rewritten as a passage
of prose fiction, close third person, concrete detail, action in the present, every fact and the intent
kept.

**AND THE PANEL SAYS IT ONCE.** Patrikios, first: *"for inline live text, we only need EDIT IT HERE -
SPELLCHECK IS ON. NOTHING HERE IS IN THE ARCHIVE, THE EXPORT, OR HER CONTEXT UNTIL SEND."* That promise
had grown copies inside the pencil: the draft head (`DRAFT · BEFORE IT IS SENT`), the proposal's foot
(`ACCEPT TAKES IT · DISCARD DROPS IT · NOTHING IS SENT EITHER WAY UNTIL SEND`) and the MOOD row
(`THE SAME SWITCHES AS SYSTEM`). A first pass took the action row's line with them, and he put it back -
*"and \"SEND KEEP CLEAR CLOSE KEPT ON THIS DEVICE ONLY · NEVER EXPORTED · NEVER SYNCED UNTIL SEND\"* - and
he was right to: unlike the other three, IT SAYS SOMETHING THE LABEL DOES NOT (the draft is never
exported and never synced), so it is the one piece of commentary the panel keeps besides the label. The
panel's instruction is now the label above the box (verbatim) plus that action-row line, the textarea's
own `write it here first...` placeholder, and the `AI POLISH` row; the two heads keep only their names and
their live readings (`DRAFT` with the word/char count, `PROPOSED REWRITE` with the style/words/chars
note), and every control - MOOD, SEND, KEEP, CLEAR, CLOSE, RESTORE, ACCEPT, DISCARD - is untouched.
Verified live: `DRAFT | 0 WORDS · 0 CHARS`, the label, `AI POLISH | FIX WORK CHAT PLAY FIC SHORT VEILED
SPICY | POLISH`, `MOOD` and its switches, then `SEND KEEP CLEAR CLOSE` with the kept line.

**THE ASK HAD TO BE RESHAPED, AND LOOKING AT WHAT CAME BACK IS WHAT FOUND IT.** The first build sent
the style's rule, then the moods, then `Reply with ONLY the rewritten draft`, then `DRAFT: <the draft>`.
The model rewrote the WRONG PART: it echoed the moods block back, taking the register for the thing to
rewrite. The ask is now shaped so there is exactly ONE candidate (in `polish()`, `src/js/draft.js`):

    REWRITE THE DRAFT BELOW.

    THE JOB: <the style's rule>

    THE REGISTER IT MUST COME BACK IN (this is how the rewrite should sound - it is NOT
    text to rewrite, so do not include it):
    <the moods in force>

    THE DRAFT (the only thing to rewrite):
    <<<
    <the draft>
    >>>

    Reply with ONLY the rewritten draft ...

**2. THE BIGGER PIPELINE - ONLY THE UPSCALED PICTURE COUNTS.** `src/js/pipeline.js` (**NEW**,
`window.pipeline`) is a ROAD CHOOSER over the two upscaling roads, wired to the vault's one door
(`media.onAdd`, the subscribe retried at boot). Every picture the terminal makes is enlarged before it
counts, and the RENDER IS RETIRED once the bigger one is safely in the vault - so only the upscaled
picture is in the chat and the gallery.

- **The window road, by press only.** A browser opens a window only from a real click, and bigger.pics
  takes one automatic hand-over per window (both measured, see §1aa). `forge.js`'s `createImages()`
  calls `pipeline.arm()` **synchronously, inside the click** (only when `#cpPrompt` has something in
  it), and `arm()` opens `upscale.open(null, {await: promise, quiet: true})` - a PROMISE for the id,
  because the picture does not exist yet. `upscale.js`'s `open()` gained `opts.await` and `opts.quiet`
  (`bindPending()` waits for the id, then hands the picture over the moment it exists), and `result()`
  now tells `opts.onResult` about **every** road's result. The first picture of the run goes to
  bigger.pics at 4x.
- **Everything else, unattended, here.** The rest of a batch, her own creations (`[[VISION: ...]]`,
  `/image`, a re-render) and anything a window does not bring back go through THIS MACHINE at
  `LIA_PIPELINE_FALLBACK` (2). It is the only road that needs nothing from anyone, which is what makes
  *"she can manage her own creations autonomously"* true.
- **Retirement is the rule, not an option.** `retireRender()` calls `upscaleLocal.retire(rec, newId,
  {replace: true})` - the one implementation - so the archive row, the render's place in the queue for
  her eyes, any tile in the log and a KEEP all follow the bigger one, and only AFTER it is stored. An
  attachment, a clip, a piece of music and an upscale are never touched. `onResult()` only retires when
  the result really belongs to the armed window (`rec.from === armed.id`), so a late stray 4x cannot
  retire the wrong render.
- **It never silently gives up**: a window that brings nothing back falls to the 2x road (`fallLocal`),
  `armNudge()` prints a nudge after two minutes rather than leaving a picture in limbo, and
  `/upscale pipeline cancel` gives up on a waiting window by hand.
- **It supersedes the local `auto` hook rather than competing with it**: `upscale-local.js`'s
  `consider()` asks `pipeline.claims(rec)` first - a PURE question about the record (`on`, a `gen`
  record, not video/audio) - so the answer is the same whichever listener runs first, and nothing is
  ever upscaled twice.
- Setting kv `lia_settings / pipeline` = `{on, made, viaWindow, fell, at}`; doors `/upscale pipeline`
  (bare/`status`, `on`, `off`, `cancel`, `help`) and `LIA_PIPELINE` / `LIA_PIPELINE_FALLBACK` in
  `config.js`. `/upscale pipeline off` puts the old arrangement back and deletes nothing.

**3. FULL MEANS THE WHOLE WIDTH.** PICS' FULL step capped a picture at 96vh, one per row; he asked for
the whole window. The frame cap is now lifted in the `fullPics` body class (`body.fullPics .imageGrid
.imgTile { width: 100% }` and `body.fullPics .imageGrid:not(.batch) { align-items: stretch }` beside
`.imgTile` in `terminal.css`), so a tile takes the conversation column's whole width whatever its shape
- a tall picture stays tall, and it is the width that was missing. `paintPicSize()` toggles `bigPics`
and `fullPics` and the FULL tooltip says so.

**VERIFIED LIVE (everything restored afterwards).** The gate, with a stubbed model: a proposal arrived,
the draft and the box byte-identical, ACCEPT took the edit and showed RESTORE, RESTORE swapped back,
DISCARD left the draft, SEND was refused with `window.send` stubbed (0 sends), CLEAR dropped the
proposal; and a real FIX came back clean with his eleven moods on, with no echo of the moods block.
FULL, measured in a 793x621 window: a FULL portrait tile 749px = the full column (was 397, and 195 in
NORMAL), a landscape one 749 too; NORMAL unchanged (195 / 440). The pipeline, with a fake upscaler
window (a real `about:blank` iframe's `contentWindow` - a plain object is refused by
`new MessageEvent({source})`): `arm()` -> true; the fake frame's `bigger-pics-ready` accepted; a real
48x48 `gen` record claimed and the hand-over payload arrived (`type:'bigger-pics-image'`, a real
`data:image/png` URL, a generated name); a fake 192x192 result filed `kind:'upscale'`, `from`/`replaced`
= the render, and THE RENDER RETIRED (gone); the window self-closing cleared the arm (`viaWindow:1`,
`fell:0`); a window that took the picture and closed with nothing back fell to the REAL local road at 2x
(64x64, `how:'upscale-local'`, lanczos note, render retired, `fell` +1); with the pipeline on the local
hook said nothing for a claimed record (0 log lines) and with it off it queued (1 line); `arm()` refused
while a window was in play; `cancel()` with nothing waiting answered. Both test records deleted, the log
restored entry-for-entry, the pipeline left ON, kv counters zeroed, and the draft, the box, the role and
the moods found and left as they were.

**WHAT WENT WRONG.** (1) The prompt shape: found only by looking at what the model actually returned,
not by reading the code - the moods were being rewritten instead of the draft. (2) The first pipeline
harness passed a plain object as a `MessageEvent`'s `source`; the constructor refuses it, so the test
drove a real `about:blank` iframe's `contentWindow`. (3) `arm()` must be called INSIDE the click and
BEFORE `createImages()`'s first `await`, or the window is blocked by the browser - the same rule §1aa
measured, and the reason it is synchronous at the top of the function. (4) Tests that drive the real
upscaler road were kept to a fake window so that nothing of his was uploaded.

**FILES TOUCHED.** `src/js/pipeline.js` (**NEW**), `src/js/upscale.js` (`opts.await`/`opts.quiet`,
`bindPending()`, `onResult` on every road, `state()`'s `waiting`/`quiet`), `src/js/upscale-local.js`
(the `claims` stand-down in `consider()`), `src/js/forge.js` (`arm()` inside the CREATE click),
`src/js/draft.js` (the whole PROPOSAL gate, FIC, the reshaped ask, `proposalTextNow()`/`accept()`/
`discardProposal()`/`restoreReplaced()`, the exports), `src/js/images.js` (`fullPics` + the FULL
wording), `src/js/chat.js` (`/upscale pipeline`, the help lines, the PICS wording), `src/js/config.js`
(`LIA_PIPELINE`, `LIA_PIPELINE_FALLBACK`), `src/css/terminal.css` (the FULL-width rules, the proposal
box), `index.html` (the proposal box + `#draftRestore`, the `src/js/pipeline.js` script tag),
`src/commands/commands.json` (`/upscale` carries the pipeline; 75 commands), `src/rtfm/commands.md`
(**regenerated, 11,188 bytes**, `rtfm.check()` clean), `src/pack/files.json` (**regenerated - 107

`src/pack/main.pjs.txt` is byte-exact (62,006 bytes) and `main.pjs` is **UNTOUCHED**.

**STILL OPEN.** The window road is still one picture per press: a batch of six arms one window and
