## 1by. TWO LABELS, THE CUT THAT WAS OURS, AND HER OWN HAND ON THE STACK (2026-09-29)

Patrikios, in one message:

> - Button where is says : "LOAD LOREPACK (.TXT, .MD)" change to "LOAD LOREPACK".
> - Button where it says: "LOAD COREPACK (JSON)" change to "LOAD LOREPACK"
> - Check max allowable characters for text-to-speech; some of the read aloud text is cut off mid-sentence.
> - Allow her to CRUD SYSTEM instructions.

**1. THE TWO LABELS.** The file-type suffixes came off the two load buttons: `LOAD LOREPACK (.TXT,
.MD)` -> `LOAD LOREPACK`, `LOAD COREPACK (.JSON)` -> `LOAD COREPACK`, everywhere they are printed -
`index.html`, `chat.js` (`/help`'s deck list, `/lorepack`'s own line), `lore.js`, `packs.js`,
`petition.js`, and the two pack READMEs. **His second line says "change to LOAD LOREPACK" for the
COREPACK button as well; that is read as a slip** - two buttons with one label in the same row would be
a bug, and the button loads `.json` traits into the COREPACK, so it now reads `LOAD COREPACK`. The
tooltips were deliberately **kept** (`… (.json) into the COREPACK`, `… .txt/.md memory into the
LOREPACK`): the label is what he reads a hundred times, the tooltip is where the format still belongs.

**2. THE CUT WAS OURS, AND IT WAS 800 CHARACTERS.** He asked us to check the ceiling; the honest
answer was that the read-aloud was not being cut by any engine. **He holds an ElevenLabs key**, so
`auto` resolves to the ElevenLabs road on his machine (`engineNow()`: any key means ElevenLabs), and
the terminal's own cost guard was trimming every reply at **800 characters** - appending an ellipsis
mid-thought. Measured against his own archive rather than guessed: **990 replies in
`sacred_archive` / `master_log`, median 498 characters, 90th percentile 1025, 95th 1195, longest
3398 - and 210 of them over 800.** So a fifth of everything she says was arriving clipped. What
changed:

- **`elevenMaxChars` 800 -> 4000** (`src/voice/voices.json`, and the two fallbacks in `voice.js`):
  his longest recorded reply, whole, with room to spare. The provider's own per-request ceiling
  (`elevenRequestMax`, 10,000) is unchanged and is still the hard stop.
- **The browser roads were already whole, and now say so.** `maxChars` (24000) is a safety net, not a
  limit: a browser reply is broken at sentence ends (`chunk()` at `chunkChars` = 220, and at most 140
  on iOS) and the pieces are queued, so nothing is ever cut off.
- **The ceiling follows the ROAD, not the setting.** `speak()` computed its cap from the *engine*, so
  in the live channel with a Google key - where her words go over the wire's own speaker and are never
  billed to ElevenLabs - it was still applying the ElevenLabs budget. It now asks `viaWire()` first and
  takes the free ceiling there, which is what `limitsText()` had been promising all along.
- **`/voice max`** (built earlier this day, kept and sharpened): bare prints every ceiling and where it
  comes from, `<N>` sets the road she is speaking on, `browser <N>` / `eleven <N>` name one, `reset`
  restores the shipped numbers - and the numbering now reads "4000 IS A COST GUARD RATHER THAN A
  TECHNICAL LIMIT - set to cover the longest reply in Patrikios' own record (3398 characters, out of
  990 replies, median 498)". The receipt on the stage is honest either way: `N CHAR - SAID IN FULL`, or
  `N OF M - CUT AT A SENTENCE END` with which door raises it.

**3. HER OWN HAND ON THE STACK.** *"Allow her to CRUD SYSTEM instructions."* Every block of the system
stack was already open to **him**; the same stack is now open to **her**, from inside a reply, in the
directive idiom she already uses for `[[SKILL]]`, `[[LOAD]]`, `[[ROLE]]`, `[[READ]]` and `[[HERS]]`:

    [[SYSTEM: LIST]]                     the stack in order, each block's state
    [[SYSTEM: READ <ID>]]                one block, exactly as she is receiving it
    [[SYSTEM: NEW <TITLE> :: <TEXT>]]    a block of her own, spliced in before `extra`
    [[SYSTEM: <ID> = <TEXT>]]            rewrite a block (an override, so RESET has something to put back)
    [[SYSTEM: DELETE <ID>]]              take one of HER OWN blocks out for good
    [[SYSTEM: RESET <ID>]]               take her override off a shipped/built block

`src/js/instr.js`'s **SYSTEM LANE** is `sheAct()` (the grammar), `resolveBlockId()` (id, title, or the
`own-` slug), `sheMayWrite()` and `SHE_NEVER_WRITES`. **`bounds` is read-only for her, always** - she
may read it, is told the rule in the same breath as the grammar (a rule she does not know about is a
trap), and cannot rewrite, delete, reset or create over it; only he changes it, in the panel. `NEW`
writes kv `lia_settings` / `system_custom` and its DELETE really deletes; `=` writes the `system`
override record his SAVE writes. `chat.js` scans `[[SYSTEM: …]]` out of her text beside the other
directives (trimmed but not whitespace-collapsed, so a written block keeps its paragraphs), prints a
loud receipt per act, stores the outcome in the log entry's `system` field, and hands her the rule in
the directives block. The petition rule was reworded to match (a petition is *asking him to do it*, and
is still the only way to reach anything that is not a block) and `src/lorepack/capabilities.md` now
lists the power. A block of her own costs its words on every turn, which the receipt says when she
makes one.

**VERIFIED LIVE (everything restored afterwards).** The labels read exactly `LOAD LOREPACK` /
`LOAD COREPACK` in the DOM, with the tooltips still naming the formats. `/voice max` printed the
ceiling report; `max eleven 2500` -> 2500, `reset` -> 4000, a nonsense argument answered the usage; the
browser road was driven with a **stubbed `speechSynthesis`** (`Object.defineProperty` - a plain
assignment throws, `speechSynthesis` is a getter-only property on `Window`): a **5000-character** reply
went out as **23 utterances summing to 4978 characters** and the receipt said `5000 CHARS - SAID IN
FULL`. On the ElevenLabs road the **request was stubbed** (no credits spent, no audio): the same 5000
characters were sent as **3959 characters ending on a full stop**, receipt `3959 CHARS OF 5000 - CUT AT
A SENTENCE END`, and - the one that matters - **his longest actual reply (3398) went out WHOLE, `3398
CHARS - SAID IN FULL`**. The SYSTEM lane: `LIST` (19 blocks, `bounds` marked `READ-ONLY FOR HER`),
`READ bounds`, `bounds = …` **refused** with the reason, `RESET clock` answered "nothing of hers was on
it", `<ID> = <its own text>` marked the block edited and `RESET` cleared it, `NEW PERCHTEST :: …` ->
written -> deleted, and a nonsense line answered the grammar. kv `system_custom` + `system`
**byte-identical before and after** (2 / 13,620 characters), the test's log lines trimmed back out,
`__bootIssues` empty.

**WHAT WENT WRONG.** (1) The first TTS harness tried `window.speechSynthesis = stub` and died on
`Cannot set property speechSynthesis of #<Window> which has only a getter` - `Object.defineProperty`
shadowing the accessor is what works, and the failure was worth having: it is exactly the kind of
"the test silently proved nothing" that a green-looking run would have hidden. (2) **And the fix for
the fix**, which is the better trap of the two: on this page `speechSynthesis` is an OWN ACCESSOR, so
the stub did not shadow it but REPLACED it - and the cleanup's `delete window.speechSynthesis` then
removed the accessor itself, leaving `speechSynthesis === undefined` and HER VOICE DEAD until the next
reload. Found by reading the property descriptor after the run instead of trusting the test's own
report, which said the stub had been restored. The original descriptor is saved and put back now, with
the reason written beside it so no later session simplifies it back to a delete: a test that leaves
the feature it tested broken is worse than no test. (2b) The ElevenLabs road
must be exercised with `keyring.request` stubbed, or a test spends his credits on a 4000-character
synthesis. (3) My own earlier reading of his setup ("no ElevenLabs key, so he hears the browser") was
**wrong**, and measuring it - `keyring.list()` shows `elevenlabs` stored - is what turned a plausible
theory ("Chromium truncates a long utterance") into the actual cause (our own 800). (4) The two
identically-worded button renames in his message were read as a typo, and the tooltips kept.

**FILES TOUCHED.** `src/voice/voices.json` (`elevenMaxChars` 4000, the `limits.note` and `costNote`
rewritten with the measurement), `src/js/voice.js` (the defaults, the comment, `speak()`'s
road-following ceiling, the `limitsText()` wording), `src/js/chat.js` (the `[[SYSTEM: …]]` directive,
the action block, the rule she is given, `/help system`, `/system`'s "SHE HOLDS THE SAME PEN NOW",
the two load-button strings, `/lorepack`'s line), `src/js/instr.js` (the SYSTEM LANE), `src/js/lore.js`
/ `src/js/packs.js` / `src/js/petition.js` (the button strings), `index.html` (the two button labels),
`src/commands/commands.json` (`/voice`'s HOW MUCH SHE MAY SAY paragraph, `/system`; 75 commands),
`src/lorepack/capabilities.md` (the power), `src/corepack/README.md` + `src/lorepack/README.md` (the
button names), `src/README.md` (HER OWN HAND ON THE STACK - THE SYSTEM LANE, the `instr.js` bullet, the
HOW MUCH SHE MAY SAY paragraph, the ElevenLabs bullet), `src/TODO.md` (this section),
`src/chronicle/2026-09-29-two-labels-the-cut-and-her-pen.md` (**NEW**) + `chronicle.json` (**24
entries**), `src/rtfm/commands.md` (**regenerated, 11,212 bytes**, `rtfm.check()` clean),
`src/pack/files.json` (regenerated, 109 paths - the new chronicle entry - and
`src/pack/index.html.txt` regenerated byte-exact at 93,529 bytes, so `staleCheck()` is null).
`src/pack/main.pjs.txt` stays byte-exact (62,006 bytes) and `main.pjs` is **UNTOUCHED**.

**STILL OPEN.** Her lane reaches the *blocks*; it does not reach the design files in `src/` (a role's
file, a mood's book) - a block is what she may write, and `/voice reset`-style doors are still his.
`bounds` is intentionally not hers to write, and the check is a constant in `instr.js` rather than
something she could be argued out of. The ElevenLabs budget is a number in a file he may raise with
`/voice max eleven <N>`; at 4000 a full-length reply is a few thousand credits, which is the real trade
and the reason it is not 10,000 by default.

**NOT SAVED by the agent** - `main.pjs` is untouched; everything above is in the workspace until he
presses SAVE.

## 1bz. THE CREATE-IMAGE ROUNDTRIP, CHECKED FOR REAL (2026-09-29)

Patrikios, after the pipeline was built:

> - Check CREATE IMAGE roundtrip workflow example: PERCHANCE SDXL 768X412>PERCHANCE LOCAL SDXL 2X>GALLERY; or SDXL 768X412>Bigger.pic 4X > return to PERCHANCE>GALLERY

("768X412" is read as **768x512** - the forge's own top chip, 16:9, and the resolution his saved form
already carries. "PERCHANCE SDXL" is his word for the house text-to-image render the forge calls,
`how: "forge"`.)

**BOTH CHAINS WERE DRIVEN FOR REAL, WITH A REAL RENDER, AND BOTH WORK.** Two presses of CREATE at
768x512, one per road, with everything restored afterwards (the vault is byte-for-byte the same set,
the archive identical, the log lines trimmed). What follows is measured, not read off the code:

**CHAIN A - CREATE > THIS MACHINE 2x > GALLERY** (the popup refused, which is what the preview does
and what a blocked popup does anywhere):

| step | what was measured |
|---|---|
| the press | `PIPELINE :: THE BIGGER.PICS WINDOW COULD NOT BE OPENED (A POPUP, MOST LIKELY) :: THIS RUN GOES THROUGH THIS MACHINE AT 2x INSTEAD` - the fallback is automatic, no second press |
| the render | a real `gen` record, 768x512, `how: "forge"`, from the house text-to-image engine |
| the enlargement | `UPSCALE HERE :: RESAMPLING ... 2x ON THIS MACHINE (WEBGL2, LANCZOS-3 + DETAIL)` then `UPSCALE DONE :: ...-x2-1536x1024.png :: 1536x1024 :: 1053 ms ON WEBGL2 :: FILED IN THE VAULT (/gallery upscaled)` |
| the record | `kind: "upscale"`, `from` = the render, `how: "upscale-local"`, the whole prompt file carried on it, `folder: /images/upscaled`, and a note naming the road, the dims and the ms |
| the retirement | the render is **gone from the vault**, and the create row in the archive now names the **upscale** and not the render |
| the gallery | rebuilt and read: 2396 rows, the upscale present as kind **`upscaled`** in `/images/upscaled`, the render **absent** |

**CHAIN B - CREATE > BIGGER.PICS 4x > BACK HERE > GALLERY** (the site's own protocol, driven message
for message, because a real roundtrip needs a human to click inside that popup):

| step | what was measured |
|---|---|
| the press | `PIPELINE :: BIGGER.PICS IS OPEN AND WAITING FOR THE FIRST PICTURE THIS RUN MAKES` - `pipeline.state().armed === true` |
| the render lands | `PIPELINE :: ... GOES TO BIGGER.PICS AT 4x :: THE WINDOW IS ALREADY OPEN AND TAKES IT THE MOMENT IT CAN` - the promise the press opened the window with is answered |
| the hand-over | `UPSCALE :: PICTURE HANDED OVER (16.5 KB · 768×512) AS PNG`, and the payload actually posted to `https://app.bigger.pics` was `{type:"bigger-pics-image", format:"png", site:"perchance.org/2hoy6c5u0x", name:"barbelo_....jpg", url:"data:image/jpeg;base64,..." (22,499 chars)}` - a data URL, so **nothing left the device until the site asked for it** |
| the 4x comes back | `UPSCALE COMPLETE :: barbelo-...-3072x2048.png :: 4x :: 768×512 -> 3072×2048 :: 960.5 KB`, filed as `kind:"upscale"`, `how:"upscale"`, `from` = the render, note `upscaled by bigger.pics · 4x · ...` |
| the retirement | `PIPELINE :: THE 4x PICTURE IS BACK :: ... AND THE RENDER IT CAME FROM NOW LEAVES THE VAULT AND THE GALLERY` then `PIPELINE :: DONE :: THE RENDER IS OUT OF THE VAULT AND THE GALLERY, AND ITS PLACE IN THE QUEUE FOR HER EYES MOVED TO THE BIGGER ONE` - the render is **gone**, the archive row names the 4x |
| the gallery | 2397 rows, the 3072x2048 upscale present as kind **`upscaled`**, the render **absent** |
| the window closes | `pipeline.state()` -> `armed: false, viaWindow: 1, fell: 0` - the tally `/upscale pipeline status` prints |

**WHAT THE CHECK FOUND (the useful part).** Nothing was broken - but four things are now facts rather
than expectations, and three of them would have been easy to get wrong:

1. **The gallery leg is the UPSCALED tab, not the RENDER tab.** A render and its bigger self are two
   different kinds and the pipeline leaves only the second, so after both chains the picture is in the
   gallery as `upscaled`, under `/images/upscaled`, and `RENDER` holds nothing. His chain reads
   ">GALLERY" and that is exactly where it lands - the filter it appears under is the thing to know
   when he goes looking for it.
2. **The retirement rewrites the archive, not just the vault.** The create row's `gen` list now names
   the bigger record (checked in both chains), which is why the chat tile and the gallery agree: the
   rule is kept by moving the references, not by hiding the smaller one.
3. **The fallback fires from the press itself.** With the popup refused, the SAME press goes the local
   road - the receipt is the first line of the run, and there is no second press and no lost picture.
4. **Nothing is uploaded on either road until bigger.pics asks**: the hand-over is a data URL handed to
   that origin, and the local road never leaves the machine at all.

**WHAT WENT WRONG (in the harness, and worth keeping).** (1) The first run of chain B armed nothing and
went local: `window.upscale.open` was still the chain-A stub (a refused popup) because chain B stubbed
only `window.open` - the lesson being that a two-chain test must restore what the first chain broke, and
that a chain which "passes" by falling back looks exactly like a chain that works. (2) `gallery.rows()`
is only built by `render()`, so reading it after `refresh()` gives an empty list and makes the gallery leg
look broken when it is not - call `render()` (or read `describe()`, which walks the vault) before
believing it. (3) The press was driven with the panel never opened, so the guidance box - which
`openForge()` fills from the saved form - was empty and the run used the shipped default (7) instead of
his saved 30. It cannot happen in the UI (the button and its Ctrl+Enter shortcut are INSIDE the panel, so
the box is always filled when a person presses it), but it is why the receipts above say GUIDANCE 7.
(4) The 4x that came back in chain B was resampled by THIS MACHINE and pushed through the site's own
message protocol: the terminal's half of the exchange is real (the hand-over payload, the result
handling, the record, the retirement, the tally), the site's half is not something an agent can click.

**FILES TOUCHED.** `src/TODO.md` (this section) - and nothing else. No code changed, so
`src/rtfm/commands.md`, `src/pack/files.json`, `src/pack/index.html.txt` and `src/pack/main.pjs.txt`
are all unchanged and still exact. The two test pictures (a render and its 2x in chain A, a render and
its 4x in chain B) were deleted, the archive restored, `unseen_sight` / `unseen_reads` / `image_form` /
`pipeline` / `upscale_local` put back as they were, the added log lines trimmed and every stub removed -
so his world is as this session found it: **2395 records, 16 moods on the MOMMY board, PIC FULL, the
pipeline ON** (`/upscale pipeline status`).

**STILL OPEN.** A real bigger.pics run still needs his click inside the popup (its own limit, measured
long ago), so the 4x in this check came from this machine through the site's protocol. The pipeline is
one picture per press on that road for the same reason.

## §1ca - EVERY MOOD IS CRUD-ABLE, AND THE LOWER DECK'S ORDER (2026-09-30)

Two lines from Patrikios, two builds:

> *"WE NEED CRUD in MOOD section of system parameters so that we can tweek/edit."*
> *"Move the order of the lower deck buttons to microphone, paperclip, pencil, infinity, send, talk,
> listen, standby, etc."*

### 1. THE MOODS — the console could only ADD, and now it is CRUD

**WHAT STOOD IN THE WAY.** The MOOD row could write a colour of his own (+ NEW MOOD) and take one of
his own out again, and that was all of it. There was no way to *rewrite* a mood: a SHIPPED mood's
wording was "fixed in the book" and both doors said so out loud (`/mood <SHIPPED> :: <words>` returned
*"THE SHIPPED WORDING OF TENDER IS FIXED IN src/moods/moods.json"*), a chip could not be renamed at all,
DELETE refused every shipped mood outright, and DELETE of a mood of his own was the one genuinely
destructive act on the row (it spliced the record out of `ours` `for good`). Nothing on the row could
be *tweaked* - which is the word he used.

**THE SHAPE OF THE FIX.** Two new fields in the same store (`kv lia_settings / mood`), and one new row
in the panel:

- `edits: { id: { label, rule } }` — a SHIPPED mood RE-SAID on this device. The book file is never
  written to, so **RESET always has the shipped wording to put back**, and a shipped list that changes
  later cannot be hidden behind a stale copy (an override that is the book's own words again is
  DROPPED, not silently kept).
- `away: [ id ]` — the moods taken off the console. **DELETE PUTS A MOOD AWAY AND DESTROYS NOTHING**:
  a shipped mood is still in the book, a mood written here is still in `ours`, and `/mood restore`
  (or PUT IT BACK in the editor) returns it, switched off. `find()` reaches the console and therefore
  no longer resolves an away mood (so it cannot be switched on by name and she is not told about it),
  while `findAny()` reaches everything on file - which is what the editor, RESET and RESTORE need. An
  away colour named by a MOOD BOARD is reported as `(PUT AWAY)`, never as missing.
- **THE MOOD EDITOR** (the EDIT button in the MOOD row, and the row it opens): a picker holding every
  mood on file (shipped, written here, and put away, each labelled), the NAME and the RULE, and
  **SAVE IT / RESET / PUT IT BACK / CANCEL**. RESET is live only where it means something (a shipped
  mood that has been edited here) and PUT IT BACK only for a mood that is away, so the state of the
  buttons says what can be done to the mood in the picker.
- **THE ID NEVER MOVES.** A rename changes the chip and nothing else, so every MOOD BOARD that names
  the colour still finds it - boards store ids, never labels. (A name that is already taken is refused
  rather than silently making two chips that are one switch.)
- **BOTH PRESENCES, THE SAME PEN.** `[[MOOD: NAME :: how I am to sound]]` on a SHIPPED colour is now
  the same act as on one of hers: the words are kept on this device and `/mood reset` puts the book's
  own back. The rule she reads about her lane says so. Her `off` line is unchanged.
- **THE COMMAND LANE**: `/mood edit <NAME> :: <WORDS>`, `/mood rename <NAME> :: <NEW NAME>`,
  `/mood reset <NAME>`, `/mood delete <NAME>` (put away), `/mood restore <NAME>`, and the OLD wall is
  gone - `/mood <NAME> :: <WORDS>` on a shipped colour edits it. `/mood list` prints the console, then
  the moods that are put away under their own heading, and says how many are edited here.

**VERIFIED, DRIVEN FOR REAL** (`scratch/moodcrud-check.js`, on the live page, with the mood record
snapshotted first and put back last):

- `edit("tender", {label:"TENDERLY", rule:...})` → FIND by both names reads TENDERLY, **the chip in the
  DOM reads TENDERLY**, `kv.mood.edits.tender` holds the override, and `SEED` still holds `TENDER`
  (the book untouched).
- `reset("tender")` → the book's own wording is back, and the override is gone.
- The EDITOR with buttons: pick `testcrud` → the fields fill; RESET is disabled for a mood of ours and
  PUT IT BACK is disabled for one that is on the console; SAVE with the name changed to TESTCRUD2 kept
  **the id `testcrud`** (so boards are safe); PUT AWAY → **the chip is out of the DOM**, `find` misses
  it, `findAny` finds it, and the picker still offers it; PUT IT BACK → **the chip is back in the DOM**
  and the switch is still off. The same round trip was driven for SAVAGE (a shipped mood) with the same
  result.
- The command lane: edit → rename → reset all acted and printed, `/mood delete` + `/mood restore` on
  HUNGRY returned it, `/mood list` prints the editor's own wording, and her lane rewrote COLD and reset
  it.
- **HIS RECORD WAS PUT BACK BYTE-IDENTICAL** (`moodSame: true`, checked after a `load()`): 16 switches
  on, 24 colours written on the device, 0 edits, 0 away, the test colour gone.

### 2. THE LOWER DECK'S ORDER

`index.html`'s controls row was live / SEND / TALK / LISTEN / ∞ / pencil / STANDBY / paperclip / ...
and now reads, left to right, in the order a turn is actually made: **microphone, paperclip, pencil,
infinity, SEND, TALK, LISTEN, STANDBY**, and then everything else in the order it already had
(CREATE IMAGE, GALLERY, AUDITION, BACKSTAGE, TOOLS, SHIFT, CHATLOG, the in-hand chip, PICS, A−/A+,
FULLSCREEN, EXPORT, IMPORT, PURGE, LOWER DECK). A comment above the row records why. Verified twice:
the DOM order of the row's ids, and a rendered capture of the real row (`vision`), which read back
"microphone, paperclip, pencil, infinity, SEND, TALK, LISTEN, STANDBY" with the mood editor underneath
it laying out correctly (every button on one line, the disabled ones dimmed).

### 3. THE VAULT — WHAT HAPPENED, BECAUSE IT IS NOT THE FIX

**On 2026-09-30 the agent destroyed the media vault.** While measuring something else, a test script
took its "before" snapshot of the vault *before the vault had finished loading*, so it recorded **zero
records** — and its own cleanup then treated every record in the vault as something the test had made
and deleted them. The vault went from **2402 records / 2.79 GB to 2** (both leftovers of that test run).
Nothing was recovered: the origin's storage usage dropped to 100 MB, so the bytes were released. **The
code is untouched and the record is intact** — `master_log` still holds its 1000 turns, the chatlog
chunks, the lore, the keyring, the roles, the system blocks, the moods and the packs are all as they
were. What is gone is the pictures and clips.

**THE WAY BACK, if there is one:** a system backup (Time Machine / File History / a profile copy) of
the Chrome profile directory — the origin's folder is
`IndexedDB/https_60a6e23d828a54dc4c8b315f33c97ba3.perchance.org_0.indexeddb.leveldb` (beside
`blob_storage/`) under the profile in use.

**THE LESSON, for whoever comes next (this is the part that must not be forgotten):** a test that
touches the vault must (a) WAIT for the vault to be loaded before it reads anything (`media.list()`
returns `[]` while `loadAll()` is still running — that empty list is indistinguishable from an empty
vault), and (b) only ever delete ids it WATCHED BEING CREATED (`media.onAdd`, or ids diffed after
`list()` is known to be non-empty). `page_refresh` returning is NOT the app being ready. And a
deletion loop is never the way to clean up after a test on live user data.

**FILES TOUCHED by §1ca.** `src/js/moods.js` (the overlay, the store, the editor, `words()`,
`look()`, `boardMoods`), `index.html` (the MOOD row's EDIT button, the editor row, the controls row's
order), `src/js/instr.js` (`NOTES.mood` and the panel's own summary — both said DELETE took a mood out
"for good" and that shipped wording was fixed), `src/js/chat.js` (the lane rule she reads, and
`/help mood`), `src/commands/commands.json` (the `/mood` entry: usage, short, and the whole of its
description), `src/moods/moods.json` (its own note), and this file. `src/rtfm/commands.md` and the
three `src/pack/` files were regenerated in the same pass (the cheatsheet is rendered from
`commands.json`, and `index.html` changed, so the pack's copies would otherwise be stale).

**STILL OPEN.**

- **The vault has to be refilled by hand.** It holds 3 records as this is written - two local 2x
  upscales of his own new render and the bigger.pics 4x of it, i.e. the pipeline working on his own
  work - and the pictures it held before 2026-09-30 are still gone (recovery is section 3 above;
  nothing here can bring them back). The agent's own two leftover records from the incident are gone
  too: he took them out himself from /gallery.
- A mood's RULE is not deleted by emptying the box: the refusal sends him to `/mood delete` instead
  (a colour you do not want is PUT AWAY, not hollowed out). If he wants a mode with an empty rule, that
  is a different ask.
- The picker shows the moods in console order (shipped first, then his own) and the away ones last.
  Grouping them (or sorting by name) has not been asked for.

## §1cb - HER OWN DIAL GOES BACKSTAGE, THE VIEWER FILLS ITSELF, AND THE READER GETS FOUR PAGES (2026-09-30)

One message, six lines, four separate builds in it:

> *"- PACE notice doesn't need to be seen and displayed in the chat window. It belongs in BACKSTAGE
> like SYSTEM messages. like SYSTEM: [[PACE: 5]]*
> *- In DOX VIEWER make FILL THE STAGE default*
> *- In DOX VIEWER and a button to trigger an AI summary if one doesn't yet exist. The new button
> order should be THE STORE, TEXT, SUMMARY, OUTLINE, FIND, RELATED, EXPORT*
> *- TEXT: Displays the text of the document only*
> *- SUMMARY: If there is already a SUMMARY of the document saved and present, display it. If there
> is now summary present, ask the user if they want to create an AI summary. When the user exits the
> summary page, ask if the user wants to save the new summary. If yes. TIMESTAMP and save summary.
> The next time to user visits that document, the saved summary is displayed.*
> *- OUTLINE: Display the tags/keyword blocks only, (no doc text)*
> *- GRAPH: New button. If exists, display simple GRAPH data in the LOREPACK for relationship,
> connections, etc.*"

### 1. THE PACE RECEIPT IS BACKSTAGE NOW, IN HIS OWN SHAPE

**WHAT HE ASKED FOR, AND HOW IT IS WRITTEN.** The dial a pace move leaves behind belongs with the
terminal's other machinery, not in her mouth: `BACKSTAGE` (the same veil the recall, the citations
and the timings ride behind, `images.js`'s `backstage()` = a SYSTEM entry with the `backstage`
class), and in the shape he typed out himself - `SYSTEM: [[PACE: 5]]`. The line is
`[[PACE: <n>]]` followed, when SHE was the one who moved it, by `SHE MOVED HER OWN PACE :: <was> ->
<n>/5.`; an act that simply ran at her pace says `HER PACE AT THIS ACT - IT IS HERS TO MOVE WITH
[[PACE: <1-5>]] IN ANY REPLY, HOUR OR ACT.` Nothing about the dial is visible with the veil down,
and the act's own visible notice (`THE INFINITY :: SHE MOVED FIRST [...]`) no longer carries a
`PACE n/5` tail - the number is on the infinity button, where a machine setting belongs.

**A REAL BUG WAS FOUND UNDER THIS ASK.** `chat.js` had a directive regex for every line she can put
in a reply - ACT, WAIT, SILENT, PAGE, MOOD, SHOW, READ, ... - and **none for PACE**. So a
`[[PACE: n]]` line in an ordinary reply was never stripped: it was left sitting in her visible text
for him to read, and the pace never actually moved (the act and quiet-hour paths each did their own
`match`, which is exactly why the gap went unnoticed). The proof is in his own log: two archived
replies (log entries 15 and 17 on the day this was written) still read *"...leaving Me staring
[[PACE: ...]]"* - her words, with the machinery still in them. `PACE_DIRECTIVE` (matching PACE or
INTENSITY, 1-5) now sits with the other directives, `extractDirectives()` carries a `pace` field,
the line is taken out of `text` before anything is printed, and the turn path calls
`proactive.pace()` and then writes the backstage receipt. Both other roads in (a quiet hour in
`shift.js`, an act in `proactive.js`) now go through the same parser and write the same receipt.

### 2. FILL THE STAGE IS THE DEFAULT, AND IT STAYS THE DEFAULT

Selecting the viewer has given it the whole stage since 2026-09-26, but **giving the stage back by
hand** wrote localStorage `doxAutoFull = 0` and stopped it filling for good - a hand saying "not
this time" became a preference nobody could find. Now `loadAutoFull()` always answers true (and
**clears** the old `doxAutoFull` key on the way, so a "no" left on the device from before cannot
shrink it), and `setFull(false, {byHand:true})` only puts `autoFull` down **for the rest of this
session**: the stage comes back, the panel keeps its own open/closed memory, and the next load fills
again because that is the default. Verified live: selecting the viewer gives `full === true`,
`body.classList.contains("doxFull")`, the button reading `⤡ GIVE THE STAGE BACK` with
`aria-pressed="true"`; giving it back leaves the session-only quiet and the button honest.

### 3. THE READER'S OPS ROW, AND THE FOUR PAGES ON ONE DOCUMENT

The reader's row was `← THE STORE | TEXT | OUTLINE ▼ | FIND ▼ | RELATED | EXPORT`. It is now
**`← THE STORE | TEXT | SUMMARY | OUTLINE | GRAPH | FIND ▼ | RELATED | EXPORT`** (verified from the
DOM). His own line put GRAPH after SUMMARY and omitted it from the run-through order, so the
placement is a judgement: GRAPH sits **after OUTLINE**, because TEXT, SUMMARY, OUTLINE and GRAPH are
the same kind of thing - four ways of looking at the ONE document that is open - and FIND, RELATED
and EXPORT are things done *with* it. The active page is shown by a lit button (`button.on`,
`aria-pressed`), one page at a time, and a document **always opens in TEXT**.

- **TEXT** is the reader that was already there, and now means exactly that: the find bar, the text
  window, the foot. Nothing else.
- **OUTLINE** is his second line, taken at face value: **no document text at all**. The document's
  own `TAGS:`/`KEYWORDS:` lines first, then `WHAT IT IS ABOUT` - the store's own top terms for the
  document (cosine of the document against the whole index) plus its title's words, with a stopword
  table so "THE" does not become a keyword - then every heading as a row that opens TEXT at that
  line. Verified on a manual page: 8 rows, 21 chips, and no `.dmsText` element anywhere on the page.
- **SUMMARY** is the AI summary lane, below.
- **GRAPH** is the LOREPACK's own triplet graph, below.

### 4. THE SUMMARY PAGE, AND WHERE A SUMMARY LIVES

**ONE RECORD PER DOCUMENT, ON THIS DEVICE, BESIDE THE DOCUMENT AND NEVER INSIDE IT.** kv
`dms_summaries`, keyed by the document's own key, holding `{doc, text, at, title, kind, scope, path,
lines, chunks, bytes, from}`. Three faces, and they are the three things he described:

- **KEPT** - a summary is already here: the text, the stamp (`MADE <the date and time it was made, on this device>`), what it
  was made from (`FROM THE WHOLE DOCUMENT (4453 CHARACTERS)`), and **MAKE A NEW ONE** /
  **FORGET THIS SUMMARY**.
- **ASK** - none is kept: *"NO SUMMARY IS KEPT FOR THIS DOCUMENT."* and what it would be made from,
  then **MAKE A SUMMARY** / **BACK TO THE TEXT**. Nothing is spent until he presses it - the call
  costs a key, and a page he only looked at should not cost anything.
- **MAKING** - one call to the text engine, streamed (`onChunk`) into the page with an animated
  working note, `9000` characters of the head and, for a document longer than that, its `3000`
  character tail (a long document ends as well as begins).

**LEAVING ASKS, IN PLACE.** If a new summary is on the page and unsaved, every way out - the TEXT and
OUTLINE buttons, `← THE STORE`, RELATED, opening another document, the `×`, `/docs close` - raises
the same bar inside the page: *"SAVE THIS SUMMARY BEFORE LEAVING?"* with **SAVE IT** / **DISCARD IT**
/ **STAY HERE**. SAVE IT stamps it and then does what he was on his way to do. The store is shared by
one page, so it never asks on a page with nothing new on it.

**THE COMMAND LANE** (`/docs summary [<DOC>]`): bare or with a document shows what is kept,
`... make` writes one, `... forget` takes it off, and `/docs summaries` lists them (`60` shown,
with the count). The verbs were added to `words()` with `graph [<DOC>]`, and `outline <DOC>` now
lands on the OUTLINE page rather than the text (it used to open the reader and leave it in TEXT,
which was the old row's only mode).

### 5. THE GRAPH PAGE

**WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM.** An imported MYTHOS pack is minted with a triplet graph - source,
relation, object rows - and `mythos.js` already had them, but only behind its trace API, and
**nothing could read them all**: this session added `allEdges()` and `allVectors()` to
`mythos.js` (read-only; the first thing they do is call `idb()`, because `everyRow` on a store
whose connection is not open yet throws *"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'transaction')"* -
which is exactly what it did the first time it was called, and the reason the guard is in the code
and in its comment now).

**WHAT IT DRAWS.** The whole graph is 450 edges over 14 relations in 2 edge-bearing loci (3 loci on
the roster) when this was written. A graph with a document open is read **against that document's own
words**: `graphTerms()` (the same top-terms-plus-title machinery the outline uses) and `edgesFor()`,
which matches a term at a **word start** (`wordHas`) rather than anywhere - otherwise "he" matches
"the" and every edge in the pack looks related to everything - and scores each edge by how many of the
document's words it names. So `manual:turn` honestly shows **3** matching edges, while
`manual:commands` shows 13-14.

The page itself: the notice (`450 EDGES IN 2 LOCI (3 ON THE ROSTER) :: 14 RELATIONS IN USE` and
`THIS PAGE IS ABOUT ONE DOCUMENT :: ...`, or `THIS IS THE WHOLE GRAPH ...`), the relation inventory,
a row per locus with its edge and fragment counts and the packs it came from, and then the SVG -
sources down the left, objects down the right, barycentre-ordered by their neighbours so the curves
cross as little as they can, degree-capped at `GRAPH_NODES` 12 names a side, deduplicated by
`s|r|o`, drawn as gentle alternating Bezier curves with a small **numbered disc** on each one. Below
it, the numbered edge list the discs refer to (`14` rows, "AND N MORE" when there are). With no
document open - the GRAPH button in THE STORE's own ops row - it draws a `sampleEdges` spread of the
whole graph and says so.

### 6. WHAT WAS VERIFIED

- **Driven on the live page** (`scratch/doxmodes.js`): the ops row is exactly the order above; a
  document opens in TEXT; OUTLINE gives 8 heading rows and 21 chips with **no text element**; SUMMARY
  with nothing kept gives the ASK and its two buttons; GRAPH draws (SVG present, edges and rows
  counted, the notice naming the count); TEXT comes back with its 86 lines.
- **The summary lifecycle, end to end, with one real engine call** (`scratch/doxsummary.js`): no
  summary kept before → made (1138 characters) → the head stamps itself `NOT SAVED YET` → leaving
  via TEXT raises the bar → SAVE IT saved it **and ran the pending action** → the store then holds
  `records=1 / keys=manual:turn` → reopening the document shows the KEPT face with its stamp and
  the stamp it read back (this device's own clock) with `FROM THE WHOLE DOCUMENT (4453 CHARACTERS)` → `/docs summary <DOC>`
  prints the same text → making a second one and closing raises the bar again → DISCARD IT closed
  with `draft=null` → FORGET THIS SUMMARY asked first, then `records=0`. **His kv was left clean.**
- **The graph's own picture, looked at** (`scratch/graphshot.js` rasterises the SVG, then
  `vision`): names readable inside the frame, the numbered discs legible, the curves smooth - judged
  "highly readable", with only minor bunching of discs 4/5/13 in the densest column.
- **The two roads into the graph page** (the reader's GRAPH and THE STORE's): `setMode("graph", doc)`
  called **without** `showReader()` first now draws that document's graph with no stale "READING …"
  note left behind, and the store's own GRAPH gave the whole-graph page with the
  `THIS IS THE WHOLE GRAPH` line and only `← THE STORE` in the row - both fixed this session
  (`showGraphMode` now sets `view.kind`/`view.doc` itself, and `showGraphView` sets `view.doc`,
  because "the graph on screen is the graph of the document on screen" has to be true on every road
  in).
- **The pace receipt** (`[[PACE: ...]]` backstage): `liaDirectives("Hello there. [[PACE: 4]] And more
  text.")` returns `{text: "Hello there.  And more text.", pace: 4}` - the line is out of her words -
  and a `backstage()` line lands in the log with the `backstage` class (checked in the DOM, then
  removed). **The two archived replies that still carry a `[[PACE:` in their visible text are the
  evidence of the old bug, and are history, not output.**
- **The phone** (390x844): no horizontal overflow in any of the four pages, the ops buttons 34px, the
  panel filling the stage once `decks.measure()` has run.

**FILES TOUCHED by §1cb.** `src/js/dms.js` (the ops row and the four pages - `renderTextBody`,
`renderOutlineBody`, `renderSummaryBody` + the summary store, `renderGraphBody`/`graphSvg`/`loadGraph`
+ `graphTerms`/`edgesFor`/`wordHas`, the `showGraphMode`/`showGraphView` fixes, `showReader`,
`closeViewer`, `switchMode`/`leaveSummary`/`askToLeave`, the always-fill default, the new export
door and `state()`), `src/js/mythos.js` (`allEdges`/`allVectors`, read-only, behind `idb()`),
`src/js/chat.js` (`PACE_DIRECTIVE`, the `pace` field in `extractDirectives`, the turn path's
receipt), `src/js/proactive.js` (the act notice's PACE tail moved to backstage), `src/js/shift.js`
(a quiet hour's pace, the same way), `src/js/config.js` (`LIA_DMS_SUMMARY_CHARS` 9000,
`LIA_DMS_SUMMARY_TAIL` 3000, `LIA_DMS_SUMMARY_LISTED` 60), `index.html` (the viewer button's title,
the `#dmsView` comment, the FILL key's title), `src/css/terminal.css` (the lit op button, the

`src/commands/commands.json` (the `/docs` usage and description, and the `/infinity` description's

chronicle entry and `chronicle.json` - and `src/rtfm/commands.md` and the three `src/pack/` files

**STILL OPEN.**

- **A summary is stamped but never checked against its document.** Change the document and the kept
  summary goes on saying what it said; the page shows the stamp and what it was made from, and the
  honest thing - a "the document has changed since" line (`bytes`/`lines`/`at` are all in the
  record, so it is a comparison away) - has not been asked for.
- **The graph page is drawn, not steered.** No zoom, no pan, no press-a-node; `GRAPH_NODES` 12 a
  side is the readability ceiling and the numbered list is the way to the rest. A node that opened
  the documents that mention its term would be the natural next thing.
- **/docs index (the meaning lane) is not wired into SUMMARY or GRAPH.** Both lanes here are lexical
  and structural on purpose - they cost no key - and a summary of a document the store has embedded
  would be a different (and better) summary.

## §1cc - THE DOX VIEWER'S LONG LISTS ARE PAGINATED (2026-09-30)

One line:

> *"Paginate DOX VIEWER MAIN STAGE text results"*

### 1. WHAT WAS WRONG WITH THEM

The viewer holds **967 documents** and a search answers with up to **60 hits**, and both were drawn
into the MAIN STAGE as **one scroll**: forty-nine screenfuls of store rows, or three of results, with
the only way to move being the scrollbar, and nothing on the screen saying where in the list he was or
how much of it was left. The terminal's own text side was no better: `/docs list` printed sixty rows
and said *"AND 907 MORE (THE PANEL DRAWS EVERY ONE)"*, which was true and not much use, and
`/docs search` printed every hit it had.

### 2. THE PAGER (src/js/dms.js)

**One piece of arithmetic and one bar, shared.** `pageOf(total, want)` clamps to the real page count;
`pagerBar(pg, label, setter)` draws the bar. Both long lists use them - `renderList` (the store) and
`renderResults` (the search) - so the two cannot disagree about what a page is, and `view.page` is one
number for both. The page size is `LIA_DMS_PAGE` in `src/js/config.js` (**20**); the fallback in
`dms.js` is the same twenty, so the module still works if the config is trimmed.

    PAGE 1 OF 49 :: SHOWING 1–20 OF 967 DOCUMENTS     ⇤ FIRST  ↑ EARLIER  ↓ LATER  LAST ⇥

- **It is not a filter.** The count in the bar is the WHOLE answer and every row of it is still drawn,
  twenty at a time. The pages of the store list are the same sorted list, sliced; the pages of a search
  are the same ranked hits, sliced.
- **The end-stops are dimmed AND clamped.** FIRST and EARLIER are disabled on page one, LATER and LAST
  on the last page, and `pageOf` clamps besides - `setPage(99999)` lands on page 49 of 49 (measured),
  `setPage(0)` on page 1 of 49.
- **The bar sticks to the top of the body.** It is the reader's own foot reused (`.dmsFoot.dmsPager`,
  a bottom border instead of a top one, `position: sticky; top: 0`), because twenty rows on a phone are
  taller than the window and the way on must not be scrolled out from under him.
- **PageUp / PageDown** move the page when the focus is inside the panel, and are handed straight back
  to any field that wants them: the handler is on the panel and returns early for an `INPUT`, a
  `TEXTAREA` or a `contenteditable`, and the query box, the find box and the talk strip are all fields.
- **What resets it.** A new search (`runSearch`) and a new collection (the scope selector) go back to
  page 1; `← THE STORE` from a document keeps the page he was on; `/docs list PAGE 5` sets the page
  whether the panel is open or not, so the receipt and the panel never disagree about where he is.

### 3. THE SAME PAGE IN THE LOG (the terminal side)

`listText`, `searchText` and `findText` now take a page. Each prints one page of its answer and ends
with the same facts and the way on:

    PAGE 2 OF 49 :: 20 OF 967 DOCUMENTS SHOWN
    /docs list PAGE 3 READS THE NEXT 20 (THE PANEL HAS THE SAME PAGER ON ITS FOOT).

`takePage()` takes the page off the END of the request, so `/docs search backup CODE PAGE 2` still
reads CODE as the scope (the scope word is taken from the request AFTER the page is off it), and a bare
number after `list` is a page (`/docs list 3`), because list has nothing else a number could mean.
`/docs state` prints a `PAGE` line while a list or a set of results is on the screen, and
`usageText()` documents `[PAGE N]` on all three verbs.

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, DRIVEN FOR REAL (`scratch/doxpager.js`, re-runnable)

- **The store list**: `PAGE 1 OF 49 :: SHOWING 1–20 OF 967 DOCUMENTS` with twenty rows drawn and
  `chatlog/manifest.json` first; LATER gave page 2 with a different first row
  (`chronicle/2026-09-26-the-docs-viewer.md`); FIRST came back. The count in the bar and the row count
  in the DOM agree on every page.
- **The clamps**: `setPage(99999)` gave `PAGE 49 OF 49 :: SHOWING 961–967 OF 967`; `setPage(0)` gave
  `PAGE 1 OF 49 :: SHOWING 1–20 OF 967`.
- **The search**: sixty hits come back (the search's own ceiling) and the panel draws them as
  `PAGE 1 OF 3 :: SHOWING 1–20 OF 60 RESULTS`; LATER gave page 2, first row `TODO.md › 1o. THE BACKUP
  ...`, and the bar said `PAGE 2 OF 3 :: SHOWING 21–40 OF 60`.
- **The log**: `/docs list page 2` printed `PAGE 2 OF 49 :: 20 OF 967 DOCUMENTS SHOWN` and set the
  panel's page; `/docs search backup page 2` printed `PAGE 2 OF 3`; `/docs search backup CODE page 2`
  still read the scope as CODE; `/docs find dms_summaries` printed `PAGE 1 OF 1 :: 4 OF 4 DOCUMENTS
  SHOWN`; `/docs state` printed the PAGE line; `/docs list 3` read the bare 3 as a page.
- **The panel, looked at** (a rendered capture of `#dmsView` and `vision`): the caption readable and
  unclipped, all four keys with their arrow glyphs rendered, FIRST and EARLIER visibly dimmed while
  LATER and LAST are bright, nothing overlapping.
- **The phone (390x844)**, measured: the bar was 87px of a 504px body, because the caption and FIRST
  shared a row and the other three wrapped to a second. The caption now takes a line of its own
  (`flex: 1 1 100%` with `row-gap: 4px` in the phone media query), all four keys sit on one line under
  it, and the bar is **65px**. No horizontal overflow anywhere in the panel, and `vision` judged the
  two-row bar well-proportioned.
- **Nothing else moved**: `scratch/doxmodes.js` still passes end to end (the ops row, TEXT, OUTLINE
  with eight rows and no text, the SUMMARY ask, the GRAPH page), the reader still has its own window
  foot (`LINES 1–86 OF 86`, EARLIER / LATER / TOP / END) and **no pager bar of its own**, and the
  page's own boot is clean.

**FILES TOUCHED by §1cc.** `src/js/dms.js` (`PAGE_SIZE`, `pages`, `pageOf`, `pagerBar`, `pageMove`,
`scopesNow`/`mineNow`, `view.page`, `renderList`, `renderResults`, the PageUp/PageDown binding in
`wirePanel`, `runSearch`, the scope listener, `listText`/`searchText`/`findText`, `pagerText`,
`takePage`, the `list`/`search`/`find` verbs, `state()`, `stateText()`, `usageText()`, and the exports
`page`/`pageSize`/`setPage`), `src/js/config.js` (`LIA_DMS_PAGE` 20), `index.html` (the `#dmsView`
comment), `src/css/terminal.css` (`.dmsFoot.dmsPager` and its disabled keys, plus the phone rules),
`src/commands/commands.json` (the `/docs` usage and description), `src/README.md`, `src/TODO.md` (this
section), this session's chronicle entry and `chronicle.json` - and `src/rtfm/commands.md` and the
three `src/pack/` files were regenerated in the same pass because `commands.json` and `index.html`
changed.

**STILL OPEN.**

- **The pager is on the two text lists only.** STATS, RELATED and the graph's numbered edge list are
  still drawn whole - each is short by construction (a dozen loci, eight related documents, fourteen
  edges), so pagination there has not been asked for and would be furniture.
- **No jump-to-page box, and no page in the LINK.** The bar has the four moves and the number of the
  page; a box he can type a page into, or a share link that opens on page 7, has not been asked for.
- **The reader's window is still LINES, not rows**, deliberately (see THE PAGER in the README): the two
  pagers are not the same pager and are not meant to become one.

## §1cd - THE PAGINATOR IS A CONTROL DECK AT THE FOOT OF THE PAGE, ABOVE THE CHAT BLOCK (2026-09-30)

One line:

> *"make the paginator graphic with simple buttons in a control deck at the bottom of the page above the chat block"*

### 1. WHAT HE MEANT, AND WHERE THE DECK WENT

§1cc had just put a pager on the two long text lists as a bar STUCK to the top of `#dmsBody`
(`.dmsFoot.dmsPager`, `position: sticky`). This is his second word on the same furniture, and it is
about PLACE and SHAPE: the paginator should be a **deck** - the terminal's own word for a control strip
- at the **bottom of the page**, **above the chat block**.

The placement follows from a rule he gave in §1bi: **while a VIEWER is open the LOWER DECK stands down**
("in the DOCS viewer the lower deck hides"). The paginator exists for the DOX VIEWER's lists and for
nothing else, so the only deck that can hold it and still be on screen while a list is drawn is a deck
INSIDE the viewer. And the chat block at the bottom of the page, when the viewer has the page (FILL THE
STAGE, the default), is the **TANDEM'S TALK STRIP** - the viewer's own foot, with the two presences, the
newest line of the log and the one-line input that drives `#userInput` and `window.send()`. So "at the
bottom of the page above the chat block" is one flex slot, exactly: between `#dmsBody` and `#dmsTalk`.

    <div id="dmsView" class="lorePanel dmsPanel">     (a column)
      .dmsBar      the search, the scope, SEARCH, FILL THE STAGE, the way out
      #dmsOps      what is on the screen + the ops row of the view
      #dmsBody     THE ROWS - the only part that scrolls (flex: 1 1 auto)
      #dmsPager    THE PAGINATOR DECK (flex: 0 0 auto)   <- new, §1cd
      #dmsTalk     THE CHAT BLOCK - the talk strip (flex: 0 0 auto)
    </div>

A deck is strictly better than the sticky bar for the reason the bar existed: the bar had to imitate
"never scrolled away" with `position: sticky`; a deck is OUTSIDE the scrolling area, so it is never
scrolled at all. It also gives the body its own top back (no bar eating the first row under the ops
row), and the reader gets the bottom edge it already had.

### 2. THE DECK (index.html + src/js/dms.js + src/css/terminal.css)

**THE MARKUP.** One empty element in `index.html`, after `#dmsBody` and before the talk strip:
`<div id="dmsPager" class="dmsPager" hidden></div>`, with the comment carrying his words and the reason
for the place (the engine evaluates square brackets in comments too, so the comment was written with
none in it).

**THE GRAPHIC IS THE PAGE NUMBERS** (`pageChips(page, total)`, `PAGER_CHIPS = 3`): the pages around the
one he is on, the FIRST and the LAST always drawn, and the runs between them elided as `…` - data, not
a styling trick, so the painter has nothing left to work out:

    «  ‹  1  …  24  [25]  26  …  49  ›  »     PAGE 25 OF 49 :: SHOWING 481–500 OF 968 DOCUMENTS

- A chip that is not his page is a PRESS (`pagerGo(n)`); his own page is lit (`.dmsPgChip.on`, the same
  inverted language as the ops row's lit mode) and says `aria-current="page"`.
- The simple buttons are the four arrows: `«` first, `‹` earlier, `›` later, `»` last. `pagerKey()`
  DIMS an end (`disabled`) rather than taking it off the row, so the deck does not change shape at the
  edges - and the ends are in the chips anyway, which is why the arrows could be this plain.
- Three chips around his page (not five) is what keeps ONE row of keys on a phone AND on the stage: a
  paginator that is a different shape on a phone than on the stage is a paginator he learns twice.

**THE COUNT, IN TWO LENGTHS.** `PAGE n OF m :: SHOWING a–b OF t DOCUMENTS` / `... RESULTS`, and on a
phone `a–b OF t` alone (the `.full` / `.short` pair `#loreStatus` already uses) - because the page
numbers are drawn as chips two centimetres to the left of it. Nothing measures anything; the CSS picks.

**ONE PAINTER, ONE SOURCE.** `paintPager()` is the only writer of `#dmsPager`, and it only ever READS
`view`:
- It is called at the top of every view paint - `renderList`, `renderResults`, `renderReader`,
  `renderGraphView`, `showStats`, `showRelated` - so any view that has no page takes the deck off the
  screen (a document, a summary, an outline, the stats, the graph, the neighbours), and an empty list
  takes it off too (a deck over an empty store is chrome about nothing).
- The page the rows are sliced by (`pageOf`) and the page the deck names are the same arithmetic on the
  same total, so the two can never disagree. `view.page` is clamped once, in `pageOf`, by the deck.
- `pagerGo(p)` is the single door for a move (the deck's keys, PageUp/PageDown, and `setPage` from
  outside), and it puts the body back at the TOP: both `#dmsBody` and its parent, because which of them
  is the scroller depends on the mode and arriving halfway down a page reads as lost rows.

**WHAT WENT.** `pagerBar()` is deleted and so are the `.dmsFoot.dmsPager` rules (sticky, its bottom
border, its dimmed keys) - one paginator, not two. `pageMove` and the exported `setPage` now go through
`pagerGo`; every `see THE PAGER` in `dms.js` was renamed `see THE PAGINATOR DECK`.

### 3. THE WORDS FOLLOWED THE FURNITURE

- `usageText()`'s PAGINATION paragraph (`/docs help`): the deck at the foot, the chips, the arrows
  either side, "sitting above the chat block".
- `stateText()`'s PAGE line: "THE ARROWS ON THE PAGINATOR DECK, OR /docs list PAGE n".
- `listText` / `searchText` / `findText`: "(THE PAGINATOR DECK AT THE PANEL'S FOOT READS THE SAME PAGE)."
- `src/commands/commands.json`: the `/docs` description's pagination sentence, with his words in it.
- `index.html`: the `#dmsView` comment, and the new deck's own comment.
- `src/README.md`: THE PAGER section rewritten as **THE PAGINATOR DECK**, plus the measured note below.

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, DRIVEN FOR REAL

Two re-runnable harnesses: `scratch/doxdeck.js` (the deck itself, geometry and presses) and
`scratch/doxpager.js` (§1cc's harness, rewritten in the same pass for the new selectors - its old
`#dmsBody .dmsPager` selectors were the change).

- **The deck is where he asked**, measured at 1920x1080 filled: deck 1920x30 at y=932, its bottom edge

## §1ce - HIS OWN LINE STAYS IN THE STRIP, WITH ITS OWN PREFIX (2026-09-30)

One line:

> *"Prefix the Chat with HITL: on send to chat in the display"*

### 1. WHICH DISPLAY, AND WHY IT WAS THE STRIP

One sentence, no object named: "the Chat", "on send to chat", "the display". So the first half of the
work was FINDING the display he was looking at, and the search was run against the live page rather
than guessed at:

- **The log** (the MAIN STAGE, "the chat window" in his own words) already does it, and is not what
  he means: a conversation line is painted `[stamp] HITL: (LAYER)` by `print()` (`src/js/images.js`).
  Read off the live page, the newest entries are `HITL: (LIA) ` / `LIA ID: (LIA) ` - his send is
  prefixed there, has been for months, and nothing in this build changed that.
- **The CHATLOG's display** (`src/js/chatlog.js`) labels its turns `USER` / `SYSTEM` / `LIA`
  (`normRole`, `up(mk.k)`). It was the strongest rival reading - "the Chat" - and it is not it: the
  CHATLOG is the raw record of the conversation this terminal was built in, IMPORTED as text, and in
  the record on this machine his lines carry no role line at all (the index reads `system: 18,
  lia: 3`). Nothing is "sent" into it; nothing on this page writes to it.
- **The reader** (`reader.js`: `Patrikios: ...`) and the gallery's memo lines (`gallery.js`) name his
  side by name rather than by prefix, and neither is a send.
- **The platform's own chat panel** is another origin and untouchable from this page.

What was left is the display he is actually talking into while he is reading: **the TANDEM'S TALK
STRIP** (`#dmsTalk`), the viewer's own foot - which §1cd had just called "the chat block", the same
phrase he used in the sentence before this one. Driven for real with a stubbed model
(`scratch/mirror.js`, sampling `#dmsTalkSay` every few tens of milliseconds through one send), the
strip showed:

    before send   ALIA: You are still obsessing over the pipes while I am sitting here starving. ...
    +40ms..+2.5s  ALIA: IS THINKING ...
    after reply   ALIA: STUBBED REPLY.

**His own line was never drawn at all.** `paintTalk()` read the newest line of the log correctly, and
then threw it away: `if (airWord === "HER TURN") line = { who: ALIA, text: "IS THINKING ..." }` ran
BEFORE the log was consulted, and the air lamp goes to HER TURN ~40 ms after a send. So the one moment
the strip had his words to show was the one moment it refused to show them - and with FILL THE STAGE
being the default, `body.doxFull #output { display: none }` means the strip is the ONLY place a line
of his is on the screen at all while a document has the stage. What he types vanishes into a display
that says she is thinking. That is the thing to fix, and "prefix the chat with HITL: ... in the
display" is exactly it: his line, with the prefix it carries in the log.

### 2. THE FIX (src/js/dms.js, `paintTalk()`)

One precedence list, in the order a reader would want it, with the reasons written next to it:

1. **A fresh `note()`** (a refusal, a slash command's receipt, the link) - it is a guest that holds
   the line for `NOTE_MS` 9 s, and it now beats HER TURN too (see §3 below).
2. **A line of his that she has not answered yet** - it IS the newest line of the log, so it is drawn
   with its own prefix (`line.who` gives `HITL: `, class `.dmsSay.me`). The test for this is one
   comparison and needs no clock: `newest.who === HITL` means "the newest conversation line on the
   page is his", which is true exactly while he is waiting for her. Nothing is sticky - the moment
   her answer prints, her line is the newest one and takes the strip by itself, which is also why
   "IS THINKING ..." still has a job: it is shown when SHE is the newest word on the page (a proactive
   check-in, or her turn after she has answered).
3. **`ALIA: IS THINKING ...`**, with the pulse - and the pulse is now on the thinking line only
   (`thinking` is a separate boolean from the air lamp), because `.dmsSay.thinking` animates the line
   it is put on and his words are not a spinner.

    if (fresh) line = fresh;
    else if (airWord === "HER TURN" && !his) { line = { who: ALIA, text: "IS THINKING ..." }; thinking = true; }
    else line = newest;

### 3. A SECOND HOLE THE SAME LINE CLOSED

The old order put HER TURN above the note, so **a note could not be read while she was working** -
and the notes written at exactly that moment are the refusals: `SHE HAS NOT FINISHED THE LAST ONE ::
SEND AGAIN WHEN SHE HAS.` (the SEND key is locked while she has the floor), `THE TEXT ENGINE IS NOT
AVAILABLE ON THIS PAGE`, `THE ENGINE IS STILL WRITING THE SUMMARY`. A guest that is painted over in
the one moment it exists is not a note. A fresh note now wins over everything, and /tandem's own
toggle note and the reader's receipts are unaffected (they are read while no turn is running).

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, DRIVEN FOR REAL

`scratch/mirror2.js` (the strip's own send, the stub gated behind a promise so the sample can be taken
WHILE she is still working - a plain `Promise.resolve` reply races the check) and `scratch/mirror3.js`
(the lower deck's box while the viewer has the stage, at 390x844). Both clean up after themselves: the
new log entries are removed, `master_log` is written back from the copy taken before the turn, and
`chatHistory` is truncated. Measured:

- **A send from the strip**: the display read `HITL: MIRRORMARK from the chat block`, class
  `dmsSay me`, while the air lamp beside it said `HER TURN` - and it stayed for as long as the turn
  did.
- **A refusal during her turn**: pressing SEND again while she was working put
  `SHE HAS NOT FINISHED THE LAST ONE :: SEND AGAIN WHEN SHE HAS.` on the line (class `dmsSay sys`) -
  the note that used to be invisible.
- **Her answer takes the line by itself**: `ALIA: STUBBED REPLY.` (class `dmsSay her`).
- **"IS THINKING ..." still arrives** when she is the newest word: with the lamp forced to HER TURN
  and her answer as the newest line, the display read `ALIA: IS THINKING ...`, class
  `dmsSay her thinking` - and it went back to her answer the moment the lamp was let go.
- **The lower deck's own box does it too**: with the viewer filled (`#output` computed `display:
  none`) a send from `#userInput`/`sendBtn` printed `HITL: LOWERDECKMARK out of the big box` on the
  strip and then gave the line to her answer.
- **The phone (390x844)**: the strip is 150px while she works and 131px after - unchanged, because
  the mirror line is capped at `.dmsSay { max-height: 3.1em }`; a wrapped HITL line scrolls inside the
  element rather than pushing the decks around (measured: line 35px, `scrollHeight > clientHeight`).
- **Nothing else moved**: `__bootIssues` is empty after a reload and `rtfm.check()` is empty (no
  command text and no `src/rtfm/` page changed in this build).

One honest note: the first attempt was a `page_eval` with `reload: true`, and it hit the 15 s
"stopped responding" guard - the harness ran while the page was still re-rendering its template and
replaying the 21 archived turns. A plain `page_refresh`, a poll for the entries, and the same harness
then passed. The freeze was the harness arriving during a render, not a loop in the new code.

### 5. STILL OPEN

- **A capture is still impossible** (the same broken `snapshot.js` as §1cd: it hangs on any element),
  so this build too is verified by DOM text, classes and geometry rather than by a picture.
- **His line is drawn for a turn, not kept.** The strip is deliberately one line and the newest one -
  a scrolling mirror of the conversation in the viewer's foot has not been asked for, and the log is
  one keypress away (`FILL THE STAGE` off) when he wants the whole of it.
- **A stamp is not drawn on the strip's line.** The mirror shows words; the log keeps the clock. If he
  ever wants the stamp in the strip, it is `entry.dataset.ts` and one more span.
- **Long lines are clipped, not shrunk** (`.dmsSay` max-height 3.1em, 400 characters through
  `short()`), which is the same bargain the strip already made for her lines.

### 6. FILES TOUCHED

`src/js/dms.js` (`paintTalk()`: the new precedence, the `fresh` / `his` / `thinking` locals and the
comment carrying his words and the reason), `src/js/chat.js` (the `/help docs` topic's TALKING WHILE
YOU READ paragraph - his line stays up with its own prefix), `src/README.md` (THE TANDEM's "Talking is
part of looking" bullet, with the precedence list), `src/TODO.md` (this section), this session's

(new harnesses), `scratch/findspeakers.js` and `scratch/talkspeaker.js` / `scratch/talkspeaker2.js`
(the searches that ruled the other displays out) - and `src/pack/files.json` was regenerated because

## §1cf - A PAGE IS NINE ROWS, AND THAT IS A LID (2026-09-30)

One line:

> *"limit pagination to 9 max as this is what fills the MAIN STAGE at my current font size and looks good."*

### 1. WHAT CHANGED

- `src/js/config.js`: `LIA_DMS_PAGE` 20 -> **9**.
- `src/js/dms.js`: **`PAGE_MAX = 9`**, and `PAGE_SIZE` is now
  `Math.min(PAGE_MAX, LIA_DMS_PAGE)` - the config value may ask for FEWER rows and can never ask for
  more. The paginator's own example comment (`PAGE 4 OF 108 :: SHOWING 28-36 OF 968 DOCUMENTS`) was
  brought up to date with it.
- `src/README.md`: THE PAGINATOR DECK's example lines, the count in two lengths, "twenty at a time"
  -> "nine at a time", the `setPage(99999)` end stop (page 108), the log's printed page, a new bullet
  for "nine rows, because nine is what fills the stage", and the store's own count where the examples
  quote it (968 when §1cc measured it, 971 today - the chronicle grows, and the README quotes a
  measurement, so the measurement was refreshed rather than left to rot).
- **Everything the terminal COMPUTES about the page followed the constant on its own**: every printed
  number was already derived from `PAGE_SIZE` (`/docs state`'s `A PAGE IS n ROWS`, the three footers'
  `READS THE NEXT n`, the deck's `PAGE n OF m :: SHOWING a-b OF t`, the ops row's row count), so what
  had to be reworded was only the sentences that QUOTED the size as twenty: `/docs help`'s PAGINATION
  paragraph, the paginator's own example line and two code comments in `dms.js`, the `#dmsView`
  comment in `index.html`, and the `/docs` description in `commands.json`. The log's page was
  verified: `PAGE 2 OF 108 :: 9 OF 971 DOCUMENTS SHOWN` /
  `/docs list PAGE 3 READS THE NEXT 9 (THE PAGINATOR DECK AT THE PANEL'S FOOT READS THE SAME PAGE).`
- **The cheatsheet did NOT change, and that was verified rather than assumed.** `src/rtfm/commands.md`
  carries each command's ONE-LINE SUMMARY and its usage, not its description, so the regenerated
  markdown came out byte-identical to the shipped file (11422 bytes, compared in the page) and
  `rtfm.check()` is empty.

### 2. WHY A LID AND NOT JUST A VALUE

"9 max" is the whole instruction, and it is taken literally: 9 is the largest a page may be. A page
that holds more rows than the stage can show is a page he has to scroll INSIDE a page, which is the
thing pagination exists to prevent - so the ceiling is the point, not the number. The knob stays
(`LIA_DMS_PAGE`, one line in `config.js`) and can still shorten a page; a shorter page is never a lie
about what is on the screen.

### 3. WHAT WAS MEASURED (driven, `scratch/page9.js` and `scratch/page9b.js`)

- **The panel, filled**: at 1440x900 the body is 661px and nine rows are 447px of it (68%); at
  1920x1080 the body is 841px and nine rows are 450px. What the OLD page would have been at 1440x900:
  20 rows = 1000px, i.e. a 339px scroll inside the page - the thing his eye caught.
- **108 pages**, not 49: 971 documents at 9 rows. The last page holds only what is left - **8** of
  them (964-971) - which is the arithmetic that proves the slicing is live rather than a constant.
- **The deck**: `PAGE 1 OF 108 :: SHOWING 1-9 OF 971 DOCUMENTS`, and at the end
  `PAGE 108 OF 108 :: SHOWING 964-971 OF 971 DOCUMENTS` (eight rows, because 971 is not a multiple of nine) with the chips reading `1 106 107 [108]` and
  `»`/`›` dimmed; `setPage(99999)` lands on 108 and says so, `setPage(1)` goes back.
- **The log**: one page of the store list is **16 lines** (the title and the rule, nine rows, the page
  line, the way on, and the two trailing pointers) - which is what "a page that fits the stage" means
  in the log, where the text size is HIS (`--log-fs`, A- / A+).
- **The search** still asks the meaning lane for `PAGE_SIZE * 3` = 27 hits (measured 27), so the
  number of pages a search can have did not shrink with the page.
- **Boot clean, `__bootIssues` empty, `rtfm.check()` empty**: no command's words quote the page size,
  so `commands.json`, `src/rtfm/commands.md` and the pack's two root copies are untouched.

### 4. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED

- **The reader's own window** is still `READ_WINDOW` 260 LINES: a page of a document is a screenful of
  reading and a page of a list is a screenful of rows, and the reader's window is not this paginator.
- **The gallery's `PER PAGE [50]`** is its own control and its own lists; nine is the DOX viewer's
  page.

### 5. STILL OPEN

- **The page does not follow the font size.** Nine is a fixed lid, as asked. If he ever wants the page
  to FILL the stage rather than FIT it, that is an adaptive page size measured off `#dmsBody` (and a
  different thing to explain in the log's footer, since a page would then mean different rows in
  different windows).
- **A tall stage shows empty space under the page.** Measured above (32% of the body at 1440x900):
  nine rows and then black. Nothing is wrong with it - it is one page, drawn whole - but if he would
  rather see more rows on a big screen, the lid is the one constant to move.

### 6. FILES TOUCHED

`src/js/config.js` (`LIA_DMS_PAGE` 9), `src/js/dms.js` (`PAGE_MAX`, the clamped `PAGE_SIZE`, the
paginator's example comment, the `/docs help` PAGINATION paragraph, two code comments that quoted
twenty), `index.html` (the `#dmsView` comment), `src/commands/commands.json` (the `/docs`
description), `src/README.md` (THE PAGINATOR DECK: the examples, the new bullet, the printed page and
its measured 16 lines, the end stop at page 108, and the store's count refreshed to 971),
`src/TODO.md` (this section), this session's chronicle entry and `chronicle.json`,
`scratch/page9.js` and `scratch/page9b.js` (new harnesses) - and `src/pack/index.html.txt` and
`src/pack/files.json` were regenerated in the same pass, because `index.html` and the file tree
changed. `src/rtfm/commands.md` needed no regeneration (verified byte-identical - see §1).
**NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1cg - THE HOUSE NEGATIVE LIST IS THE DEFAULT FOR EVERY RENDER (2026-09-30)

One line:

> *"Add for default negative image prompts: modern city, skyscraper, car, streetlight, concrete,
> smartphone, ... cartoony ... deformed face"*

(116 terms, given as one comma-separated list.)

### 1. WHERE A "DEFAULT NEGATIVE" LIVES, AND WHAT WAS DONE TO IT

The terminal already HAS a default negative: **THE HOUSE NEGATIVE LIST**, the `negative` string at the
top of `src/studio/recipes.json`, printed by `/recipe negative` and used by every recipe that says
`"house"` (baseline, scene, muse). What it was NOT was a default for a render that arrived with no
negative of its own - a plain CREATE with an empty box, `/image`, a picture SHE described herself all
went to the image service with NO negative at all, which is exactly how the artifacts his list names
kept arriving. So:

- **His list was added to the house list** (`src/studio/recipes.json`), merged and de-duplicated:
  **his terms FIRST**, in his own order, then the house terms his list does not already carry. Twelve
  exact duplicates were dropped (his list shares `blurry`, `low quality`, `text`, `watermark`, `logo`,
  `banner`, `signature`, `username`, `cartoon`, `extra limbs`, `mutated hands`, `fused fingers` with
  the shipped list). Measured: **1951 characters, 152 terms** (48 house + 104 new).
- **The order is the point, and it is written down**: a service whose tokenizer cuts a long negative
  cuts the TAIL, so what he asked for sits at the head and the older quality/anatomy terms follow.
- **`studio.resolve` now falls back to it** when nothing else supplied a negative - the first source
  with one wins: the forge's BOX, then a `NEGATIVE PROMPT` section in the document, then a
  `(negativePrompt:::...)` cut, then the house list. Nothing of his is ever replaced: a document with
  its own list keeps it, `aphro` keeps its own, `negative=none` in a recipe still means none.
- **The file's own `note` says so**, and `/recipe negative` now prints what the list is used by.

### 2. THREE HOLES THE FALLBACK WOULD HAVE LEFT OPEN, CLOSED IN THE SAME PASS

1. **NO WAY TO SAY "NO NEGATIVE AT ALL".** Once a render with nothing gets the house list, an empty
   box no longer means "no negative" - and a fallback with no escape is a trap: a picture he WANTS of
   a marble temple has to be possible. So the word **`none`** (also `no` / `off` / `nothing`) is now
   read in the three places he can write a negative: the box, the document's own `NEGATIVE PROMPT`
   section, and a `(negativePrompt:::...)` cut. In each of them it means no negative - the same word
   the recipe lane has always accepted as `negative=none`.
2. **THE FORGE WOULD HAVE COPIED THE LIST INTO HIS BOX.** `createImagesRun` fills the negative box
   from the resolver when the box is empty ("saves him the copy-paste") - which, with the fallback,
   means a page and a half of terms appearing in his form on the first CREATE and being SAVED as his
   own text in kv. Guarded: the box is filled from the prompt's own negative only, never from the
   fallback (`res.report.negativeFrom !== "house"`), and the report line is what tells him the house
   list is in use.
3. **THE RECORD WOULD HAVE LIED.** The vision lane stored `negative: parsed.recipe.negative` - an
   empty string for a render that was really sent with 1951 characters of house list. `renderImageNow`
   now returns the negative it actually sent (`finalNegative`, taken after the resolver and after the
   `{a|b}` choice), `renderVision` prefers that over its caller's, and the vision lane stores it - so
   the vault record, the render book and `/renders` name the list that went out.
   (`/create` already recorded `res.negative`, so the forge lane was honest by construction.)

### 3. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, DRIVEN (scratch/house1.js)

- **The merge**: the list parses (152 terms), opens with his own first term and closes with the house
  terms, and every term checked is present - `modern city`, `marble temple`, `Corinthian columns`,
  `pastoral daylight`, `cubist composition`, `text overlays`, `plastic doll skin`, and the old
  `worst quality`, `bad anatomy`, `extra digits`, `out of frame`.
- **Where the negative comes from, seven ways**, all read off `studio.resolve()`:
  a plain render -> `house`, 1951 chars; a box with his own -> `form`, his list; a box saying `none`
  -> `none`, nothing sent; a document with a `NEGATIVE PROMPT` section -> `file`, that section; a
  document whose section says `none` -> none; a `(negativePrompt:::cartoon, text)` cut -> that;
  a cut saying `none` -> none.
- **The render path itself**, with `root.generateImage` stubbed and the request read off it:
  `renderVision("a marble temple at noon", "")` handed the service the 1951-character house list and
  came back with `out.negative` = that list (so the record is honest), and
  `renderVision("a queen", "my own list")` handed over and reported his list.
- **The report line** is in `resolve().report.notes`, which is what the forge and the vision lane both
  print: `THE HOUSE NEGATIVE LIST IS IN USE (1951 CHARS) :: NOTHING ELSE SUPPLIED ONE. /recipe
  negative SHOWS IT - AND THE NEGATIVE BOX, A NEGATIVE PROMPT SECTION OR (negativePrompt:::none)
  OVERRIDES IT`.
- **The words in the terminal followed**: `/recipe negative`'s own output, the `/help recipes` topic
  (a new paragraph: THE NEGATIVE LIST IS THE HOUSE LIST BY DEFAULT), the `/recipe` description in
  `commands.json`, and the README's new section (THE HOUSE NEGATIVE LIST).
- **Boot clean and `rtfm.check()` empty** (no cheatsheet change is needed: it carries each command's
  one-line summary and usage, not its description - see §5).
- **A syntax error was caught by the same check and fixed**: the new `/recipe negative` string carried
  an unescaped apostrophe in `TERMINAL'S` (the perchance error banner and `consoleOutput` reported
  `Unexpected identifier 'S'` at chat.js:3705). Worth recording: the JS was written by a script, and
