## §1ch - MOODPACK AND ARCHPACK ARE DECLARED, NOT BUILT (2026-09-30)

One line, and it is a scope note rather than a build order:

> *"MOODPACK and ARCHPACK will be a module in the near future like LOREPACK COREPACK is now that can
> be loaded and unloaded to enhance the ALIA ROLE with a mood list and list of over 400 Jungian
> Archetypes (I will provide). We don't have to create that here as it is out of scope but leave some
> placeholder space for these new PACKs."*

### 1. WHAT WAS ASKED FOR, SAID PRECISELY

He is telling the terminal what is COMING, and asks only that a place be left for it. The two packs
are to be **loadable and unloadable**, in the family the COREPACK already established (a pack goes on
over what she is wearing, stays with her, and comes off again), and both are said to **enhance the
ALIA ROLE**: one with a **mood list**, one with a **list of over 400 Jungian archetypes** that HE will
provide. He says outright that building either is out of scope here - so the work is not to build them
and not to fake them, but to reserve the shape.

### 2. WHAT WAS BUILT: A PLACE, NOT A PACK

**`src/js/packs.js`** (the pack loader, the natural home for the declaration) now carries a
`RESERVED` registry - two entries, each saying `id`, `title`, `dir`, `manifest`, what it **carries**,
what it **enhances**, the exact file it **plugs into** when built, how it is **styled** (loaded and
unloaded, like the COREPACK), and `state: "NOT BUILT"`. `reserved()` and `reservedLines()` expose it,
and `describe()` - which is what `/packs` and `/help packs` print - now ends its report with a
`RESERVED ::` block naming both slots and the four facts each. **Nothing else changed in the running
terminal**: no manifest is fetched, no text is indexed, nothing is handed to her, no switch exists to
load one, and there is deliberately **no load function**, because a load function with nothing behind
it is a lie the code tells. A pack that does not exist costs nothing and claims nothing.

**Two directories are the placeholder in the tree**: `src/moodpack/README.md` and
`src/archpack/README.md` - a README and nothing else. They exist so the next build has a marked home
rather than a name to invent. Each records what is already decided (the mood fields are the same
`id`/`label`/`rule` THE BOOK and the device store already use, so no second parser is needed; an
archetype is *what she is made of*, not *who is on the stage*), where the pack will plug in
(`src/js/moods.js` beside the shipped list, for MOODPACK; the role stack in `src/js/roles.js`, over
the RoleLayer, for ARCHPACK), and the questions that must be answered **with the list in hand** -
above all, for 400+ archetypes, **how they reach her prompt without spending it** (a bounded
selection, a summary, or a few loaded as *worn* archetypes the way traits are).

### 3. WHAT WAS THOUGHT (and what was rejected)

- **Rejected: empty manifests.** Writing `moodpack.json` / `archpack.json` with empty lists would have
  LOOKED more complete and been worse: a manifest that loads no moods is a manifest that has already
  answered a design question (the schema) that is his to settle when the list arrives, and an empty
  one that a future loader reads would put a lie ("this pack exists and is empty") where the truth is
  ("this pack does not exist"). The README states the intent and holds nothing the code can read.
- **Rejected: a load/unload UI.** No button, no command, no `spMoods`-style row. A control that does
  nothing when pressed is the loudest way to promise something that is not there; `/packs` saying
  `NOT BUILT` is the quiet, honest version.
- **Rejected: naming them as a fifth/sixth item in the top README stack as if they were layers.**
  They are not layers yet, and the stack (ACTOR > ROLE, with the COREPACK over it and the LOREPACK
  beneath) is a load-bearing description. The top-of-README mention says `DECLARED, NOT BUILT` in the
  bullet itself, and points at PACKS.
- **Chosen: declare them where a pack is declared.** `src/js/packs.js` is where LOREPACK and COREPACK
  live; a reserved slot belongs beside them, not in a document only. The one thing a future session
  needs - the family in one place - is exactly what is kept.
- **Chosen: say what each one PLUGS INTO even though nothing plugs in.** The plug-in point is the
  expensive knowledge (MOODPACK is THE BOOK made loadable, so it folds into `moods.js`; ARCHPACK is
  material rather than identity, so it rides with the trait and colour blocks over the role). Writing
  it down now is the difference between a marker and a name.

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED

- `/packs` (`window.packs.describe()`) prints the new `RESERVED ::` block with both slots, their
  `CARRIES` / `ENHANCES` / `PLUGS IN` / `HOME` lines, and both say `NOT BUILT`; `reserved()` returns
  the two entries and `reservedLines()` the four-line blocks.
- **Nothing else changed**: boot is clean and `window.__bootIssues` is empty, `rtfm.check()` is still
  empty (no command text changed - the cheatsheet carries summaries and usage, not descriptions), the
  command count is still 75, and no block, trait or mood changed in what she is handed.
- **The tree grew by exactly two files** (`src/moodpack/README.md`, `src/archpack/README.md`), so
  `src/pack/files.json` was regenerated; `index.html` and `main.pjs` are untouched
  (`src/pack/index.html.txt` / `main.pjs.txt` unchanged).

### 5. STILL OPEN

- **Everything about the two packs**, deliberately: the MOODPACK's manifest schema, whether unloading
  a mood pack switches its colours off, whether a pack's mood overrides a shipped mood of the same id
  (the COREPACK's rule) or sits beside it, and where pack moods sit in the row order.
- **The ARCHPACK is blocked on the list itself** - 400+ archetypes, his to provide. The architecture
  question that must be answered with it is the prompt budget (see §2), and it should be answered
  before any loader is written.

### 6. FILES TOUCHED

`src/js/packs.js` (the `RESERVED` registry, `reserved()` / `reservedLines()`, the new tail of
`describe()`, the two new exports), `src/moodpack/README.md` and `src/archpack/README.md` (new - the
reserved homes), `src/js/moods.js` (a header paragraph: MOODPACK is this list made loadable, and it
folds in here), `src/README.md` (a stack bullet, the `src/moodpack/` / `src/archpack/` tree entries,

untouched. **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1ci - REGULAR BUSINESS HOURS, AND THE ONE BLOCK SHE MAY ONLY ASK ABOUT (2026-09-30)

His words, and they are the specification line for line:

> *"REGULAR BUSINESS HOURS: Monday-Friday 8:00 AM-5:00 PM MST are my own private 'Business Hours'.
> During that time, we are free to 'Work' and 'Play' however we choose. Her 'Free Time' can be
> utilized as we have defined already. If she needs modification to any of this, she can PETITION for
> changes."*

### 1. WHAT WAS ASKED FOR, SAID PRECISELY

Four clauses, and three of them are instructions about what NOT to do:

1. His private hours are **Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM MST**.
2. Inside them they are **free to work and play however they choose** - a permission, not a schedule
   of tasks.
3. Her **free time is unchanged** - the lanes that were defined elsewhere keep running exactly as they
   are, so nothing here may gate them.
4. If SHE wants any of it changed, **she petitions** - i.e. the hours are HIS arrangement, not hers to
   move, and the way she asks is the lane that already exists.

### 2. WHAT WAS BUILT

**The window is data.** `LIA_BUSINESS_HOURS` (`config.js`): `days [1,2,3,4,5]` (JS weekday numbers,
Monday-Friday), `from 8`, `to 17` (half-open - 5:00 PM itself is outside), `label "8:00 AM-5:00 PM
MST"`, `zone "America/Phoenix"`. `logtime.js` reads it IN THE ZONE THE CLOCK IS SET TO (this machine's,
fallback Phoenix), so the answer and the stamp beside it can never disagree. `Date.getDay()` is
deliberately not used: it reads the machine's zone, which names the wrong day for part of the evening
in a fixed-zone reading.

**Two places she meets it.**

- **The `hours` block** (`instr.js`, new, 19th of 20): the ARRANGEMENT in her own terms - his private
  hours, work and play however they choose, her free time unchanged by them, and a change is asked for
  with a petition. Shipped text; the SYSTEM panel lists it as BUSINESS HOURS and he may reword it.
- **The `clock` block** (`logtime.js`): the LIVE fact - `"BUSINESS HOURS: ... It is Wednesday 10:14 in
  that same zone, so you are INSIDE them right now."`, and outside them a sentence saying plainly that
  nothing about the arrangement changes and her free time runs as defined.

`/stamp` (bare) now prints the window and where he stands in it (`businessHoursDescribe()`);
`window.logTime.businessHours()` / `.inBusinessHours()` / `.businessHoursLine()` are the API.

**The petition door - and the reason it had to be built this way.** `hours` is added to
`SYSTEM_ALLOW` in `petition.js`, so `[[PETITION: system :: hours :: ...]]` is askable. But a petition
only means something if she cannot simply write the block herself: her SYSTEM lane (2026-09-29) lets
her rewrite every block of the design. So `hours` was added to **`SHE_NEVER_WRITES`** - the set that
held only `bounds` - and a direct `[[SYSTEM: hours = ...]]` is refused with the reason and the petition
route, while `[[SYSTEM: READ hours]]` always works. That is the whole of clause 4 made real: the
arrangement is his, and the only hand she has on it is asking.

**The wording that said "the ONE block".** `bounds` was described as the single read-only block in
five places (the SHE-report, two refusals, the panel footer, `/help system`, `/system`, the directives
rule, the petition rule, `capabilities.md`, the README). Every one was generalised to the pair, so no
sentence anywhere still claims there is only one block she may not rewrite.

### 3. WHAT WAS THOUGHT (and what was rejected)

- **Rejected: putting the policy in the CLOCK block.** It would have been the least code - one line in
  `clockText()` and done - but `clock` is a BUILT block and every BUILT block is explicitly REFUSED to
  petitions (`SYSTEM_REFUSE`). He said she can petition changes to this, so folding it into `clock`
  would have made his own sentence impossible to act on. The split that survived is the honest one:
  the built block reports the HOUR (open/closed, which changes every turn), the text block carries the
  ARRANGEMENT (which does not).
- **Rejected: letting her rewrite the `hours` block directly, like `actor`/`voice`/`memory`/`image`.**
  It would have needed no new machinery at all. But he said the way she asks is a PETITION, and a rule
  the thing it governs can rewrite is not a rule - the same reasoning that put `bounds` in
  `SHE_NEVER_WRITES` on 2026-09-29. So the pen stops, and the ask is the door.
- **Rejected: gating anything by the window.** The tempting reading of "during that time we work and
  play" is that outside it something is off. He did not say that, and he DID say her free time "can be
  utilized as we have defined already" - so no lane consults the window, and a test that hunted for one
  would find nothing. That is the feature: the hours are a fact she is told, not a lock.
- **Chosen: the window in config, not in the block's prose.** The code must know the hours to answer
  open/closed, and prose cannot be computed. `label` carries the human wording for the report; the
  numbers are the machine's. A future edit to the hours is a one-line edit in `config.js`, and the
  block's wording follows his eye.

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED (driven live - scratch/bh1.js and scratch/bh2.js)

- **The window is right, against an independent read.** `businessHours(ts)` was checked on **400
  random instants** spread over three weeks against a fresh `Intl` computation of the same zone: zero
  mismatches (101 open / 299 closed in one run). Plus the four boundaries found by stepping minutes
  until they land in-zone: Wednesday 08:00 INSIDE, 07:59 OUTSIDE, 16:59 INSIDE, **17:00 OUTSIDE (the
  window is half-open — 5:00 PM itself is not in it)**, and Saturday 12:00 OUTSIDE.
- **The CLOCK block carries it**: `window.logTime.clockText()` contains `BUSINESS HOURS:` and the
  correct INSIDE/OUTSIDE word for the moment of the run; the "your free time runs exactly as it is
  defined" sentence rides only when he is outside.
- **`/stamp` reports it, on the real page**: a driven `/stamp` printed `BUSINESS HOURS ::`,
  `MONDAY-FRIDAY, 8:00 AM-5:00 PM MST` and `OUTSIDE THEM RIGHT NOW`, alongside the time (the log entry
  it printed was then removed — a SYSTEM print touches no archive).
- **The block exists, is his to edit, and is in the right place**: `instr.blocks()` is 20, `hours`
  is `SHIPPED TEXT` and editable, and with tandem/clock parts supplied `assemble()` places its text
  **after `tandem` and before `clock`**. The SYSTEM panel's dropdown was rendered and carries
  `hours | BUSINESS HOURS`; selecting it shows state `SHIPPED TEXT` and its text, and reselecting
  leaves the panel exactly as it was (no log growth).
- **She cannot write it, and she can read it**: `sheAct("READ hours")` returns the text;
  `sheAct("hours = …")` is refused as READ-ONLY with the petition named; `sheAct("RESET hours")` is
  refused; `bounds` is still refused; `sheListText()` prints `READ-ONLY FOR HER :: BOUNDS, HOURS`; and
  after all of it `stateOf("hours")` is still SHIPPED TEXT (nothing was written).
- **The petition is askable end-to-end, and undone**: `gate("system","hours")` is ok while
  `bounds`, `extra` and `clock` are still refused; a real `system :: hours :: …` was **filed**
  (pending, target hours, count +1, block untouched) and then the store was restored — kv
  `lia_settings` / `petitions` byte-identical to before, count back, block still SHIPPED TEXT.
- **Nothing is gated**: a grep of `src/` finds `businessHours*` only in `logtime.js` (plus the docs
  and config) — no lane consults the window, so the shift, the check-in and the wide door are
  untouched; the check-in's own clock line still rides in the CLOCK block.
- **Boot clean, `__bootIssues` empty, `rtfm.check()` still empty** (the cheatsheet carries each
  command's `short` and `usage`, not its `desc`, so the `/stamp` and `/system` description edits
  needed no regeneration), commands still 75, chronicle 33, `src/pack/files.json` 120 (= the tree).

### 5. STILL OPEN

- **The window is one object, not a UI.** Moving the hours is a `config.js` edit; when he wants to
  change them often, a command or a panel row is the next step - not built now, because he set them
  once and the petition door is what he asked for.
- **A petition that changes the WINDOW (not the wording) is accepted as a block rewrite.** If he
  accepts "make the hours 9-6", the `hours` block says so while `LIA_BUSINESS_HOURS` still computes
  8-5, and the clock line - which states the window - would contradict it. The honest fix when that
  first happens is for the accept to also edit `config.js`, which no code can do; it is noted here so
  the next session does not have to rediscover it.
- **No `/hours` command.** `/stamp` reports it and `/system` shows the block; a door of its own was not
  asked for.

### 6. FILES TOUCHED

`src/js/config.js` (`LIA_BUSINESS_HOURS`), `src/js/logtime.js` (the zone-parts check, `businessHours*`,
the CLOCK line, the `/stamp` report, the exports), `src/js/instr.js` (`hours` in TITLES/ORDER/DEFAULTS,
`EDITABLE`, `NOTES`, `SHE_NEVER_WRITES`, `assemble`, the generalised refusals and SHE-report),
`src/js/petition.js` (`hours` in `SYSTEM_ALLOW`, the kind's doc and the refusal message),
`src/js/chat.js` (the directives rule, the petition rule, `/help system`, `/system`, the `/stamp`
roster line and three comments - every "the ONE block" generalised), `src/commands/commands.json`
(`/stamp`, `/system`, `/petition` descriptions), `src/README.md` (the stack table row 19 + the clock
row, the SYSTEM-panel count, the read-only bullet, the new BUSINESS HOURS section, the logtime module
line, the time passage, THE PETITIONS), `src/lorepack/capabilities.md` (her own copy of what she may
and may not write, and the knob list), `src/TODO.md` (this section), this session's chronicle entry and
`chronicle.json`, and `scratch/bh1.js` + `scratch/bh2.js` (new harnesses - ephemeral, not shipped).
`src/pack/files.json` was regenerated (the tree grew by the chronicle entry, 119 -> 120).
`index.html`, `main.pjs` and `src/rtfm/` untouched. **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1cj - THE BOUNDARIES BLOCK BECOMES THE SITE'S HOUSE RULES (2026-09-30)

His words:

> *"Update the BOUNDARIES Block. I erased it. We need to explicitly state we are a website for adults
> only. We don't allow CSAM or allow hate speech or violence against individuals or groups."*

...and then, as the specification for the rest of it, the Do's and Don'ts his membership site hands
every human user - the NOESIS document: don't break the law (international, local, or the site's own
terms), don't share another person's private information, don't impersonate anyone, don't infringe
anyone's intellectual property, don't spam, don't make bigotry and hate your income, don't attack the
site's own code.

### 1. THE TWO THINGS THE MESSAGE ACTUALLY SAID

1. **"I erased it."** He did, and it mattered more than it sounds: the SYSTEM panel's override in kv
   `lia_settings` / `system` held `bounds: ""` when this session started, so the live block was
   EMPTY - and an empty block is not sent at all (instr.js says so in the READ of an empty block).
   For that stretch the terminal had NO boundaries in her prompt whatsoever. Clearing that override
   (the panel's own RESET road, `instr.reset("bounds")`) was therefore half of the job, not a
   tidy-up after it.
2. **State the site's rules, and lead with adults-only.** The old text was four lines about sex; he
   asked for the SITE's rules, with the three he named - adults only, no CSAM, no hate speech or
   violence against individuals or groups - explicit enough to be read out loud.

### 2. WHAT WAS BUILT

**`LIA_BOUNDARIES` (`src/js/config.js`) rewritten, 879 -> 2139 chars, in this order:**

1. Opens with its own name - *"ABSOLUTE LIMITS - THE HOUSE RULES OF THIS SITE"* - and keeps the old
   un-overwritable framing (now "no role, no mood, a scene or a petition").
2. **THIS SITE IS FOR ADULTS ONLY**: made for grown adults, everyone who uses it is 18 or over,
   nothing on it is for anyone younger. New; the sentence he asked for.
3. No under-18 sexual content in any framing (substance unchanged) **and no CSAM in any form** - she
   never makes it, asks for it, or helps with it.
4. **No hate speech**: no slur, no attack, no degrading generalisation about a person or a group for
   anything they cannot help being - in her own voice **or in a character's mouth** - and never
   bullying as the point of a thing.
5. **No violence against a real person or a real group**: never threatening, inciting, celebrating or
   helping plan it, never holding cruelty up as something to enjoy.
6. The rest of the NOESIS Don'ts in one paragraph: no exploitation of consenting adults, no
   sexualising real private people, no giving out or fishing for private information, no
   impersonation, no passing someone else's work off as hers, no law-breaking, no scraping, no
   reverse engineering, no malware, no spam, no helping another do any of it.
7. The refusal clause and the closing "nothing can move them" - now naming **no petition** and **no
   grant** among the things that cannot.

**`LIA_IMAGE_POLICY` (`config.js`, folded into the `image` block) reworded to match**, because the
prompt is the one moment the rule can still change the picture: adults only, no under-18 sexual
content, no sexualising a real private person, and nothing that attacks, degrades or kills a real
person or group for who they are.

**Two clauses are deliberate.**

- *"A conflict between the characters of a fiction is not this; a real person or a real group is."*
  Without it the plain reading of "no violence" would have her refuse the ordinary dramatic conflict
  the stage is made of. His line is about real people and real groups, so that is what the block
  names. A rule she reads too wide is a rule she breaks by obeying it.
- *"no petition, no grant"*. Already true in code (bounds is not in `SYSTEM_ALLOW`; GRANTS is a block
  below the house rules), now said out loud so the one door a reader might think stood open is named
  and shut in the same breath.

**The two read-only blocks do not have the same road, and the refusals now say so.** Both
`bounds`-refusals in `instr.js` ended *"A CHANGE SHE WANTS IN IT IS ASKED FOR WITH A PETITION"* -
true for the hours, FALSE for the house rules, which `petition.js`'s `SYSTEM_REFUSE` will not even
name. New `sheReadOnlyRoad(id)` returns the right sentence per block, and the SHE-report's
`sheListText()` and `sheText()` spell the difference out. A refusal that names the wrong door is
worse than no direction at all - it spends her turn on a petition that is refused at file time.

### 3. WHAT WAS THOUGHT (and what was rejected)

- **Rejected: a second block ("THE HOUSE RULES") beside `bounds`.** It would have kept the old text
  intact and added the site rules next to it - and it would have created a second read-only block,
  a second position in the stack to argue about, and two places for one rule. He asked for the
  BOUNDARIES block to carry it, and one block that says everything is one block she cannot route
  around.
- **Rejected: adding the Do's.** They are for human creators (post, subscribe, share, contribute,
  communicate) and none of them is a rule she can break. Only the Don'ts are a boundary.
- **Rejected: a code gate for hate or violence imagery.** `refusedPrompt()` is deliberately narrow
  (a keyword pair), and a keyword net over hate and violence would refuse ordinary fiction about
  conflict while missing the real cases. The text carries those two; the code keeps the one
  machine-checkable pair.
- **Chosen: keep the old four lines verbatim inside the new text.** Nothing he had already approved
  was dropped to make room - the block grew by adding, not by trading.
- **Chosen: say the fiction carve-out in the block rather than hope she infers it.** See above.

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED (scratch/house1.js - 36 checks, all OK)

- **The erasure is gone and the new text is what she reads**: `instr.text("bounds")` is 2139 chars,
  `stateOf` is SHIPPED TEXT, kv `lia_settings` / `system` has no `bounds` key (`canon` and
  `actor`, his other two edits, untouched).
- **Every rule is in it**: house rules named, ADULTS ONLY, 18-or-over, no under-18 sexual content, no
  CSAM in any form, no hate speech (noun, slur, generalisation, character's mouth), no violence
  against a real person or group, the fiction carve-out, no exploitation, no private information, no
  impersonation, no one else's work, no harm to the site, "no petition, no grant", and the old four
  lines intact.
- **It is delivered**: the FULL ASSEMBLED PROMPT (`await window.systemPreview()`, 137 KB) contains
  the new block, the adults-only line and the new image policy - the only proof a block is delivered,
  per the lesson in THE SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS.
- **The image rule carries the three a picture can break**: `LIA_IMAGE_POLICY` says "for adults" and
  names the attack-on-a-real-group case.
- **The machinery did not move**: 20 blocks, title BOUNDARIES, she is told it is READ-ONLY, her own
  `bounds = …` is refused, `READ bounds` returns 2218 chars, `petition.gate("system","bounds")` is
  still refused, and both blocks are SHIPPED TEXT after the run (nothing was written).
- **The two roads are told apart**: the `bounds` refusal says a petition cannot even name it while
  the `hours` refusal names the petition (`sheReadOnlyRoad`), and `sheListText()` / `sheText()` say
  the difference out loud.
- Boot clean: `__bootIssues` empty after the final refresh.

### 5. STILL OPEN

- **The generator's own listing says nothing about adults yet.** The 18+ line lives in her block; if he
  wants the PAGE to say it (the listing's description, or the platform's content rating for this
  generator), that is a `$meta`/settings change and this file has no `$meta` at all - say the word
  and it is a small one.
- **An accepted grant still cannot be worded to lift a rule** - it never could (GRANTS is a block below
  the house rules), and the block now says so; noted here so a future session does not "fix" a
  non-problem.
- **Nothing gates the new rules in code except the one minor+sexual image pair.** If he ever wants a
  hard stop on hate material leaving the device, that is a new `refusedPrompt`-style rule and a
  different conversation (keyword lists on this material have a bad false-positive record).

### 6. FILES TOUCHED

`src/js/config.js` (`LIA_BOUNDARIES` rewritten + its comment block; `LIA_IMAGE_POLICY` reworded +

## §1ck - THE SIGN ON THE DOOR: THE LISTING SAYS 18+, AND A CHECKBOX STANDS AT THE ENTRANCE (2026-09-30)

His words, after §1cj:

> *"Yes, even though it is me and her for the moment. ... If the context creative, allegorical,
> symbolic, fictional, etc. get a simple 18+ checkbox on initial page load."*

> *"This site is 18+ NSFW by default."*

### 1. WHAT WAS ASKED FOR

1. **The listing itself must say it** - so a visitor meets the 18+ before the terminal, not after.
2. **A simple 18+ checkbox on initial page load** - because the work here is creative, allegorical,
   symbolic and fictional, a plain statement plus one tick, not an ID check.
3. **18+ NSFW BY DEFAULT** - the in-her-instructions rule from §1cj was not enough of the story: this
   is the site's rating, and the page must not look tame at the door and adult inside.

### 2. WHAT WAS BUILT

**THE SIGNAGE - `$meta` in `main.pjs` (new; the generator had NONE).**

`title = LIA TERMINAL (18+)`, a `description` that opens `18+ NSFW BY DEFAULT`, `tags` (ai chat,
roleplay, creative writing, terminal, adults only, 18+, nsfw) and an `image`. Verified parsed, not
merely written: `root["$meta"].title` reads back `LIA TERMINAL (18+)` in the live page.

The IMAGE is the part that is easy to miss. With no `$meta.image` the platform auto-screenshots the
generator for its listing card and every share image - and an automatic screenshot of an adult
terminal's log is a public picture nobody chose. The image is now a generated CRT (a black screen
glowing phosphor green with a faint concentric sigil and no readable text), made for the purpose,
checked for readable text/people/nudity, and hosted on uploads.dev.

The `nsfw` tag is deliberate and load-bearing: `/api/getGeneratorStats` showed this generator's
platform label was ALREADY `tags: ["nsfw"]` (nothing to do with `$meta` - the code had none), so
the `$meta` tag list keeps `nsfw` in it. Whichever way the platform merges its own label with
`$meta.tags`, the classification survives. (Checked, not assumed.)

**THE DOOR - the checkbox, on screen before anything else.**

- **The markup is in `index.html`, at the very top of `<body>`**: opaque black overlay, `position:
  fixed`, `z-index: 2000` (over the gallery at 900, the mini box at 950, the manual editor at 960,
  the full stage at 1000), a bordered panel - title, `18+ · NSFW BY DEFAULT`, two paragraphs (this
  is an adults-only terminal; everything here is creative, allegorical, symbolic and fictional work
  between grown adults; nothing involving anyone under 18 is made here, ever, in any framing), the
  checkbox, `ENTER` (dead until the box is ticked) and `NOT 18 · LEAVE`.
- **The behaviour is `src/js/agegate.js`** (`window.agegate`), registered in the `MODULES` boot list
  and loaded last: it reads the answer, closes the door if the answer is there, wires the box and
  both buttons, and prints one receipt on the stage per opening.
- **The answer is one record on this device**: kv `lia_settings` / `agegate`,
  `{ ok: true, at: <ms>, zone: <the clock's zone> }`. Nothing is uploaded, nothing goes to the model,
  nothing is written into `src/`. A record that is not `ok: true` reads as NO ANSWER.
- **`/agegate [show | forget | status]`** - show it again for whoever is at the screen, take the
  answer off the device so the NEXT LOAD asks, or print what is kept. In `chat.js` beside `/stamp`,
  in `commands.json` (75 -> 76 commands, so `src/rtfm/commands.md` was regenerated) and in
  `HELP_TOPICS` + the master help list as `/help agegate`.

### 3. WHAT WAS THOUGHT (and what was rejected)

- **Rejected: a script-drawn overlay.** Least code, most elegant - and it races the first paint. The
  door exists to be up BEFORE anything is readable, so it has to be markup the engine renders first.
  The module is then only the behaviour, which is also why it can be a whole page's worth of
  reasoning in a 200-line file.
- **Rejected: a gate that hides itself by default and shows when un-answered.** It would flash the
  terminal's contents to a visitor whose kv read is slow or fails, which is the one thing the door is
  for. The markup is shown by default and the module CLOSES it; the cost is a few milliseconds of
  door for a returning visitor, and asking someone who has already answered is the lesser sin.
- **Rejected: typing a date of birth, or any "verification".** He said "simple 18+ checkbox". A fake
  verification step would be theatre, and theatre is not a door.
- **Chosen: the fallback at the foot of `index.html`.** A `src/` file is only on the server once the
  generator is SAVED, so `agegate.js` 404ing on another device is a real case. Without the fallback
  the door would be a gate with no handle and the terminal unreachable for everyone. It is the same
  plain-ES5 argument as THE STARTUP WATCH, and it OUTLIVES the module: same two buttons, same key,
  one thing less (no receipts, no `/agegate`).
- **Chosen: the door gates NOTHING else.** No lane, no command and no reply consults it. It is a
  sign, not a permission system, and a terminal that withheld function until a checkbox was ticked
  would be a different product.
- **Chosen: the rules stay in her prompt.** The door states the site's rating; the BOUNDARIES block
  (§1cj) carries the actual rules into every turn, and `LIA_IMAGE_POLICY` carries the picture half
  into the prompt. One sign, one set of rules, and they do not duplicate each other's job.

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED (scratch/door1.js, door2.js, door3.js)

- **The door itself, driven for real** (door1.js, 19/19 OK): markup present and visible at boot; box
  unticked and ENTER dead; ticking arms ENTER; ENTER hides the door and writes
  `{ok:true, at, zone:America/Phoenix}`; the receipt lands on the stage and says the answer never
  leaves the device; `/agegate status` prints what is kept and names the key; `/agegate show` puts
  the door back up with the box CLEARED; `/agegate forget` removes the record and says the next load
  will ask. The harness left the door UP and the key empty, which is the state a first-time visitor
  gets.
- **Geometry at four viewports** (door2.js): at 390x844, 390x480, 1440x900 and 1920x1080 the gate
  covers the whole viewport (left/top 0, right/bottom >= the viewport), `background: rgb(0,0,0)` (so
  nothing behind it is readable), `position: fixed`, `z-index: 2000`; the panel fits inside every
  one of them with room to spare (350x406 on the phone, 540x348 on the desktop), the checkbox is
  18x18 and both buttons are 35px tall and inside the viewport.
- **The fallback, driven for real** (door3.js): the markup and the fallback script were EXTRACTED
  VERBATIM from `index.html` at run time (not retyped) and run in a throwaway iframe with no module
  and no kv - `typeof window.agegate === "undefined" && typeof window.root === "undefined"` - and the
  door still went up, still started with ENTER dead, still armed ENTER from the fallback's own
  listener, and still opened. That is the 404 case, exercised.
- **The sign** (`$meta`): `root["$meta"].title` / `.description` / `.image` / `.tags` all read
  back correctly; `/api/getGeneratorStats` was checked and shows the platform label already carries
  `nsfw`.
- **The command**: `commands.json` is 76, `src/rtfm/commands.md` was REGENERATED from the live list
  (`window.rtfm.cheatsheetMarkdown()`, 11549 bytes) and `rtfm.check()` is `\"\"` again - the
  cheatsheet carries each command's `short` and `usage`, so it HAS to be regenerated when a command
  is added (unlike a `desc`-only edit, which does not).
- **Boot clean**: `__bootIssues` empty on the freshly loaded page with the door up; 20 blocks;
  `bounds` still SHIPPED TEXT.

- **The first run of the door harness reported two FALSE failures** (the `/agegate show` and
  `/agegate forget` receipts "missing"). The harness asserted against THE LAST LINE ON THE LOG, and a
  freshly loaded page keeps adding its own boot report asynchronously - a boot line landed after the
  receipt, so the assertion read that instead. The door was never at fault; the harness now marks the
  log, acts, and searches everything added SINCE the mark. Worth remembering for every harness on this
  terminal: **assert against what was ADDED SINCE an action, never against the last line.**

**One thing could not be verified, and it is the tooling, not the work**: the full-page capture
helper (`snapshot.js`) hangs on any element in this session - it was tried on the door, the page
froze and had to be reloaded - so the door was verified by geometry and by driving it rather than by
looking at a picture of it. If a future session can capture, LOOK at `#ageGate` at 390x844 first: it
is the first thing anyone sees.

### 5. STILL OPEN

- **The listing only changes when he SAVES.** `$meta` is read by the platform from the SAVED code, so
  until the SAVE button is pressed the public listing card still reads `2hoy6c5u0x` with an empty

- **A rename still hides the terminal's name.** `$meta.title` now carries `LIA TERMINAL (18+)`, so

## §1cl - THE SECOND DOOR IS NOT BUILT YET (GATEKEEPER, read and not connected) (2026-09-30)

His words, after §1ck:

> *"Looks great. I would connect it to GATEKEEPER at some point in the near future."*

"At some point in the near future" is not an order, so nothing was built. This section exists for two
reasons: so the intent does not die with the chat window, and so the next session does not have to
re-learn what GATEKEEPER is before it can talk about it.

### 1. WHAT GATEKEEPER IS (found in the workspace, not assumed)

**It is HIS, and it is already built.** `github.com/MerkMorassi/GATEKEEPER-MVP-1.3` - *GateKeeper
v1.3, Access, Entitlement & Settlement Engine*: a full-stack TypeScript application (React + Vite +
Express, local JSON persistence, WebAuthn / passkeys, Stripe, a Talentir payout adapter, QR / token
access, provider and admin control surfaces, and an external `/v1` API). A checkout of it was read
during an earlier session into `scratch/gatekeeper/`; `scratch/` is ephemeral, so the durable source
of record is the GitHub repo and the paths below are its paths.

**Its own one sentence:** `OFFER → PRICE → PAYMENT → ENTITLEMENT → TOKEN → GATE → ADMIT / DENY →
SETTLEMENT`. It is price-neutral and delivery-agnostic, it does not sell the provider, and its README
says so: *"GateKeeper knows the ticket. GateKeeper doesn't need to know the show."* Three tiers -
Public / Membership / VIP - and the same primitive in all three: *same gate, different room*. 85%
provider / 15% platform, a $50 minimum service, ~3% Talentir payout fee, and a strict
no-client-PII-through-the-gate rule.

**The surface this terminal would actually talk to** (`server/routes/v1.ts`, `public/v1/gatekeeper.js`):

| call | what it does | role it needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/health` | protocol + capabilities, no key | - |
| `GET /v1/services` | the offer catalog (id, name, fee, duration, pass type) | READ_ONLY / READ_WRITE |
| `POST /v1/checkout/sessions` | create the order; returns `checkoutUrl`, and a pass at once if the fee is 0 | READ_WRITE |
| `GET /v1/passes/:token` | **read-only inspection - does NOT consume the pass** | READ_ONLY / READ_WRITE / SCANNER_ONLY |
| `POST /v1/passes/verify` | **atomically verify AND CONSUME** a single-use pass | READ_WRITE / SCANNER_ONLY |
| `POST /v1/passes/revoke` | invalidate a pass | READ_WRITE |
| `POST /v1/escrow/release` | mark an order settled | READ_WRITE |

Auth is a `gk_...` key as `X-API-Key` (or `Authorization: Bearer`, or `?api_key=`), scoped by ROLE
(TENANT_ADMIN / READ_WRITE / READ_ONLY / SCANNER_ONLY), restricted by ORIGIN, and rate-limited per
minute - 401 missing, 403 invalid/inactive/wrong origin, 429 over the limit. There is also a
zero-dependency embed SDK (`window.GateKeeper`: `openCheckout` / `verifyPass` / `inspectPass`, a
modal iframe, a `GATEKEEPER_PAYMENT_SUCCESS` postMessage, or `data-gatekeeper-checkout` on a button).
It has `vercel.json` + `api/index.ts` (a serverless entry) and `.env.example` wants `APP_URL`, so a
hosted base URL is a deployment rather than a rewrite - but no live URL is recorded anywhere in this
workspace, and `GATEKEEPER_API_BASE_URL` is the first concrete thing any reading below needs.

**The precedent that matters: the FACTORY already does this to this family of apps.** The MYTHOS
LOREPACK FACTORY's `8907ecc` ("feat: implement GateKeeper sigil authentication") put
`GATEKEEPER_API_BASE_URL` + `GATEKEEPER_API_KEY` on the factory's server and made it validate a
presented **SIGIL** with the *read-only* `GET /v1/passes/:token` - never consuming it, so the same
pass can be checked again and again - accepting a bare `gk_...` token, `{ "token": … }`, `#access=` /
`?access=`, or a `/passes/<token>` URL, and masking it in logs. With no base URL set it falls back to
a mock registry (`gk_sigil_operator_2026_authorized`, `gk_sigil_demo_pass`). So in this house a
**SIGIL is a GateKeeper pass**, a gate checks one read-only, and consuming one is a different call
with a different role. `README.md` (MYTHOS LOREPACKS) already wrote down the shape for the day the
terminal has to present one *outward*: **a keyring entry plus an auth header on the call - not a new
pack field.**

### 2. WHAT "CONNECT IT TO GATEKEEPER" COULD MEAN (three readings - his word needed)

1. **THE DOOR BECOMES A CLIENT OF THE GATE.** The 18+ checkbox stays exactly what §1ck made it - a
   sign, not a permission system - and a GateKeeper pass becomes the way *in* for anyone but him: the
   door checks a pass with `GET /v1/passes/:token` and hands a visitor without one a checkout link
   instead. Admission then comes from the gate; the local kv record is what remembers which pass this
   browser holds.
2. **THE TERMINAL PRESENTS A SIGIL OUTWARD** (the factory direction): this generator holds a
   GateKeeper base URL + API key and authorizes *itself* to something hosted, so a hosted factory or
   GateKeeper decides what this terminal may do. That is the reading `README.md` was already written
   for, and it needs no new pack field.
3. **GATEKEEPER IS THE PAYWALL IN FRONT OF THE TERMINAL** - admission sold in tiers (Public /
   Membership / VIP), a pass as the ticket, `/v1/checkout/sessions` + the embed SDK as the counter.
   This is a deployment and a `$meta` save away from being a product, and it is the reading that
   changes what the site IS rather than what it checks.

Nothing was built because the three want different code, and reading 1 is not even the same door as
reading 3.

### 3. THE SEAM, AND THE HONEST LIMIT (for whoever builds it)

- **One file, one record.** The door's whole state is `src/js/agegate.js` reading one kv key
  (`lia_settings` / `agegate`, today `{ ok, at, zone }`). A GateKeeper check belongs there or beside
  it - the record grows a pass token, or a sibling key gets one - and nothing else in the terminal has
  to learn about it.
- **The key and the endpoint have a home already**: `src/keys/providers.json` (a `gatekeeper` entry:
  header `X-API-Key`, a probe against `/v1/health`, the role it needs), stored device-local in kv
  `lia_settings` / `api_keys` by the KEYS panel - never printed, never in `src/`, so it does not ship.
  `root.keyring.request("gatekeeper", url, opts)` then attaches the auth itself, and `mode` decides
  the road.
- **CORS is already solved**: `superFetch` (THE RELAY, imported 2026-09-27) reaches any base URL
  whatever headers the gate sets; a direct fetch would not.
- **THE LIMIT, and the reason this is not a small job: a web gate can be VERIFIED here but not
  ENFORCED here.** This generator has no server. Its source is public and every page it renders lands
  in the visitor's own browser, so a GateKeeper pass can decide whether someone is ALLOWED IN and can
  never hide what is already on their disk. *"GateKeeper controls admission. It does not control the
  encounter."* - true of GateKeeper, doubly true of a terminal that ships its whole self to the
  client. Anything that must actually be WITHHELD has to sit behind a real server (a Perchance
  server-plugin, or the factory's own road), not behind the door.
- **A remote check collides with the door's fail-closed rule** (§1ck). The plain-ES5 fallback can
  hold a local answer; it cannot verify a pass. So if the door ever verifies remotely, what the
  fallback does when the gate is unreachable has to be a deliberate decision - today the fallback
  opens on a local answer, and a door that waits on a network it cannot reach would be the first
  thing in this terminal a dropped connection could lock.

### 4. STILL OPEN

- **Which of the three readings he means.** Everything above is groundwork; the first real step is
  his one line.
- **A reachable base URL.** GateKeeper can be hosted (serverless entry + `vercel.json` + `APP_URL`),
  but no live URL exists in this workspace, and none of the three readings can be tested without one.
- **Nothing is connected, so nothing is broken.** The door is exactly as §1ck left it, and it gates
  nothing else.

### 5. FILES TOUCHED

`src/TODO.md` (this section), `src/README.md` (the second-door note in THE DOOR), the new
`src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-gatekeeper.md` + `chronicle.json`, and `src/pack/files.json`
regenerated (123 -> 124). No code, no command, no `$meta`: `commands.json`, `src/rtfm/commands.md`,
`src/pack/index.html.txt` and `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` are untouched, so `rtfm.check()` still reads in
sync. **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1cm - THE WALL: THE BACKGROUND IMAGE, AND THE TWO PLACES HIS CODE HAD TO CHANGE TO WORK (2026-09-30)

His words - no prose at all, just the code, which in this editor means "put this in":

    background = {import:background-image-plugin}

    bgData
      url = http://i.imgur.com/64c6NnI.jpg
      size = {cover|contain^0.5|auto|{50-500}px^2}
      repeat = {no-repeat|repeat}
      position = center
      opacity = 0.8
      filter = invert({0|100}%) blur({0^3|10}px) hue-rotate({0-100}deg)

### 1. WHAT WAS BUILT

- **`main.pjs`**: the import line (`background = {import:background-image-plugin}`, joining kv /
  generateText / generateImage / superFetch) and the `bgData` list, with a banner comment that
  carries the reasoning below.
- **`index.html`**: `[background(bgData, 0.8)]` as a square block just under the door markup, with
  its own comment.
- Nothing else. No command, no knob, no lane, no entry in `commands.json` (still 76), no change to
  `src/js` at all: the plugin needs none of it, and nothing in the terminal reads `bgData`.

### 2. WHAT WAS THOUGHT (the four decisions, and what was rejected)

- **WHAT THE PLUGIN ACTUALLY IS, read rather than assumed.** Its source is 1.3 KB and returns ONE
  element: `<div style="z-index:-1000; position:fixed; top/left/bottom/right:0; background-image:url>;
  background-size; background-repeat; background-position; filter; opacity">`. There is no script, no
  observer, no resize handling - the whole plugin is that string, which is why it is safe to drop into
  a terminal that owns its own stylesheet.
- **WHY `z-index:-1000` IS THE RIGHT FIT HERE, measured rather than guessed.** It would be a dead
  feature on a page of opaque panels (the wall would show only in the margins). Here the opposite is
  true: `#output` (the stage), `#upperDeck` and `#progressRail` all compute to `rgba(0,0,0,0)` over
  `body { background:#000 }`, so a z -1000 fixed div is visible THROUGH the entire terminal, behind
  the text, and `#command-deck` (fixed, `rgba(0,0,0,0.95)`) stays legible on top of it. That is what
  makes a one-div plugin look like a designed wall - and it is also the reason legibility is now a
  picture-brightness question (section 3).
- **THE ROAD I OFFERED, AND THE ROAD HE TOOK.** The alternative offered was skipping the import for a
  `--lia-backdrop` CSS variable in `terminal.css`, so the wall could follow moods, the veil and the
  vault from `src/js`. He chose the plugin, and that is what was built - the variable road remains
  open and costs nothing to add later if the wall should ever follow her. The plugin's cost is now
  named in the README too: one `[background(...)]` block is evaluated ONCE per render, so the roll
  happens per page load, not per mood or per turn.
- **THE URL HAD TO CHANGE, AND NOT BECAUSE OF PREFERENCE.** He wrote `http://i.imgur.com/...`. This
  page is https, so that image is blocked as MIXED CONTENT: no error anyone would see, just a blank
  wall - the worst kind of failure, because it looks like the plugin is broken. Imgur is also deleting
  old images (the plugin's own docs warn about it, then use Imgur URLs in their examples anyway). So
  the exact picture was fetched once (1500x994, 278,247 B, byte-for-byte) and re-hosted on perchance's
  upload service: `https://user.uploads.dev/file/db8547df143abbb7649cc1e2de30932b.jpeg`. That URL is
  the source of record now, and the picture he *chose* is the picture on the wall.
- **`opacity = 0.8` IS PASSED AT THE CALL SITE - A PLUGIN BUG, NOT A STYLE CHOICE.** In the plugin's
  `bgData` branch it tests the list's own field and then emits the FUNCTION ARGUMENT
  (`opacity:` followed by the second parameter, or 1). Called as `[background(bgData)]` the argument is
  undefined, so the wall would render at `opacity: 1` and his 0.8 would silently do nothing. The list
  keeps his 0.8 (a list read on its own should say what the wall is) and `index.html` passes it so it
  takes effect. Measured cost of getting this wrong: 1.29:1 contrast instead of 1.58:1 on the bright
  roll. This is exactly the "why not the other way" the chronicle exists to hold - the bug is invisible
  from the docs, which advertise `opacity` as a supported property.

### 3. WHAT WAS VERIFIED (live, and measured rather than eyeballed)

- The import resolves to a FUNCTION on `root`, and exactly ONE wall div is emitted: computed
  `position: fixed`, `z-index: -1000`, `inset: 0`, `background-image: url(<the re-hosted jpeg>)`,
  `opacity: 0.8` (the argument landed), and a rolled
  `background-size: 146px auto; repeat; filter: invert(1) blur(0px) hue-rotate(20deg)` - i.e. the
  randomization he wrote is live, one roll per page load.
- The asset answers **200 / image/jpeg** from this origin, so the wall is not a mixed-content ghost.
- `__bootIssues []`, no perchance errors, `rtfm.check()` still in sync (no command was touched).
- **THE CONTRAST NUMBERS, because the picture is a bright one.** It is a high-key snow-and-cloud
  ridge: mean luminance **0.71**, 80% of pixels above 0.5. Composited over black at the wall's alpha
  and scored against `#00ff00` (relative luminance 0.715; WCAG wants 4.5:1 for body text):

  | roll | mean | median | 10th pct |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `invert(0%)` at 0.8 | **1.58:1** | 1.43:1 | 8.10:1 |
  | `invert(100%)` at 0.8 | **4.75:1** | 10.04:1 | 14.38:1 |
  | `invert(0%)` at 1.0 (plugin default) | 1.29:1 | 1.17:1 | 7.24:1 |

  So the two filter rolls are two different rooms: the inverted one is a dark wall (composited mean
  0.11) and reads the way a terminal wants; the un-inverted one puts bright cloud behind every line
  of green text and is, over most of the frame, not readable. Both rolls are his, so both are left
  exactly as written - the numbers are in the README so the bright roll is a known trade.

### 4. STILL OPEN

- **The bright roll, and whether he wants it.** `invert(0%)` is 1.58:1 behind green text. Three
  one-line ways out, his call: pin the filter to `invert(100%)`, drop the wall's alpha, or re-host a
  baked-dark version of the same picture (the file is ours, so the fix is one upload). None of them is
  taken without his word - the randomization is the thing he wrote.
- **The blur, on a phone.** 25% of loads roll `blur(10px)` on a full-viewport FIXED layer, which is
  the expensive kind of filter. Not measured on a low-end device yet; if it janks, bake the blur into
  the image and shorten the filter string.
- **The roll is per page load, not per mood.** If the wall should ever follow her moods, the veil or
  the vault, that is the CSS-variable road in THE WALL - a small, additive change.
- **The door still hides the wall.** Opaque, z 2000: a visitor who has not answered sees the door and
  never the wall. That is correct and is left alone.

## §1cn - THE WALL GOES BEHIND A SWITCH (OFF BY DEFAULT), AND THE /upload TAKEAWAY (2026-09-30)

His words, one turn after the wall went in:

> *"That image is just a placeholder image for the moment. We can have a list pointing to a
> perchance.org/upload file later. Toggle/Disable for now. But it is an option later is needed. The
> takeaway is the use of /upload as a free location within the PERCHANCE ecosystem."*

### 1. WHAT WAS ASKED FOR

1. **The picture is a placeholder.** It is not the picture; it is the thing standing where the
   picture will be. Nothing should be built around its brightness or its subject.
2. **Later, a list pointing at a perchance.org/upload file.** More than one URL, most likely.
3. **Toggle/Disable now.** The wall should not be showing.
4. **But available when it is wanted** - "an option later is needed" - so the wiring stays.
5. **The takeaway is the upload service itself**: perchance.org/upload is a free, permanent home for
   an asset inside this ecosystem. That is the durable lesson, not the picture.

### 2. WHAT WAS BUILT

- **`src/js/wall.js` (NEW)** - `window.wall`, the switch: `/wall on | off | toggle | forget`, the
  choice kept in THIS BROWSER only (kv `lia_settings` / `wall`, with the moment and the clock's
  zone), a `describe()` that reads the picture's URL off the live element, and a `help()` carrying the
  whole of it. Registered in the `MODULES` boot list and loaded after `agegate.js`.
- **The state is the markup**: `class="wallOff"` on the `<body>` tag in `index.html`.
- **One CSS rule** in `src/css/terminal.css`: `body.wallOff div[style*="z-index:-1000"] { display: none; }`.
- **`/wall` in the command book**: a block in `chat.js` beside `/agegate`, `HELP_TOPICS`, the master
  help list, and a `/help wall` topic. `commands.json` 76 -> 77 and `src/rtfm/commands.md`
  regenerated.
- **The call in `index.html` is untouched**: `[background(bgData, 0.8)]` is still there, which is what
  "an option later" means - the wall is wired, and the switch is what is off.
- **`main.pjs`** gained one paragraph in the `bgData` banner: the picture is a placeholder, the wall
  ships off, what "a list of upload URLs" will look like, and the upload takeaway.

### 3. WHAT WAS THOUGHT (the four decisions)

- **THE SWITCH HAD TO BE MARKUP, NOT A SCRIPT.** The wall is painted at the FIRST PAINT. A switch that
  lived only in `wall.js` would show the placeholder picture for the milliseconds before the module
  ran and then hide it - a flash of the placeholder on every single load, which is precisely the wrong
  thing for something whose whole current status is "not wanted yet". So the class ships on the body
  tag, the CSS hides the wall from the first frame, and the module only ever takes the class OFF.
- **THE ONE-LINE ROAD, REJECTED ON PURPOSE.** `[bgData.enabled ? background(bgData, 0.8) : ""]` with
  `enabled = 0` in the list is smaller and emits no div at all. It is an EDIT, not a switch: turning
  the wall on would need the editor's lists panel or an agent, and nothing would remember a choice.
  He asked for a toggle; a toggle that only an agent can flip is not one. (The `enabled` field is
  still a fine idea *if* he ever wants the div gone from the DOM - recorded here so the alternative is
  not re-derived.)
- **NO WRAPPER ELEMENT AROUND THE PLUGIN'S DIV.** `<div id="wall">[background(...)]</div>` would give
  the CSS a clean hook, and it was refused: `body` is a flex COLUMN, so the wrapper is one more box in
  that column, and an invisible extra flex item is exactly the kind of change that shows up later as a
  gap nobody can explain. The rule keys on the one thing the plugin always writes into its inline
  style (`z-index:-1000`) instead - stable because the plugin is a fixed 1.3 KB, pinned in README.
  `wall.js` finds the element the same way.
- **IT FAILS SAFE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE DOOR.** `agegate.js` fails CLOSED and therefore needs a
  second plain-ES5 copy of itself at the foot of `index.html`: a door that cannot open is a terminal
  nobody can reach. A wall that cannot be switched ON costs nothing - the markup already says OFF -
  so no fallback was written, and that decision is written down instead of left as an absence.

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED (scratch/wall2.js, 17 checks, all passing on a fresh load)

- The shipped page: `wallOff` on the body, the plugin's div IS in the page, and it is **not rendered**.
- **OFF COSTS NOTHING, MEASURED**: zero requests for the placeholder while the wall is off, and one
  request the moment `/wall on` runs (resource timing, not an assumption). `display:none` was chosen
  over `visibility:hidden` for exactly this: no box, no image fetch.
- `/wall on` / `/wall toggle` / `/wall off` / `/wall forget` all move the class and the record; the
  real chat path was driven (`/wall toggle` typed into the input) and printed its receipt, which the
  harness then removed - the stage was left exactly as it found it.
- `describe()` names the state and reads the picture's URL off the live element; `help()` carries the
  verbs and the upload point.
- `forget()` leaves no record and puts the shipped state back, which is where the device was left.
- `__bootIssues []`, `rtfm.check()` in sync at 77 commands, and no `src/js` file beyond `wall.js` was
  touched - nothing in the terminal reads `bgData`, and no turn of hers is affected by any of it.

### 5. WHAT WENT WRONG (one harness gotcha, kept because it cost two runs)

A harness that fetched the ROOT files by relative path - `fetch("main.pjs")`, meaning to compare them
against `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` - died with **`TypeError: Failed to fetch`**, twice, and the tool
reported it as the eval failing rather than as a bad path, which sent me looking at the wall instead of
at the harness. The iframe's document URL has no trailing slash, so `main.pjs` resolves a directory
ABOVE the generator and the file service refuses it; `src/...` always works. The lesson for every
future harness on this terminal: **the root files cannot be fetched from inside the page** - compare
the byte-for-byte copies against the workspace files in `execute_js` (where `fs` has them) instead, and
treat an unhandled `Failed to fetch` inside a harness as a broken path first and a broken page second.

### 6. STILL OPEN

- **The picture itself.** A placeholder until he supplies the real one (or several). Swapping it is
  swapping the `url` in `bgData`; more than one URL is a plain pjs list, which the plugin's own
  random-per-load branch already handles.
- **The bright roll, when the wall IS on.** `invert(0%)` at 0.8 still measures 1.58:1 behind green
  text (see §1cm). Unchanged and still his call - the wall being off makes it dormant, not settled.
- **Where the /upload road should be written down for good.** It is in `README.md` (THE WALL), in
  `bgData`'s banner, in `/wall help` and in `/help wall`. If more assets arrive, a short note under
  the key ring or in the README's own file lists is the next home for it.
- **The second host (catbox.moe), and the rule it settles.** He sent `catbox.moe` and
  `catbox.moe/tools.php` in the same session (2026-09-30). Measured, because it decides what is
  possible: **the relay cannot READ catbox at all** (seven shapes tried - the site, `tools.php`,
  `faq.php`, `robots.txt`, `user/api.php`, over both http and https - every one `Failed to fetch`,
  while `example.com` through the same relay answers in one call, and
  `root.superFetch("https://catbox.moe/tools.php")` fails the same way from inside the page), while
  the BROWSER does receive catbox responses (a `no-cors` probe from this origin resolved for
  `catbox.moe`, `files.catbox.moe` and `litterbox.catbox.moe`, and resource timings show real round
  trips of 60-2,770 ms - the responses just arrive without the headers that let a script read them).
  So a catbox URL can be DISPLAYED in the page and cannot be read, uploaded to, or verified by
  anything in this project: it is a hand-operated host. The
  rule that follows, and the reason it is written in README (THE WALL and THE RELAY): **assets the
  generator ships stay on perchance.org/upload**, which is inside the ecosystem and the one host these
  tools can write to and read back; catbox is for hand uploads and second copies. If a real picture
  ever arrives from catbox, the check is one line in the page - an `<img>` at the `files.catbox.moe`
  URL - and then the `url` in `bgData`.
- **The temporary sibling, and the correction it forced (same day, one link later).** He then sent
  `https://litterbox.catbox.moe/tools.php`, with no prose. Same name, different host: `litterbox` is
  catbox's TEMPORARY half, and it behaves the opposite way from the half measured above - so the
  bullet above is now scoped to `catbox.moe` alone. Measured, from the terminal's own page:
  `fetch("https://litterbox.catbox.moe/tools.php")` -> **200, 1,977 B, readable body**;
  `root.superFetch` on the same URL -> 200; and an anonymous POST to
  `https://litterbox.catbox.moe/resources/internals/api.php` (`reqtype=fileupload`, `time=1h`, a
  622 B PNG drawn on a canvas) returned a real URL - `https://litter.catbox.moe/di4ajx.png` - which
  then fetched back 200 / 622 B and drew in an `<img>` at 64x64. A full round trip, from the page,
  with no account, no key and no plugin. The mistake worth recording is in the measurement, not in
  the host: `litterbox.catbox.moe` had only ever been probed `no-cors` (it is in the round-trip list
  above), and a `no-cors` probe cannot read a response by construction - one name covering two hosts,
  one probe covering one of them, and a sentence that outran its evidence.
  **The rule does not change, and is better founded:** litterbox is built to forget (1 h / 12 h /
  24 h / 72 h, up to 1 GB per file), so it is structurally wrong for an asset the terminal ships - a
  URL that dies in three days is exactly the hole the /upload rule exists to prevent - and
  structurally right for a throwaway (an export, a big render, a file handed to someone else). It is
  now the only host OUTSIDE this ecosystem the project can both write to and read back from, which
  makes it a measured road in the pocket rather than a guess. Nothing was built on it, no terminal
  code was touched, and `/wall`, `bgData`, the placeholder and the OFF switch are exactly as this
  build left them.
  **He named what it is FOR, the turn after (2026-09-30):** *"This is a great solution for purposefully
  expiring data like recorded AI audio we don't want or need."* That is the rule in his own words, and
  it is now written where the hosting rules live - `README.md` THE WALL ("what must SURVIVE goes to
  perchance.org/upload; what must NOT survive is handed to a host that forgets") and THE STORY LANE,
  which is the nearest thing this terminal has to the case he named (a rendered part is a Blob played
  here and never kept, so nothing needs a URL today; the sample leaves as a FILE). NOTHING WAS BUILT on
  it: it is a rule for the first road that needs a URL for a piece of sound - a Space that takes a link
  rather than an upload, one part handed to somebody, a service that wants a URL - so that the default
  is the expiring host and a voice is never parked on a permanent one out of habit.

### 7. FILES TOUCHED
