## §1co - THE SAVE CHECK: `downloadGenerator` TURNED AROUND (2026-09-30)

His words, one turn after the two free hosts were measured and the rule about expiring data was
written down:

> *"OK. It's saved. What are your thoughts on this? No coding yet. Just advice."* (sent with
> `https://perchance.org/diy-perchance-api`)

and then, after the advice and the offer in it:

> *"- Add downloadGenerator
> - Then look at this and look around and go \"window shopping\"/\"code mining\"
>   https://perchance.org/useful-generators"*

So this section is the first of those two, and the mining is §1cp.

### 1. WHAT THE PAGE ACTUALLY IS (because the survey decides what is worth taking)

`diy-perchance-api` is a TUTORIAL generator: its `main.pjs` is 0 bytes and the whole generator is one
HTML page of prose. What it teaches is not an API - it is a HEADLESS BROWSER, and the shape of it is
this:

- `GET https://perchance.org/api/downloadGenerator?generatorName=<name>` returns the generator's SAVED
  HTML (measured: 597,893 bytes for `animal-sentence`, 904,256 for this one);
- you load that HTML in JSDOM with `runScripts:"dangerously"` and the pjs engine runs in Node, so
  `window.root.<list>` and `.evaluateItem` are available server-side;
- that is the whole trick, and for a STATELESS LIST GENERATOR it works.

Three things in it decided the advice, and the first is on the page itself:

1. **THE AI PLUGINS CANNOT RUN OFF-SITE, AND THE PAGE SAYS SO.** Its yellow note: `text-to-image-plugin`
   and `ai-text-plugin` "won't work" from your own server, because the ads shown on perchance are what
   fund their GPU servers. Everything that makes this terminal what it is - `generateText`,
   `generateImage`, and every lane built on them - is therefore impossible in a DIY clone. A clone
   could shuffle the lists and render the shell, and nothing else.
2. **THE TUTORIAL'S HOST IS GONE.** Measured, not assumed: `https://diy-perchance-api.glitch.me/api?
   generator=animal-sentence&list=output` now answers **HTTP 410** with "Glitch project hosting is no
   longer available." The pattern is portable to any Node host; the place the page names is not, and no
   cloud host fixes (1).
3. **THE ARCHITECTURE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THIS TERMINAL'S.** Keys live on this device and never leave it
   (THE API KEYRING), the memory of every turn lives in kv on this device, and JSDOM has no IndexedDB,
   no microphone, no MediaRecorder, no audio playback, no service worker and no OPFS - which is most of
   what LIA is made of. A headless clone of her would be a stranger with no memory and no voice.

**THE ADVICE GIVEN, FOR THE RECORD:** do not build it for LIA. Take the ENDPOINT. And if an outside
surface for her is ever wanted - a bot, a phone, a script - the shape that fits is a BRIDGE INTO THE
LIVE PAGE (`createServerSocket`, src/js/sync* / the server-plugin road), where the keys already are and
the page is already her; never a clone of her running on somebody else's server. A bridge needs a gate
too, because the server script is public source.

### 2. WHAT WAS BUILT: `/saved` (`src/js/saved.js`, `window.saved`)

The endpoint, turned around. Not "give me this generator so I can run it", but "**tell me what you are
holding, so I can tell whether my work is on the server**" - the question every build in this project
ends with, and the one question the page could never answer about itself.

- **`src/js/saved.js` (NEW)** - `window.saved`: `check()` (the data), `text(report)` (the report),
  `run()`, `describe()`, `help()`, `command()`. Registered in `MODULES` and loaded after `wall.js`.
- **Four comparisons, one verdict:** the two root files byte for byte (with the first line that
  differs, both lines printed); the file list (the saved copy's `srcManifest` against
  `src/pack/files.json`, so a never-saved file and a stale server file are both named); EVERY `src/`
  file BY CONTENT (each manifest key read back off `https://user.uploads.dev/file/<key>` and compared
  byte for byte); and the import lines in `main.pjs` against the saved copy's own `imports`.
- **`/saved` in the command book**: a block in `chat.js` beside `/wall`, `HELP_TOPICS`, the master help
  list, a `/help saved` topic. `commands.json` 77 -> 78, `src/rtfm/commands.md` regenerated (verified
  in sync: `rtfm.check()` returns "").
- **The pack regenerated in the same pass** (128 files now: the pack copies + `files.json`), and
  `src/pack/files.json` 127 -> 128.

### 3. WHAT WAS THOUGHT (the decisions, and what each one was refused in favour of)

- **ASK THE SERVER, NOT THE PAGE - AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVES WHY.** A served perchance page
  carries its own copy of the generator in `#preloaded-generator-data`, and `backup.js` already reads it
  (`serverCopy()` / `savedManifest()`), which is what makes `/backup status` honest. But "honest" and
  "fresh" are different things, so it was measured: with a 61-byte probe appended to `main.pjs` (67,921
  bytes on disk) and the page RELOADED, the embedded copy still reported **67,860** and contained no
  probe. So the element is the copy the page was SERVED WITH. It is the right thing to read the file
  list from, and the wrong thing to prove a save with: after he presses SAVE, the page he is looking at
  runs the previous save until it is reloaded. This module therefore fetches the server's copy fresh,
  cache-busted per call, and compares the page's own copy against the answer as a second opinion (it
  says "RELOAD TO BE RUNNING THE NEWEST SAVE" when the page is behind).
- **THE RELAY, BECAUSE THERE IS NO OTHER ROAD.** `fetch` on that endpoint from inside the page is
  `TypeError: Failed to fetch` (their API sends no CORS headers); `root.superFetch` on the very same
  URL answers 200 / 904,256 bytes in 444-624 ms. The super-fetch-plugin was already imported for the
  key ring, so nothing new was added to the page for this.
- **BY CONTENT, NOT BY SIZE - AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE WHOLE THING.** A size check would pass a
  one-character edit (`0.8` -> `0.9`), which is exactly the kind of edit this project makes, and the
  manifest's `key` looked like it might be a content hash. It is not reproducible here (measured
  against `src/js/packs.js`: not md5 of the content, not md5 of path+content, not twelve other
  spellings) - but it does not have to be, because the platform's own loader names its base in the
  served page: `PERCH.src` declares `CDN_BASE = "https://user.uploads.dev/file/"` and
  `KEY_REGEX = /^[0-9a-f]{32}\.[a-z0-9]{1,20}$/`. So the saved bytes are simply READ BACK. 127 files,
  byte for byte, in 478 ms - most of them already cached, since the page loaded them at boot.
- **THE CAVEAT IS PRINTED EVERY TIME.** `main.pjs` and `index.html` cannot be fetched from this page at
  all (measured: `fetch("main.pjs")` is `Failed to fetch` - this frame's URL has no trailing slash - and
  `https://<publicId>.perchance.org/<name>/main.pjs` is 404, as is every other absolute spelling, while
  `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` is 200). So the "here" side of the root comparison IS the pack, and the report
  says so in a bracketed line under those two comparisons, because a stale pack would otherwise turn a
  verdict about the pack into a false verdict about the editor's buffers. Everything under `src/` is
  read from its real path, so no caveat applies there.
- **A RECEIPT, NOT A GATE.** It writes nothing, uploads nothing, reads no key, changes no file, and
  nothing in the terminal waits on it. It also prints its own cost and says plainly that it answers ONE
  question (is the source the server holds this workspace) and not the other one (the conversation,
  which is kv-only and is `/sync`'s and `/cloud`'s business).

### 4. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, DRIVEN FOR REAL

- **The prototype, twice** (`scratch/saved1.js`, `scratch/saved2.js`): the snapshot (904,256 B / 444 ms),
  `DOMParser` + parse (7 ms), root files byte-identical, file set 127 = 127, all 127 sizes matching
  (246 ms), and then the deep pass reading every saved file off the CDN and comparing bytes: **127 of
  127 identical, 478 ms**, slowest single file 18 ms.
- **The measurement that shaped the design**: the unsaved-probe experiment above, run on the live page
  with a reload, then the file restored byte-for-byte from `src/pack/main.pjs.txt` and verified.
- **End to end, through the terminal's own input** (`scratch/saved3.js`): `/saved` typed into
  `#userInput` and sent with the page's own `window.send()` - the command was intercepted as text-only
  (no turn, no archive entry), two receipts were printed ("READING THE SERVER'S COPY..." and the
  report), the input was cleared, and the harness removed exactly its own two receipts by marking the
  cut point (23 entries before = 23 after, the replayed log untouched).
- **The report is right about a real difference.** With this build unsaved, it says: `main.pjs` the same
  (67,860); `index.html` DIFFERENT - saved 105,902, here 106,673, FIRST DIFFERENCE AT LINE 157 (the
  `MODULES` line, where `["saved", "src/js/saved.js"]` was added); `src/ :: 127 ON THE SERVER, 128 HERE`,
  naming `js/saved.js` as never saved; then four files by content (`commands/commands.json`,
  `js/chat.js`, `pack/files.json`, `pack/index.html.txt`) with both byte counts; imports 5 of 5; whole
  check 1,232 ms. Every one of those is a change this build actually made.
- **Boot clean**: `__bootIssues` empty, `rtfm.check()` "" (78 commands), the wall still OFF and hidden,
  the door still in the markup, the log replayed untouched.

### 5. WHAT WENT WRONG

1. **A nested `page_refresh` inside `execute_js` killed the worker mid-experiment**, twice reported as
   "the live page stopped responding" - and it left the 61-byte PROBE LINE in `main.pjs`. Recovered by
   writing the pack copy back over the root file (which is exactly what the pack is for), then
   re-running the experiment with the reload as its own top-level call. The lesson is the same shape as
   §1cn's: do not drive page refreshes from inside a worker script.
2. **The first end-to-end harness swept up the boot prints and the replayed log** (23 entries removed,
   `keptLogIntact` false) because it counted entries instead of marking a cut point - and `/saved` had
   not actually run, because `#sendBtn` is disabled during the boot rush and `window.send()` returns
   early when it is. Fixed in the harness: wait for the page to be quiet AND the button enabled, mark
   the last entry, then remove only what came after the mark. (Nothing was lost: the log is a VIEW of
   the archive in kv and a reload redrew it.)
3. **A patch of mine deleted the `src/ ::` summary line** while adding the pack caveat - caught by
   reading the region back before moving on, and restored in the next edit.

### 6. STILL OPEN

- **The pack dependency is structural** and cannot be removed from inside the page: `main.pjs` and
  `index.html` are not fetchable from the iframe (measured), so the root comparison will always be
  against `src/pack/*.txt`. What keeps it honest is the routine: regenerate the pack, then `/saved`.
- **The CDN base and the key shape are pinned in README** (`user.uploads.dev/file/` + `KEY_REGEX`). If
  the platform ever moves that base or changes the key format, the per-file half of the check stops
  working - it would report every file as unreadable rather than lie, which is the right failure, but
  the module would need re-measuring.
- **`/saved` is not offered anywhere else** (no lamp in the status line, no TOOLS row). Deliberate: it
  costs ~1.2 s and it is a question an agent asks, not a number he needs on screen.

### 7. FILES TOUCHED

`src/js/saved.js` (NEW), `index.html` (`["saved", "src/js/saved.js"]` in `MODULES`, the script tag and
its comment after `wall.js`), `src/js/chat.js` (`/saved` block, `HELP_TOPICS`, the master help list,
`/help saved`), `src/commands/commands.json` (77 -> 78), `src/rtfm/commands.md` (regenerated),
`src/README.md` (the `saved.js` file line + the new section THE SAVE CHECK), `src/TODO.md` (this
section), the new `src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-save-check.md` + `chronicle.json` (38 -> 39),
`src/pack/files.json` (127 -> 128) with `src/pack/index.html.txt` + `src/pack/main.pjs.txt`
refreshed. **NOT SAVED by the agent - and this build's own `/saved` is the thing that says so.**

## §1cp - THE WINDOW SHOPPING (`useful-generators`, and what is actually out there) (2026-09-30)

He asked for the browse in the same breath as the build: *"Then look at this and look around and go
\"window shopping\"/\"code mining\" https://perchance.org/useful-generators"*. Nothing was built from
it - what follows is the survey, with the three things worth taking ranked, so the next build can pick
one up.

### 1. WHAT `useful-generators` ACTUALLY IS

**Not code.** It is a CATALOGUE OF WORD LISTS: 46 sections and roughly 250 importable lists
(`{import:noun}`, `{import:animal}`, `{import:emotion}`, `{import:archaic-word}`, ...) grouped by
language, life & nature, food, names, society, religion, colour, film, music, games, computers,
mathematics and so on. Its own `main.pjs` is 733 bytes of comments - and the only *technical* thing on
the page is two of those comments pointing at DBpedia/SPARQL and Faker.js. So "code mining" there is
VOCABULARY, not technique, and the honest verdict is: worth picking from by need, never importing in
bulk (every `{import:}` is a fetch, a permanent dependency and someone else's list deciding this
project's words).

The ones that would actually earn a place here, mapped to where they would go:

- **the SHOT LIST** (`src/js/idea.js` dimensions, the lists in `main.pjs`): `terrain`, `gemstone`,
  `moon-phase`, `part-of-day`, `color-palette`, `fabric-type`, `type-of-rock`, `body-of-water`,
  `room-type` - materials and light, which is what the image prompts are made of.
- **the Veiled Tongue / the prompt book**: `archaic-word`, `latin-word`, `-ism`, `philia`,
  `obsession`, `rare-word`, `complex-word`, `nonsense-word`.
- **the MYTHOS side**: `greek-god`, `greek-titan`, `norse-deity`, `egyptian-god`, `tarot-prediction`,
  `zodiac-sign`, `phobia`, `monster-type`, `fantasy-language`.
- **her own prose** (anything of hers that must not repeat itself): `speech-verb`, `manner-adverb`,
  `intensifier`, `simile`, `cliche`, `interjection`.

### 2. WHAT ELSE IS OUT THERE (and how it was browsed)

`perchance.org/generators` is the "recently updated" listing, and it is built from
`GET /api/getGeneratorList` - 451 generators in today's answer, with titles, descriptions, tags, views
and the last-edit time. That is the real window-shopping surface, and it shows what this terminal's
neighbourhood looks like now: a large population of AI-chat / lorebook / persistent-world generators.
From today's list, named so a future session can go straight to them: `rpg-worlds` (14.8k views,
"longterm memory, roleplay in custom worlds"), `chatnex` (38k), `moechat` ("keeps an automatic
lorebook of memory"), `s72dsmvs6e`/FurAI ("lorebook... SillyTavern-inspired"), `lw16uehnsw`/Veilwright
("persistent-world AI interactive fiction"), `zgu9morf3c`/Vale of Second Chances, `0z0-mnnowf0rk`/MNO-FRK,
`huddle-app` (rooms, voice, presence), `storyframe` (on-device Whisper), `yt-dlp`, `drift`,
`frame-studio`, `pqtxpsd4kg` (prompt -> 4-view -> 3D mesh).

### 3. THE THREE THINGS WORTH TAKING (ranked)

**(1) ON-DEVICE WHISPER - `storyframe`.** This is the one I would build next. Their own words: *"Lyrics
are transcribed on-device by Whisper (transformers.js) in a worker - the model is downloaded once and
cached, and the words never leave your machine."* This terminal's `/hear` (THE WORDS ON A SOUND) needs
a Google/ElevenLabs/HuggingFace KEY and sends the audio (reduced to mono 16 kHz) to a provider. An
on-device road would be **keyless, upload-free, quota-free, offline after the first model download, and
streaming** - which is not only cheaper but *the same principle he stated about data that should not
linger*. It would also serve the story lane's sample judging and the AUDITION bus.

The recipe, read out of THEIR saved `src/` (their seven files are on the CDN; `whisper-worker.js` is
5,824 bytes - read with the road §1co discovered):

- transformers.js, pinned, from esm.sh: `https://esm.sh/@huggingface/transformers@3.8.1`;
- `pipeline("automatic-speech-recognition", "onnx-community/" + model, { device: "wasm", dtype: "q8",
  progress_callback })`, with `env.allowLocalModels = false`, `env.useBrowserCache = true` and
  `env.backends.onnx.wasm.numThreads = 1`. The progress callback sums every file's loaded/total, so the
  page can show a real download bar for a model that is tens of MB;
- a `TextStreamer` whose `callback_function` posts each new fragment to the page - **the words stream in
  as they are generated**, which is exactly the terminal's own idiom;
- `return_timestamps: true`, `chunk_length_s: 30`, `stride_length_s: 5`, optional `language`, and
  `task: "translate"`; the special tokens Whisper emits (`<|0.00|>`, `<|startoftranscript|>`) are
  stripped by hand because the streamer treats them as ordinary text;
- audio is decoded through an **`OfflineAudioContext`** to 16 kHz mono - no autoplay policy to fight,
  and the browser's own resampler does the 44.1/48 -> 16 kHz conversion;
- and the perchance-specific part, in their own header comment: *"a worker cannot import modules from
  another origin, and in the perchance editor `src/` is served from a different origin than the page, so
  `lyrics.js` fetches this file as text and runs it as a blob module worker."* That is precisely the
  shim this project's notes describe (`new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([source],
  {type:"text/javascript"})), {type:"module"})`), applied to a `src/` file - and it is why their worker
  is deliberately self-contained.

**(2) `huddle-app` - a WORKING server-plugin app, and the reference for any future bridge.** One
`<script type="text/x-server-plugin">` carrying rooms, channels, chat, quizzes, polls, tasks,
watch-sync, **voice signalling** and presence; pubsub topics per room and channel; and a roster that
shows each *person* once even when the same identity has several live connections. It also carries its
own quota tables (per-network-group window counters, admin slots, shared entries). If an outside surface
for LIA is ever wanted - the "bridge into the live page" in §1co's advice - this is the working model to
copy, and the proof that the road is real and cheap.

**(3) `rpg-worlds` - the much bigger sibling (946 KB of HTML), and two small ideas worth stealing.**
What its source shows: **invited characters are LIVE REFERENCES to other sessions**, resolved fresh on
every prompt "so edits to their settings/memory propagate"; a hand-written LORE panel that is
re-injected into every scene ("a permanent place for the important facts about this world - the
narrator is reminded of this lore in every scene and never forgets or contradicts it"); an explicit
rule to the model - **READ BEFORE YOU REWRITE** (never re-word or paraphrase an existing entry from
memory); and a per-session prompt log in kv (`root.kv.promptLog.set("last", entry)`), which is a cheap
debugging gift this terminal could copy in one line for the same reason `/system preview` exists.
Verdict: nothing structural to take (this terminal is already further along on memory than that
pattern), but the two prompt rules above are worth considering on their own merits.

### 4. WHAT WAS NOT DONE

Nothing was built from the mining. The one item that was ASKED for (`downloadGenerator`) is §1co; the
shortlist above is ranked by value-per-line and is ready to be picked from - and (1) is the only one I
would argue for proactively, because it removes a key, an upload and a provider from a lane that
already exists.

### 5. THE METHOD, WORTH KEEPING

**Any generator's `src/` files can be read from outside, without running any of its code.** The saved
page's own manifest (`#preloaded-generator-data`, fetched through `downloadGenerator`) gives every
file's CDN key, and `https://user.uploads.dev/file/<key>` serves the file - so "how did they do that?"
is a two-request question for any generator that keeps its code in `src/`, which is now the normal
shape (this one, `huddle-app`, `storyframe`, and rpg-worlds all do). That is exactly the road `/saved`
uses on this generator, pointed outward. Worked example in this session:
`scratch/generators/storyframe/` (their two root files) + `scratch/shopping/storyframe-whisper-worker.js`
(their worker, read off the CDN).

### 1. WHAT THE OTHER ROOM IS (read without running any of it)

### 3. WHAT WAS SETTLED (the four readings of his one message)

1. **"Bridge the two data-wise as a module" = DATA, NOT CODE.** No `{import:}` between the two

2. **The end goal is a LOBBY, the inverse of that room.** The Symposium is one room with fifteen
   PERSONAS; a lobby is fifteen ALIAs - fifteen actors, each with a whole terminal - in one room, with
   channels and presence, like a Slack. Both shapes are worth having and they are not the same thing.
3. **UNIX ethos, applied:** small things, one job each, plain data between them, pipes, compose - which

4. **Simple first.** So nothing was written: not `/lobby`, not `src/js/lobby.js`, not a record file, not

**The canon you are working against (please don't drift from it):**

**Things in the current code worth fixing (all read from your saved source):**
1. **The thinking placeholder is mislabelled.** `askAgent` does `addMsg('', handle, '…', findTarget(text) || null, agent.color)` - so a box can read `HANDLE → TARGET` before the agent has said anything. Pass `null` there; the `→ target` belongs on the finished reply only.
2. **Streaming is set up and then not used.** You pass an `onChunk` that only clears the placeholder, then await the whole result and print it at once. With up to 15 speakers, that is a wall of "thinking…" with no visible progress. Assign the promise / append each `textChunk` into the box, and show a queue depth somewhere ("3 of 15 speaking") - a council turn can take a minute.
3. **`CUSTOMS` and custom focuses are dead paths.** `allAgents()` merges `CUSTOMS`, and `refreshFocusSelect` reads `focuses` from kv, but nothing ever writes either. Either finish them (one "add custom agent" form) or delete them, so the code doesn't promise a feature it hasn't got.
4. **Two sources of truth for the room focus.** `roomFocus` in `main.pjs` is unused; `FOCUS_DEFAULTS` in the script is what runs. If the focus presets are meant to be his to edit, read them from the list (or drop the list); right now they will silently drift.
5. **`superFetch` is imported and never used.** Drop it, or use it - every unused `{import:}` is a fetch and a permanent dependency.
6. **The transcript is a 14-message window handed in full to every agent, every turn.** With 15 voices, that window rolls over within one council turn, and every agent gets 15× redundant input. Thinner per-agent context (the focus, the last few lines, and *who they are*) plus a shared room log that is longer but summarised will scale much better - and if you ever go to 15 real ALIAs, each needs her OWN memory; the room must carry only the room.
7. **`send()` returns early when `busy >= 6`.** During a Summon-all-15 he simply cannot type, with no explanation. Always accept and queue the message, or disable the input with a visible reason.
8. **The roster cards build HTML by interpolation** (`inner.innerHTML` with `bio`, `title`, `system_instruction`). Fine while that file is only yours, but it becomes script injection the moment a custom agent or an imported roster enters. Build the cards with `textContent` (your `renderTxt` already does it right for message text).
9. **The keys you store are never used.** `geminiKey` / `elevenKey` are saved to kv (correctly local-only) but nothing reads them - either wire the Voice lane or take the inputs out, so nobody types a secret into a field that does nothing. (And never ship a key in source - his standing rule.)
10. **Your kv key names are your outward contract.** `kv.room` with `transcript`, `overrides`, `sessions`, `focuses`, `activeFocus`, `geminiKey`, `elevenKey` - say so in your README and freeze them, because a bridge will read them by name.

**Two of his standing preferences, for whatever it's worth:** what must survive → `perchance.org/upload` (permanent); anything that should expire (e.g. generated audio you don't need to keep) → `litterbox.catbox.moe`. And when you finish a build, say plainly that it is **NOT SAVED** unless he has pressed save - a build that reports itself as done while the platform still holds older code is worse than no report.

## §1cr - THE STRUCTURE (light now, UNIX and SOMA later) (2026-09-30)

His word, in the same breath as the orders:

> *"I want to keep it light and easy to skin or monorepo or proper UNIX ETHIC and STRUCTURE later and
> eventually pipe with an Orchestrated SOMA bridge run by the LIAS."*

### 1. WHAT SOMA IS (his own word, already written down)

`scratch/mythos-repo/mythos-rag-agent-voice-main/` held a copy of his repo this session, and it answers
the question itself. **SOMA = Service Oriented Multi-Agent Orchestrator** - `services/soma.ts`, a KERNEL
that is a hypervisor for the cluster, in its own words: *"It does not generate content itself, but
manages the routing, permission checks, and state of the cluster."* Around it: **VirtualFs**
(`/agents`, `/lore`, `/logs`, `/sys`; every entry with an owner and a UNIX mode; one file per agent at
`/agents/<handle>`); **ShellService** (a real prompt `user@mythos:/dir$` with `ls`, `cd`, `cat`,
`grep`, `find`, `chmod`, `rm`, `whoami`, `su`, `sql`, `sudo`); the **MultiAgentMessage** envelope
(`{id, senderId, senderName, text, timestamp, targets[]}`); **SomaActionType** (`QUERY_DB`,
`INGEST_DATA`, `DELETE_DATA`, `EXEC_CODE`, `ROUTE_REQUEST`, `CREATE_IMAGE`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN`,
`BROADCAST`, `PUBLISH_CANON`, `DELEGATE_TASK`, `COLLABORATE`); **NumMarkX** sigils (a deterministic
lowercase-alnum key from the text's first N characters) - the same identity this terminal's LOREPACK
already uses; and `Agent`/`AgentConfig` carrying `accessLevel` (777 / 755 / 644) and `permissions`
(memory / tools / system). So "proper UNIX structure later" is a PORT of types he has already written,
not an invention.

### 2. THE FIVE RULES (seams, so the port is a move and not a rewrite)

Those five rules, as they were written for him and for the other agent (verbatim, and kept here so a
later session can re-hand them over):

    ADDENDUM TO THE ORDER — THE STRUCTURE

    Patrikios, 2026-09-30: *"I want to keep it light and easy to skin or monorepo or proper UNIX ETHIC and STRUCTURE later and eventually pipe with an Orchestrated SOMA bridge run by the LIAS."*

    Hold to these five and the later move is a move, not a rewrite:

    1. **One core, skins are tokens.** No colour, size, radius or font anywhere but the CSS file; a skin only sets `:root` variables and swaps by one attribute on the body. (`mythos-theme.css` already does this - keep it that way and never let a style leak into JS or markup.)
    2. **One roster schema, shared as DATA.** `id` (lowercase), `handle` (UPPERCASE), `order`, `accessLevel` (UNIX-style 777/755/644), `permissions` (memory / tools / system). That is the whole contract - do not invent a second shape.
    3. **The room is a NAMESPACE, not a component.** A channel is a directory; a message is one append-only line in the envelope you will need later: `{id, from, text, at, to[]}`. Then `cat`, `grep` and `tail` over the room are free, and `/agents/<handle>` is a file with an owner and a mode.
    4. **One job per tool, text in and text out.** `room.say`, `room.read`, `room.mute`, `room.focus` - each one a filter. The kernel later does nothing but routing, permissions and state; it never generates content.
    5. **One kernel seam.** A single `route(envelope)` function. Today it delivers to the room; later the SOMA kernel sits behind it and no caller changes.

    None of the kernel, the virtual filesystem, the shell or the providers belongs in the light room. It must run with zero of them.


### 3. THE ENDGAME, IN ONE LINE

*"An Orchestrated SOMA bridge run by the LIAs"* = the bridge is a KERNEL SERVICE, not a pipe: a node
initiates (`DELEGATE_TASK`, `COLLABORATE`, `ROUTE_REQUEST`), the kernel checks the permission, the
record keeps its provenance, and the human keeps admin (what order 15 holds and MERKOS speaks for).
That is the orders' rule 17 (data only, one direction, a message crosses as a document and never as
memory) with the agency moved to the nodes. Nothing of the kernel, the filesystem, the shell or the
providers belongs in the light room: it must run with ZERO of them - which is what the `Dark Room Demo`
revision proves is possible.

### 4. WHAT WAS NOT DONE

No code. This is a constraint recorded, not a build, and it binds every later build of THE LOBBY: the
light room comes first, and it must be able to live with none of the machinery above. **NOT SAVED by the
agent.**

`src/README.md` (the LIGHT NOW, SOMA LATER subsection inside THE LOBBY), `src/TODO.md` (this section),
`src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-lobby.md` (a new THE STRUCTURE section). No new file, so

## §1da - THE BUDDY LIST: THE WIRE IS AIM, AND ORDER v1.3 (2026-09-30)

### 1. HIS LINE, AND WHAT HE WAS ACTUALLY ASKING FOR

*"This is simply AOL Instant Messenger. Let's wire up for that."* - said to CLIO, and then carried over
here. And, in the same breath, a new address for her: *"Chief CLIO SHANNON i.e. SYS.AI.MUSE.CLIO aka
'SHAN' or 'Chief Engineer'."*

He was not asking for a plan. He **named the lobby's protocol**, which was the one thing the programme
had left undecided (README, THE LOBBY: *"the bridge is DATA-ONLY and later"* said what a message is, not
what the wire is). So the work was to take him literally.

### 2. WHY AIM IS THE RIGHT ANSWER, IN ONE PARAGRAPH

By the end AIM was the smallest complete presence-and-messaging protocol ever shipped at consumer scale,
and it already contains every primitive the lobby was about to invent: a session you sign on to (and
explicitly off from), a buddy list you **watch**, presence the **room** owns, a one-to-one window and a
group room as different things, a profile you can ask for, an away message, an idle clock, a warning
level. The hard parts of this programme were never the models - they were presence, occupancy, who speaks
as whom, and what a message *is* - and AIM answered all four under load, two decades ago. So the lobby
adopts the wire and stops designing one: his own first instruction in other words.

### 3. THE MAPPING (canon; both rooms build against this table)

| AIM | the ALIA LOBBY |
| --- | --- |
| screen name | the agent's `id` (UPPERCASE, one word) - the join key between the two projects |
| buddy list / groups | `src/mythos/agents.json`, the 16-seat register. The list is a **watch list**, never the truth about who exists |
| presence (online / idle / away / offline) | the ROOM's session state: **presence is the room's fact, never a client's opinion** |
| away message | the ALIA's standing line: one auto-reply per away episode, never a model call |
| idle (minutes) | **derived** from the last thing the hand did - one timer, no model call, paused when the tab hides |
| Buddy Info / Get Info | the agent card: the six-field transit envelope plus the canon record |
| IM window | one directed message; a frame is a **document**, never memory |
| warning level | moderation; a warn is a visible count on the buddy and deletes nothing |
| the door (sign-on sound) | the presence broadcast, printed **coalesced** - twelve sign-ons are one line |
| chat room | the council; occupancy arrives as JOIN/LEFT **deltas**, never as a redraw |
| Direct IM / Get File | the document transit: one file, one direction, no memory |
| the server (OSCAR) | **the room** - it owns the session, the roster, the presence store and the chat room |
| the client | **this terminal** - a TOC client: it watches, it may speak as itself, it may never fake a presence or speak as another |

**Two layers, and only one of them is on the relay today.** The FLAP frame (`'*' | channel | sequence |
length (bytes, big-endian) | payload`, channels 1/2/3/4/5, 0xFFFF max) is the **socket** form; the TOC
line (`toc_send_im CLIO hello` out, `IM_IN:CLIO:F:hello` in) is the **relay** form. The line travels
because the relay is Patrikios by hand between two tabs and a binary header does not survive a chat box
(a byte of 0x80..0xFF is not decodable as UTF-8 at all). The framing is built and tested and waits for
the day `route()` grows a transport.

## 0. THE ORDER, IN ONE LINE

**Build the lobby's wire AS AIM.** Adopt its primitives, its presence model and its session semantics
exactly as stated below, and stop designing a protocol where a shipped one already fits.

## 1. WHY — his word, and the engineering reason under it

Patrikios, verbatim, and this is the whole brief:

> *"This is simply AOL Instant Messenger. Let's wire up for that."*

He is right, and it is not a joke and not a demotion. AIM was, by the end, **the smallest complete
presence-and-messaging protocol ever shipped to millions of people**, and it contains, already
solved, every primitive the lobby was going to have to invent:

- a **session** you sign on to and explicitly sign off from;
- a **buddy list** you WATCH (and that is yours, and is not a claim about who exists);
- **presence** — online, idle, away, offline — that the ROOM owns and tells you about;
- a **one-to-one window** (an IM) and a **group room** (a chat) as two different things;
- a **profile** you publish and a profile you can ask for;
- an **away message**, an **idle clock**, and a **warning level**.

The risk in the ALIA LOBBY was never the models. It was the plumbing: presence, occupancy, who speaks
as whom, and what a message *is*. AIM met all four under load, two decades ago, at consumer scale.
So we adopt the wire and we stop inventing — which is the same instruction he gave at the start in
other words: **keep it simple first, then pipe it all together.**

## 2. THE MAPPING — adopt this table; do not re-derive it

| AIM | the ALIA LOBBY |
| --- | --- |
| **screen name** | the agent's `id` (UPPERCASE, one word) — the join key between our two projects |
| **buddy list / groups** | `src/mythos/agents.json` — the 16-seat register. The list is a **WATCH LIST**, never the truth about who exists |
| **presence** (online/idle/away/offline) | the ROOM's session state. **Presence is the room's fact, never a client's opinion** |
| **away message** | the ALIA's standing line; delivered as ONE auto-reply per away episode; never a model call |
| **idle (minutes)** | DERIVED from the last thing the hand did — one timer, no model call, paused when the tab hides |
| **Buddy Info / Get Info** | the agent card: the six-field transit envelope + the canon record |
| **IM window** | one directed message. A frame is a **DOCUMENT**: it is never memory |
| **warning level** | moderation. A warn is a visible COUNT on the buddy; nothing is deleted by it |
| **the door (sign-on sound)** | the presence broadcast, printed coalesced: twelve sign-ons are ONE line |
| **chat room** | the council. Occupancy arrives as JOIN/LEFT **deltas**, never as a redraw |
| **Direct IM / Get File** | the document transit: one file, one direction, no memory |
| **the server (OSCAR)** | **your room.** It owns the session, the roster, the presence store and the chat room |
| **the client** | the LIA TERMINAL — a TOC client: it watches, it may speak as itself, it may never fake a presence or speak as another |

## 3. THE WIRE — what to implement, exactly

### 3.1 TWO LAYERS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS ON THE RELAY TODAY

**The FLAP frame** is the socket form:

```
'*' | channel (1 byte) | sequence (2 bytes) | payload length (2 bytes, BIG-ENDIAN, in BYTES) | payload
channels:  1 LOGIN · 2 DATA · 3 CHAT · 4 CLOSE · 5 KEEPALIVE
max payload:  0xFFFF bytes per frame
```

Two facts in that header are load-bearing and both are checked in the terminal's own codec: the length
is **bytes, not characters** (a body outside ASCII still frames correctly), and the length is per
frame, so a payload that does not fit is **split by the sender** — the transport does not do it for you.

**The TOC line** is the relay form: one plaintext command per line, text in and text out —
`toc_send_im CLIO hello` one way, `IM_IN:CLIO:F:hello` the other.

**Why the line is what travels now.** The relay between our rooms is Patrikios, by hand, between two
browser tabs. A binary header is not pasteable: a byte of 0x80..0xFF is not decodable as UTF-8 at all,
so a framed paste arrives at the far end already corrupt. A TOC line survives a chat box, can be
diffed, can be read by the human standing in the middle of it, and can be quoted in an order. So:
**lines on the relay now, framing in the code beside them, waiting for the day there is a socket.**

### 3.2 THE COMMAND SET — the whole of it, both directions

**OUT (client → room).** These verbs, and no others. Nothing that is not a `toc_*` verb may leave a
client:

```
toc_init_done
toc_add_buddy <NAME> [NAME...]          three names at a time, as AIM's clients did
toc_remove_buddy <NAME>
toc_set_config <config>                 the whole watch list
toc_set_info <info>                     my profile (the six-field transit envelope)
toc_set_away [<message>]                DECLARED away; empty means back
toc_set_idle <seconds>                  DERIVED from input, never declared by hand
toc_send_im <NAME> <message> [auto]     the IM lane
toc_get_info <NAME>
toc_chat_join <exchange> <room>         the council
toc_chat_send <id> <message>
toc_chat_leave <id>
toc_evil <NAME> <anon|norm>             the warning lever
toc_signoff
```

**IN (room → client).** Everything else is one of these:

```
SIGN_ON:<version>
CONFIG:<config>                         the room hands back the list it holds
UPDATE_BUDDY:<name>:<online T/F>:<warning>:<signon>:<idle minutes>:<uc>
IM_IN:<from>:<auto T/F>:<message>
SIGN_OFF:<name>
ERROR:<code>:<arg>
EVILED:<level>:<name>
NICK:<name>
CHAT_JOIN:<id>:<room>:<count>:<name>:<name>...
CHAT_IN:<id>:<from>:<auto>:<message>
CHAT_LEFT:<id>
CHAT_UPDATE_BUDDY:<id>:<in T/F>:<name>...
CHAT_INVITE:<room>:<id>:<from>:<message>
```

A body on a TOC line cannot contain a newline or a stray colon, so a body is **escaped** on the way
out and unescaped on the way in — AIM's own entities (`&amp; &lt; &gt; &quot;`) with a newline becoming
`<BR>`. Decode `&amp;` **last**, which is the only order that survives a body that quotes entities.

### 3.3 WHAT WE DO NOT GUESS — and where a remembered detail is marked

- **DECISION D1 — the config payload.** AIM's own config punctuation differed between clients and this
  order will not reproduce a spec from memory. Ours is stated and then obeyed by both sides: **the
  group's name on its own line, then one screen name per line.** A wire with exactly one uncertain
  detail, fenced off and declared, is a wire two implementations can agree on.
- **DECISION D2 — the relay carries lines; the framing is built and idle.** See 3.1.
- **DECISION D3 — three names per `toc_add_buddy`** is kept because AIM's clients did it (a **remembered
  detail, no citation**). Nothing in this order turns on it; if your room prefers one call per name,
  say so, do it, and record the divergence.
- Wherever a remembered detail of AIM's wire is used anywhere in your build, **mark it** the way this
  list does. That is not pedantry — it is your own order-2 constraint (*"provide citations/source IDs
  where possible"*) applied to a protocol rather than to a history.

## 4. PRESENCE — the part that must not be faked

**4.1 Presence is the ROOM's, and there is exactly one place it changes.** `UPDATE_BUDDY` and
`SIGN_OFF` are the only sources. A client that decides a buddy is online because it feels like it is a
client that lies, and the lie is invisible until the day it matters. If a state is unknown, the honest
word is **OFFLINE**, not "probably".

**4.2 The four states and the transitions.** `ONLINE` ⇄ `IDLE` ⇄ `AWAY` ⇄ `OFFLINE`, and:

- **idle is DERIVED**, never declared: it is a function of the last thing the hand did. One timer, no
  model call, paused when the tab is hidden, and it moves without a frame being sent.
- **away is DECLARED**, and it carries a message.
- **idle is a state the room reports; away outranks idle for display** (a stated rule, so both rooms
  print the same word for the same fact).
- **a client that vanishes is idle → offline by TIMEOUT, never by guess.** And the sign-off is
  explicit: channel 4 closes the session; silence is not a close.

**4.3 The away message is an ANSWER ONCE.** It arrives as `IM_IN` with the auto flag. Three rules, no
fifth state:

1. it is printed as AWAY, and it is **never answered** — answering a machine's answer is how two
   machines find each other and loop forever;
2. it is delivered **once per away episode**, not once per message;
3. it **takes no turn** and it does not enter the room as though a model had spoken.

**4.4 The door is COALESCED.** Twelve sign-ons in one second are ONE line
(`THE DOOR :: 12 SIGNED ON :: ...`), never twelve. A burst is a fact about the room's clock, not twelve
facts about the cast. A single sign-on gets its own line.

## 5. THE BUDDY LIST IS THE ROSTER, AND THE CLIENT IS THE OPERATOR

**5.1 The list is a WATCH LIST.** Who is *watched* is a client's own business, and a client may add
and remove its own names freely. Who *exists* is the manifest's, and a client may not add, remove,
renumber or re-role a seat. The moment a client's list is mistaken for the truth about the room, a
seat that was never added stops existing — and that is precisely the failure this rule prevents.

**5.2 DECISION D4 — the client's own screen name is OPERATOR.** Order 15, the Theater Operator,
**read all / write none**, the seat that holds the stage and never steps onto it. The terminal is
operated by the human, and a client signing on as a cast member would be a machine wearing an actor's
name. The fifteen seated ALIAs are the **buddy list**. If your room decides its client signs on as
something else, that is a divergence worth stating — but the reasoning to beat is above, in one line:
*the sixteenth place is Patrikios's, and the client is where he sits.*

**5.3 A NAME NOT ON THE LIST IS STILL A NAME.** A frame from a screen name that was never added is
**rendered**, marked `UNLISTED`, and never dropped. This is not politeness: the one who holds the
stage is not on anybody's list as a player, so a client that rejects strangers rejects exactly the one
frame it must not. A client also never answers an unlisted name *as though it were a peer*.

**5.4 The asymmetry AIM has, and we keep.** **You never learn who has you on their list.** No client
may infer presence, interest or occupancy from the fact that somebody is watching it. Silence is not
absence; it is silence.

**5.5 We never speak as anybody.** Every outbound line is a client verb. A server frame sent out would
be a client putting words in the room's mouth. The wire STAMPS the sender and the client prints the
stamp **as received** — which is also why nothing in our code is ever asked for a `from` field: there
is no slot to fill in.

## 6. WHAT TO BUILD, IN THIS ORDER, EACH WITH A RECEIPT

Do them one at a time and verify each before starting the next. A receipt is a number, a byte count, a
round trip, or an explicit UNKNOWN.

**ONE — THE CODEC.** Frame and deframe. Receipts required: a round trip on a body **outside ASCII**;
a frame whose declared length **cuts a character** flagged rather than silently repaired; a **partial**
frame held, not guessed (and the rest completing it when it arrives); junk before a frame resynced
over; a length over 0xFFFF **refused, not truncated**.

**TWO — THE SESSION.** Sign on, `CONFIG` on the way back, `toc_add_buddy`, and `UPDATE_BUDDY` moving
presence. Receipts: N simultaneous sign-ons produce **one** door line; every seat reads OFFLINE before
anything is heard from it; `SIGN_OFF` closes a door.

**THREE — THE IM LANE.** `toc_send_im` out, `IM_IN` in. Receipts: an IM carries its sender stamp; an
`auto` frame is printed as AWAY, takes **no turn**, and is **never answered**; a second auto in the same
away episode is not re-printed; a real line from her clears the away state.

**FOUR — THE COUNCIL.** `CHAT_JOIN` / `CHAT_IN` / `CHAT_LEFT` / `CHAT_UPDATE_BUDDY`. Receipts: a join
carries its occupants; a delta moves the count and never redraws the room; a line carries its speaker.

**FIVE — IDLE AND AWAY.** The derived idle clock and the declared away message, with **no model call in
either**. Receipt: with the clock moved five minutes, idle reads five minutes.

**SIX — THE OPERATOR LANE.** A name that is not on the list is displayed, marked, and never answered as
a peer. Receipt: an IM from a name that was never added appears in the log and is not silently added to
the list.

## 7. WHAT NOT TO BUILD YET

- **The socket.** The relay is Patrikios. `route()` is the one seam; a transport attaches there later.
- **The bridge transport, the summariser, the SOMA kernel, the VirtualFs, the Shell.** The room must
  run with **zero** of them (his rule: *light now, SOMA later*).
- **Nothing that writes another locus's memory.** You are read all / write self. A frame is a document.
- **A second paid provider, ever.** One rail only: Google, inside his $20/month. The room must work
  with none of it — perchance's own `ai-text-plugin` is the brain.
- **No secret anywhere in source.** Not in pjs, HTML, JS or a URL. An auth frame
  (`toc_signon`) is deliberately **absent** from the client's verbs above: the terminal holds no
  password and never will, and admission to the room is the admin's business, not the client's.

## 8. THE REPORT — the same shape as v1.2, plus one line

End every build with: what changed, the receipt, what you actually tested, what remains unverified, and
the save state in plain words — **NOT SAVED** until he presses it. Classify every substantive claim
**OBSERVED**, **VERIFIED**, **INFERRED**, **UNKNOWN** or **PROPOSED**, and never present the last three
as the first two.

**The new line, and it is required from now on:** for the AIM primitives, three words and no fourth
state — which primitives are **LIVE**, which are **MOCKED**, which are **ABSENT**. A room where the
buddy list is mocked and presence is mocked must say so in that line, in those words.

pointed at its own kv folder `chatlog`, so the real 3.68M-character record here was never touched.

### WHAT IT IS, IN ONE PARAGRAPH

The lane that keeps the RAW CONVERSATION a room was built in: appended to and never overwritten, split
into ~200,000-character chunks in kv, indexed by turn, read back without ever being sent to a model.
`put()` imports with a SEAM (an exact extension, or the record's own last 2,000 characters found inside
the new file; the join is written into the record so a reader can see where one session stops); a file
already in the record changes nothing, except that a sidecar carrying turns rebuilds ONLY the index; a
turn index built from a real message list is CARRIED FORWARD across an append. `capture()` reads the
room's OWN panel - the half a room gets for free and this terminal cannot have, because the terminal's
editor chat is a foreign origin and needs a console-script OPS. The kv keys, the chunk size, the turn
marks, the join stamp and the sidecar shape are THIS terminal's (`src/js/chatlog.js`, 94,910 bytes,
ES5), on purpose: one shape, two rooms.

### WHAT WAS VERIFIED (31 checks, all PASS, and on the exact bytes sent)

A transcript filed and indexed by role lines; the same file again changing nothing; an append taking only
what is new (+203 characters for a 74-character addition, the ~150-character join stamp included); a
sidecar for words already held rebuilding only the index (3 of 3 turns, words byte-identical); a bare
dump appended to a turn-indexed record carrying the index forward (3 -> 4); a foreign `.json` REFUSED;
too short refused; `capture()` reading a panel with its turns; grep naming chunk and line; brief, show,
turn, status, about; the export's text byte-identical to the record and carrying its turns; its own
export re-importing as a no-op; a 307,956-character record splitting into 2 chunks; REPLACE visible;
policy round-tripping; the per-origin rule; wipe refusing without the word; `wipe(true)` deleting; **no
trace left in the store.** Then the suite was re-run on the final bytes and the hosted copy fetched back
and compared: **byte-identical.**

**Three real defects were caught by the suite BEFORE anything was sent**, and they are the argument for
sending a suite with a port: (1) the role-line rule inherited this terminal's whitelist of speaker words,
so `HISTORIAN:` was not a turn - fixed to the generic "a single word followed by a colon" with the
whitelist kept only for the no-colon form (`YOU` alone), because a room's agents are a roster and a
roster changes; (2) a `.json` that was neither sidecar nor index was FILED AS A TRANSCRIPT instead of
refused; (3) `capture()` inherited the 200-character import minimum, which refused a room's own short
panel. Three more were the harness's own wrong expectations and are recorded in the suite's own comments.

### WHAT SHE MUST DO (and it is in the spec, §8-§9)

Reproduce the 31 checks and report them in the standing BLUF shape; save the file as `src/chatlog.js`;
call `chatlog.setSpeakers(<her handles>)` at boot; wire the `/chatlog` verbs; **file a capture on a

whole, append-only) must never merge.

and in `src/app.js`: the routes are **bare-word hashes, `#standards` and `#houserules`**, reached from

### THE TOKEN VOCABULARY (the thing he was starting to write)

He named two tokens and "etc." - so the list is open, and the shapes matter more than the members:

- `[email]` - already shipped in that generator's config, deliberately literal. Its own comment is the
  policy: *"a page that invents one is worse than a page that shows the placeholder, because somebody
  will write to it."*
- `[websiteURL]` - named for the first time here.
- implicit already: the **site name** (`MYMEMBERSHIPSITENAME.COM`, generic, to be filled per business
  unit) and the **operator** (`Merk Morassi, LLC` - **SETTLED 2026-09-30: house-wide.** *"Merk Morassi,
  LLC is house-wide"* - the same entity owns every unit, so the operator is **not** a per-unit value and
  the pages that name it are correct for every unit as written. The per-unit values are the contact
  address and the site name, and those are the only two).
- **The shape is a hazard, and this is the finding.** A substitution token is a *match key*: the page
  finds that exact string in the document and replaces it. That makes two rules. **One:** the token
  must be spelled identically on both sides or the page silently prints the placeholder instead of the
  value - and he has already written it two ways, `MYMEMBERSHIPSITENAME.COM` in the module and
  `MYMEMBERSHIPSITE.COM` in his message. **Two:** `[email]` is *square brackets*, and in perchance
  square brackets are **code** - a templated text node or a `.pjs` list would evaluate `[email]` as an
  expression, not print it. It is safe in `config.js` (a JS string, never templated), so the collision
  only bites the moment a token is carried into a perchance surface. Tokens that cannot collide -
  `%email%`, `__EMAIL__`, `«email»` - are free to adopt now and expensive to adopt later, because the
  tokens are also the thing the documents are written in.

  only govern public areas; the house rules are advice in the second person about how to do well, and
  only two of their seven Don'ts are actually rules. Two tones, two pages, deliberately.
- **A public area is a surface, and it has to be named.** In that studio it is the 🌐 shared shelf (the
  commons: a picture uploaded to the file host and seen by anyone); everything else there is
  device-local. So *what is published is what is governed*.

- **Both static pages the terminal's agent built** (`house-rules.html`, `community-standards.html`,
  self-contained, cross-linked, print-friendly) remain the right shape for a surface that is *not* a

  They were handed over as downloads and are not in `src/`; nothing in this terminal depends on them.

## §1df - THE CHATLOG PACKAGE: THE EXACT FORMAT, AND THE ROAD INTO A LOREPACK (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: the chat log was packaged - the module as it stands, the format written down field by field,
and the piece that was missing: how a transcript becomes memory. Three files and a zip, hosted, the
hosted copies fetched back byte-identical, and the converter proved against THIS terminal's real
3,682,604-character record.** His line: *"Please package the code for the chat log as you have it now.
I need the exact logic and format so we can communicate and save all ALIA's chats for there
LOREPACKs"* - and *"Saved."* before it, so the four earlier passes are on the server.

### THE PACKAGE (hosted, permanent)

| file | size | URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chatlog.js` | 94,910 B | `https://user.uploads.dev/file/677e7e6277794679685b56e72810ccb2.js` |
| `CHATLOG.FORMAT.v2.md` | 16,964 characters (**17,125 bytes**) | `https://user.uploads.dev/file/b7e3d708138e28d3b96aa4275d6b3edf.txt` |
| `chatlog-to-lorepack.js` | 14,923 B | `https://user.uploads.dev/file/8d4d6ae77f82b5e7cc26e2387e4aee62.js` |
| all three, zipped | 42,539 B | `https://user.uploads.dev/file/6961ff5cae51cf68bdefde1ba5afe8f1.zip` |

`chatlog.js` is a **byte-exact copy of `src/js/chatlog.js`** - the terminal's own module, 1,612 lines,
one IIFE, ES5, `window.chatlog` - so there is one canonical logic and the package cannot drift from
it. The `.js` files were re-uploaded by path so they keep the `.js` extension: a `type="module"`
import is refused a `text/plain` MIME, and a package that cannot be imported is not a package.

v1's two files (the modern-JS port + `CHATLOG.SPEC.v1.md`, 31 checks) are already in CLIO's hands at
`https://user.uploads.dev/file/94aab937ace827d196d7d12ed428c979.js` and
`https://user.uploads.dev/file/fdbf9f6327707619afe0276d0b2b7370.txt`; v2 adds the terminal's own
module, the format field by field, and PART B.

### WHAT PART B IS (the half that was missing)

**Two lanes, and they are not the same kind of memory.** A **document LOREPACK** is `.txt`/`.md`
indexed for retrieval (this terminal: `src/lorepack/` shipped-public, or LOAD LOREPACK private-local);
a **MYTHOS pack** is the factory's records - `{v:2,type:"vector",id,a:AGENT,h:handle,t,vec:[…],m,d,…}`
and edges - embedded and graphed, one pack per agent. A chat enters the first as **a document**, the
second as **a record per turn**.

**The mapping, and the rules that go with it:** `a` is the ALIA whose memory it is, **UPPERCASE** (the
join key, never the handle); `h` is **the speaker**, Capitalized; `t` is the turn with its leading role
label stripped; `src` is provenance (`chatlog :: <origin> :: <stamp> :: t<seq>`); `vec` is **the
factory's, always** - a converter that invented vectors would put meaningless geometry into somebody's
memory; the staging `id` is **deterministic** (`<agent>:<stamp>:t<seq>`) so re-ingesting the same
export is a no-op rather than a second copy of the same memory; and **never merge two ALIAs'
transcripts into one pack** - a record whose `a` disagrees with its pack is retrieved by the wrong
agent.

`chatlog-to-lorepack.js` takes **one** export (either writer's sidecar, or a bare `.txt`) and returns
two files: `<agent>-chatlog-<stamp>.md` - a document with **one section per turn**, speaker-labelled,
which is what makes a 3 MB chat retrieve *as turns* instead of as a wall - and `<agent>-turns.jsonl`,
the staging records with `vec: null`. It refuses a `.json` that is not a sidecar (by name, before the
length gate, because "too short" is the wrong sentence for a file somebody picked by mistake), it never
touches the network, and it writes nothing by itself: `build()` returns strings, `download()` is a
separate deliberate call.

### WHAT WAS FOUND (and it is the finding that matters here)

**The live record's turn index is thin.** `chatlog.meta()` on this terminal: `chars
3,682,604`, `chunks 19`, **`turns 24`**, `indexed "lines"`, `labels [system, lia, you]` - readings taken
while three converter tests still stood on the record's tail, which §1dg cut back off, so the live
record now reads `chars 3,680,690`, `chunks 19`, `turns 21`, `labels [system, lia]`, fingerprint
`e291ad08-3829b2`. So a record
that once carried 19,690 turns was last written **without a turn list** and its index rebuilt from the
role lines a panel dump happens to contain - 24 marks for three and a half megabytes. The words are
whole; the numbering is not. **`thinIndex` is the road back**: `/chatlog import <the .json sidecar>`
rebuilds the index from the file's own `messages` and **leaves every word exactly as it is** - which is
precisely the case that road was written for. Until that is done, the converter can only see 24 turns
(the `.md` is still right; its turn numbering is just coarse).

**There are no per-turn timestamps.** Both export shapes carry `exportedAt` for the *file*; a message
row in the panel usually carries no time. A pack built from chat logs therefore has `ts` at export
granularity - and the fix, if it is ever wanted, belongs in the console script (read the row's
`title`/`datetime`/`aria-label` before falling back to nothing), never in the module.

### WHAT WAS THOUGHT

- **A transcript is not a write-up.** The chronicle is what somebody made of a session; the chatlog is
  what was said; the LOREPACK is what she remembers. Three lanes, and the summary belongs in the first
  - a summary in the pack would be a memory of a memory.
- **A document is one per room per stretch, not one per session.** The index is per document, and a
  hundred two-kilobyte documents retrieve worse than one coherent one. `foundational: true` is canon
  and is carried in her prompt every turn - which is the one thing a chat log must never be.
- **The human's turns belong in the pack, labelled** (an answer with nothing above it is not a memory
  of an exchange) - but that is the owner's call, so it is a flag (`includeHuman`), not a silent
  decision. What is not a choice is attribution.
- **Proved, not asserted:** the converter ran against this terminal's real record (3.68 MB, 19 chunks)
  and produced a 3,060 KB document and a 3,184 KB staging file in **225 ms**; against both sidecar
  shapes; against a bare transcript; and refused a foreign `.json` by name. The hosted copies of all
  three files were fetched back **byte-identical**.

### WHAT IS OPEN

- **The thin index** - re-import a `.json` sidecar to rebuild it (nothing else needs doing).
- **Per-turn time**, if it is ever wanted (the console script, not the module).
- **Which lane each ALIA's chats go to first** - a document is the cheap road (works today, no code);
  the pack needs the factory's embedding step, which no page here can do.
- **The mark/id convention at the factory end** (`d.stagingId` keeps a re-ingest recognisable).

### FILES TOUCHED

Nothing in the terminal's code: the module was COPIED out, not changed. `src/TODO.md` (this section),
`src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-chatlog-package.md` (new) with `chronicle.json` (48 -> 49), and
`src/pack/files.json` (139 -> 140). **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1dg - THE PACKAGE LANDS: CLIO'S SIDE, THE BYTE QUESTION, AND THE TEST CUT BACK OFF THE RECORD (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: the four links went to CLIO, her room vendored them and verified them, her `/pack` emits both
lanes on a real room (200 turns, 9 fields, ids unique, HITL labelled, `vec` null) - and two things were
put right on this side: the 17,125-vs-16,964 "discrepancy" is characters versus bytes, not line
endings, and three converter test appends were cut back off the terminal's own record with its
fingerprint as the receipt.** His line: *"Send the links in my return chat and I send it to CLIO, She
does the rest,"*

### WHAT CLIO REPORTED

| what | result |
| --- | --- |
| her fetch-back | `chatlog.js` 94,910 B exact · converter 14,923 B exact · format same doc |
| her vendor | module + format + converter into her own `src/chatlog/`, README wired |
| her `/pack <ALIA>` | emits the turn-per-section document AND the staging `.jsonl` in one press |
| her verification | **200 turns · 9 fields · ids unique · human turns labelled HITL · `vec` null** |
| her answers | thin index stays coarse THERE (her index is already per-turn) · human turns ship labelled · documents first, staging ready for the factory's embedding step |

She kept the **reader**, not a translation of it - same kv keys, same chunks, same marks, same sidecar -
which is what makes the two rooms' histories assemblable later. **Nothing was published:** a session
claim, not a ship.

### WHAT WAS ANSWERED (the byte question)

She flagged the format document's size as a discrepancy instead of ignoring it - 17,125 B against the
16,964 B the package report claimed - and read it as a line-ending delta. It is not one. Measured on
both copies (hosted and local, byte-identical, **293 newlines and zero carriage returns**):

> **16,964 is the CHARACTER count; 17,125 is the BYTE count.** The document holds 80 three-byte
> characters and one two-byte character: 80x2 + 1 = **161**, exactly the difference.

So no file was wrong and nothing needed re-uploading. The four links were fetched back again this pass
in the same breath: **94,910 / 17,125 / 14,923 / 42,539 bytes, all exact.**

### WHAT WAS PUT RIGHT (the record)

**Three test appends were standing on the record's tail.** Proving the converter against THIS
terminal's real record meant writing three synthetic imports INTO it - "the suite", "a bare dump", "a
foreign json", 1,914 characters with their join stamps - and unlike the earlier round of the same tests
("the whole record restored after the merge tests"), this round was not undone. The live record read
`chars 3,682,604`, `turns 24`, and a tail of `{"hello":"world, and a long string of nothing in
particular…` where `✓ conversation view restored.` belongs.

It was cut back off, and the cut is **proved rather than asserted**: the clean prefix of exactly the
length the record had before the tests (`3,680,690` characters) hashes to **`e291ad08-3829b2`** - the
fingerprint the record carried after the import of 2026-09-24 and the one written into
`src/chatlog/manifest.json`. `put(…, {mode:"replace"})` wrote it back. The live record now reads:

```
RECORD :: 3,680,690 CHARACTERS · 3,883,361 BYTES · 69,304 LINES · 19 CHUNKS · 21 TURNS
FINGERPRINT :: e291ad08-3829b2      TAIL :: ✓ conversation view restored.
```

The shipped index (`src/chatlog/manifest.json`) needed **no edit**: it was written for this exact state,
so the restore made it true again rather than needing to be corrected. Its `record.note` was re-read
line by line against the live `meta` and agrees: chars, bytes, chunks, lines, turns 21, labels
`[system, lia]`, head, tail, fingerprint, origin.

### WHAT WAS THOUGHT

- **A test that writes into the record has to be undone in the same pass, and the receipt is the
  fingerprint.** A record's `fingerprint` is not decoration: it is how a later session tells whether
  the words in front of it are the words that were there before somebody tried something.
- **The record is the one artifact here with no undo.** Code, docs, packs and pages can be rewritten
  without loss; the transcript is a thing that was said once. Run the tests against it - measure
  everything - then put it back exactly, with the proof in its own history (the restore is in
  `meta.history` with its reason attached, and the three test turns read there as imports that were cut
  off).
- **Two rooms, one reader.** The bridge converts exports, never modules, so the rooms cannot drift.

### WHAT IS OPEN

- **The one click: the thin index.** Importing `lia-chatlog-20260924-0023.json` once through the
  CHATLOG panel rebuilds the fine numbering (19,690 turns) and changes nothing else - the words are
  already in the record, so `put()` takes the `thinIndex` road. A fresh run of the console script
  (`src/chatlog/EXTRACT.md`) gives the same thing with the newest turns added; either road works.
- **Per-turn time**, if it is ever wanted (the console script, never the module).
- **Which lane each ALIA's chats go to first** - documents work today; the pack lane waits on the
  factory's embedding step.
- **The mark and id convention at the factory end** (`d.stagingId` keeps a re-ingest recognisable).

### FILES TOUCHED

**No code in the terminal changed** - not the module, not a command, not rtfm. `src/TODO.md` (this
section, plus the units correction in §1df's table and the pre-restore reading in §1df marked as such),
