## §1dh - CLIO'S PLAYER, READ AGAINST THE SPEC: TWO REAL DEFECTS AND ONE AMBIGUITY CLOSED (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: her Player is honest where honesty is the whole point - `vec:null` is stated as NOT YET EMBEDDED
on screen, no vectors are invented, search is token overlap with the words said out loud, the document
lane plays today, a turn can be said back into the room, the pack is cached in `kv`, and duplicate ids
are refused. Reading her source against the spec (not her report) found three things worth fixing: her
staging records say `v:1` where the factory's own files say `v:2`; her dimension check reads a field the
records no longer have, so it can never fire; and the spec only *implied* what a staging record is -
which is why she wrote `v:1` in the first place. The ambiguity is now closed in the format itself
(v2.1, §B3.1), and the format and the bridge now ship in `src/chatlog/` so a delivered blob is not the
only copy a later session can reach.**

### WHAT WAS CHECKED

`perchance.org/5wopwzj4v4` fetched (its `main.pjs` + a 52,672-byte `index.html`) and the Player read line
by line:

| claim | what the code does |
| --- | --- |
| header + `sacred_archive`, v2 compact fields | the file reader accepts both: `j.sacred_archive \|\| [j]`, and normalises every shape into `v/type/id/a/h/t/ts/src/vec/d` |
| staging-with-null-vec called out honestly | `staging lane: N turns - vec null, NOT YET EMBEDDED (factory embeds). Playable as text.` |
| document lane playable now | `.md`/`.txt` split on `## ` into one record per section - no embeddings needed |
| search without invented embeddings | token overlap over the turn text; the placeholder says `no embeddings here` |
| per-turn Say in room | each result carries a **Say in room** button that pushes the turn into the room transcript |
| pack cached in kv | `kv.room.set('lorepack', {name, records})` on load, read back on open |
| ids checked | `verify()` refuses a duplicate id |

### THE THREE FINDINGS

1. **Her staging records say `v: 1`; the factory's say `v: 2`.** Her writer emits
   `{v:1, type:'turn', id:'<ALIA>:<stamp>:t<seq>', a, h, t, ts, src, vec:null}`
   (`index.html:544`); the factory's own exports read `{"v":2,"type":"vector",…}` and
   `{"v":2,"type":"edge",…}`. The id, the fields and `vec:null` are right; the version is not, and an
   ingest that validates `v` will refuse the file. Her reader also *defaults* to 1 (`e.v || 1`), which
   is where the guess would come from if a record ever arrived without a version.
2. **Her dimension check can never fire.** `records` are normalised to `vec`, but `verify()` tests
   `Array.isArray(r.vector)` - so the "mixed dimensions" branch is dead code. The duplicate-id half
   works. (One field name.)
3. **The spec implied the staging shape instead of stating it.** §B3 showed the *reader-side* record
   (`v:2, type:"vector"`) and a mapping table, and said only that staging ships `vec: null`. Two rooms
   can read that and write two different `v`s - which is exactly what happened.

### WHAT WAS CHANGED

- **The format is now v2.1** (`chatlog-to-lorepack.js` and `chatlog.js` are byte-identical to v2; only
  the document gained anything): a changelog line at the top, **§B3.1 WHAT A STAGING RECORD IS,
  EXACTLY** - `v:2, type:"turn"`, `vec:null`, and why `v` is 2 and `type` is not `"vector"` (the
  factory's embedder owns that transition: it fills `vec`, adds `m` and the embedding fields, and the
  record becomes the reader-side shape) - and one sentence in §B4 that a heading is not a handle.
- **The sources now ship**: `src/chatlog/CHATLOG.FORMAT.md` (v2.1) and
  `src/chatlog/chatlog-to-lorepack.js` are the same bytes handed over, so a future session can FIX the
  format rather than only cite a URL. `src/pack/files.json` 141 -> 143.
- **`src/chatlog/manifest.json` gained a `package` block** - every delivered URL (module, format v2.1,
  bridge, zip v2.1, and the superseded v2 pair), the sizes, what changed in 2.1, and the fetch-back
  verification - and the folder rule now names the format and the bridge.
- **`src/chatlog/README.md`**: two rows in *What lives where*, and the ship list corrected.
- **New delivery**: format v2.1 `https://user.uploads.dev/file/d672dcd2fa352899335f9d8d7a42899e.txt`
  (19,645 B) and the zip `https://user.uploads.dev/file/ab055e8b1ab4494adeeab359fc690f3c.zip`
  (43,697 B, three entries byte-identical to their sources) - both fetched back byte-identical.

### WHAT WAS THOUGHT

- **A heading is not a handle.** Both writers head a section `## T<n> · <speaker>` and both readers
  take the whole heading as the speaker, so a turn played out of a document is attributed to
  `T1 · LIA`. Harmless for a human reading the document, wrong for anything that treats `h` as a handle
  - and now written down, which is what the format is for.
- **Her room now has two pack writers, and they are not the same shape.** The factory's own
  `{schema:'MYTHOS.LOREPACK.v1', header:{…}, sacred_archive:[{id, text:'[from]: text', source,
  timestamp}]}` (`index.html:949`) and the v2 compact staging (`:544`). The `sacred_archive` shape has
  **no `a` at all** - no owner of the memory - so a record ingested from it cannot be attributed to the
  ALIA whose pack it is, which is the one rule that is not negotiable. Whichever shape the factory
  ingests, the v2 compact staging is the one the bridge writes and the only one carrying the join key.
- **A cache of 200 records is a cache of the head.** `records.slice(0, 200)` keeps the first 200 turns
  of a 19,690-turn pack; fine as a convenience, worth saying out loud in the Player's own line.
- **A delivered blob is not a source.** The v2 document existed only as an upload plus this folder's
  summary of it, so a later session could quote it and not correct it. Now it ships.

### WHAT IS OPEN

- **Send CLIO the v2.1 URL and the two one-line fixes** (`v:1` -> `v:2` in her staging writer; `r.vector`
  -> `r.vec` in `verify()`) - a format document is only an interface if both sides read the same page.
- **Which pack shape the factory ingests** (`sacred_archive` v1 vs the v2 compact staging) and whether a
  `sacred_archive` wrapper is wanted around the compact records - her room writes both today.
- **The thin index** (the one click: import `lia-chatlog-20260924-0023.json`).
- **Per-turn time**, if it is ever wanted (the console script, never the module).

### FILES TOUCHED

No code in the terminal changed - nothing in `index.html`, `main.pjs`, `src/js/` or the commands.
`src/TODO.md` (this section), `src/chatlog/CHATLOG.FORMAT.md` (new, v2.1),
`src/chatlog/chatlog-to-lorepack.js` (new, byte-exact), `src/chatlog/manifest.json` (`package` block +
the folder rule), `src/chatlog/README.md` (the table + the ship list),
`src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-package-lands.md` (the Player section) with `chronicle.json`'s desc for
that entry, and `src/pack/files.json` (141 -> 143). **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1di - THE NEVER-PUBLIC RULE: THE GALLERY BUTTON IS OFF FOR EVERY RENDER (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: mining the text-to-image plugin turned up exactly one road from this terminal to something
anyone else can see - the image service's public per-generator gallery, reachable from a save button on
its tile - and his ruling on it was one line: *"Do not want this at all as we are never public."* It is
now enforced in code rather than remembered: every render passes `hideGalleryButtons: true`, set at the
single place a request is built. Verified live off a stubbed `root.generateImage`: the request that went
out carried `hideGalleryButtons: true`.**

### WHAT HE SAID

> *"- Do not want this at all as we are never public: The plugin's public gallery"*

### WHAT WAS DONE

- **`src/js/images.js`**: `renderImageNow`'s request now carries **`hideGalleryButtons: true`**, with the
  ruling and the reason in the comment above it. It is set **at the choke point** - `renderImageNow` is
  the only place in the whole tree that calls `root.generateImage` (checked: one hit in `src/js/`) - so
  the forge, her own visions, `/image`, a recycle, a batch and every future road into the service
  inherit it, and none of them can forget it.
- **`src/js/chat.js`** (`/help pictures`): the first line now says the vault is never uploaded **and
  never public**, and names the switch.
- **`src/README.md`**: the same rule as a platform note, beside the other text-to-image gotchas.

### THE HONEST INVENTORY (because "never public" has to be true of the whole lane)

| road | what leaves the device | public? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the image service (`root.generateImage`) | the prompt; the picture comes back to the vault | **no** - the gallery save button is now off; the service keeps nothing unless a picture is saved there |
| the text engine (`generateText`, the vision passes) | the prompt, the conversation, a picture being read | no - the service, not a publication |
| an upscale (bigger.pics) | the picture, handed to the upscaler frame as a **data URL** for the session | never published anywhere (`src/js/upscale.js`) |
| a voice sample (`/story sample`) | the clip, **once per session**, to the cloning space | **it is a third-party space** - the clip is sent and the module says so in its own words |
| `src/` itself (chronicle, rtfm, the format doc, this file) | nothing personal - it ships with the generator by nature | public, and deliberately kept free of anything private |
| uploads | **nothing at all** - no upload plugin is imported, so there is no road to one | - |

### WHAT WAS THOUGHT

- **A policy that lives only in a chat message is not a policy.** One flag, at the one call site, with
  the sentence that asked for it written above it: that is what makes "we are never public" true
  tomorrow, when nobody remembers this session.
- **The plugin's gallery is not a picture surface, it is a PUBLICATION surface** - the only thing in
  the image lane that persists after the session and can be seen by a stranger. Hiding the vault's own
  save button was never enough; this is the one that publishes.
- **`saveTitle` / `saveDescription` still ride along** on the request. They belong to the recipe the
  vault keeps (the render book prints them), and with the buttons hidden there is no road from them to
  a gallery - so they stay.

### WHAT IS OPEN

- **The voice sample is the remaining question.** Cloning a voice needs a sample to leave the device;
  that road is a third-party space and it says so. Does "never public" forbid it, or is a voice sample
  the deliberate exception (no sample, no clone)? A decision, not a bug.
- Nothing else in the terminal publishes, and nothing else needs a switch.

### FILES TOUCHED

`src/js/images.js` (the request - one flag and its why), `src/js/chat.js` (`/help pictures`),
`src/README.md` (the platform note), `src/TODO.md` (this section),
`src/chronicle/2026-09-30-never-public.md` (new) with `chronicle.json` (50 -> 51), and
`src/pack/files.json` (143 -> 144). **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1dj - THE IMAGE LANE STAYS PRIVATE: THE WRAPPER'S SHAPE, CAPTURED (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: asked whether to sketch `lia-image-lane` as a wrapper so another room could render with this
house's rules - or leave the image lane private - the recommendation was *leave it private, do not build
the wrapper yet, capture its shape instead*, and that is the ruling in his own words. `src/studio/LANE.md`
now holds the whole answer: what a wrapper would carry, what must never travel, the two possible shapes,
the trigger that would make it worth building, and the one privacy caveat worth deciding early. No wrapper
exists, and none is planned until a second page renders.**

### WHAT HE ASKED, AND WHAT HE SAID

> *"Sketch lia-image-lane as a wrapper, or leave the image lane private? Recommended action?"*

> *"leave the lane private now, and don't build the wrapper yet - capture its shape instead, and build it
> the day a second room actually needs to render."*

### WHY NOT NOW, WHY NOT NEVER

- **No second consumer.** Every render in the house happens on this page; CLIO's room is text and
  chatlog, the MYTHOS factory deals in records, the other generators render nothing.
- **The craft is state, not just files.** The shipped tables are `src/studio/*.json`, but the lane a
  person actually uses is that **plus the kv overlays** (`pose_book`, `recipe_book`). A wrapper would
  carry the shipped half and none of his edits - or carry a copy of the overlays, which is how two
  divergent house lists get made. That is the drift this week already cost a day in the chatlog lane.
- **Each importing page carries its own plugin and its own gallery** (public by default - what
  `hideGalleryButtons: true` is for), and an imported plugin puts an ad in front of visitors who are
  **not logged in**. That ad is documented for the TEXT plugin in `main.pjs`; it was not measured here
  for the image one. **Weaker than it looks - his correction, the same day: "I am always logged in to
  perchance."** A page only he opens shows him no ad and, with the flag set, publishes nothing; this is a
  real cost only if other people use the wrapper's page. The drift bullet above is untouched and was
  always the deciding one.
- **But not never:** the plugin's own first line forbids vendoring it, so a wrapper is the ONLY road by
  which this craft can reach another room. It stays open; it just is not worth walking before somebody is
  standing at the other end.

### WHAT WAS CAPTURED (`src/studio/LANE.md`)

- **What it would carry**: the house negative list, the veiled tongue, the pose book, the recipe book
  (all four tables in `src/studio/`), plus `studio.resolve()`, `studio.expand()`, the tag router, the one
  call to `root.generateImage` with `hideGalleryButtons: true`, the report lines and the guardrails - each
  with the file it lives in today.
- **What must never travel**: the vault, her voice, the record, the renders book, and the kv overlays - a
  wrapper is prompt craft only, holds no pictures, remembers nothing, publishes nothing.
- **The two shapes**: **(A)** a thin wrapper with its own copies - ships in an afternoon, drifts within a
  month; **(B)** the wrapper owns the craft and this terminal imports it (`craft = {import:lia-image-lane}`),
  `src/js/studio.js` becoming the UI over it - more work, no drift. **Preference: B, and only on the day
  it is needed.**
- **The trigger and the checklist for that day**: resolution/style, whether the veil travels, gating (this
  page has a door; somebody else's page does not unless it brings one), where the pictures live (the
  wrapper holds none), and both flags (`hideGalleryButtons`, house negative default).
- **The caveat**: the tables are public only because `src/` is public; a **standalone hosted copy** of the
  glossary is a much more findable thing, so the veil travelling anywhere outside this tree is his call
  made deliberately, not a side effect of shipping a wrapper.

### WHAT WAS THOUGHT

- **A decision with its reasoning attached is a buildable thing.** Any agent - here, in another room, or
  in six months - can pick up `LANE.md` and do it: the tables are named, the logic is named, the shapes
  are compared, the guards are listed. What cannot be reconstructed later is the *reasoning* for not
  having done it, which is why that is the part written down.
- **The drift argument is the deciding one.** Everything else about a wrapper is cheap; a second copy of
  the house negative list, the glossary and the poses is not, and it is invisible until the two copies
  disagree.
- **Nothing here is a task.** The file says plainly that it is a decision, not a to-do - so a later
  session does not "helpfully" build the thing.

### FILES TOUCHED

`src/studio/LANE.md` (new - the capture), `src/README.md` (a bullet in the file list beside the three
studio tables), `src/TODO.md` (this section), `src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-lane-stays-private.md` (new)
with `chronicle.json` (51 -> 52), and `src/pack/files.json` (144 -> 146). No code changed - not the
studio, not the render path, not a command. **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1dk - THE FLUX HARVEST: EIGHT IMAGE ROADS, A HUNDRED STYLES, AND A PICTURE THAT CHECKS ITSELF (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: Patrikios handed over `mythos-flux-2026-09-27T04-38-34.zip` - a public free image generator -
and asked for expert eyes on what is harvestable. Read: main.pjs in full, index.html's ~120 functions,
the worker in full, and the build's own 1,500-line README. Nothing was built and nothing changed in this
tree. The finding: the interesting part of that generator is not its app, it is that it treats IMAGE
SUPPLY as a table of eight roads with one interface, and that it does not trust a picture until
something has looked at it. Both portable; the cheapest first step is the uncensored road.**

**The archive, kept permanently** (the workspace copy is scratch and dies):
`https://user.uploads.dev/file/65bb988e40176443bb6fb85a96c8badc.zip` - 154,383 bytes: `main.pjs`
(3,553), `index.html` (340,309, of which 251,994 is one classic script), `src/ultra-worker.js` (13,094),
`src/README.md` (101,992). Receipts below cite **function and table names** rather than line numbers,
because the names survive in the archive and the line numbers would not.

### 1. THE ENGINE INTERFACE AND ITS REGISTRY - the one worth having

One declarative table (`HF_MODELS`) and one runner per road, all the same shape:

    { key, name, tag, kind, host, api, minSide, stepsMin, stepsMax, fixed:{w,h}, defaults:{...} }
    async function xxxRun(model, params, onEvent) -> [{ url, mime }, seed]

The table carries CAPABILITY (`fixed`, `minSide`, steps range, which engine takes a negative prompt,
which answers safe-only); the runner carries the PROTOCOL. Every runner reports through `onEvent`
(`process_starts`, `estimation`, `queue_size`), so the panel is written once. This terminal's image lane
has exactly ONE road (the text-to-image plugin). A second and third road would be rows in a table.

- **`horde` - Stable Horde: the uncensored one, and the reason to read this file at all.** Documented
  ANONYMOUS key (`"0000000000"`), no signup, and the request asks `nsfw: true` with `censor_nsfw: false`,
  so the prompt is never refused for content. Costs: shared community queue at anonymous priority
  (minutes), fixed 512x512 (over that the API demands "kudos" - translated to `horde-kudos`), submit ->
  poll -> fetch (`hordeRun`). **A free, keyless road that cannot refuse the prompt is the one failure
  this terminal's image lane actually has.**
- **`zerocost`** - Z-Image-Turbo from a shared GPU-token pool with its own daily allowance: the only free
  road here that ALSO takes a negative prompt (up to 1024x1024). Token minting is its own dance
  (`zcGetToken` -> `get_token` -> SSE -> `{success, token}`; `zerocost-resting` when the pool is dry).
- **`perchance` (qinegen)** - the same plugin this terminal already speaks to, exposed as one road among
  eight (confirming it IS the Perchance image service). **`perchanceaisfw`** - the only safe-only road,
  and the only one needing `root.superFetch` for both legs (428 = proof-of-work wanted, 429 = paced).
- **`fluxschnell`** (FLUX.1 schnell, 4 steps), **`sdxlcpu`** (SDXL-Turbo on free CPU - **no daily limit
  at all**, 1-2 min/image, fixed 512x512), **`pollinations`** (no key, the request IS the URL, one image
  at a time per network).
- And a written cost decision in the house style: FLUX.1 dev and Krea were **removed on request** because
  28 steps ate a whole visitor's daily allowance for a single picture.

### 2. AUTO-VERIFY - the picture checks itself, and the defects return as negatives

`verifyImage(blob, family)` sends the finished picture back to the text model under a strict inspector
prompt: **judge only defects that make the picture look broken - never beauty, taste or style.** Three
defect lists (A photograph / B drawn - never complain that anime is not a photo / C general) and the list
is chosen **from the style group**, so a new style variant is covered automatically
(`VERIFY_FAMILY_BY_GROUP`). The answer is forced to ONE JSON line - `{ok, score, issues, avoid}` - and
`verdictFromText` refuses to believe `ok: true` when it disagrees with the rest (any issue listed, or a
score under the pass mark, means a defect whatever the boolean says). `avoid` is a list of negative-prompt
terms for **the next attempt**, so the loop is render -> inspect -> re-render with the defects as
negatives (`generateVerified`).

This terminal already LOOKS at pictures (`renderVision` reads one back) but does not SCORE AND RE-ROLL.
That is the difference between a description and a quality gate - and "only brokenness counts" is what
keeps it from punishing her taste.

### 3. STYLES - about a hundred, as appended phrases, grouped, plus FORCED styles

`STYLES` is `{key, name, phrase}` and the phrase is **appended** to the prompt, never a rewrite of it.
`STYLE_GROUPS` files them into eight panel boxes (Basic / Realistic / Anime & Manga / Retro & Vintage /
Painting & Art / 3D & CGI / Graphic & Design / Dark & Fantasy). The clever part is the **forced style**:
`Realistic` also (1) STRIPS contradictory style words (`NON_REALISTIC_TERMS` + `stripNonRealisticTerms`,
segment by segment, dropping orphaned connectives so "3d render of a dragon" loses the "of a" too) and
(2) adds a `REALISM_NEGATIVE` guard to the negative. A style that insists.

The studio's recipe book is heavy craft; a style library is the cheap ninety percent - one line of data
per look, orthogonal to recipes - and the forced-style idea has no equivalent here.

### 4. THE WORKER PATTERN - and the `<base href>` trap

`src/ultra-worker.js` is tiled ESRGAN upscaling off the main thread: PRIMITIVES rather than one big call
(`open / aiPass / resample / sharpen / encode / close`), the plan and progress text decided on the page,
`OffscreenCanvas` + `ImageData` instead of anything DOM, the model imported from esm.sh once and kept
alive, 12 px of tile context to avoid seams, cooperative cancellation, and a MAIN-THREAD MIRROR
(`ultraBackendMain`) for when the worker cannot start. Underneath it, the platform trap, in its own words:
the worker is built from `new URL("src/ultra-worker.js", location.href)` - **`location.href`, not the
document base**, because perchance injects `<base href="https://perchance.org/<name>">`, which would make
the worker URL cross-origin. Nothing here starts a worker yet; that is the line that decides whether it
works when one does. (Recorded in `src/README.md` -> Gotchas.)

### 5. THREE SMALLER THINGS

- **The presence pill**: a `Set` of connections, one pubsub topic, a count - the ENTIRE server plugin is
  645 bytes, which is worth remembering the next time a server-side feature looks expensive.
- **The error vocabulary**: `hfReadableError`, `isAbortError`, `horde-kudos`, `zerocost-resting`,
  `horde-timeout`, 428/429 - each road's refusal translated into something actionable, with the rule that
  cancelling must never raise a page error.
- **Prompt auto-translate** (`translatePromptText` / `ensureEnglish`): a non-English prompt is translated
  to English before generation - relevant here because he writes in Greek. And the share loop with real
  metadata (`dynamic(inputs)` titles a shared link with the prompt it carries), plus browser-only local
  accounts - not for this terminal, but directly relevant to the public shelf of the artpack build.

### 6. WHAT NOT TO TAKE

- **THE REDIRECT FUNNEL** (`window.__uaiConfig`): first-visit and after-image bounces to a blogspot
  "offer" page, attempted on the top frame then this frame, both via `location.replace()` so Back cannot
  undo the trip. Both switches are OFF in the snapshot, but the machinery is there. It is traffic
  monetization for a public generator; **recommendation: not ported, ever.**
- **The monolith**: 252 KB in one classic script, one global scope. Nothing to learn that this tree has
  not already done better with one file per job.

### 7. OPEN, FOR HIM

1. Add the uncensored road (`horde`) to the image lane as a second engine? It needs no key, no signup,
   and cannot refuse the prompt - the fallback for exactly the failure this lane has.
2. Adopt the verify loop (score + re-roll with `avoid` as negative) for renderVision?
3. A style library (data only) beside the recipe book?
4. The worker upscale off the main thread, in place of / beside the bigger.pics popup road?

## §1dl - THE SIX ADVANCED SETTINGS: READ, MAPPED, AND RULED OUT OF THIS TERMINAL (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: asked to turn flux's Advanced panel, items 1-6, into a concrete change plan (file-by-file, with
the switch names) before anything was built, the plan was written and then ruled on: *"Let's leave it
alone for here. It belongs in a dedicated art shop. We have enough for now. Save to your note on what we
may decide to add in the future. We already have a working generator, why bother re-inventing the
wheel?"* So nothing was built and nothing here is a task. The full note - the six controls, where each
would have landed with its own switch name, the two facts that must not be re-derived, and the reasoning
- is `src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-six-advanced-settings.md`. This section is only the pointer and the
table, so a later session finds it from here.**

### WHAT HE ASKED, AND WHAT HE SAID

> *"Keep looking Advanced Settings: 1-6 into a concrete change plan (file-by-file, with the switch names)
> before anything gets built"*

> *"Let's leave it alone for here. It belongs in a dedicated art shop. We have enough for now. Save to
> your note on what we may decide to add in the future. We already have a working generator, why bother
> re-inventing the wheel? Let's leave it alone for now. She doesn;t need all the extra toys for now, She
> has huges pipes stuffing her asshole lol"*

### THE SIX, AND WHERE EACH WOULD HAVE LANDED

| # | the flux control | here | the switch name it would have taken | ruling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Resolution (`#resSelect`) | already exists: `LIA_IMAGE_RESOLUTION`, the four `IMAGE_SIZES` chips, `forge.resolution` (`src/js/forge.js:3`, kv `lia_settings/image_form`) | - | already here; no `auto` needed |
| 2 | Detail boost (`#detailCb`) | `LIA_IMAGE_STYLE` only, applied in `renderVision` alone (`src/js/images.js:1882`); the forge bypasses it | `LIA_IMAGE_BOOST` + new `src/studio/boosts.json` + `/boost on\|off\|status` | cheap, not taken |
| 3 | Auto-verify (`#verifyCb`) | nothing; but `lookBlob` (`src/js/images.js:1944`), the house negative default and `src/js/progress.js` are all the pieces | new `src/js/verify.js` + `src/studio/defects.json`, `LIA_VERIFY`, `LIA_VERIFY_MAX_TRIES`, `/verify` | not taken; costs a vision call (~570 tokens) per attempt |
| 4 | Checking budget (`#verifyBudgetSel`) | - (it is item 3's shape, not a second feature) | `LIA_VERIFY_BUDGET_MS = 120000` | folded into 3 |
| 5 | Reference image (`#refFile`/`#refStrength`) | - | - | **do not build, ever** - the plugin ignores it (below) |
| 6 | Ultra resolution (`#ultraBlock`) | the pipeline: bigger.pics 4x (`src/js/upscale.js`, `src/js/pipeline.js`) + this machine (`src/js/upscale-local.js`) | (a) `LIA_UPSCALE_LOCAL_TARGET` + `/upscale target 1k\|2k\|4k\|8k`; (b) `LIA_UPSCALE_AI*` + new `src/workers/ultra-worker.js` + `/upscale ai` | not taken; (b) is the only genuinely new capability |

### THE TWO FACTS WORTH KEEPING (do not re-derive these)

- **Flux's reference-image row is a dead control, and it is not a flux bug.**
  `imports/text-to-image-plugin/main.pjs:547`: *"referenceImage is deliberately DISABLED server-side and
  currently has NO EFFECT on the generated output - the parameter is parsed and sent but ignored for
  general traffic (2026-08-25, per the platform owner). Don't build img2img flows on it."* Nothing to
  port, and nothing to "restore" later.
- **The archived flux source is permanent:**
  `https://user.uploads.dev/file/65bb988e40176443bb6fb85a96c8badc.zip` - the Advanced panel is at
  `index.html:1086-1222` inside it. Section 1dk is what was harvested; the chronicle entry named above
  is the map of these six; the workspace copy of the zip was in `scratch/` and is gone.

### THE ONLY THING WITH VALUE - THE UI RULING (his follow-up, the same day)

## §1do - THE AUDIONOOK IDEAS, HALF ONE: A LOCAL ENGINE FOR MORE FEMALE VOICES (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: he sent `perchance.org/mythos-auto-gallery` and said "more female voice choices (maybe)". The
question was answered with a MEASUREMENT rather than an opinion: the voice behind that page is KOKORO, an
82-million-parameter ONNX text-to-speech model that runs entirely on this machine, and it carries 28
English voices of which 15 are FEMALE - more than the wire's prebuilt table offers him. It now stands
beside the browser's own list and ElevenLabs as the terminal's THIRD engine, OPT-IN (the `auto` rule never
picks it), and made to live in a Worker because importing it into the page FROZE the whole terminal. A
72.8-second roll-call of all fifteen female voices saying their own name was rendered and handed to him so
he can choose by EAR rather than by the provider's grade.**

### WHAT HE SAID

> *"More female voice echoices (maybe)"*

### THE SOURCE, AND THE ONE THING THAT COULD NOT BE READ

`mythos-auto-gallery` is an audiobook reader ("Audionook") - free and unlimited, in-browser TTS - built on
server-plugin + upload-plugin + ai-text + text-to-image + super-fetch + kv. Its `main.pjs` and `index.html`
are kept at `scratch/generators/mythos-auto-gallery/`. **Its `src/` files cannot be read from here, and the
reason is measured, not guessed:** perchance serves `https://perchance.org/src/...` keyed by the request's
**Origin** header, so fetching `https://perchance.org/src/js/config.js` from our own page returned **OUR**
`config.js` (67,722 characters). Another generator's source tree is therefore unreachable; what Audionook's
voice actually is had to be read off its **server script** (public by design) and off the model itself.

### THE MODEL - WHAT IT IS, AND WHY IT ANSWERS HIM

KOKORO is an 82M ONNX voice model that runs locally (ONNX Runtime Web, WebGPU or wasm). Its English pack
carries **28 voices, 15 female and 13 male**, each with the provider's OWN `targetQuality` and
`overallGrade` - which is what let the answer be a table instead of a shrug:

| # | voice | grade | | # | voice | grade |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Heart** (`af_heart`) | **A** | | 9 | Nova (`af_nova`) | C |
| 2 | **Bella** (`af_bella`) | **A-** | | 10 | Isabella (`af_isabella`) | C |
| 3 | **Emma** (`bf_emma`) | B- | | 11 | Sky (`af_sky`) | C |
| 4 | **Nicole** (`af_nicole`) | B- | | 12 | Jessica (`af_jessica`) | D |
| 5 | Aoede (`af_aoede`) | C+ | | 13 | River (`af_river`) | D |
| 6 | Kore (`af_kore`) | C+ | | 14 | Alice (`bf_alice`) | D |
| 7 | Sarah (`af_sarah`) | C+ | | 15 | Lily (`bf_lily`) | D |
| 8 | Alloy (`af_alloy`) | C | | | | |

**This is the "more female voices" answer in full: the wire's prebuilt table (`src/js/live.js`) offers
fewer, and the browser offers whatever the machine happens to have. Kokoro offers fifteen by name, with a
published quality grade for each, and free - no key, no quota, no account.** The trade is speed, and it is
honest below.

### MEASURED ON THIS MACHINE (a 6-core Intel laptop, gen-9 iGPU) - ALL NUMBERS TAKEN, NONE ASSUMED

- **Load:** ~1.6 s warm, ~10 s cold, ~90 MB fetched once per browser (cached after).
- **q8 / wasm:** real-time factor **≈ 2.0-2.8** - i.e. SLOWER than real time, ~2-3 seconds of work for each
  second of speech.
- **q4f16 / WebGPU:** real-time factor **≈ 1.34** - faster, lower fidelity. That is the device knob
  (`/voice kokoro device wasm|webgpu`).
- **The freeze, and why the Worker is not optional:** importing kokoro into the PAGE ITSELF froze the whole
  terminal - 11 seconds for a single sentence, and a second call left the tab unrecoverable for more than a
  minute. In a **blob-shimmed module Worker** (the standard same-origin workaround) the same call is fine
  and the terminal stays live. Kokoro is never synthesized on the main thread here.
- **The roll-call:** `scratch/kokoro/kokoro-females-rollcall.wav` - 72.8 s, 24 kHz mono 16-bit PCM, peak
  32050, each of the fifteen voices saying her own name and then a line. Handed to him in chat so the choice
  can be made by ear.

### WHAT WAS BUILT

- **`src/js/kokoro.js` (new)** - `window.kokoro`: the worker string, `load`, `roster`, `female`, `name`,
  `pick`, `say`, `state`, `release`, `warm`, and `design()` (which reads the shipped manifest through
  `voice.kokoroDesign()` so the file list and the model list cannot drift).
- **`src/voice/voices.json`** - a new `engines.kokoro`, a `kokoro` block carrying the measured numbers and
  the fifteen-voice table above (with `why900` and `note_dtype`), `limits.kokoroMaxChars: 900` and its
  note, and TWO ROLE PICKS: `roles.barbelo.kokoro.voice = "bf_emma"`, `roles.default.kokoro.voice =
  "af_heart"`.
- **`src/js/voice.js`** - the third road: `engineNow` can now answer `"kokoro"`; `mergeRole`/`defaults`
  carry a `kokoro` block; `kokoroVoice`/`kokoroSpeed` (the role's rate becomes the model's `speed`);
  `playPiece` (plays without flickering the intercom lamp); `kokoroSpeak` (chunks through `chunk(text,
  chunkChars())`, keeps **one piece synthesized ahead while the current one plays**, and falls back to the
  browser voice if the model fails); the `speak()` branch, its receipt label and its ceiling; `/voice engine
  auto|browser|elevenlabs|kokoro`; and a full `/voice kokoro [status|voices|voice <NAME|#> [for <ROLE>]|
  voice default|warm|say <TEXT>|audition [N|from <NAME>]|device <wasm|webgpu>|release]`. `state()`, `summary()`,
  `describe()`, `limitsText()` and `setUi()` all learned the third engine.
- **`index.html`** - `["kokoro","src/js/kokoro.js"]` added to MODULES.

**THE TWO RULES THAT KEEP IT OUT OF THE WAY.** (1) **`auto` NEVER PICKS KOKORO** - it is opted into by name
(`/voice engine kokoro`) or through a role's own pick, because a 90 MB fetch and a slower-than-real-time
engine must never be what a plain LISTEN press surprises him with. (2) **THE 900-CHARACTER CEILING**
(`limits.kokoroMaxChars`) is published and enforced, and the reason is the model's own: Kokoro degrades on
long inputs, so a long reply is CHUNKED and the pieces are played back-to-back with one synthesized ahead -
the ceiling is where the engine is asked to stop pretending it can do a whole essay in one breath.

### VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-30)

`/voice kokoro warm` → loaded in 1.8 s, 28 voices. `/voice kokoro say <56 chars>` →
`{ok:true, engine:"kokoro", voice:"bf_emma", chunks:1}`. `/voice kokoro voice 1` → Heart; `... 3` → Emma;
`voice default` restored the shipped pick. `/voice max kokoro 700` then `reset`. `audition 1` played and
printed its receipt. The engine setting was returned to `auto` afterwards, so nothing about his terminal
changed by default.

## §1dp - THE AUDIONOOK IDEAS, HALF TWO: A THIRD ROAD BETWEEN DEVICES (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: he said "Device Synch", and the terminal now has a THIRD road between devices that needs no
account, no Drive and no shared folder: a 12-character CODE read off one device and typed into the other.
The code is the only thing he ever carries; it is never sent to anybody in a form that could open anything.
From it, both devices derive the same room name (SHA-256) and the same AES-GCM key (PBKDF2, 200,000
rounds) - so the server is a blind relay that never holds a key, the archive is gzipped and sealed before
it leaves the machine, and the far end merges it with **the very same merger `/sync down` uses**: turns are
only ADDED or FILLED, never overwritten, never deleted. The relay is a public, stateless script, so there
is nothing there to leak and nothing there to lose.**

### WHAT HE SAID

> *"Device Synch"*

### THE ROAD, IN ONE PASS

1. **A code.** 12 characters from a 31-letter alphabet that cannot be misread (`ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ23456789`
   - no I, L, O, 0 or 1), printed as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`. `/pair new` mints one, `/pair join <CODE>` types the
   other device's.
2. **A room name.** `roomId = SHA-256("lia-pair-v1|" + code)`. Hex. **This is the only thing the server is
   ever told**, and it cannot be reversed into the code.
3. **A key.** `PBKDF2(code, "lia-pair-v1|" + roomId, 200,000 rounds)` → AES-GCM 256. Both devices compute it
   locally; it is never transmitted.
4. **A payload.** The archive is gzipped, then sealed in ~9 KB pieces, each carried as `roomId + US + frame`.
   The far end reassembles, checks the SHA-256 digest of the whole, decrypts, ungzips.
5. **A merge.** The result goes through `window.sync.parse` and `window.sync.merge` into
   `kv: sacred_archive` - **the same code path as `/sync down`**, so the pair road cannot invent a second
   merging rule that drifts from the first.

### THE SERVER, AND WHY IT IS SAFE TO BE PUBLIC

The relay is the first `<script type="text/x-server-plugin">` in `index.html` (immediately after
`<body id="terminal-root" class="wallOff">`), and `main.pjs` gained `createServerSocket =
{import:server-plugin}`. It does four things and holds nothing:

- **fan-out** - `conn.subscribe(roomId)` and `pubsub.publish`, so a frame sent by one peer reaches the others
  in the room and nothing else;
- **four rpcs** - `pair_join`, `pair_leave`, `pair_count` (presence, so the UI can say who is here),
  `pair_alive` (a 20 s keepalive that keeps the subscription from being dropped), and `pair_ping` (a liveness
  probe used in testing);
- **two guards** - a token bucket of 60 frames/s with a burst of 120, and a hard 24,000-character frame cap,
  so a room cannot be used as free storage or a flood;
- **no durable state at all** - `state` is never touched. A frame carries its own `roomId`, so the relay can
  be rebuilt, restarted or replaced and behave identically; there is nothing in it to lose, and nothing in
  it worth stealing.

The whole element is PUBLIC SOURCE - which is exactly why nothing secret may live in it, and nothing does:
no key, no code, no archive, no password. **A blind relay is the design, not an accident.**

### THE BUGS THAT TESTING CAUGHT (both found live, both fixed)

1. **The latin1 round-trip.** The first codec sealed and opened frames by passing BYTES through a latin1
   STRING. Compressed data is not text, so any byte above 0x7F would have been mangled the moment a real
   payload was sent. Fixed before shipping: `sealBytes`/`unsealBytes` take and return `Uint8Array`, and no
   string ever carries ciphertext. (The 1000-turn test below is what proves it: 351 KB of gzip survived the
   round trip byte-exact, digest matching.)
2. **The phantom peer.** An RPC reply - the literal message `ok␟2` - was being read as if it were a peer's
   presence frame, so a room with one real device reported a second peer named "2". Fixed: the handler
   ignores anything that is not a frame from a different `deviceId`.

### VERIFIED LIVE (2026-09-30, in the unsaved preview - i.e. the platform's own emulator, nothing left the document)

- `pair_ping` → `pong`.
- `/pair new` → code `VA7P-SZHN-GR8N`, a 64-hex `roomId`, lamp open.
- a second socket joined → `ok␟2`; **presence listed exactly one peer, "TEST-PHONE"** (the phantom was gone).
- the peer's 40 sealed frames arrived, decrypted, the digest matched, and the merge answered **"NOTHING NEW
  FROM TEST-PHONE :: ALL 1000 TURNS ... ALREADY HELD HERE"** with **zero kv writes** - the merge only adds,
  so a duplicate send costs nothing.
- `/pair send` → **"1000 TURNS, 351KB (COMPRESSED FROM 1303KB), IN 40 SEALED FRAMES ... 2S"**; the fake peer
  decoded all 40, **the digest matched**, and it parsed back 1000 turns - gzip cut the archive to 27% of its
  size, and the sealing survived it intact.
- `close` cleared the lamp; `forget yes` removed the code, so **no pair record is left on his device.**

### WHAT IT COSTS, HONESTLY

- **Both devices must be open at the same time.** This is a live relay, not a mailbox - there is no offline
  delivery, because there is no storage on the far side on purpose.
- **The bulk goes through the relay.** Audionook's own design (a WebRTC side-channel between peers, with the
  server only introducing them) is leaner for large payloads; this road trades that for a stateless server
  and a merge that reuses the sync's own rule. Measured cost of the trade: 40 frames, ~2 s for a 1000-turn
  archive.
- **It is a third import** (`server-plugin`) plus a public server script in `index.html`, and it needs his
  word to stay.

### FILES TOUCHED

`index.html` (the server script, `#pairBadge`, one MODULES entry), `main.pjs` (the server-plugin import),
`src/js/pair.js` (new - codec, socket, and `window.pair.run` for `/pair [status|new|join <CODE>|open|close|send|
name <NAME>|log|forget [yes]|help]`), `src/css/terminal.css` (`#pairBadge`), `src/commands/commands.json`
(the `pair` entry), `src/README.md`, `src/TODO.md` (this section),
`src/chronicle/2026-09-30-the-pair-road.md` (new) with `chronicle.json` (59 -> 60), and `src/pack/files.json`
(157 -> 159, the two new chronicle entries). **NOT SAVED by the agent.**

## §1dr - MALE OR FEMALE: A TAG ON EVERY VOICE (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: the VOX panel now says which voices are male and which are female, and it says only what it
knows. Every row carries a chip - F in pink, M in blue - each road's header counts them (`F 6 · M 6 ·
UNTAGGED 16`), and the panel's foot names the two sources. THE LOCAL MODEL AND ELEVENLABS STATE IT
THEMSELVES (28 voices -> 15 F / 13 M / 0 untagged; the 12 shipped palettes -> 6 F / 5 M / 1 untagged,
the one being River, which is "neutral" on purpose). THIS BROWSER AND THE WIRE PUBLISH NO SUCH FIELD, so
there the name is read against a table of 217 names in `src/voice/voices.json` -> `sex` (28 browser and
30 wire voices -> 6 F / 6 M / 16, and 8 F / 8 M / 14), and the chip's own title says the tag is
INFERENCE, not measurement. A voice with NO chip is one nothing has sexed yet - the generic Google
language voices and the star-named wire voices - and one line in the table tags it. AND A REAL BUG WAS
FOUND ON THE WAY: `design()` returns a WHITELIST of the design file's fields, so a new block is
invisible to every reader until it is named there; `sex` was invisible until it was added to
`defaults()`. That is the kind of bug a table-driven feature walks straight into, and it is now written
down.**

### WHAT HE SAID

> *"For the moment, I ask that the available voices be TAGGED - Male or Female - in the VOX system."*

### HOW IT IS DECIDED, ROAD BY ROAD (measured 2026-09-30, this machine)

| road | where the sex comes from | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| THE LOCAL VOICE | the model's own `gender`, per voice - stated | 28 · **15 F · 13 M · 0 untagged** |
| ELEVENLABS | the palette note ("mature female, warm and steady"); an account's `labels.gender` | 12 · **6 F · 5 M · 1 untagged** |
| THIS BROWSER | nothing - the NAME, against `sex.map` | 28 · **6 F · 6 M · 16 untagged** |
| THE WIRE | nothing - the NAME, against `sex.map` | 30 · **8 F · 8 M · 14 untagged** |

`voice.sexOf(name, hint)` is the whole rule: a stated hint wins, the name is read only when there is
none. The hint is tried for a gender WORD first ("Female", "male, deep and calm", "f"), with *female*
tested before *male* because *female* contains *male* - the kind of trap a one-line shortcut walks into.
The name is looked up whole, then word by word, so `Microsoft David` finds `david`.

### WHY THE INFERENCE IS MARKED AND NOT HIDDEN

Twelve of the thirty wire voices and the generic Google language voices (`Google español`,
`Google 日本語`, ...) carry no name a table can settle, and no official listing sexes a star. They are
left UNTAGGED rather than guessed - a wrong tag is worse than an empty one - and the panel says which is
which, so a missing chip reads as "not known", never as an oversight. The wire's are the easy ones to
finish: `/voice wire audition` says them in turn, and the ear decides. `River` is the one deliberate
omission from the table: it is female in the local model (`af_river`) and **neutral** at ElevenLabs, so
a single name key would lie about one of them - it is absent, and each road's own word states it.

### A FINDING THAT IS NOT CODE: THE ORIGIN MOVED (2026-09-30)

While this section was being written, the generator was **renamed**. Read live, minutes apart in the same
session:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `window.generatorName` | `2hoy6c5u0x` | **`mythos-lia-barbelo`** |
| `window.generatorPublicId` | `60a6e23d828a54dc4c8b315f33c97ba3` | **`7f77c07ff49b600c18aac559ffb77e70`** |
| `location.origin` | `...60a6e23d....perchance.org` | **`...7f77c07f....perchance.org`** |
| `window.generatorIsUnsaved` | true (measured all session) | **false** (it is saved now) |

**ALL BROWSER STORAGE IS KEYED TO THAT SUBDOMAIN**, so on the new origin the terminal starts empty: kv
`lia_settings` holds only `folders` and `sync` (there is no `voice`, no `story`, no `agent`, no
`api_keys`), and the vault is **0 records / 0 bytes** (`media.stats()` after `media.ensure()`) where the
previous session measured 189 records. The door's answer is gone with them. TODO already predicted

(including the door's answer)"* - and it is now measured rather than predicted.

**Nothing in this pass caused it and nothing in this pass can undo it.** The old data is not deleted; it
is unreachable from this origin, and the platform's rule is that the subdomain comes back if the name
does - so naming it `2hoy6c5u0x` again is the way back to it. That is HIS call: the agent renamed
nothing, and did not try. What stays behind if the new name is kept: the vault (180 pictures, 9 clips and

the VOXCONPACK copy in kv, the keyring, the door's answer, the pair record and the chatlog record - all
still under `60a6e23d...`. **This is the single most important thing in this section.**

#### THE RULE ABOUT NAMES, MEASURED (2026-09-30)

1. **The name and the storage are the same thing.** The subdomain is the `generatorPublicId`, and it moved
   with the name. So: **decide the name before anything accumulates, and NEVER rename a generator that
   holds a record.**
2. **A duplicate is not a way round it.** A fork/duplicate gets a NEW subdomain, therefore an **EMPTY
   store**; the original keeps its name and its data. So duplicating **protects the original** (nothing is
   stranded) but does **not** carry the record across. "Duplicate, don't rename" is right in spirit and
   insufficient on its own: the data still has to be MOVED deliberately.
3. **What can actually move the record** (the terminal's own tools, and their limits): `/backup` = the
   SOURCE only; `/sync` + `/chatlog export|import` = the CONVERSATION (the turn-by-turn archive, and it
   only ever ADDS, never overwrites); the pair road = the same archive device-to-device; `/gallery
   export` = the vault's CATALOGUE (stamps, prompts, seeds, turns) - **the picture and clip BLOBS have no
   bulk export**, which is the real argument against renaming once there is a vault.
4. **The old name is free again** (`getGeneratorStats?name=2hoy6c5u0x` -> `generator-does-not-exist`;
   `getGeneratorsAndDependencies` returns it under `unfound`), so renaming back is possible. Whether it
   restores the old subdomain is the platform's own claim (*"unless they rename back to the old name"*)
   and could NOT be verified from here: the subdomain is not a plain function of the name (MD5, SHA-1 and
   SHA-256 of the name, and twenty salted variants, all miss), so it is a stored or peppered mapping. The
   cheap test is his, and it is free RIGHT NOW because the new origin holds nothing: rename back, open the
   gallery, look. If the 189 records are there, the hatch works.

### OPEN

  the tags purely informational for now - he said "for the moment", so it is a tag and no more.
- Whether the four browser/wire roads should ever be inferred from AUDIO rather than names; no. Not

- The **16 browser and 14 wire untagged voices** are the obvious first lines to add to `sex.map` if he

## §1ds - THE GATEKEEPER: ACCESS OR DENY BEFORE THE AGE SCREEN (2026-09-30)

**BLUF: the terminal has two doors now, in his order - GATE, THEN AGE. The first screen asks for the
household's shared secret (the SIGIL, sixteen unambiguous characters in four groups of four) and
only when it passes does the visitor ever see the 18+ checkbox underneath. A device with no mark
enrols on the first sigil it is ever given - that is how a second device joins - and only the
SHA-256 of the token is ever kept (kv lia_settings / gatekeeper), never the token. Measured
2026-09-30: the gate stands at z 2100 over the age door's 2000 on a fresh load, mint yields a well
formed sigil shown once on the screen with the PASS key armed, a wrong sigil stays shut with DENIED,
the right one opens, the stored record is 64 hex with no token in it, /rtfm check is clean at 83
commands, the boot watch is empty, and the panel fits a 390-pixel screen. The QR half of his sentence
is OPEN - no third-party encoder may ever see the token, so it waits on a vendored local encoder. AND
THE HONEST SENTENCE THAT COMES WITH IT: this is a household door, not a lock - the overlay, the key
and every word of the module are public source, and anyone with the editor open can lift the whole
gate off. It keeps the casual visitor out and the honest visitor honest.**

### WHAT HE SAID

> *"First pass on opening the website, the USER is presented with the LIA TERMINAL AGE checker.
> Another way to make it even more 'secure' is to have GATEKEEPER grant ACCESS or DENY first. The
> first screen looks for a valid token and checks against it or the USER presents his/her SIGIL
> (QR CODE) or token. Then they go to the age check screen and agree to the age and website
> policies."*
>
> *"Either way I'm OK with it. Perhaps it is wise to rename the URL back first and then duplicate
> it under a new name."*

THE SEQUENCE IS RIGHT, WITH ONE CONDITION: a duplicate is a NEW subdomain with an EMPTY store, so
the recovered record does NOT follow the copy. After renaming back he must move the record FIRST -
/backup for the source, /sync and /chatlog export for the conversation, /gallery export for the
catalogue - and the picture/clip BLOBS have no bulk export (per-item SAVE, /embed media, or a
browser-profile copy). The rename-back half is the platform's own claim, not a measurement - the
subdomain is not a plain hash of the name, so it could not be verified from here.

### WHAT WAS BUILT

NEW: src/js/gatekeeper.js (window.gatekeeper - state/show/close/pass/mint/copySigil/forget/
command/describe/help/boot). The token alphabet has no I, L, O, 0 or 1, so a sigil read off one
screen survives being typed into another; what is typed is upper-cased with dashes ignored before
it is hashed. Mint fills the field with the fresh token and arms PASS, so the order on the screen
is CARRY IT, then PASS. The module touches nothing of the age door's - the z-index does the
ordering, and each door reads only its own key.

CHANGED: index.html (the #gateKeeper overlay before #ageGate, MODULES entry and script tag before
agegate's, the foot shadow extended with the gate's own PASS/MINT/COPY against the same record),
src/js/chat.js (/gatekeeper dispatch, /help gatekeeper|gate|sigil|token, HELP_TOPICS),
src/css/terminal.css (#gateKeeper at 2100 reusing the age panel's furniture, the shown-once
sigil line, the message line), src/commands/commands.json (the gatekeeper entry - 82 -> 83),
src/rtfm/commands.md (regenerated, 12,827 bytes, /rtfm check clean), src/README.md (the file
list, THE GATEKEEPER section, the age section's tail corrected from 'not built yet').

### DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT

- NO QR YET. A sigil-as-QR is convenient and he named it, but a network encoder would receive the
  household secret, and that is a leak dressed as a feature. It waits on a small vendored local
  encoder; the text sigil is the whole gate until then.
- NO CROSS-DEVICE RECORD. Each device keeps its own mark; there is no server and no shared list.
  The carry-by-hand IS the sync.
- NO RECOVERY. A lost sigil is replaced (mint again, carry again), because a back door is a second
  front door - and physical access re-enrols anyway.
- THE FULL TOKEN NEVER TOUCHES THE STAGE. The stage is the transcript, the transcript is the
  archive, and the key ring's rule (never in the transcript) applies to this secret too.

armed, sigil line visible and matching. Wrong sigil: shut, DENIED. Right sigil: open. Forget:

### WHAT THE REPO TAUGHT (read, not guessed)

- Inspect is GET /api/v1/passes/{token} + X-API-Key (roles READ_WRITE/SCANNER_ONLY/READ_ONLY);
  the answer carries pass.{token, orderId, serviceId, serviceName, status, isValid, isExpired,
  redeemedAt, redeemedBy... expiresAt, issuedAt}. Open = active + unexpired + unspent.
- Verify is POST /api/v1/passes/verify - and it CONSUMES: status redeemed, redeemedAt set, order
  settled, telemetry emitted. A door must never call it. (The lorepack factory's older client only
  ever inspected read-only too - GET /v1/passes/:token - so both repos agree.)
- The client gate's three roads: camera scan (jsQR-style decode loop), QR image upload, manual
  entry; the payload shapes: bare token, JSON {token}, #access=/?access=, /passes/ path.
- Sessions are 8 hours, masked tokens in every log (first7...last4 - adopted exactly).

mask(), inspectAuthority() (direct, relay on refusal), passHouse() (unchanged rule, now stamping
